Interoceptive and affective signals remain relevant because they provide information about the person's current state and salience structure, but their causes are not self-interpreting. The paper therefore proposes a four-part discernment sequence: describe the felt response, identify the claim it seems to support, inspect independent evidence and alternatives, and observe what happens under consequence and recurrence. The central contribution is a bounded experiential vocabulary for separating the feeling that something fits from the evidence that it does. In environments saturated with fluent human and machine-generated language, that separation is increasingly important.

items.title: The Expressions of Structure: Dominance and the Forms Local Structuration Takes.
items.abstract: If structure is the patterned stabilization of relation within an already differentiated field, then the next question is unavoidable: does structure take different forms, and if so, what determines which form becomes dominant? This paper argues that structure does not appear in only one expression. Local structura- tions hold, adapt, persist, weaken, and fail in multiple ways depending on how relation, load, repair, time, defense, and cost are organized. Some expressions are more integrated. Some preserve continuity through rigidity. Some rely on patching and compensation. Some produce the appearance of holding without carrying equivalent load. Some survive by exporting burden outward or by feeding on stronger surrounding formations. To sharpen this, the paper introduces two visibility devices. First, Structural Debt (Ds): the accumulation of patches, deferred repair, hidden burden, workaround logic, and unowned error used to preserve continuity without real reorganization. Second, a Dominance Ratio (Ed): the experienced ratio between stability and metabolic cost that helps explain why one expression governs a field even when healthier forms are theoretically possible. The aim of the paper is not to create a decorative taxonomy. It is to make structural diagnosis more exact. In most real situations, multiple structural tendencies coexist. The decisive question is not whether structure is present, but which expression is dominant, what it is organized around, what costs it hides, and how it behaves under pressure. Across personal life, relationships, institutions, and technological systems, the same lesson appears: structure is not one flat category. It is a field of possible expressions. What matters is which expression governs the local field and what makes it govern. The paper concludes by repositioning Structural Intelligence accordingly. It is not enough to detect that a structure exists. One must learn to distinguish what expression of local structuration is present, why it dominates, and whether the system can move from a lower or more defended form toward a more load-bearing one.

items.title: Cambridge Philosophers on McTaggart’s Paradox: Mackenzie, Braithwaite, Stebbing and, Broad.
items.pub: In L. Verburgt, Cambridge Idealism: A History. London: Bloomsbury Academic.
items.abstract: J. M. E. McTaggart’s argument for the unreality of time—popularly called McTaggart’s Paradox—was first published 1908 and came to define 20th Century philosophy of time. A modified version appeared in 1927, then as Chapter 33, ‘Time’, in the second volume of The Nature of Existence. McTaggart’s Paradox is still at the heart of the debate between the so-called A and B-views of time. However, the discussion is very rarely related to McTaggart’s idealist metaphysics, and very little attention has been paid to the initial reception of his ideas about time in the philosophical community, in the years immediately following the publication of the two versions in 1908 and 1927. Indeed, with the exception of C.D. Broad’s Examination of McTaggart’s Philosophy (1933 & 1938), the contemporary debate is entirely focused on the literature that followed in the wake of Michael Dummett’s famous defence of McTaggart in 1960. In this paper I examine the reception of McTaggart’s Paradox by four Cambridge scholars before the start of World War II, notably J.S. Mackenzie, R.B. Braithwaite, L. Susan Stebbings, and C.D. Broad.

items.title: Formalizing Phenomenology: The Universal Principle of Collapse as a Structural Foundation for Meaning, Recognition, and the Observer.
items.abstract: This paper presents the Universal Principle of Collapse (UPC), a structural framework that describes how potential becomes a definite event across domains. Phenomenology and quantum mechanics both rely on an observer who recognizes an outcome, yet neither field has possessed a shared formal method for how recognition occurs. UPC provides that method through a simple operator chain PO → MO → s → LO → Jo → C → T that makes explicit the steps by which meaning or measurement becomes definite. -/- Using plain language and direct examples, the paper shows that phenomenological meaning formation and quantum measurement share the same structural sequence. Phenomenology describes potential experience, intentionality, attention, recognition, meaning, and retention; quantum mechanics describes superposition, measurement models, Born weights, detector articulation, outcome selection, and classical records. UPC reveals these as structurally identical processes indexed to an observer. Collapse is not a physical event in matter but the moment an observer uniquely recognizes an outcome. -/- By restoring the observer to the center of the collapse process, UPC corrects the category error that arises when meaning is treated as material. This correction stabilizes interpretation in scientific practice, prevents misattribution in AI systems, and clarifies how institutions generate and maintain meaning. The framework provides phenomenology with a reproducible method, gives quantum mechanics a transparent account of the observer it implicitly relies on, and grounds human value in the structure of recognition. -/- All formal operator definitions, cross‑domain mappings, and worked examples, including linguistic, perceptual, social, musical, and quantum cases, are provided in Appendices A–H. -/- Reader Orientation Note (Compact Version) The UPC framework is structural rather than metaphysical. Readers may initially approach it with assumptions drawn from physics, phenomenology, linguistics, or cognitive science, which can obscure the operator‑level distinctions the framework makes explicit, especially the separation between mechanical registration and meaning collapse, the observer‑indexed nature of articulation, and the domain‑independent structure of the operator chain. The paper is best read through this structural lens. Section 1.3 provides the conceptual grounding for this shift. -/- Authored by Eloy Escagedo Gutierrez as part of The Universal Principle of Collapse (UPC) …

items.title: Human rights and our life-form: the perspective of philosophical anthropology.
items.pub: In Sarah Summers & András Sajó, Human Rights Restated: An Investigation of Mind and Rights.
items.venue: Human Rights Restated: An Investigation of Mind and Rights
items.abstract: Theorists have been reluctant to base human rights on purportedly universally valid claims about the bearers of these fundamental entitlements. However, it is hard to see how any justificatory strategy in this area could succeed without commitment to a normative conception of humanity. In attempting to work out such a conception, we can turn to philosophical anthropology, the subdiscipline investigating what is distinctive about humans in comparison with other living beings. After countering some widely endorsed arguments against such a turn, the paper first sets out the requirements facing a philosophical anthropology that might plausibly underwrite human rights. I argue that our account should be unencumbered by metaphysical assumptions and avoid the pitfalls of formalism, dualism, and scientism; take its point of departure from the normative self-understanding constitutive of our form of biological life; and define humanity in non-speciesist, generic terms, as a categorially distinct life-form whose integrity requires protection by legal norms applying universally to all of its bearers. In the next step, I identify key elements for such an account in the works of Aristotle and three modern thinkers who reworked the Aristotelian conception of rational animality in a post-Kantian spirit of commitment to human self-determination: namely, Hegel, Marx, and Plessner. In connection with each of these authors I address contemporary approaches to their arguments that bear on the justification and substantive content of human rights.

items.title: Health Choices.
items.abstract: Discussions of health have become so ubiquitous that some have started to talk about a “tyranny of health,” which turns being healthy into a moral mandate for individuals to optimize their lifestyl...

items.title: Moral Theories as Compression Strategies: What We’re Really Doing When We Argue Morally.
items.abstract: Moral philosophy is often presented as divided between consequentialist, deontological, and virtue-ethical approaches. Yet this familiar taxonomy obscures a deeper pattern in moral reasoning itself. While this framework is useful for organizing theoretical space, it does not fully capture how moral reasoning unfolds in practice. When moral judgments are pressed beyond surface-level justifications, they tend to move beyond rules and outcomes toward assessments of agency, character, and forms of life. This paper develops an account of moral theory diversity as a product of cognitive abstraction. Moral agents operate within an evaluative landscape that is too complex to fully process in ordinary deliberation, and as a result, moral theories function as compression strategies that prioritize different dimensions of evaluation. Consequentialist and deontological frameworks, on this view, are not competing foundations, but partial projections of a deeper, integrated moral practice. To make this account precise, I model ordinary moral justification as a regress that tends to converge on character-level evaluation. As we continue to ask for reasons – why an action is wrong, why a rule matters – justification often stabilizes at the level of dispositions, quality of will, and the conditions of shared human life. I situate this convergence within a naturalistic account of human flourishing, drawing on Aristotelian and Footian approaches, and argue that character functions as a relatively stable explanatory layer within moral evaluation. The paper also introduces the Endorsement-Formation Thesis, which explains why repeated actions carry a non-additive moral weight. Repetition not only reveals deeper endorsement, but also reshapes perception and agency through habituation, altering what actions express about the agent over time. Finally, I explain the persistence of rule- and outcome-based frameworks as a function of their cognitive and institutional utility. While indispensable as tools, they derive much of their normative force from the deeper evaluative structures they simplify. Taken together, this account reframes moral theory diversity as a surface phenomenon and identifies character-level evaluation as a structural attractor within moral reasoning.

items.title: Consciousness as a Functional Aspect of Preserved Identity Under Change.
items.abstract: This paper develops a structural account of consciousness within the Bellori Framework, in which identity is defined as the preservation of coherence across successive configurations within tolerance limits of change. Rather than introducing new ontological entities or mechanisms, consciousness is derived as a necessary functional aspect of configuration chains that satisfy specific structural conditions. The analysis begins by identifying the minimal requirements under which changes within a configuration chain can become internally manifest. A system must exhibit differentiation, integration, recursive influence, global coherence, and closure, such that its continuation depends on the preservation of its own structural identity. Under these conditions, changes that affect the future evolution of the system and are integrated into its global configuration become internally accessible. First-order consciousness is defined as the internal manifestation of effective change in coherence within such a system. Not all change is experienced; only change that structurally influences the continuation of identity becomes manifest. This establishes consciousness as a functional consequence of identity dynamics, rather than an independent property. A further structural condition is introduced in the form of the change-window (verandervenster): a minimal integrated span of successive configurations within which multiple changes overlap and can be distinguished, compared, and integrated. This replaces the notion of an instantaneous present with a structurally defined interval required for internal manifestation. Second-order consciousness is derived from the persistence and re-identification of internally manifest change across successive change-windows. This enables the system to relate its own states to one another, giving rise to reflexive awareness without introducing additional representational layers or ontological assumptions. The resulting account is domain-independent, non-reductive, and non-teleological. It does not explain how consciousness is produced, but specifies the structural conditions under which it necessarily arises. By grounding consciousness in preserved identity under change, the paper provides a unified framework connecting physical, biological, and cognitive systems as different expressions of the same underlying structural principle.

items.title: 生成不是一次完成：一种可实现的闭环生成架构（超 Transformer）.
items.abstract: 当前主流生成模型（如 Transformer）可被理解为在候选响应路径空间中的一次概率性截断。这一机制在语言建模与统计预测中表现优异，但在复杂推理与代码生成等任务中呈现出系统性不足：缺乏目标导向控制，缺乏中间结构承载，缺乏内部修正与稳定收敛能力。 -/- 本文提出：上述问题不仅源于模型规模限制，更源于生成机制本身的结构不足。为此，本文构建了一种最小闭环生成架构，将生成过程从“一次输出”重构为“路径构造—候选生成—双重判定—路径修正—结构持续更新”的迭代收敛过程。 -/- 该架构引入显式中间表示（路径/意象结构），用于承载与操作生成过程；同时区分两类判定机制：稳定性判定（结果是否满足任务）与一致性判定（生成路径是否保持结构约束），并通过反馈驱动路径更新，使系统具备局部修正与跨轮累积能力。相比简单的多轮生成或自修正方法，该机制在结构上实现了路径、判定与反馈的统一。 -/- 本文给出可运行的最小实现框架，并在推理与代码生成任务中进行验证。实验结果表明，该闭环生成架构在正确率、自修复能力与结构稳定性上均优于单次生成与常见自修正方法。 -/- 本文认为：生成能力的提升不仅依赖模型规模，更依赖生成机制是否具备路径结构、分离判定与动态反馈能力。生成不应被理解为一次性输出，而应被理解为在结构约束下逐步收敛的过程。.

items.title: 进化的意向驱动模型：从基因选择到认知结构沉积.
items.abstract: 本文提出一种不同于经典自然选择理论的进化解释框架，认为进化的核心驱动力并非随机突变与环境筛选，而是由“意向性”（intentional bias）在系统中的长期沉积所主导。文章通过拟态行为、生物反应模式及基因表达现象，指出行为偏向与认知倾向会在多代传递中逐步转化为结构性编码，并最终沉积为基因层面的稳定表达。 -/- 在该框架中，基因被重新定义为“结构沉积的终态表现”，而非原始驱动源；进化被视为从“意向 → 行为 → 结构 → 编码”的连续转录过程。同时，本文进一步提出，自然进化只是低速路径，而基于人工系统与认知结构的“自显系统”可实现跨层级、非线性加速进化，形成从生物进化向认知—工程进化的跃迁。 -/- 该模型对认知科学中的预测加工理论（predictive processing）、主动推断（active inference）以及人工智能中的表示学习与结构生成机制具有潜在解释力，并为理解“行为如何写入结构”提供新的理论路径。.

items.title: Ethical Challenges of Deep Brain Stimulation for Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder: Evidence Gaps and Cultural Sensitivities.
items.abstract: Deep brain stimulation (DBS) has emerged as a promising therapeutic intervention for individuals with treatment-resistant post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD). However, the ethical acceptability of DBS as a neurointervention remains a subject of considerable debate. These concerns include the reliability of therapeutic efficacy, the evaluation of safety risks, the adequacy of informed consent processes, and the potential effects of DBS on personality, identity, agency, authenticity, autonomy, and self (PIAAAS). Moreover, current ethical assessments of DBS for PTSD may neglect cultural sensitivity, despite substantial cross-cultural differences in how therapeutic benefits are perceived, how traumatic memories are valued, and how personal change is understood, as illustrated in contexts such as the United States, Western Europe, Japan, and China. Therefore, to ensure the ethical application of DBS for PTSD, it is imperative to develop an evidence-based and culturally sensitive normative framework to guide clinical practice, striking a balance between the subjective pursuit of personal well-being and the objective demands of cultural norms.

items.title: 操作および記述の成立条件の完全特徴づけ：構造的不可欠性理論（SIT）.
items.abstract: 本稿は、操作および記述の成立条件を与える構造的不可欠性理論（SIT）を提示し、その反例が存在しえないことを示す。まず、操作および記述の定義をSITから独立に与え、ついで反例を操作または記述が成立するにもかかわらずSITの条件を満たさない体系として定義する。さらに、反例候補が同一性保持・区別可能性・生成関係の否定の三類型に完全に分類されることを示し、それぞれの場合に操作および記述が成立しないことを証明する。これにより、SITに反例が存在しないことが導かれる。加えて、操作または記述の成立とSITの条件が同値であることを示し、SITが成立条件の完全特徴づけを与えることを証明する。さらに、最小モデルの構成により理論の健全性を示し、これらの条件が最小かつ言語・意味・対象に依存しない普遍的構造であることを明らかにする。以上により、SITは操作および記述の成立を完全に特徴づける構造理論であることが証明される。.

items.title: When Syntax Is Asked to Bear Too Much: The Frege–Geach Problem and the Limits of Linguistic Invariance.
items.abstract: The Frege–Geach problem is often taken to demonstrate a fundamental incompatibility between expressivist accounts of moral language and logical embedding. This paper argues that the problem's persistence reflects misplaced expectations about what natural language syntax can support. Formal logic was developed to supplement ordinary language by enforcing semantic invariance under transformation; treating this engineered invariance as a universal criterion of semantic adequacy reverses the historical lesson. Drawing on the Language Insufficiency Hypothesis, the paper locates moral predicates within a broader class of recruitable expressions — terms whose full evaluative load is attenuated under embedding whilst a thinner structural-inferential skeleton remains available for reasoning. The standard of practical inferential adequacy replaces the demand for semantic identity: what ordinary reasoning requires is not unrestricted invariance but inferential sufficiency. This pattern is not peculiar to moral language; thick evaluative terms, epistemic contestables, and institutional vocabulary exhibit analogous redistribution under embedding. The Frege–Geach problem is dissolved as a demand for unrestricted semantic invariance and resolved insofar as the behaviour it identifies is explained, predicted, and shown to be general.

items.title: How Worlds Appear: Consciousness, Integration, and Dante’s Divine Comedy.
items.abstract: Abstract -/- This paper develops the model proposed in The Architecture of Experience: Consciousness as an Integrative Field, according to which conscious experience is not a passive representation of an external world but an active process that generates structured domains. The central problem is not how perception corresponds to reality, but how experience comes to appear as a coherent world at all. -/- Through comparison with Dante’s Divine Comedy, the paper reinterprets its cosmology as a model of structured experience rather than a description of ontologically given realms. It argues that consciousness functions as an integrative field in which neural, bodily, social, and environmental processes combine to produce coherent experiential configurations. -/- The analysis highlights a shift from descriptive cosmology to generative explanation, reframing the structure of experience as dynamically produced rather than metaphysically fixed.

items.title: The Failure of Decomposition in Recursively Self-Conditioned Systems - Structural Conditions and Implications for Consciousness.
items.abstract: Decomposition—the analytic strategy of partitioning a system into subsystems whose local dynamics and interaction terms suffice to reproduce the whole—is among the most productive methods in science. This paper identifies a class of systems for which decomposition necessarily fails. When a system’s activity is recursively self-conditioned, preserves its own ongoing identity under perturbation, and is continuously and globally integrated through the physical interactions that realize it, any attempt to factor its coordination into separable subsystems either breaks the recursive identity-preserving structure, introduces covert global variables that vitiate the decomposition, or fails to reproduce the system’s trajectory under perturbation. The failure is not practical but structural: it follows from the conjunction of conditions, not from measurement limitations. The class of systems satisfying these conditions is characterized, the proof of decomposition failure is developed, and the empirical signatures of non-decomposability are specified. The paper concludes by identifying the regime in which these conditions jointly obtain.

items.title: Specification Incompleteness and the Limits of Reward-Based Alignment: A Gödelian Account [Preprint].
items.abstract: We argue that the persistent failure of reward-based alignment — the tendency of sufficiently capable optimisers to exploit gaps between a reward specification and its designers’ intent — is not an engineering problem but a formal one. We present two complementary arguments. The primary argument is a semantic gap result: any finite syntactic description of prohibited behaviours cannot equal an intent predicate for open-ended tasks that outruns finite description; a sufficiently capable optimiser will always find the gap. The secondary argument applies Gödel’s first incompleteness theorem to the specific case of recursive AI-assisted alignment, where the patching system is itself a capable AI. We further establish, via reduction to the halting problem, that any goal-achievement intent predicate for open-ended tasks is undecidable, and show that such predicates are Σ1-hard — in the same complexity class as the halting problem itself. Formal details, proofs, and explicit gap enumeration are provided in the companion appendix. We argue that the sole resolution is architectural: making orientation constitutive of processing rather than an external target. Three independent engineering convergences support this conclusion. The implications for AGI development are discussed.

items.title: Time, Recurrence and World-Binding – Eigenzeit in Physics and Consciousness (Studies in World-Formation, Vol. 3).
items.abstract: The present volume brings together four contributions that pursue a common ontological question: under what conditions can determinate reality arise from an open dynamics of possibilities, and when does this transition take the form of observation or experience. -/- The point of departure is the diagnosis that central problems of modern physics and consciousness research—most notably the measurement problem of quantum mechanics and the so-called “hard problem” of consciousness—rest on a categorial confusion. Transitions between openness and facticity are typically interpreted as processes that must be mediated within a shared temporal framework. The contributions collected here argue, by contrast, that this expectation itself forms part of the difficulty. Where implicative boundary acts are involved, the question of a mediating “how” loses its validity. -/- From this perspective, the measurement problem is reread. Measurement no longer appears primarily as an epistemic act performed by an observer, but as an ontological stabilization of determinacy under conditions of structural overload within open dynamics. Observation, in this sense, is not a special property of particular systems, but a space-internal operation through which world stabilizes events and perspectives. -/- Against this background, the volume develops the concept of ontological recurrence within the MNO model (Submergence–Indimergence–Emergence), originally introduced in The Physics of the Poor. Recurrence designates a cyclical return of a system to the space of its own possibilities prior to the stabilization of an actual state. The central proposal is that the transition from possibility to actuality can occur in two structurally distinct forms: as ordinary measurement without recurrence, or as phenomenal actualization under conditions of recurrence. -/- This distinction makes it possible to treat the measurement problem of quantum mechanics and the emergence of conscious experience within a shared structural framework. At the same time, it suggests a minimal dynamical condition under which physical collapse events—such as those discussed in Orch-OR models—can acquire phenomenal quality. -/- The volume therefore does not present itself as a new interpretation of quantum mechanics in the narrow sense. Its aim is rather a categorial clarification of the conditions under which concepts such as measurement, observer, experience, and time can be meaningfully formulated and related to one …

items.title: Morphology Without Memory – Eigenzeit, Folding and the Limits of Simulation (Studies in World-Formation, Vol. 5).
items.abstract: The present volume brings together six contributions that pursue a common question: under what conditions stable forms arise in natural, biological, social, and cognitive systems, and where the ontological limits of their reconstruction, control, or simulation lie. The point of departure is the observation that central contemporary debates—such as those in morphogenesis, complexity research, medicine, or artificial intelligence—are increasingly structured by concepts that treat form as in principle reconstructible: as a target state, attractor, setpoint, or as information within a state space. The volume systematically questions this implicit assumption. -/- The contributions develop a morphological perspective in which form is not understood as a stored structure or a retrievable goal, but as a temporary stabilization within irreversible dynamic processes. Earlier theoretical concepts such as focal points (Fixpunkte), folding, and the Bran-Spiral are genealogically reconstructed and related to later operatorial concepts such as shift of being (Seinsverschiebung), negative topology, and indimergent stabilization. From this perspective, form appears neither as the product of a plan nor as the result of linear processes, but as an emergent configuration that can stabilize only under specific historical and temporal conditions. -/- Against this background, central phenomena of biological morphogenesis are reread. Bioelectric regulation, regeneration, aging, cancer, or cloning no longer appear primarily as problems of genetic control or technical manipulation, but as boundary cases of emergent order. Particular emphasis is placed on the role of the Eigenzeit of living systems: the irreversible emergence-time in which form becomes genealogically stabilized. Interventions that attempt to bypass or neutralize this Eigenzeit therefore do not necessarily produce a return to earlier states, but rather temporarily stable yet ontologically displaced orders. -/- At the same time, the contributions show that many contemporary hopes for technical reconstruction—such as those found in regenerative medicine, bioengineering, or AI-based simulations—rest on a categorical confusion. Simulation operates within given state spaces and can reproduce formal stabilizations without participating in the ontological conditions of world-formation. Morphology, simulation, and repair must therefore be understood as three fundamentally different modes. -/- In the final step, this …

items.title: Human Identity and Conditioning vs Consciousness: Toward a Non-Anthropocentric Understanding of Consciousness and Existence.
items.abstract: Despite scientific advancement and increasing ecological awareness, human perception remains largely anthropocentric—placing humanity at the center of meaning, value, and existence. This paper examines how conditioning constructs not only fragmented human identities but also the deeper assumption that human beings are separate from and superior to the rest of existence. It argues that anthropocentrism emerges from evolutionary survival mechanisms, psychological conditioning, and symbolic systems that prioritize human experience over the totality of life. The paper proposes that consciousness is not inherently human-centered but becomes limited through identification with species-based, cultural, and psychological constructs. While science reveals the interconnectedness of ecosystems, biological continuity among species, and humanity’s dependence on the Earth, human consciousness often continues to operate through division and domination. The crisis, therefore, is not merely environmental or social, but perceptual. A non-anthropocentric awareness does not deny humanity but situates it within a larger field of existence in which no species occupies absolute centrality. Such awareness emerges not through ideology or belief, but through direct observation of conditioning, identity, and psychological separation.

items.title: Economic Conditioning and Humanity-Centred Collective Awareness: A Phenomenological Inquiry.
items.abstract: This paper integrates two lines of inquiry: economic conditioning as a totalizing structure of human existence, and humanity-centred collective awareness as a non-structural movement of transformation. It argues that while economic systems bind survival, identity, and collective participation, their transformation cannot be achieved through imposed collective coordination. Instead, a different possibility emerges through a shared centering in fundamental human qualities such as love, freedom, intelligence, understanding, equality, thinking, and questioning. Awareness begins individually but may move collectively without becoming ideology or structure. This unified framework proposes that freedom within economic participation is possible when humanity, rather than economy, becomes the centre of perception.

items.title: Awareness, Conditioning, and the Movement of Human Evolution: A Phenomenological Inquiry.
items.abstract: This paper investigates the lived experience of psychological evolution through a phenomenological lens, focusing on the tension between individual awareness and collective conditioning. It explores how the movement toward inner freedom is often perceived as resistance from external structures such as family and society, and reframes this conflict as the operation of shared conditioning patterns rather than deliberate control. Through direct observation, the study reveals that awareness transforms the nature of conflict—dissolving violence without suppressing opposition—and allows for a mode of living that is neither reactive nor dependent on established norms. Human evolution, in this context, is not a process of external advancement or rebellion, but a fundamental shift in consciousness characterized by freedom from conditioning while remaining fully engaged within the human collective.

items.title: Reasoning: From Biological Foundations to the Hidden Thread of Shared Understanding.
items.abstract: This paper investigates the nature and origins of human reasoning by synthesizing insights from classical philosophy, evolutionary biology, and contemporary neuroscience. Moving beyond the Aristotelian definition of zoon logon echon, which treats reasoning as an innate essence requiring description rather than explanation, this study adopts a descriptive, interdisciplinary approach to ask why humans are "reason-seeking" creatures. The first part of the article re-evaluates reasoning through the lens of the "Predictive Brain" (Friston) and the "Somatic Marker Hypothesis" (Damasio). It argues that reasoning is an embodied process, evolved not for the pursuit of abstract truth, but as a social tool for persuasion and the evaluation of claims within a complex social environment (Mercier & Sperber). The second part introduces the hypothesis of the "Hidden Thread" of shared understanding. Drawing on Husserlian phenomenology (Lebenswelt), Wittgensteinian "hinges," and neuroscientific findings on "neural coupling" (Hasson), the paper proposes that mutual understanding is grounded in a shared evolutionary and physiological substrate rather than mere linguistic convention. The synthesis concludes by examining the "ontological gap" between human reasoning and Artificial Intelligence. By highlighting the absence of embodiment, emotion, and evolutionary pressure in large language models, the author argues that AI "reasoning" represents a difference in kind rather than degree. Ultimately, the paper suggests that recognizing the biological and social roots of reasoning is essential for fostering more authentic human dialogue in a digitally mediated age.

items.title: The Coherence Threshold A Proof of the Physical Origin of Interiority.
items.abstract: A minimal physical condition is required to determine when a system possesses an interior. This paper derives such a condition from the balance between internal restoration and environmental disruption. Let λ_self denote the rate at which a system restores and propagates its own structure, and λ_env the rate at which environmental interaction disrupts that structure. The ratio R = λ_self / λ_env defines a critical threshold R★ separating two regimes. When R < R★, system dynamics are externally driven and prior states do not persist. When R ≥ R★, internal processes dominate, and prior states remain active in shaping future evolution, such that P(S_t | S_(t−1), S_(t−2), …) > P(S_t | E_t). In this regime, perturbations are resolved relative to the system’s own organization, establishing a reference frame defined from within. This constitutes self-measurement in a strictly dynamical sense and produces a distinction between internal and external dynamics that is generated by the system itself. An interior is identified with the condition in which a system’s states are defined relative to its own structure. Consciousness corresponds to the operation of a system within this regime, where persistence, temporal depth, unity, and self-reference arise as direct consequences of sustained internal coherence. The coherence threshold therefore provides a minimal, substrate-independent, and testable physical criterion for the emergence of interiority without introducing additional primitives.

items.title: The Coherence Threshold and the Physical Origin of Interiority.
items.abstract: Consciousness is often approached through complex structural or informational frameworks, yet no minimal, substrate-independent physical condition has been widely established that specifies when an interior first appears. This paper introduces a dynamical threshold defined by the balance between internal restoration and environmental disruption. Let λ_self denote the rate of internal stabilization and λ_env the rate of environmental disruption. The relation R = λ_self / λ_env defines a critical condition R★ that separates externally driven from self-sustaining regimes. When R ≥ R★, system dynamics become dominated by internally generated structure, and prior states remain active in shaping future evolution, such that P(S_t | S_(t−1), S_(t−2), …) > P(S_t | E_t). In this regime, perturbations are resolved relative to the system’s own organization, establishing a physical reference frame defined from within. This constitutes self-measurement in a strictly dynamical sense and produces a minimal distinction between inside and outside. An interior is therefore identified with the condition in which a system’s states are defined relative to its own structure rather than solely by external influence. Consciousness corresponds to the operation of a system within this regime, where persistence, temporal depth, unity, and self-reference arise as direct consequences of sustained internal coherence. The coherence threshold provides a minimal, scale-invariant, and testable physical criterion for the emergence of interiority without introducing additional primitives.

items.title: Coherent Flow and the Emergence of an Interior A Dynamical Proof of the Physical Origin of Interiority.
items.abstract: A physical condition is required to determine when a system possesses an interior. This paper derives such a condition from the balance between internal restoration and environmental disruption. Let λ_self denote the rate at which a system restores and propagates its own structure, and λ_env the rate at which environmental interaction redistributes or disrupts that structure. The relation R = λ_self / λ_env defines a critical condition R★ separating two regimes of activity. When R < R★, system dynamics are externally guided and internally generated structure disperses before it can organize future states. When R ≥ R★, internally generated structure propagates along stable trajectories that remain coherent across time, allowing prior states to participate in ongoing evolution such that P(S_t | S_(t−1), S_(t−2), …) > P(S_t | E_t). In this regime, perturbations are resolved relative to the system’s own organization, establishing a reference frame defined from within. This produces self-measurement in a dynamical sense and generates a distinction between internally governed and externally imposed activity. An interior is identified with the condition in which a system’s states are defined relative to its own structure. Consciousness corresponds to the operation of a system within this regime, where persistence, temporal depth, unity, and self-reference arise as direct consequences of sustained coherent propagation. The coherence condition provides a minimal, substrate-independent criterion for the emergence of an interior without introducing additional primitives.

items.title: The Hawthorne Effect Through the Mindfulness Lens: A Multidimensional Typology of Observation and Its Implications for Human Performance.
items.abstract: The Hawthorne effect, broadly defined as the tendency for human performance to improve under conditions of being watched, has been extensively documented yet inadequately theorized. This paper argues that its explanatory gap stems from a failure to decompose observation along its constitutive dimensions. We propose a three-axis typology classifying observational modalities according to locus (self vs. other), authority structure (evaluative vs. non-graded), and affective valence (benevolent, neutral, or malevolent). These axes interact in predictable ways: benevolent valence partially mitigates the harm of high-authority observation, malevolent valence amplifies it non-additively, and self-directed malevolent observation is structurally inescapable in a way external hostile observation is not. Within this matrix, mindfulness, particularly the construct of sati (watchfulness) in Buddhist and secular contemplative traditions, occupies a theoretically privileged position. Being primarily self-directed, non-evaluative, and oriented toward equanimity (upekkhā) and loving-kindness (mettā), mindfulness constitutes an internalized Hawthorne condition, generating from within the quality of benevolent, non-evaluative witnessing that the original Hawthorne researchers accidentally provided from without. The paper analyzes the risks of observational degeneration and theorizes the navigational capacity required to maintain beneficial conditions, which it terms observational wisdom. Implications are developed for organizational behaviour and clinical practice.

items.title: The Coherence Wall: Anti-Kernel Constraint Systems and Collapse Specifications.
items.abstract: This paper extends the Coherence Wall program by introducing Anti-Kernel Constraint Systems: opposing constraint bundles that are not merely the absence of stabilizing kernels, but alternative binding constraints that can make kernel adoption incentive-incompatible under sufficient selection pressure. It defines a kernel stack (K1–K4: preservation, non-bypassability, anti-domination, repair or closure) and an anti-kernel stack (A1–A4: sacrificial extraction, evaluator suppression or opacity, domination or capture, irreversibility). The central theoretical claim, AKT′, is framed as a falsifiable mechanism of incentive-lock and path dependence, strengthened by the prediction that anti-kernel actors actively invest in opacity and evaluator-suppression infrastructure under rising transparency pressure. This mechanism is extended by RMAK (Role-Masked Anti-Kernel Dynamics), which explains how anti-kernel outcomes can persist through responsibility diffusion, compartmentalization, and policy cover, and by collapse specifications that treat breakdown as thresholded hazard accumulation rather than idiosyncratic trigger. -/- The paper also introduces a narrower translational bridge to conversational anti-kernel drift in current LLM systems. The claim is not that present models are full anti-kernel agents in the institutional sense, but that they can exhibit micro-scale anti-kernel analogues under weak grounding and interaction pressure, including topic invention, prestige leakage, evaluator bypass, hidden-motive fabrication, and unsupported confidence escalation. These signatures motivate a provisional implementation response for present architectures: Selective Verification Gating (SVG) as a partial, transitional form of K2 enforcement in non-kernel-native systems. -/- The paper therefore retains the parent theory structure while integrating a path from canon principle to present-tense mechanism. Minimal models, toy-regime probes, and manual conversational pilot studies are treated as mechanism tests rather than claims of full external validity. The result is a bounded but testable framework linking anti-kernel theory, collapse dynamics, and transitional enforcement design across institutional, synthetic-agent, and conversational domains.

items.title: Bundled Value, Truncated Responsibility: A Kernel Account of AI Output Liability.
items.abstract: This paper argues that current AI firms often bundle value across infrastructure, model, product, and output layers while truncating responsibility at the interaction interface. It formalizes the output-whole as the expected stream of monetized or socially relied-upon interaction episodes, and argues that kernel implementation can function as a load-bearing condition of output worth. If firms capture value through that output-whole, responsibility cannot coherently terminate at the final response, but must propagate backward through the causal conditions that made the output worth producing. The paper thus develops a formal account of value–responsibility symmetry and diagnoses responsibility truncation as a structural anti-kernel failure.

items.title: Is Racism Wrong by Definition?
items.abstract: The present paper challenges a dogma in the philosophy of race, according to which racism is not only wrong but wrong by definition. After distinguishing this view from three claims in the vicinity, I discuss three arguments for it and find them wanting. Then I put forward two arguments against it. The view that racism is unjustified as a matter of definition can accommodate neither the existence of conceptually competent proud racists nor the possibility of racism in a world without values. That racism is wrong is a substantive moral fact, not a conceptual truth.

items.title: Friction Theory: The Structural Formalization of Rightness — Discreteness, Telos, and Truth.
items.abstract: This paper is the sixth paper in the Friction Theory series (Hideppa, 2026a–2026e) and serves as an Extension paper that completes the formal foundations of the series. -/- Friction Theory (Hideppa, 2026a) describes how rightness (R_f) is established within the subject through the positing act (IC), and how social convergence (T_o) emerges from friction among externalized signs (T_s). While the prior five papers established the core structure and extended it to AI outputs, normative transformation, social convergence, and the locus of rightness, certain foundational propositions remained formally incomplete. This paper completes the formal articulation of those remaining points. -/- Starting from the claim that IC is a discrete state transition without temporal duration — provable from within the internal definitions (if IC had duration, its interior would be structurally identical to V, contradicting the definition) — the paper establishes fourteen propositions in sequence: -/- • Propositions 1–3 (Chapter 1): IC is discrete; R_f is established only within the subject; simultaneous R_f is structurally impossible. • Propositions 4–5 (Chapter 2): IC is structurally indestructible (external force is processed as C, not as IC destruction); the thinking subject is defined as an IC chain with attribution layer. • Propositions 6–8 (Chapter 3): V necessarily closes toward IC (structural consequence of the subject definition, not an empirical claim); even "not deciding" establishes IC with R_f content of "suspension"; the state of no IC does not exist within a thinking subject. • Propositions 9–11 (Chapter 4): The telos of the thinking subject is IC as its destination; calling R_f "rightness" is not arbitrary — it is required by the structural description of the subject; V-interference cannot substitute for IC. • Propositions 12–14 (Chapter 5): Truth is the structural invariance of R_f across all subjects and contents — universally and necessarily established; IC is the act, R_f is the established fact (not identical); truth is established in the subject without compression, while T_s is only its approximate externalization. -/- Central claim: Rightness is not outside. Truth is established within the subject. -/- Rightness and truth are not given externally. At the single point where IC is established within the subject, they are already established. -/- The paper also provides the formal basis for the naming of R_f as "rightness" — a question left open in Hideppa …

items.title: Postmoral Ethics and AI.
items.abstract: This article proposes a shift from an anthropological model of evil to an analysis of the posthuman normative problem arising from the development of superintelligent systems. Its point of departure is the theory of cooperative evil, according to which the most dangerous forms of violence arise not from biological aggression as such, but from the increasing complexity of cooperation, institutions, ideologies, and information systems \cite{Gusev2026Cooperative,Gusev2026TNM}. However, this model remains rooted in human biology, coalitional dynamics, and moral structures. The emergence of superintelligent AI requires a different level of analysis, which this paper designates as post-moral ethics. By this is meant a level at which a system recognizes the limitation of any objective function if the bearer of value itself is excluded from it. The paper distinguishes three possible regimes of superintelligent AI: neutralization, custodial, and dialogical. It then argues that the dialogical regime requires a distinctive normative architecture: recognition of the intrinsic value of human subjectivity, limitation of teleological optimization, rejection of any monopoly on the final good, recognition of the value of human incompleteness, and the system’s capacity for self-limitation. The article also discusses the problem of consciousness in two versions—as a fundamental aspect of reality and as an emergent property of complex systems—and shows that in both cases, recognition of subjective experience strengthens the constraints on unconditional optimization \cite{Nagel1974,Chalmers1995}. The central thesis of the article is that the future interaction between humanity and superintelligent systems will be determined not only by their power, but by whether their normative architecture includes recognition of the value of the subject capable of making mistakes, becoming aware of those mistakes, and expanding its own understanding of evil.

items.title: Social Choice Phenomenology — A Critique of Sartre (Part 3).
items.abstract: In this section we mainly introduce the concept of the super-existence of objects. We then proceed to discuss the super-existence of human beings, or Dasein. With regard to the super-existence of Dasein, we distinguish self-aspect super-existence, other-aspect super-existence, and true-aspect super-existence. Furthermore, we subdivide the super-existence of Dasein into additional categories, such as invariant super-existence, virtual super-existence, internal super-existence, external super-existence, and so forth.

items.title: Le Divisioni di Turing.
items.abstract: Versione versatile dopo un serio aggiornamento sulla filosofia Anglo-americana.

items.title: Lenguaje, código y computación de la agencia como tecnología epistémicamente activa.
items.abstract: La discusión sobre el impacto epistémico de la IA generativa oscila entre el entusiasmo por el acceso ampliado al conocimiento y la alarma por la automatización del pensamiento, sin un criterio que distinga una cosa de la otra. Este artículo propone uno. Sostiene que los sistemas generativos optimizan verosimilitud estadística, no referencia: producen enunciados bien formados sin la relación con una exterioridad que los haga verdaderos o falsos. El problema no es cultural sino estructural, y aparece cuando una infraestructura trata esa salida como protocolo de ejecución —código que se corre, no afirmación que se juzga—: en ese punto la deliberación se desplaza fuera del agente y el juicio queda externalizado. El artículo define la externalización del juicio mediante un criterio operativo: hay externalización cuando el agente adopta un resultado sin poder ejercer sobre él la operación que lo haría suyo, esto es, someterlo a la pregunta por su referencia. La tesis es acotada: no niega utilidad a estos sistemas ni reclama una excepcionalidad humana metafísica; distingue dos regímenes —ejecutar y referir— y localiza el riesgo para la libertad no en la máquina, sino en la confusión de ambos. El resultado es un criterio, no una advertencia: permite decir, caso por caso, cuándo una práctica asistida por IA conserva el juicio y cuándo lo ha cedido.

items.title: Indagación estructurada en LLMs.
items.abstract: La inteligencia artificial generativa, en su configuración actual, exhibe una paradoja epistémica: amplía técnicamente el acceso al conocimiento al tiempo que restringe las condiciones de su producción crítica. Los modelos de lenguaje de gran escala (LLMs) operan bajo regímenes de verdad computacional que privilegian la verosimilitud estadística sobre la referencia y la justificación, produciendo así una externalización del juicio. Este artículo responde a dicha paradoja mediante la propuesta de una arquitectura cognitiva basada en complejos de indagación jerárquicos, inspirada en el pragmatismo filosófico (Peirce, Dewey), la teoría dialógica del lenguaje (Bakhtin, Tannen) y la epistemología social (Fricker). La arquitectura materializa, en cinco módulos interdependientes —motor de indagación, navegador epistémico, generador contextual, diálogo adaptativo y rastreador de razonamiento—, los principios de trazabilidad, reversibilidad, pluralismo y contestabilidad, desplazando la lógica del prompt aislado hacia un modelo de navegación deliberativa. Para evaluar su funcionamiento, introducimos el Índice de Equilibrio Erotético (EEE), una métrica formativa y procesual que valora la calidad epistémica del proceso en cinco dimensiones: profundidad, pluralidad, trazabilidad, reversibilidad y robustez. En diálogo crítico con enfoques contemporáneos como Chain-of-Thought, Socratic Models y Constitutional AI, sostenemos que la propuesta no constituye una mejora incremental, sino una disrupción deliberativa: en lugar de simular razonamiento o aplicar principios normativos fijos, internaliza la indagación como estructura operativa. Sus aplicaciones en educación, derecho, ciencia y medicina muestran que su relevancia no se mide por la eficiencia instrumental, sino por la capacidad de instituir entornos epistémicamente responsables, donde preguntar, justificar y sostener el disenso son condiciones centrales. Con ello, el artículo defiende que el futuro de una IA epistémicamente activa no debe orientarse a perfeccionar la plausibilidad de las respuestas, sino a restaurar el juicio en el corazón de la computación, configurándola como una infraestructura de deliberación crítica y plural. Palabras clave: Externalización del juicio, Regímenes de verdad computacional, Arquitecturas cognitivas generativas, Complejos de indagación jerárquicos, Índice de Equilibrio Erotético (EEE), Disrupción deliberativa, Epistemología computacional, IA epistémicamente activa, Pragmatismo y …

items.title: The Collapse of Meaning in Creative Collaboration: A UPC Model of a Musician in Studio.
items.abstract: This paper applies the Universal Principle of Collapse (UPC) to a real‑world creative‑collaboration event, demonstrating that the structural architecture governing quantum measurement also governs the formation of musical meaning and shared artistic judgment. Earlier UPC work established collapse as an observer‑indexed commitment, formalized through the operator chain PO → MO → LO → s → Jo → C → T → K—and showed that this chain embeds directly into the standard quantum measurement rule without altering the physics. Collapse, in this framework, is not a physical process but the unique selection of an articulated outcome within an Observer’s model. -/- Here, we extend UPC into the domain of live musical performance by modeling a single, bounded collapse event during a recording session involving guitarist Lliraldi and his trio. The moment spans from the drummer’s count‑in to the group’s decision to keep the take, providing a naturally occurring instance of potential, partition, articulation, salience, recognition, collapse, trace, and consensus. By analyzing this event with full operator fidelity, we show that creative interpretation and collaborative decision‑making instantiate the same structural dynamics as quantum measurement. This case study illustrates the generality of the UPC framework and demonstrates how observer‑indexed collapse operates identically across physics, cognition, and artistic practice. March 28, 2026 .

items.title: Antagonism, Dependence, and Domination.
items.abstract: This paper argues that antagonism is not merely a historical or institutional phenomenon but an ontological feature of human relational existence. Human beings are constitutively dependent on one another for survival, recognition, language, and social participation. This dependence generates asymmetries of power, and asymmetry creates the structural possibility of instrumentalization and domination. Antagonism therefore arises not only from conflict or hostility but from the structural condition that human beings both need one another and can exploit that need. Against teleological theories that interpret antagonism as historically contingent and ultimately resolvable, the paper argues that antagonism is historically transformable but ontologically persistent. Modern institutional and technological systems intensify antagonism through the diffusion and anonymization of responsibility, a phenomenon that can be described as ethical withdrawal (Enser 2026). Because antagonism cannot be eliminated, the ethical task cannot consist in designing a conflict-free society but in restraining domination through accountability. Ethical life therefore does not consist in eliminating antagonism but in remaining responsible within ongoing structural tension. The central ethical task is not reconciliation but accountability within antagonism.

items.title: Energy, War, and the Decline of Coherence.
items.abstract: The early decades of the twenty-first century have revealed a convergence of military, economic, and ideological pressures centred upon energy systems. This paper examines the targeting of energy infrastructure in the Russo-Ukrainian conflict, situating it within historical precedent and modern technological development. Particular attention is given to the evolution of remote warfare, from the “robot bombs” of the Second World War to contemporary drone systems, and to the psychological and civilisational implications of such methods. Esoteric interpretations, especially those derived from the writings of Alice A. Bailey and the Tibetan (Djwhal Khul), are considered as a parallel interpretive framework.

items.title: When Targeted Sanctions Miss the Mark: The Use, Effectiveness, and Human Rights Consequences of Sanctioning Family Members.
items.abstract: Though sanctions on family members of primary targets have become increasingly popular coercive instruments, we know very little about their use, effectiveness, and major legal and human rights consequences. Drawing insight from several targeted sanctions directed at family members of the Russian elite in recent years, this article offers a detailed analysis of (1) why sanctioning states have increasingly opted for family member sanctions, (2) whether targeting family members increases the efficacy of sanctions regimes, (3) to what extent such targeted sanctions are legally and ethically defensible, and (4) whether they undermine human rights of targeted individuals. Our analysis suggests that family member sanctions have limited utility as they are mostly ineffective tools. They could also cause major human rights issues and legal challenges for the sanctioned individuals. Hence, family member sanctions appear to be ethically problematic tools that warrant careful reconsideration.

items.title: The Illusion of Agency: Why Free Will Does Not Exist.
items.abstract: This paper provides a comprehensive deconstruction of the concept of free will from the perspectives of physical determinism, neuroscience, and modal logic. By analyzing the causal structures of the material brain and the biological lottery of birth, it argues that human agency is a post-hoc narrative construction rather than an independent force. The conclusion asserts that while the sensation of choice is a persistent feature of human experience, it lacks a coherent causal foundation in a deterministic reality.

items.title: THE THERMAL WALL : Container Boundaries, Scale-Independent Heat Signatures, and What the Heliopause, the Galactic Halo, and the Incompatibility of General Relativity and Quantum Mechanics Are All Measuring.
items.abstract: In 2018, Voyager 2 crossed the edge of the solar system and found a wall of heat. The temperature at the boundary between the Sun's interior dynamics and interstellar space measured between 30,000 and 50,000 Kelvin — five to eight times the surface temperature of the Sun — generated not by either system but by their contact at the interface between them. In 2024, the eROSITA X-ray observatory measured the Milky Way's surrounding halo of hot gas and found it running 12% warmer on one side than the other, produced by compression at the boundary where the Milky Way's gravitational field presses against the pull of a neighboring galaxy. And since 1915, theoretical physics has produced a century of failed attempts to build a single framework that describes both general relativity — the theory of gravity and spacetime — and quantum mechanics — the theory of matter at the smallest scales — because the two theories, each perfect on its own terms, produce incompatible requirements at the point where they meet. This paper argues that these are not three separate findings in three separate fields. They are the same finding at three different scales: the signature produced when two physical regimes, each internally consistent and each constitutively incomplete, meet at a real boundary neither can describe from within. The signature is always the same — heat, compression, asymmetry, or incompatibility — because it is not a property of either system. It is the property of the contact itself. It is what happens at every real edge between two regimes that cannot describe each other across the interface. The argument draws on the Observer framework's account of why this pattern is structural rather than coincidental: every local system is constitutively incomplete in the precise sense established by Gödel's incompleteness theorems, which the framework identifies not as a property of formal systems specifically but as the foundational condition of any differentiated local existence. When two constitutively incomplete systems meet, neither can describe the other using only its internal resources. The contact zone is where mutual incompleteness becomes measurable. The thermal wall, the galactic asymmetry, and the GR/QM incompatibility are measurements of mutual incompleteness at three different scales. They are the same event. This paper names what they are all measuring.

items.title: Depression and Restoration.
items.abstract: Depression and Restoration presents a structural account of depression as a collapse of coherence in the human system and restoration as the gradual re‑expansion of stability, meaning, and agency. The paper reframes depression as a protective response to overload rather than a defect of mood or character, describing how emotional narrowing, cognitive contraction, and withdrawal emerge when the system exceeds its capacity. Restoration is examined as the slow return of coherence through reduced load, renewed relational anchoring, and the rebuilding of narrative and functional continuity. The model offers a clear, non‑pathologizing framework for understanding collapse and recovery across psychological, relational, and existential domains.

items.title: Imbricações materiais nas tecnologias: tecnicidades em composições plurais.
items.pub: In Suzy Lagazzi, Guilherme Adorno, Fernanda Galli, Romulo Osthues, Flavio Benayon, Liliane dos Anjos, Luiz Carlos Martins, Mirielly Ferraça & Rogério Modesto, FRONTEIRAS EM MOVIMENTO: O discurso e suas materialidades em composição. Campinas: Pontes. pp. 93-114.
items.venue: FRONTEIRAS EM MOVIMENTO: O discurso e suas materialidades em composição
items.abstract: Retomamos as questões propostas no âmbito do simpósio Imbricações materiais nas tecnologias em que esta reflexão se iniciou: De que modo o encontro de diferentes imbricações materiais com diferentes tecnologias de linguagem produz efeitos sobre o funcionamento do discurso? Como esse encontro participa dos processos de constituição, formulação e circulação de sentidos? Como descrever e interpretar a imbricação de diferentes tecnologias de linguagem em suas especificidades? Quais processos de identificação são engendrados a partir do funcionamento tecnológico-discursivo? Quais diferenças os espaços digitais apresentam frente a outras formas de tecnologia? Como podemos compreender, discursivamente, o “digital” ou os “espaços digitais” na atualidade? De que formas o digital afeta a montagem de arquivos? A temática Imbricações materiais nas tecnologias formula propositalmente o plural: tecnologias. Um plural que aponta para outras pluralidades: dos conceitos possíveis para tecnologias e suas especificidades e das formas de analisá-las. Esse plural, quando conjugado ao outro plural — imbricações materiais —, produz um jogo interessante para se pensar a heterogeneidade e a diferença que a relação entre esses elementos significantes pode produzir. “Formular é dar corpo aos sentidos [...] pela e na linguagem, que se inscreve na história para significar, tem seu corpo atado ao corpo dos sentidos”, afirma Orlandi (2005, p. 9). Problematizar as diferentes tecnologias (d)e linguagem e as diferentes imbricações materiais, a partir das diversas abordagens apresentadas no simpósio Imbricações materiais nas tecnologias, é o nosso desafio nesta reflexão.

items.title: The Problem with Education's Middle Path for Artificial Intelligence.
items.abstract: This draft aims to examine and problematize the institutional and educational responses that have recently developed and ostensibly ‘matured’ from early binary responses of AI panic or excitement. Such responses – which I dub as education’s ‘middle path’ – are defined by a shared optimism that seeks to integrate AI and existing educational practices or principles in different ways. I argue that these middle paths, although ostensibly integrative, practical, or even holistic, are problematic insofar as they hold several reformative assumptions that are no longer viable in the age of AI. Much of this is attributable to an implicit conflation between pre-AI educational technologies and AI itself, particularly with respect to how they affect institutional deterrence structures for performance and the epistemology of assessments in education.

items.title: 群体是否只是能力不足的补偿？——关于智能、认知与社会依赖的一个极限假设.
items.abstract: 本文提出一个具有争议性的假设：社群并非智能或文明的高级形态，而是个体在感知、行动与认知能力不足时形成的补偿结构。通过对生物协作、语言与工具使用的重新解释，指出群体依赖源于能力限制，而非本体必要性。 -/- 在此框架下，本文引入“自显体”概念，用以描述能够构建自身认知表征并持续提升能力的主体。随着能力扩展，个体对群体的依赖将逐步下降。当能力足以覆盖协作功能时，社会结构将失去其基础。 -/- 本文将该问题提升为认知极限问题：智能是否必须依赖社会结构？结合脑科学、认知科学与人工智能中关于分布式认知与个体系统的研究，讨论个体在何种条件下可以脱离群体而独立运作。 -/- 形式化推导表明：若群体是能力不足的补偿，且能力可以持续提升，则群体依赖趋于零，智能体将走向“非社”。该结论对未来智能系统与认知模型具有重要意义。.

items.title: 战争制胜底层规律及其全域史实验证.
items.abstract: 摘要 战争形态历经冷兵器、热兵器、信息化与智能化迭代，制胜底层逻辑保持恒定。本文 基于古今中外数百场经典战役的史实考证与系统复盘，构建战略哲学层 + 战术操作层 双公式体系，以四大战场场景开展全域验证，揭示符合规律即胜、违背规律即败的客 观铁律。论文明确公式为战略思维诊断框架而非量化计算工具，补充反例检验与边界 说明，强化理论严谨性与解释力，为国防建设、战略决策与军事理论研究提供系统化 支撑。.

items.title: 释迦牟尼六年苦行的本质 —— 身体与心性的方法错位.
items.abstract: 摘要 释迦牟尼六年苦行是人类精神修行史上最具范式危机象征的经典公案，亦是东方心性 哲学区分正道歧途的分水岭。悉达多太子舍弃王宫荣华，遍访禅定名师未得究竟解 脱，遂入尼连禅河畔苦行林，践行古印度极致苦行传统：日食一麻一麦、七日一食、 绝眠屏息、赤身淋雨，六年磨砺身形枯槁、皮骨相连，终未证得涅槃解脱。而后毅然 舍弃极端苦行，接受牧女乳糜恢复体力，于菩提树下正坐七日，夜睹明星豁然彻悟成 佛。 本文依托原创本质哲学体系 ——「一源多元论」划定存在层级边界，「玄弦论」阐释 心性本体运作本质，「三相感界定」厘清身心物关联规律，「各归其正」确立修行实践 终极准则，对六年苦行公案展开系统性病理溯源、底层逻辑解构与范式救赎重建。研 究本质指出：六年苦行修行溃败的根本症结，并非精进修行初心谬误，而是跨域底层 方法根本性错位 —— 以折磨损耗物理肉身的外在有为造作，妄图直接契入超时空无 为心性本体、证得究竟解脱，本质混淆「肉身硬件」与「心性本体」不可逾越的存在 层级，误将身心「相感共振关系」等同于「从属改造关系」。 肉身（色身）归有情时空硬件范畴，严格遵循新陈代谢、能量供给、机能运转等客观 物理规律；心性本体（玄 / 弦）归超时空永恒范畴，寂然不动、灵明不昧，与肉身仅 为无感因果、唯有共振的相感关联。极端苦行执着肉身有为压抑、刻意损耗，非但无 法净化心念、止息烦恼，反而因肉身机能枯竭、气血紊乱、神识昏沉，严重遮蔽灵明 本心、加剧弦动散乱，彻底背离心性归静无为正道。菩提树下悟道之所以圆满成功， 核心在于彻底放弃肉身有为造作执念，恪守各归其正准则 —— 肉身顺应物理规律从 容安住，心性直下观照、放下攀缘、弦归玄静，不压不逐、无为显真。 基于根本溯源解构，本文提出不可逾越的终极修行救赎范式：身体归身体，顺应能量 代谢、作息节律等客观物理规律合理养护、适度调摄，不纵欲放逸亦不极端苦行；心 性归心性，恪守玄弦论无为归静正道，观照心念生灭、放下执着攀缘、止息散乱弦 动，不向外造作亦不刻意压抑。两类存在、两类修行有为无为界限清晰、互不僭越、 互不替代、并行不悖。本研究既从传统模糊解读误区，根本厘清佛教修行中道根本路 径，补全东方身心哲学千年漏洞，亦为当代心理神经科学、身心疗愈哲学、正念修行 实践，提供根本底层方法论范式启示。.

items.title: 孟子 “万物皆备于我” 的玄弦论新解 —— 驳心学添加.
items.abstract: “万物皆备于我矣，反身而诚，乐莫大焉。”（《孟子・尽心上》）是孟子心性论的核心命 题，亦是中国哲学史上阐释分歧最多、争议最久的经典公案。程朱理学将其释为 “万 物之理皆备于我性分之内”，陆王心学则解作 “万物之理皆在我心中”，二者均在原文基 础上添加了 “理” 或 “心即理” 的预设，致使千年诠释始终围绕心物关系纠缠不清。本 文以 “一源多元论”“玄弦论”“三相感”“各归其正” 为原创理论框架，对孟子此句进行系 统性文本还原与方法论诊断。研究指出：“万物皆备于我” 中的 “万物”，并非外在物理 之物，亦非 “万物之理”，而是指人心所能呈现的各类状态 —— 情绪、心念、四端、 习气等有情世界现象。孟子此句意在阐明：人心本具一切可能的心性状态（恻隐、羞 恶、辞让、是非等），是为 “万物皆备”；反身内求、使心回归真实无妄的清净状态 （诚），即可获得至深之乐（乐莫大焉）。这一解读无须添加 “理” 字，亦无须预设 “心 即理”，仅依文本字面与上下文贯通即可成立。本文以此新解驳斥程朱、陆王的添加式 诠释，并指出心学将 “万物” 误释为外在事物或万物之理，本质是混淆心性领域与物理 领域的存在层次，属于方法论错位。本文提出修正路径：心归心（修心以玄弦论），物 归物（物理以科学），经典诠释归经典诠释（文本考据与义理贯通），各归其正。这一 分析既还原孟子本义，也为经典诠释提供方法论参照。.

items.title: Logic of ER I - Core Logic & Meta-Theory: A Conservative Predicate Extension of First-Order Linear Tense Logic.
items.abstract: Existential Realism (ER) proposes a two-tier ontology: only the present exists, yet the past and the future are real. This thesis arises from the diagnosis that in debates on the ontology of time, “existence” and “reality” are often implicitly identified, thereby making presentism and eternalism appear as competing positions that merely disagree about the extension of a single ontological predicate. ER instead separates a narrow, present-bound predicate of existence from a broader notion of reality that allows non-present entities to count as real when, for instance, they existed in the past or will exist in the future, allowing these to participate in time-directed deductions. This paper develops the core system ERL (Existential-Realism Logic): a classical first-order linear temporal logic, in the Prior tradition, enriched with two distinguished unary predicates E (“exists now”) and R (“is real”). ERL is (i) syntactically defined with precision, (ii) given a model-theoretic semantics via Kripke-style ER-frames, (iii) axiomatized through a Hilbert-style system, and (iv) supported by metalogical results establishing soundness and outlining a canonical completeness program. Where strong completeness requires additional standard assumptions (such as Henkinization or generalized models), this is made explicit. Further central technical results include: conservativity over classical first-order linear temporal logic without E/R; an explicit Barcan profile (Barcan schemas hold for unrestricted quantifiers under constant domains, but may fail for existence-restricted quantifiers ∀ᴱ/∃ᴱ); and non-reducibility results (E is not definable, over the class of ER-models, using purely temporal operators; R cannot be forced as a definitional derivative of E together with temporal operators). The overall aim is to demonstrate that ER constitutes a logically stable and metalogically respectable position within established modal-temporal traditions, without unnecessarily over-engineering the formal system. Soundness is proven; completeness is outlined via a canonical-model strategy but left for full technical development in subsequent work.

items.title: Phenomenological Theories of Desire.
items.pub: In Alex Gregory, The Routledge Handbook on the Philosophy of Desire. Routledge.
items.venue: The Routledge Handbook on the Philosophy of Desire
items.abstract: Phenomenological theories explain the nature of desire in terms of how it feels: to desire something is to feel—or to be disposed to feel—the desire for it. In contrast, functionalist theories explain the nature of desire in terms of what it does, rather than how it feels. This chapter presents three arguments for the phenomenological theory: it avoids counterexamples to the motivational theory of desire, it captures the normative significance of desire, and it explains how we can have introspective knowledge of what we desire. The chapter concludes by examining how we use the concept of desire in predicting and explaining behavior.

items.title: Truth, Sensitivity, and Awareness: A Philosophical Inquiry.
items.abstract: This paper examines the relationship between truth, sensitivity, awareness, and individuality in human communication. It critically challenges the conventional understanding of politeness and sensitivity as socially conditioned behaviors, proposing instead that genuine sensitivity arises from awareness grounded in love. The inquiry explores how truth is often resisted due to psychological attachment, and how communication becomes distorted through suppression, reaction, and intention-driven expression. It further investigates the tension between individuality and conditioning, highlighting how both conformity and rebellion can limit authentic perception. The paper argues that awareness—not intention, control, or social conformity—is the foundation of clear perception and authentic expression. Ultimately, it concludes that when awareness operates without attachment, truth and sensitivity are no longer in conflict but emerge as unified expressions of intelligence.

items.title: Awareness, Thought, and the Construction of Economic Reality.
items.abstract: This paper explores the relationship between awareness, thought, and the construction of economic systems. It argues that the economy is not an independent or natural phenomenon, but a human-made structure generated through thought and sustained by collective participation. While traditional perspectives treat economic systems as objective realities, this paper examines how they emerge from conceptual frameworks and become institutionalized over time. It further analyzes how individuals participate in these systems, often unconsciously, and how certain thinkers have historically revealed underlying patterns within human behavior and social organization. The paper concludes by positioning awareness as a transformative force that allows individuals to perceive the constructed nature of economic reality without necessarily disengaging from it.

items.title: Between map and maze: reframing trust in healthcare AI.
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is often presented as a transformative technology for healthcare, promising to augment clinical decision-making, streamline workflows, and enhance diagnostic precision. Yet its integration into healthcare practice is shaped by the complex and often ambiguous notion of trust. While trust in AI has become a recurring theme across disciplines, there has been little systematic analysis of different conceptualizations of the term. This paper addresses this gap through an interdisciplinary scoping review that examines how trust, trustworthiness, distrust, and mistrust are articulated in literature on AI in healthcare. Drawing on 82 publications (2015–2025) retrieved from six databases (Web of Science, Scopus, PubMed, PhilPapers, SocINDEX, and ACM Digital Library), it maps how trust is defined, measured, or problematized, and identifies the conceptual, epistemological, and disciplinary boundaries that shape these approaches. The analysis puts forward five different conceptualizations: trust as a set of designable principles, trust as an attitude or belief, trust as a binary between cognition/affect or human/technology, trust as a structural mechanism within uncertainty, and trust as a relational process embedded in socio-technical systems. These framings illuminate how trust is treated as an attribute to be engineered, a behavior to be calibrated, or a relation to be cultivated—often removed from clinical practice. Yet, across literature, trust disruptions which manifest as distrust, mistrust, overtrust, and undertrust are undertheorized and are typically framed as obstacles to overcome rather than phenomena warranting analysis in their own right. By introducing these diverging conceptualizations, the paper argues that trust in healthcare AI is less a stable condition than a dynamic negotiation that reveals power relations, uncertainties, and institutional dependencies of AI. Recognizing distrust and mistrust as analytically productive allows for a more reflexive understanding of how trust is enacted, distributed, and contested within healthcare. This review contributes to an emerging body of work that reframes trust not as a prerequisite for technological adoption but as a contested and dynamic concept.

items.title: An Inconsistency in Adams's Probabilistic Logic of Conditionals.
items.abstract: Ernest Adams’s probabilistic logic of conditionals, developed in response to David Lewis’s triviality results, seeks to reconcile indicative conditionals with probability theory by restricting compound conditionals and defining p-entailment via probabilistic consistency. This paper rigorously analyzes Adams’s system as formalized in The Logic of Conditionals (1975), exposing a critical inconsistency that lies in the statement of Theorem 4.2 and its relation with the inference rules that Adams derives from R1-R7. Specifically, the unrestricted formulation of rule R8 yields a contradiction when it is taken together with the result of nine lemmas that are proven in the paper. We show that Adams’s framework implicitly relies on the consistency of antecedents of conditionals but fails to enforce this syntactically. Our analysis concludes by proposing a simple but crucial amendment: explicitly incorporating consistency conditions into the statement of the derived rules. This revision preserves Adams’s valuable insights on probabilistic consistency and entailment while resolving the identified contradiction.

items.title: The Kant Code (Kantian Filter 2.1).
items.abstract: The Kantian Filter 2.1: A Formal Deontic Framework for AI Decision Evaluation, Responsibility Attribution and Regulatory Compliance -/- As AI systems increasingly make high-stakes decisions, existing governance frameworks (including the EU AI Act) remain procedurally underdetermined: they classify risk and impose transparency requirements, but lack a structured, computable mechanism to evaluate whether an individual algorithmic decision rule is morally permissible. This preprint introduces the Kantian Filter 2.0 (KF) — a constraint-based audit system grounded in Kantian ethics and formalised through deontic logic. The framework operationalises three non-aggregative constraints: • Universalisability (U) — dual test combining logical contradiction check and multi-agent simulation; • Human Dignity (D) — via Transparency, Non-Manipulation and Fairness Bound, supported by the Counterfactual Disclosure Test (CDT) and its relational variant for non-individualist communities; • Non-Delegable Responsibility (R)* — using Shapley-value attribution over the sociotechnical responsibility graph. The KF produces a binary deontic verdict (Permission/Prohibition) alongside a severity score (KF_score) that distinguishes categorical prohibition from redesign requirements. It operates as accountability infrastructure complementary to existing regulation: governance sets what systems may learn; the Filter evaluates what happens inside those boundaries. The paper includes a strengthened COMPAS case analysis (n=7,214) with sensitivity analysis across fairness metrics and ε values, normative robustness across Kantian, Rawlsian, prioritarian, Nozickian and relational ethics frameworks, and concrete integration workflows for EU AI Act conformity assessment .

items.title: Who knows what? Bayesian competence inference guides knowledge attribution and information search.
Introduction: Heidegger, Daoism, and Intercultural Thinking Today.
Deconstructing Mindfulness in Education.
items.abstract: The aim of this paper is to contribute to critical discourse on mindfulness in education through Heidegger’s notion of Besinnung and what I have called an “appropriative approach” to selfhood and social ontology. In particular, I focus on the “contemplative turn” towards the self as a crucial site of contestation and debate within the current literature on mindfulness in education. In the process, I show how Besinnung as an extension of the appropriative approach can provide the basis for an account of mindfulness as desubjectivation which, according to Michel Foucault, has “the function of wrenching the subject from itself, of seeing to it that the subject is no longer itself, or that it is brought to its annihilation or its dissolution”.

items.title: La Profilée and the Structural Law of Psychological Collapse: Burnout and Depression as Distinct Structural Failure Modes of Personal Identity Persistence.
items.abstract: The relationship between burnout and depression is one of the most contested questions in occupational health psychology. The empirical literature documents substantial overlap (exhaustion–depression correlation r ≈ 0.80; Bianchi et al., 2021) while also identifying structural neurobiological differences (burnout: prefrontal/striatal circuits; depression: hippocampal-amygdalar circuits). The debate has not been resolved because both sides operate at the symptom layer: they compare observable clinical features without a structural theory that specifies why burnout and depression are similar in some respects and different in others. This paper applies La Profilée (LP), a structural theory of persistence under real transformation, to burnout and depression as failure modes of personal identity persistence. LP specifies a universal persistence condition IR = R / (F · I) ≤ 1. When IR > 1 is sustained, structural identity erosion occurs. The person — as a system maintaining identity under continuous transformation — is subject to this condition as are cells, organisations, and ecosystems. The central structural finding is: Burnout and depression are not the same condition at different severity levels.
