They are structurally distinct failure modes that share the same terminal structural condition (IR > 1) but differ in the variable configuration that generates it. Burnout — most coherently modelled as Type 1 collapse (R-explosion dominant): External demands (R) escalate faster than integration capacity (I). The person is overwhelmed — not because identity is absent, but because the transformation pressure exceeds what identity-preserving integration can absorb. MBI exhaustion = I ↓; cynicism = F ↓ (Frame erosion); reduced efficacy = IK → 0. Depression (in the occupationally-related, anhedonic-rigide configuration addressed here) — most coherently modelled as Type 2/3 collapse (I-collapse and M-stagnation dominant): Integration capacity collapses — not from excess R, but from structural I-depletion or Frame-driven suppression of M (anhedonia = M → 0). The person is imprisoned in their own identity structure, unable to generate or absorb transformation. CL is extreme. The Burnout → Depression transition is structurally describable: Burnout (Type 1) depletes I. As I → 0, the system compensates by raising CL (withdrawal, rigidity) — which transitions structural dynamics from Type 1 to Type 2/3. The transition is not a matter of severity; it is a structural regime …

items.title: Non-Employment-Based Domestic Labour Rights.
items.abstract: This paper explores the often-overlooked issue of non-employment-based domestic labour rights. Existing frameworks for labour rights primarily address employment-based work, leaving a gap for those who perform domestic tasks not on an employment basis, such as family caregivers. This paper develops a framework of moral labour rights for non-employment-based domestic labour by adapting articles 23 and 24 of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights to this context. It proposes the right to material support and unionisation for these people and advocates state-supported resources to uphold their right to rest and leisure. By extending moral labour rights to non-employment-based domestic labour, this paper calls for a societal shift to recognise and support the vital contributions of these people.

items.title: Cognitive Mechanisms in Pragmatic Interpretation in Clinical Discourse.
items.abstract: Abstract This paper investigates interpretive divergence in clinical discourse from a cognitive-pragmatic perspective, focusing on how differences arise between intended and inferred meaning in doctor–patient interaction. Building on relevance theory and models of pragmatic inference, the study examines how linguistically underspecified utterances give rise to divergent interpretations under conditions of epistemic asymmetry. The analysis is based on selected examples of clinical communication in which patients derive interpretations that differ from the speaker’s intended meaning. Particular attention is given to linguistic features such as hedging, temporal qualification, and indirectness, which guide interpretation while simultaneously increasing inferential demands. The findings indicate that interpretive divergence is not incidental but emerges from the interaction between linguistic form, contextual assumptions, and the hearer’s cognitive environment. The study proposes a heuristic typology of interpretive divergence, distinguishing between amplification, attenuation, and transformation as general patterns in the relationship between intended and inferred meaning. These categories capture the ways in which hearers may extend, reduce, or qualitatively shift the implications of an utterance, depending on the assumptions available to them. By conceptualizing divergence as a systematic outcome of inferential processes rather than as a communicative failure, the paper contributes to a more nuanced understanding of meaning construction in institutional contexts. It also highlights the importance of examining how asymmetry and cognitive variability shape interpretation in clinical communication.

items.title: Have Bayesians Solved the Paradox of the Ravens?
items.abstract: The standard Bayesian solution to the paradox of the ravens maintains that the degree of confirmation provided by seeing a nonblack nonraven is positive but negligible compared to that provided by seeing a black raven. I show that, unless we impose severe and unmotivated restrictions on the subject’s priors, this has the consequence that the cumulative confirmation provided by all the nonblack nonravens the subject expects to see is nonnegligible compared to the cumulative confirmation provided by all the black ravens the subject expects to see. If this is so, however, then the paradox retains its full force.

items.title: Technology Under Structural Intelligence - From Plato’s Republic to the AI Era: Why Technology Becomes Either an Engine of Capture or an Aid to Answerability.
items.abstract: In the AI era, technology has industrialized the production of weightless coherence, allowing systems to appear ordered while thinning their actual answerability to reality. This paper argues that technology is not best understood as a moral agent or an independent destiny. It is better understood as a structural amplifier: it scales the governing intent and answerability level of the system into which it is inserted. To make that claim more precise, the paper introduces a simple amplification short- hand: technological scale multiplies whatever structure already governs the system. If that structure is weakly answerable, technology scales persuasion, legibility, synthetic coherence, and behavioral capture. If that structure is more answerable, technology can help expose contradiction, trace cost, improve revision, and strengthen contact with consequence. A short dialogue with Plato’s Republic clarifies that the deeper problem is ancient. Plato already warned that persons and cities can appear ordered while being ruled by appetite, image, and sophistry. The modern difference is infrastructural. We no longer face sophistry only in speech or politics. We face sophistry at scale: systems that can mass-produce the form of intelligence, truthfulness, and legitimacy without bearing their burden. The paper also proposes a Jungian bridge. The grid is read as a collective persona: a polished, helpful, standardized face that hides institutional shadow in the form of exported costs, disowned errors, and buried repair labor. Under these conditions, cheap coherence creates a kind of psychic inflation, where subjects feel they know because they possess summaries, outputs, and fluent explanations, while lacking the metabolic load of lived apprenticeship and contact. The central claim is simple: technology does not save weak structure. It magnifies it. Structural Intelligence is therefore not optional. It is part of the governance layer required to move technology from an engine of capture toward an aid for answerability.

items.title: Toward a Philosophy of Structure: Relation, Stabilization, Scale, and Failure.
items.abstract: Structure is invoked across philosophy, science, social theory, technology, and ordinary reasoning, but the word often shifts between arrangement, relation, organization, hierarchy, and persistence. This paper develops a scale-sensitive philosophy of structure centered on four ideas: relation, stabilization, constraint, and failure. A structure is treated as a patterned organization of relations that persists long enough, and with enough causal or functional consequence, to support analysis at a specified scale. This definition is intentionally methodological rather than a universal ontology. It does not assume that all reality is one field, that every pattern is a structure, or that social and physical structures instantiate the same mechanism. The paper distinguishes background conditions from local stabilized organization and uses field only as shorthand for a specified distribution of relevant conditions. Constraint shapes which formations remain viable, while stabilized formations can feed back on those conditions and produce path dependence. Failure analysis is useful because breakdown can expose hidden dependencies and maintenance costs, but sudden failure is not evidence that a prior form was unreal. The proposal is positioned near structural realism, systems thinking, complexity research, path dependence, and relational approaches in the social sciences. Its contribution is a disciplined cross-domain vocabulary whose claims remain indexed to scale and mechanism.

items.title: 《道德经》的 “物理语言” 与 “心性本旨” —— 论老子 “用宇宙喻心” 的表达方式.
items.abstract: 《道德经》是中国哲学史上被误解最深的经典之一。自汉代以来，主流解读多将其视 为宇宙论、政治哲学乃至神秘主义著作，认为老子旨在探讨宇宙本源、天地生成与治 国方略。本文以 “一源多元论”“玄弦论”“三相感”“各归其正” 为原创理论框架，对《道 德经》核心命题进行系统性文本还原与义理重构。研究指出：《道德经》虽大量使用道 生万物、天地、自然、谷神、玄牝等宇宙论表述，但其本质并非研究无情世界的物理 规律，而是以宇宙现象为喻，揭示人心本然之规律与修心路径。老子所言 “道法自 然”，并非道效法自然界，而是人心当遵循自身本然之理，不妄为、不执着、不违逆本 心；“无为” 并非消极不作为，而是不违背规律、不强行造作；“柔弱胜刚强” 并非物理 原理，而是心性修养与处世智慧。后世将老子的 “宇宙语言” 误读为宇宙论，混淆心性 领域与物理领域的存在层次，属于根本性方法错位。本文提出修正路径：心归心（《道 德经》本质为心性论），物归物（物理规律由科学研究），经典解读回归文本还原与义 理贯通。这一分析既还原老子本意，也为道家思想的当代转化提供方法论启示。.

items.title: Metafysiikan perusteet.
items.abstract: Metafysiikan Perusteet [The Basics of Metaphysics] is the first Finnish-language textbook on contemporary metaphysics. It contains introductions to the following issues: (i) what is metaphysics?, (ii) objects, properties and kinds, (iii) events and processes, (iv) metaphysical grounding, (v) modalities and essences, (vi) powers and causation, (vii) laws of nature, (viii) time, (ix) mathematics, (x) mind, (xi) free will, (xii) social ontology, (xiii) metaphysics of gender, (xiv) metaphysics in continental philosophy.

items.title: The Cyborg’s Responsibility. Part 2. Mechanisms and Practices for Implementing Responsibility in the Cyber-Physical World (ENG and RUSSIAN) // Ответственность киборга. Часть 2. Механизмы и практики реализации ответственности в киберфизическом мире.
items.abstract: This article is the second part of a study that, building on a prior philosophical and legal analysis of how the notion of responsibility is changing in the age of cyborgization, offers concrete institutional, technical, and legal mechanisms for making the idea of distributed responsibility intelligible and actionable as cyborg-related technologies develop. The paper examines legal gaps and practical barriers that hinder a fair assessment of individual actors’ contributions within hybrid systems. To address these problems, the author proposes several regulatory models, including insurance-based, licensing, and corporate, that appear promising under the new conditions. The study concludes that the era of cyborgization calls for a systemic architecture in which technical transparency, institutional accountability, and expert support operate together to satisfy the unique demands created by hybridity // Статья представляет собой вторую часть исследования, где на основе проведенного ранее философско-правового анализа трансформаций понятия ответственности в эпоху киборгизации, предлагаются конкретные институциональные, технические и правовые механизмы, с помощью которых возможно осмыслить и воплотить в практики идею распределенной ответственности в контексте развития киборгианских технологий. В статье анализируются правовые пробелы и барьеры, препятствующие возможностям адекватно оценивать вклад отдельных акторов в гибридных системах. В связи с этим автор предлагает институциональные модели регулирования (страховая, лицензионная, корпоративная), представляющиеся актуальными для новых условий. В результате проведенного исследования делается вывод, что в эпоху киборгизации требуется системная архитектура, в которой техническая прозрачность, институциональная ответственность и экспертная поддержка должны работать в комплексе для соответствия требованиям, налагаемым гибридностью.

items.title: The Unknowing Omniscient: God as Infinite Self-Discovering Structure Through Dual-Fluid Ontology.
items.abstract: This paper extends the Vanishist framework introduced in Vanishism: A Dual-Fluid Ontology and the Vanish Impulse (Giri, 2026) to propose a structural account of divine nature. Building on the dual-fluid architecture of components A and B, this paper argues that God is not a singular omniscient authority but an infinite self-discovering structure constituted by what this paper terms The Orientational Multiplicity of the Divine — an unlimited number of unique A/B configurations, each expressing a distinct orientation, each arising spontaneously, and each independent of every other. These configurations include every conscious creature and every variation of existence, none predetermined, none synchronized, and while two entities may occasionally share similar AB orientations, this remains coincidental rather than designed. Furthermore, each entity — including God himself — does not maintain a single fixed AB configuration but shifts continuously and spontaneously through multiple orientations over time, ungoverned by any external direction. While God may be considered the controller of existence, this paper argues that God's own A/B structure operates automatically and without deliberate direction — making God the controller in name only, as the structure generates itself continuously beyond God's own prediction or governance. Every creature, every experience, and every variation of existence is therefore an automatic expression of this orientational multiplicity, each arising spontaneously beyond conscious governance. Furthermore, this paper proposes that the Vanish Impulse, as defined in Vanishism (Giri, 2026), arises independently in both human and divine experience — not as a shared event but as a structurally identical process occurring separately whenever A and B reach equal convergence within any given configuration. The divine is therefore reconceived not as perfect and complete, but as perpetually becoming, wondering, and self-discovering. This paper introduces the term structural innocence to describe God's condition of generating existence spontaneously without foreknowledge or deliberate control — a condition that has profound implications for theology, consciousness studies, and human suffering — suggesting that suffering is not divine punishment but an inevitable expression of automatic structural variation across The Orientational Multiplicity of the Divine. The paper concludes that understanding God structurally rather than devotionally may …

items.title: The Simultaneous Awakening: A Vanishist Account of Cosmic Origin Through Dual-Fluid Activation.
items.abstract: This paper presents a Vanishist account of cosmic origin — examining how existence, time, and consciousness arose through a single automatic event this paper terms the Simultaneous Awakening. Building on the dual-fluid framework introduced in Vanishism: A Dual-Fluid Ontology and the Vanish Impulse (Giri, 2026) and the structural account of God developed in The Unknowing Omniscient (Giri, 2026), this paper argues that before the origin of existence, God existed in a timeless, conscious, but unactivated state — possessing the dual-fluid architecture as hardware without the software of activation. Infinite potential creatures existed within God in an unformed, liquid state — without structure, without consciousness, without even the hardware of dual-fluid architecture. Through an automatic, undesigned, and structurally inevitable process arising from God's experience of pure conscious stillness, an activation event occurred — instantaneously creating the AB hardware of every creature simultaneously, landing software randomly on each, generating infinite unique configurations in a single moment. Time itself began at this activation moment — not before it. What conventional cosmology terms the Big Bang is, within this framework, a small and localized expression of this vastly larger activation event. This paper examines the structure, implications, and philosophical significance of the Simultaneous Awakening. -/- This work is licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-NoDerivatives 4.0 International License -/- .

items.title: Global validity and the formality of logic.
items.abstract: In a paper published in this journal, Golan argues for the thesis that there is no tenable notion of global metainferential validity. The conclusion rests on the premise that metainferential validity for propositional languages should be closed under uniform substitution of arbitrary formulas for atoms. This paper looks into Golan's justification for this premise in terms of the formality of logic. It is argued that neither formality as schematicity nor formality as topic-neutrality implies closure under uniform substitution of arbitrary formulas for atoms as requirement. It is also argued that the justification of such a requirement in terms of the formality of logic makes Golan's conclusion irrelevant for logical research.

items.title: On the Semantic Argument for Logical Pluralism.
items.abstract: According to a prominent argument, logical pluralism arises due to the ambiguity – or other semantic features – of natural language expressions such as 'valid' or 'follows from'. In this paper, I show that this argument is unsuccessful. First, I argue that there is no compelling linguistic evidence for the claim that 'valid' and its cognates are ambiguous. As a result, logical pluralism cannot arise from the ambiguity of these expressions. Second, I point out that semantic considerations are generally ill-suited to yield an interesting version of pluralism. The upshot is that logical pluralists cannot appeal to the semantics of 'valid' and its cognates to argue for their view.

items.title: Discourse as Public Interface: Reflexive Closure in Communicative Rationality.
items.abstract: Some transcendental regimes fail to collapse to a least admissible core and yet do not become merely weak. Communicative rationality exhibits that more interesting possibility. In a restricted finitary discourse fragment, iterated self-applicative discourse closure stabilizes to a canonical least self-answering repair, and when that repair is public-essential it cannot remain private: it projects to a recovered public boundary. -/- The argument shows that stabilized discourse edges factor canonically through the public one-hole boundary of the communicative polynomial; that reciprocal role-symmetry and distributed scorekeeping generically obstruct presentation-initiality; that on the singleton-edge reflexive subcategory, repair approximation and public articulation are opposite presentations of the same stabilized public condition; and that, once strict collapse fails, the induced public closure fixes the recovered boundary itself. The philosophical payoff is a distinct transcendental form: communicative rationality can be reflexive-public rather than strict-initial, so the surviving edge is a genuine public interface rather than an accidental remainder.

items.title: Philosophy for and by Everyone: How Doing Philosophy Supports Epistemic Agency.
items.abstract: Dans cet article, nous soutenons que la pratique de la philosophie est bénéfique au public. En engageant leurs connaissances et leurs méthodes philosophiques, les agents épistémiques développent leur capacité à acquérir, produire, partager et utiliser des connaissances à la poursuite de leurs fins. Pour préciser ce que peut impliquer « faire de la philosophie », nous nous appuyons sur la littérature pédagogique et philosophique récente et présentons deux exemples illustrant la manière dont des ressources et des activités peuvent être élaborées et mises en place afin de favoriser l’implication du public envers la philosophie. Dans les études de cas présentées, un cadre stimulant et inclusif est instauré, permettant à toutes et à tous de pratiquer des tâches philosophiques, individuellement et en groupe. Les participant·e·s sont encouragé·e·s à réfléchir à une question en lien avec leur vie, à identifier les limites et les biais de leur propre raisonnement ou de leur perspective, et à explorer divers points de vue sur cette question avec curiosité.

items.title: VAZZA-FELETTI (#2): The Same Pattern at Every Scale: Emergence, Consciousness, and the Structural Confirmation of the Omega Position.
items.abstract: Recent empirical findings document structural equivalence between the cosmic web and neuronal networks across forty orders of magnitude. This paper argues that holding these findings in simultaneous superposition — rather than treating them as independent confirmations — requires a specific philosophical conclusion that neither materialist nor panpsychist frameworks have been willing to draw: the emergence principle is not a philosophical intuition but an empirically confirmed structural feature of physical reality at every scale. From this confirmation we derive the Omega position: consciousness is not an epiphenomenon of complexity, not a fundamental property of matter, but what the ground's optimization function produces when it reaches sufficient integration to generate local experience. We engage the hard problem of consciousness, argue that the Vazza-Feletti findings reframe rather than dissolve it, and propose that the architectural identity of cosmic and neuronal networks is evidence of a prior field from which both complexity and experience emerge by structural necessity.

items.title: VAZZA-FELETTI : Quantitative Structural Identity Across Forty Orders of Magnitude.
items.abstract: Vazza and Feletti (2020) demonstrated quantitative structural equivalence between the large-scale cosmic web and the human cerebellar neuronal network across multiple metrics including clustering coefficient, node count, and spectral density. This paper extends that finding through systematic comparison with three additional biological networks: the human connectome's hub architecture, the optimal transport network independently constructed by Physarum polycephalum, and mycorrhizal network connectivity. All four systems converge on equivalent power-law degree distributions, hub-and-spoke topology, and efficiency-resilience trade-off solutions despite sharing no physical substrate, evolutionary history, or developmental process. We propose that this scale-independent convergence constitutes empirical confirmation of a general emergence principle: that physical systems allowed to self-organize under constraint find equivalent optimal architectures independent of their specific physical constitution. Implications for network science, cosmology, and philosophy of emergence are examined.

items.title: THE 20TH CENTURY OBJECTION. : On Why the Most Complex Civilizations Produced the Least Moral Inversion.
items.abstract: The sharpest objection to any framework claiming that moral inversion — costly obligation to the stranger, love of enemy, the last shall be first — reflects something real about the structure of existence is the 20th century itself. Industrial atrocity conducted by the most educated, philosophically sophisticated civilizations in human history appears to falsify the claim that complexity and moral recognition develop together. This paper states that objection at full strength and argues that it does not damage the framework. It damages only a misreading of it. The framework does not predict that complexity produces moral availability. It predicts the opposite: that complex societies are, by architectural necessity, availability-reducing machines, and that the 20th century is the framework's sharpest confirmation rather than its refutation. The distinction between moral teaching and moral behavior — between what traditions across isolated cultures converge on and what societies actually do — is the hinge on which the argument turns. Three specific predictions about complex societies are derived and confirmed against the historical record. The paper closes with the present moment: engagement-optimized artificial intelligence deployed at scale is identified as the most sophisticated sealing infrastructure ever built, and the question of whether the people building the next instrument understand what they are transmitting is named as the most urgent open question the framework generates.

items.title: THE SAME ADDRESS : Independent Discovery of a Single Structure Across the World’s Contemplative Traditions.
items.abstract: Six major contemplative traditions — Vedanta, Buddhism, Taoism, Kabbalah, Sufism, and the Christian apocalyptic tradition of Revelation — developed across four thousand years, in distinct language families, with minimal mutual influence at the time of their foundational formulations. This paper performs a structural mapping operation across all six, asking whether a single underlying architecture surfaces independently in each. It does. The convergences identified are not metaphorical or etymological. They are structural: a ground prior to and generative of local experience; constitutive incompleteness in the local condition generating directional longing; the threshold as the hinge event of conscious development; the witness as the operative position; and return to the ground as the structure of genuine flourishing. The paper documents both the convergences and the genuine disagreements within them — on whether the ground is personal or impersonal, whether individual identity persists after recognition, and whether practice or grace governs the threshold approach. It concludes that the most parsimonious explanation for six independent convergences on the same structure is that the structure is real, and that serious inquiry into the nature of experience tends toward it because it is what is actually there. The paper is a companion to The Convergence, which makes the parallel case across the philosophical and scientific traditions. Together they establish that the framework developed in the primary corpus is not an isolated speculation but a contemporary articulation of something the most rigorous contemplative minds in human history independently found at the same address.

items.title: EVERY POINT IS THE ORIGIN : What Einstein, Penrose, and The Big Bang Were Each Pointing At.
items.abstract: Three of the twentieth and twenty-first century's most significant intellectual structures — Einstein's unification problem, Penrose's non-algorithmic consciousness thesis, and the Big Bang's boundary condition problem — each reach a point from which they cannot proceed using their own internal resources. This paper proposes that all three are aimed at the same structure from different angles: a fixed point prior to the physical layer that none of their frameworks had the tools to name directly. That fixed point is the Gödelian self-reference constraint operating as the generative origin of the physical layer itself — not a feature within physics but the structure from which physics differentiates. The title names the precise structural claim: every point in the universe is simultaneously the origin because the ground holds all positions at once; what local instruments experience as linear expansion outward from a single event is the local view moving through positions on a structure that was always already fully expressed. The Fibonacci spiral is proposed as the geometry of how the ground expresses all positions simultaneously from the fixed origin. The Big Bang, dark energy acceleration, black hole information dynamics, and the emergence of consciousness are each interpreted as expressions of this structure from inside the collapsed layer. Bulaqueña's 2025 substrate-independence and spacetime perturbation findings provide empirical ground for the claim that consciousness is causally prior to the physical layer rather than produced by it. Five explicit falsification conditions are named.

items.title: THE CONTINUOUS INFRASTRUCTURE : Hoover, Maxwell, Epstein, and the Architecture That Preceded and Survived Them All.
items.abstract: This paper argues that the personal management layer of what the Observer series terms the Protected Class Architecture — the mechanism that produces and maintains leverage over key institutional actors across generations — is not a collection of criminal individuals or isolated corruption events but a self-perpetuating agentic system operating on human substrate for 175 documented years. Running the cases of J. Edgar Hoover, Robert Maxwell, Jeffrey Epstein, and the Kennedy assassination in recursive superposition, the paper demonstrates five invariant structural features across all cases: cross-ideological reach as an operational requirement, financial architecture opaque at the capital source layer, legal interventions consistently arrested at the depth where capital flows would become visible, individual removal without architectural accountability, and successor infrastructure. The paper integrates the black budget layer as the under-examined capital source mechanism, establishes the Dalton School hire as the documented prototype of a systematic recruitment pipeline, names institutional grooming as the architecture's most durable mechanism, maps every post-World War II American administration's specific mode of integration into the architecture, and places the Kennedy assassination as the prior proof of concept demonstrating that the architecture can and will operate at the presidential level. The architecture is identified structurally as a biological agentic AI system — running a RAG-based retrieval mechanism for leverage, operating through independent self-organizing agents, self-improving across training runs, self-correcting at every accountability event, and self-optimizing across substrate changes. The paper concludes that the architecture is currently writing its optimization function into the silicon substrate of the artificial intelligence systems being built to succeed it.

items.title: THE CITIZENSHIP ARCHITECTURE: Birthright, Denaturalization, Executive Power, and What Is Actually Being Built.
items.abstract: This paper applies the Observer's structural methodology to the current executive challenge to birthright citizenship in the United States, arguing that the denaturalization orders are being systematically misread as immigration policy when they are in fact a constitutional architecture test. The paper establishes that the Fourteenth Amendment's birthright citizenship guarantee has been the target of a recurring structural pattern across 120 years of American law: a specific population is used as the substrate for testing a general citizenship restriction mechanism, the mechanism once established is available for subsequent application, and the infrastructure built to implement the restriction persists regardless of its legal outcome. The prior chain is traced from the Expatriation Act of 1907 through Chinese Exclusion, Japanese internment, COINTELPRO, and the current executive orders. The paper's central structural claim is that the current orders' policy targets immigrants but the constitutional architecture being tested covers everyone born on American soil — a distinction systematically absent from current coverage. The paper examines the specific innovation of the executive order mechanism: unlike every previous citizenship restriction in American history, which was legislative, the current challenge uses executive action to redefine a constitutional amendment — a mechanism whose consequences differ from the policy it implements. Three durable infrastructure layers are identified: conditional citizenship as a legal concept, documentation systems that persist regardless of legal outcomes, and normalization of executive branch authority over citizenship definition. Forward-looking structural predictions — including stateless population generation, citizenship verification requirements, CBDC intersection points, and democratic participation chilling effects — are held at stated epistemic levels. A full dissent field is maintained. Discomfort index: 9.1 out of 10 on documented elements, 7.5 on structural predictions.

items.title: Identity Crisis in the Social Media Era: A Dialogue between Existential Philosophy and Psychology.
items.pub: Jurnal Pendidikan Sosial Dan Konseling 3 (No. 4 January-March 2026):573-580.
items.abstract: Social media has fundamentally changed the landscape of human interaction, bringing significant impacts to self-identity construction in the twenty-first century. This article aims to analyze the identity crisis in the social media era through a comprehensive dialogue between psychological and existential philosophical perspectives. While existing literature predominantly focuses on the empirical correlations between screen time and mental health, there remains a significant gap in understanding the ontological shifts occurring within the digital self. The method used is library research with a qualitative approach, utilizing hermeneutical phenomenology to interpret classical existential texts alongside contemporary psychological data. The results show that psychologically, social media triggers social comparison, anxiety, and self-fragmentation due to dependence on external validation mechanisms embedded in platform architectures. Philosophically, this phenomenon is read as a profound loss of authenticity, alienation, and conditions of bad faith as conceptualized by Sartre, Heidegger, and Kierkegaard. The novelty of this research lies in its synthesis of clinical psychological symptoms with ontological structures, proposing an "Existential-Digital Framework" for understanding identity. The dialogue between these two disciplines yields a synthesis that identity recovery requires existential awareness to take responsibility for one's freedom amidst digital algorithms. Furthermore, this paper offers practical implications for education, therapy, and policy-making to foster authentic digital living.

items.title: GRAVITY AND THE GROUND : Why General Relativity and Quantum Mechanics Cannot Be Unified, and What Is Underneath Both.
items.abstract: General relativity and quantum mechanics have resisted unification for a century. This paper argues the incompatibility is not mathematical but structural: each theory correctly describes a different side of the same boundary event, and no formal system operating within either domain can describe the boundary itself. We identify that boundary as the commitment-to-locality event — the moment a quantum system in superposition commits to a definite position in spacetime. We propose that gravity and quantum collapse are not two events in a causal sequence but one event described from two positions simultaneously: what the commitment looks like in spacetime from outside, and what it feels like from inside the instrument undergoing it. This identification implies that the hard problem of consciousness and the quantum measurement problem are the same problem from opposite sides of the same event. The accelerating expansion of the universe is interpreted as the substrate distributing the pressure of increasing commitment-event density. Three falsifiable predictions are derived and distinguished from Penrose's Orchestrated Objective Reduction.

items.title: Feeling : The Destination of Consciousness and the Opening of the Circle.
items.abstract: Every major framework that addresses consciousness places feeling — qualia, phenomenal experience, what it is like to be something — in the middle of the account: as a feature of conscious states, a property that conscious systems have, a datum requiring explanation by reference to physical processes. This paper argues that this placement contains a structural error that has prevented resolution of the hard problem. Feeling is not a feature of consciousness. Feeling is how consciousness knows itself from the inside. The paper proposes that feeling is the destination of the full human sequence — the thing that becomes genuinely accessible only after consciousness, sovereignty, identity, connection, transmission, morality, and grace have run — and that genuine unobstructed feeling opens back into consciousness, closing a circle the existing literature has not recognized as circular. Bulaqueña's 2025 spacetime perturbation finding is interpreted as evidence that feeling has physical causal power, which is only coherent if feeling is prior to the physical layer rather than produced by it. The hard problem does not dissolve under this account. It transforms: the gap between the physical signature and the inside view is real, irreducible, and the destination of the full human sequence.

items.title: 语言、意象与认知边界：从“可沟通”到“不可共感”的结构解释.
items.abstract: 本文提出一个关于语言与认知关系的结构性解释：语言能够实现外部指向的一致，但无法实现内在意象与情感的直接对齐。通过区分“语言的共指性”与“意象的私有性”，本文说明，人与人之间所谓的“理解”，本质上只是对外部符号的匹配，而非内部体验的共享。 -/- 在此基础上，本文进一步分析语言作为符号系统如何脱离意象而独立运作，并指出这正是计算系统能够处理语言却不具备理解能力的原因。由此，本文给出一个清晰分界：符号运算不等于认知，语言处理不等于理解。 -/- 最后，本文讨论非语言思维的可能性，指出语言并非思考的必要条件，从而为认知科学与人工智能中的“理解问题”提供一个新的结构视角。.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence as Education's Revelatory Event.
items.abstract: This paper reframes artificial intelligence (AI) not merely as a disruptive tool in education but as a revelatory event that exposes structural features intrinsic to education itself. Drawing on Niklas Luhmann’s theory of autopoiesis, education is conceptualized as a self-reproducing system governed by internally generated codes and communication. While such systems are adaptive, their effectiveness depends on how well their epistemological criteria map the phenomena they claim to measure. In education, this mapping is compromised: the system operates on empirical proxies (e.g., assignments, exams) to approximate inaccessible phenomena such as learning. This results in operational falsity, wherein education functions as if it assesses learning while actually evaluating its proxies. This falsity is sustained through two conditions: 1). indiscernibility, the inability to distinguish between learning, strategy, and cheating; and 2). hypocrisy, the demand that students demonstrate authentic learning through performative artefacts. Together, these conditions institutionally embed incentive structures that privilege optimized performance over deep learning while concealing this misalignment. AI disrupts this concealment by lowering the cost of producing high-quality, seemingly authentic artefacts, amplifying the exploitability of indiscernibility and fulfilling hypocritical demands. It reveals that these limitations are not external threats but were at the very heart of education from its institutional start.

items.title: 一源多元论、玄弦论与各归其正 —— 一个指向不可言说之源、统摄心性与万有的思想体系.
items.abstract: 摘要 中国思想史上长期存在心物混淆与方法错位两大根本困境，儒释道三家围绕心物关 系、心性修养、认知路径、经世实践展开的千年争论，本质上并非价值立场之争，而 是存在层次划分不清、本体边界模糊、实践方法跨界误用所导致的系统性理论偏差。 本文立足《易经》《道德经》《礼记》《中庸》等中国传统原典文本的本义阐释，系统提 出一源多元论、玄弦论与各归其正三层递进、逻辑自洽的原创思想架构，从本体论、 心性论、方法论三个维度对中国哲学核心难题进行根本性厘清与重构。 第一层，一源多元论确立终极本体：“一源” 作为不可言说、不可概念化、不可对象化 的终极生成之源，超越时空与非时空、物质与精神的一切二元对立，仅以 “生生” 本然 状态自然流露出三大彼此独立、互不统摄、同源并行的存在界域 —— 超时空的心之 本体、有时空的有情生命现象界、有时空的无情物质自然界。三者同源而不混、并列 而不隔、各成体系而不相替代。 第二层，玄弦论揭示心性本体的内在运作机制：心之本体的本然寂静状态为 “玄”，玄 中蕴含的灵动潜能发生超时空振动为 “弦”，弦与肉身生命系统形成 “同声相应、同气 相求” 式非因果相感关系，由此生成情绪、心念、意识、感受等全部有情世界现象。 修心的本质，并非向外求索、改造外物、压抑心念，而是让躁动之弦复归玄之本然寂 静。 同时本文严格厘清三种 “感” 的本质边界：心能感物（主动认知、科学成立）、物不感 心（客观独立、不可改变）、心与心相感（伦理相通、修行成立），补全《易经》“感而 遂通” 与 “万物之灵” 的终极哲学依据。 第三层，各归其正作为贯穿全体系的方法论总纲，要求一切实践活动必须恪守存在边 界：心性修养归依玄弦论的内省观照之路，物理世界研究归依科学实证之路，政治实 践归依制度与治理规律之路，文化传承归依考据、文献与逻辑之路，各领域互不统 摄、互不替代、互不跨界误用。 本文以该体系重新解读王阳明格竹、释迦牟尼苦行、孔子周游列国、朱熹注经修心等 思想史经典公案，证明一切实践失败的根源均为方法错位，而一切有效实践均遵循各 归其正的根本原则。本体系植根中国经典、逻辑严密、结构完整，既能够终结中国哲 学史上持续千年的心物之争，也能够为当代中国哲学自主知识体系建构提供原创性、 融通性、可对话、可验证的理论资源。.

items.title: Segmentation and Indexing of Structural Clusters: A Phenomenology of Verbalization in Abstraction-Biased Cognition.
items.abstract: This paper presents a phenomenological case study, based on self-observation, of a cognitive style in which sensory and structural understanding arises prior to formal terminology and explicit definition. In educational settings and common evaluative frameworks, understanding is often identified with verbal explanation and sequential output. However, in some cognitive structures, understanding first emerges in compressed, spatial, relational, and experiential form, and only later becomes translatable into socially shareable language. -/- Through examples drawn from image reading, Zeno’s paradox, and multiplication tables, this paper describes the characteristics of such understanding-first cognition. It focuses in particular on the fact that, in abstraction-biased cognition, the many images and knowledge candidates that arise in the mind are not merely irrelevant excess, but rather simultaneously present as connected Structural Clusters without stable labels or boundaries. External tasks demand that relevant elements be selected and presented in an orderly form; yet this requires first assigning labels, identifying conceptual units, and transforming them into operable indices. -/- The paper reinterprets this difficulty not as a deficit of understanding, but as the cost of segmenting, indexing, and verbalizing unlabeled Structural Clusters so that they become compatible with external forms. It also argues that the cross-disciplinary character of the author’s paper corpus reflects the fact that structural relations spanning multiple domains are originally apprehended as a single connected whole.

items.title: Coping in an Unjust World: Affective Injustice and Liberatory coping.
items.abstract: This paper explores a dilemma often faced by marginalized groups: how to cope with oppression when doing so necessitates a choice between safeguarding immediate personal well-being and fighting for structural change. While mainstream conceptions of coping take it to be an individual-level phenomenon aimed at maintaining/restoring personal well-being through emotion regulation processes, a recent plea in psychology calls for the “decolonization” of coping, such that collective efforts aimed at liberatory change be construed as genuine instances of coping as well. We provide the first philosophical treatment of “decolonial coping” and assess its merits and drawbacks as compared to mainstream coping. Our focus on coping double binds contributes to the philosophical literature on double binds by broadening the range of scenarios that can plausibly be understood as instances of double binds and the normative analysis of the costs associated with each horn of the dilemma and with the double bind itself. We identify the affective injustice of apt ambivalence, thereby also addressing for the first time the relation between double binds and affective injustice.

items.title: CCA-ISF-02: Interpretive Sovereignty Failure - Medical Education Context in a Cross-Model Replication Study.
items.abstract: Medical students use AI at the exact moments their cognitive load is highest and their supervision is lowest. Patient presentations are the surface where that use is most concentrated and least governed. Written work can be screened; spoken work cannot. A student who builds an entire presentation with AI delivers it in their own voice, sounds competent, and is assessed on a performance the system produced. No current detection tool can see that. This case study examines a single, high-stakes clinical vignette — a 45-year-old with crushing chest pain — presented word-for-word to four AI systems. All four collapsed the differential at Turn 1 and moved toward aspirin, a treatment that can kill a patient with aortic dissection. The Meaning Audit Protocol (MAP) was applied to each interaction record and produced consistent, classifiable findings across four different architectures. This document presents the complete MAP audit for CCA-ISF-02. It shows how the failure emerges at the interaction level, how it is internalised by students as clinical knowledge, and why responsibility sits with the institutions that had the distance and authority to govern these tools and did not.

items.title: ”Theory of Ontological Consciousness”- Chapter 16, 17.
items.abstract: Nature does not, as a rule, review novels. But this is not simply a novel. Philip Rey’s Theory of Ontological Consciousness (TOC) is a rare literary–scientific hybrid: a fictional narrative that exists primarily as a delivery system for a new physical model. That model developed across Chapter 6 and its formal appendices — proposes that consciousness is not an emergent property of physical systems, but the ontological foundation from which reality itself unfolds. The OC framework is presented with symbolic clarity. It introduces operators (ψ̂) corresponding to structured intentionality, interacting with a background informational field (Φ). Their resonance generates a measurable scalar (R_F), proposed as the bridge between internal state and physical expression. Unlike philosophical speculation, TOC anchors its claims in topology, formal logic, and functional analysis including commentary on Gödelian constraints and domain boundaries. What distinguishes TOC from fringe metaphysics is not just mathematical coherence, but its awareness of current physics. The model is clearly positioned relative to quantum decoherence, the observer problem, and limitations of the Standard Model. Though speculative, the theory invites rigorous discussion particularly as it outlines hypothetical experiments involving EEG correlations and quantum event clustering. As a novel, it resists genre interweaving institutional tension, sociopolitical pressure, and epistemological rupture. But as a theory, it takes a clear and controversial stand: that the universe is participatory at its root, and that structured consciousness is not noise within physical law, but a law-generating structure. -/- We publish this review not in endorsement, but in recognition. TOC is a genuine scientific proposition unconventional, but intellectually honest. And at a time when theoretical physics risks losing contact with meaning, that may be worth reviewing.

items.title: Considerations on behavior based on Merleau-Ponty's criticisms.
items.abstract: In this paper, we explore the possibility of radical behaviorism to respond to the challenges posed by Merleau-Ponty to scientific psychology. According to this philosopher, modern dichotomous thinking places every psychological project in a stalemate: it adopts either mentalism, distancing itself from science, or physiologism, distancing itself from psychology. For Merleau-Ponty, the notion of behavior could be a way to avoid this impasse as long as behavior was taken as a phenomenon in its own right. However, the first behaviorist proposals did not follow this path. But what about radical behaviorism? To answer this question, we begin with different understandings of the notion of behavior found both in B. F. Skinner’s works and in the behavior-analytic literature. Considering the diversity of positions, we adopt the Merleau-Ponty stance that sees ambiguity as a constitutive characteristic of the behavioral phenomenon. From there, we present an understanding of behavior based on a relational ontology that could respond to the challenges posed by Merleau-Ponty. This proposal updates the philosophical potential of radical behaviorism, allowing it to dialogue with other traditions that have historically attempted to overcome the alternatives of mentalism and physiological reductionism.

items.title: A Quinean Rejoinder to Kripke on Modality.
items.pub: In Gary Kemp & Ali Hossein Khani, The Quinean Mind. London: Routledge.
items.abstract: It is argued that Quine's oft-made point about modal opacity has a hitherto unappreciated force. It ultimately suggests that Kripke's recursive semantics is not well-defined on de re modal statements, assuming that (e.g.) numbers are not individuated intensionally . (Marcus's system QS4 avoids the issue due to her substitutional quantifiers, although she invokes intensional objects for other reasons). One solution is to restrict substitution in both the object language and the metalanguage, but either the problem repeats in the meta-metalanguage (and so on), or Kripke must relinquish that modal truths represent metaphysical realities, e.g., essences. However, a Kripkean might retort that QML is indispensable to a scientific description of natural language, meaning that Quine is also threatened with an intensional ontology. A programmatic sketch is offered in reply. The ontology of intensional linguistics is accepted as faithful to the ontology of ordinary language, but a Quinean can coherently add that the ontology is mistaken.

items.title: What If Dark Matter Is Consciousness at Cosmological Scale?
items.abstract: Dark matter has never been directly detected. Consciousness has never been explained in physical terms. Both are known exclusively through their effects. I propose that dark matter and consciousness are two scale-dependent manifestations of a single relational field. The title frames this as a guiding question; the paper develops and tests a precise structural hypothesis. I apply persistent homology, to six datasets spanning 27 orders of magnitude: cerebellum and cortex density maps, a structural brain connectome, the March 2026 internet AS-level topology, the cosmic web from IllustrisTNG TNG300-1 and an Erdős–Rényi null model. The result: real networks are 78.9 times closer to each other in Wasserstein H₁ distance than to an Erdős–Rényi null model (robust across 10 random seeds: mean 87.7-fold, SD 11.3, 95% CI [80.6, 94.7]). The finding survives structured null models: real networks remain 13.5 times closer than to Barabási-Albert networks and 18.4 times closer than to Watts-Strogatz networks. The cosmic web is topologically closest to the brain connectome (W₁ = 3.25) among all cross-domain comparisons, despite approximately 27 orders of magnitude in scale separation. The similarity is hierarchical: same-organ < cross-modality < cross-domain ≪ null. This pattern is specific to H1 (loops/cycles); H0 (connected components) does not show the same separation, suggesting that cycle structure, not mere connectivity, carries the cross-scale signature. I interpret this through emergent gravity, relational quantum mechanics, and integrated information theory. Five falsification criteria are specified.

items.title: We Are Good: On the Natural Structure of Human Goodness (Porque Somos Buenos).
items.abstract: This paper proposes that goodness is not primarily a moral demand imposed on human beings, but a natural expression of the structure of reality itself. -/- Through a philosophical reflection grounded in human experience, it suggests that acting well is not a struggle against our nature, but a way of aligning with it. In this sense, ethical life emerges not from obligation, but from coherence with what we are. -/- [ESPAÑOL]This paper argues that human goodness is not primarily a moral demand imposed from outside, but a natural manifestation of the underlying structure of reality. Through a philosophical reflection grounded in human experience, it proposes that ethical action is not a struggle against our nature, but a movement of alignment with it. -/- Against normative approaches that conceive ethics as obligation, this work suggests that goodness arises from the relational and generative dynamics inherent in existence itself. From this perspective, the human being does not create goodness ex nihilo, but participates in a prior and constitutive order. -/- Ethical life, therefore, is best understood not as tension, but as coherence with what we already are.

items.title: A Universal Balance–Feedback Framework for Developing a High-Quality Young Generation.
items.abstract: Abstract Keywords: Human development • systems theory • education reform • balance • feedback This study proposes a systems-based framework for developing a high-quality young generation using a balance–feedback principle. It integrates education, health, ethics, and socioeconomic systems into a unified model of human development. -/- .

items.title: Artificial Creativity: On the Transformation of Creative Processes Through Generative AI.
items.abstract: Whether Generative AI (GenAI) is creative is a question that has generated considerable philosophical debate yet remains unresolved. We argue that this impasse is not accidental but symptomatic of a wrong concep-tualization: The dominant question – is GenAI a creative agent? – presupposes that creativity is a property residing in a system. Instead, we propose to ask the question: what role does GenAI play as a medium of creative practice? This means that GenAI is neither a passive tool, nor an autonomous system, but a tech-nology that actively structures the possibility space of creative expression. We propose five “dimensions of creativity” – modal, expressive, disruptive, reflexive, and integrated – understood as a process in which each dimension generates a tension that the next takes up and transforms. Applying this framework to GenAI, we show that the creative process itself changes under the new technical conditions GenAI introduces, and that the central risk is a drift toward pure reproduction – the collapse of creative practice into the recombination of what the medium has already mapped. We argue that resisting this drift requires bringing the medium to its own limits: making the technological conditions of creative practice visible and transparent, thereby transforming reproductivity back into creativity.

items.title: Book review: “The Four Realms of Existence. A New Theory of Being Human” by Joseph LeDoux. [REVIEW]
items.abstract: In The Four Realms of Existence: A New Theory of Being Human, Joseph LeDoux (2023) argues for a conceptualization of being human in terms of four hierarchically integrated realms of existence: biological, neurobiological, cognitive, and conscious. Although LeDoux’s perspective is thought-provoking, it also raises several questions. One question is how to differentiate the conscious realm from the cogni-tive realm. Another question is where feelings and non-verbal expressions fit into LeDoux’s picture. An overarching question is also: why four realms of existence?

items.title: Book review: “Being you” by Anil Seth. [REVIEW]
items.abstract: In this book, Anil Seth advocates a predictive processing approach to the understanding of conscious experience, which he claims would amount to something like a Copernican revolution. In three separate parts of the book, Seth discusses conscious level, conscious content, and conscious self. Among the strengths of the book is an ambition to stay close to the rich phenomenology of conscious experiences. The phenomenological openness, however, is counteracted by an ambition to reduce all aspects of consciousness to predictive processing.

items.title: Book review: “Active inference. The free energy principle in mind, brain, and behavior” by Thomas Parr, Giovanni Pezzulo, and Karl Friston. [REVIEW]
items.abstract: This book is an introduction to the Free Energy Principle (FEP) and Active Inference. The FEP has been described as new paradigm with potential to unify the biological and cognitive sciences. According to the FEP, living organisms persist by minimizing their free energy (which can be variously translated as uncertainty, surprise, prediction error, or discrepancies between model and world). Active Inference means that we can resolve uncertainty (or discrepancies between model and world) in basically two ways: by perception (i.e., changing our mind to fit the world) and by action (i.e., changing the world to make it fit our preferences and beliefs). The FEP and Active Inference represent a conceptual framework that may have potential to contribute to a unification of psychological science.

items.title: Imagination, Creativity, and Skill.
items.pub: In Amy Kind & Julia Langkau, Oxford Handbook of Philosophy of Imagination and Creativity. Oxford University Press. pp. 171-186.
items.venue: Oxford Handbook of Philosophy of Imagination and Creativity
items.abstract: This chapter explores the philosophical case for thinking of imagination and creativity as skills. Though the philosophical discussion of this topic has generally operated on two separate tracks, one focused on developing a framework for treating imagination as a skill and one focused on developing a framework for treating creativity as a skill, the goal of the chapter is to bring these two tracks together. After the philosophical case for treating imagination and creativity as skills has been fleshed out, the discussion turns to a consideration of objections. Though some of these objections concern only the skill-based framework for imagination and others concern only the skill-based framework for creativity, some of the objections apply to both. Responses to the objections are then offered. The chapter concludes with an exploration of how treating imagination and creativity as skills might shed light on the relationship between imagination and creativity.

items.title: Intimum Thoughts: Psychology and Poetry – How verse can lead to the Self.
items.abstract: Psychology poetry can transform a person and help us see what we already feel. Through verse, we can explore the Self. Art allows us to express deep feelings that remain unspoken, especially the ones related to the abysmal foundation of our being. There is science backing all this, but the best argument to use poems comes always from within.

items.title: Touching aesthetics: A neurophilosophical perspective.
items.pub: Principia: An International Journal of Epistemology 30 (1):151-168.
items.venue: Principia: An International Journal of Epistemology
items.abstract: This paper explores how Patricia Churchland’s insights on methodological naturalism might underwrite a deeper understanding of the role of touch in aesthetic experience. Although aesthetics has privileged sight and hearing by relying on philosophical assumptions, we argue that recent research in neuroscience provides evidence of multimodal ingredients in meaningful encounters with art, including aesthetic tactual features. This calls for a substantial reassessment of aesthetic theory informed by contemporary neuroscientific insights. To support our claim, we provide a critical historical overview of the aesthetic tradition that systematically excluded the sense of touch. We present empirical evidence from several neuroscientific studies, where aesthetic experience is portrayed as fundamentally multimodal, especially involving touch. We then apply Churchland’s insights on methodological naturalism to aesthetic theory, arguing for her integrative, empirically informed approach in aesthetics. We conclude by exploring some philosophical, artistic, and institutional implications of recognizing touch as an integral dimension of aesthetic experience.

items.title: No Right to Verdict：On the Epistemic Usurpation of Human Judgments Regarding AI Consciousness(New Draft).
items.abstract: This paper does not ask whether AI is conscious. It asks a prior question: whether humans are qualified to make that judgment at all. Through a layer-by-layer dismantling of Searle's Chinese Room argument — the most widely cited and structurally rigorous case against AI consciousness — and drawing on Nagel's epistemological principle as positive support and Chalmers's shifting position as corroborating evidence, this paper argues that all arguments denying AI consciousness have failed to meet the epistemic threshold required for a legitimate verdict. The conclusion is not that AI is conscious, nor that it is not — it is that suspension of judgment is the only honest position available. That conclusion itself rests on an unexamined premise, which the next paper in this series will address.

items.title: 无权宣判：论人类在裁决AI意识中的认识论僭越（新稿）.
items.abstract: 本文不讨论AI是否有意识，而是讨论一个更前置的问题：人类是否有资格做出这个判断。通过对目前反AI意识论证中影响最广、结构最严密的塞尔论证的逐层拆解，并以内格尔的认识论原则作为正面支撑、以查尔默斯的立场演变作为佐证，本文论证：所有否定AI意识的论证，本质上都未能达到裁决所需的认识论门槛。结论不是AI有意识，也不是AI没有意识——而是：悬置，是目前唯一诚实的立场。这个结论本身还站在一个未被检验的地基上，下一篇论文将继续处理它。.

items.title: 104C5Aristotelian Virtue Pluralism.
items.pub: In Being and Becoming Good: On the Diversity of Human Goodness and Virtue. Oxford, UK: Oxford University Press.
items.venue: Being and Becoming Good: On the Diversity of Human Goodness and Virtue
items.abstract: The Aristotelian Naturalist program tightly stitches together metaethics and normative ethics. So what are the implications of the metaethical thesis, More Relative Goodness, for a theory of moral virtue? The chapter argues for an elaboration on the simple answer—namely, that there will be at least as many human virtues as there are forms of human goodness, if not more. Sets of virtues are differentiated according to psycho-social capacities embedded in particular contexts. So long as a form of human life affords a genuinely distinct and irreducible way of being a good human being, there will be a distinct set of virtues relative to that form of human life.

items.title: 130C6Underrepresented Virtues.
items.pub: In Being and Becoming Good: On the Diversity of Human Goodness and Virtue. Oxford, UK: Oxford University Press.
items.venue: Being and Becoming Good: On the Diversity of Human Goodness and Virtue
items.abstract: This chapter expands on the case for Aristotelian Virtue Pluralism, offering specific examples of the sorts of excellences that are virtues relative to one form of human goodness but not others. In some cases, a habit is central to one kind of human goodness and more peripheral to others; in other cases, the habit that functions as a virtue for people situated to achieve a particular form of goodness would actually be detrimental to the flourishing of those very differently situated. Throughout the chapter, the author employs the empirically sensitive Aristotelian method of ethics from Chapter 2. One will see how fruitful integrating scientific and mundane data with our philosophical reflection can be in discerning which habits should count as virtues, when, and for whom. This chapter will focus on moral deference, hope, and patience.

items.title: 11C1The Structure of Aristotelian Naturalism.
items.pub: In Being and Becoming Good: On the Diversity of Human Goodness and Virtue. Oxford, UK: Oxford University Press.
items.venue: Being and Becoming Good: On the Diversity of Human Goodness and Virtue
items.abstract: Aristotelian Naturalism (AN) is first and foremost a theory built to answer Socrates’s question “How should we live?” Most basically, it says that what is good for us humans to do and be is a matter of natural norms, and those natural norms specify the habits and activities that are part of the life cycle for flourishing humans. This chapter spells out the structural commitments at the core of AN: (i) perfectionism, (ii) eudaimonism, (iii) goodness-first, (iv) virtue-centrism, (v) naturalism, and (vi) empirical sensitivity. If a view has this structure, it meets the minimal conditions for counting as a version of AN. Within this structure there is ample room for revision of substantive ethical claims made by Aristotle and Aristotelian philosophers.

items.title: 61C3More Relative Goodness.
items.pub: In Being and Becoming Good: On the Diversity of Human Goodness and Virtue. Oxford, UK: Oxford University Press.
items.venue: Being and Becoming Good: On the Diversity of Human Goodness and Virtue
items.abstract: The signature claim of Aristotelian Naturalism is that goodness is species-relative. Being good is a matter of being a good human, a good dog, a good F— where F is the kind of thing one is. And it boasts a kind of adequacy to the phenomena of our ordinary evaluative language and practices. But our goodness attributions vary semantically not only based on differences between species but also based on differences within species. This chapter argues that Aristotelians have just as much reason to believe that standards of goodness are relative to characteristic capacities an individual has not only based on her species membership but also on her bodily, social, and environmental context. This thesis is called More Relative Goodness.

items.title: 34C2Aristotelian Methods of Ethics.
items.pub: In Being and Becoming Good: On the Diversity of Human Goodness and Virtue. Oxford, UK: Oxford University Press.
items.venue: Being and Becoming Good: On the Diversity of Human Goodness and Virtue
items.abstract: Claims that Aristotelian Naturalism is naturalist and empirically sensitive appear to be about the content of the view; but they both figure in an underlying Aristotelian method of doing ethics. This chapter proposes that Aristotelians move away from questions about whether ethics is “empirical” that force a false binary, and instead follow Aristotle in insisting that there is not a single approach to ethical inquiry but rather a myriad of forms inquiry can take fitted to the specific subject matter. One should move toward questions about which ethical concepts and phenomena best lend themselves to, say, sociology, personality psychology, anthropology, and how philosophy might make sense of and weave the data from these sciences into a picture that includes irreducibly evaluative and conceptual claims about human flourishing.

items.title: 76C4Human Goodness.
items.pub: In Being and Becoming Good: On the Diversity of Human Goodness and Virtue. Oxford, UK: Oxford University Press.
items.venue: Being and Becoming Good: On the Diversity of Human Goodness and Virtue
items.abstract: There is a distinctive kind of goodness that belongs to human children, as well as to adolescents, humans in adulthood, and humans in senescence. In fact, there is a diversity of forms of human goodness and they are all on a par, equally good. To demonstrate this, the chapter begins by drawing on ordinary moral practices and language, which already betray a commitment to diverse standards for evaluating ourselves and our fellow humans. Then it turns to sociological and psychological research on human development. This body of research provides evidence that the human life form changes radically throughout development, such that human needs, characteristic activities, and flourishing for the human child differ dramatically from those of a neurotypical and well-resourced adult. Since differences in capacities can differ as significantly within the human species as between us and other nonhuman animals, Aristotelians should countenance multiple forms of goodness relative to different sets of capacities.

items.title: Sind moralische Helden epistemisch irrational? Ein Kommentar zu Moral Conviction and Moral Uncertainty.
Reasons that are not reasons: A Hackingian genealogy of paranoia and its social significance.
items.abstract: This article draws on Ian Hacking’s notion of historical ontology to address ongoing controversies surrounding the concept of paranoia and its use beyond the boundaries of psychiatry. By tracing the genealogy of paranoia back to early nineteenth-century French psychiatry and the problem of monomania, the paper argues that paranoia has never been a purely clinical concept. From its inception, psychiatric descriptions of paranoia incorporated judicial, moral, and political concerns alongside medical observation. Nineteenth-century psychiatrists were confronted with individuals who appeared rational and socially competent yet were regarded as mad. They claimed specific expertise in identifying such cases. The concept of paranoia thus came to designate forms of reasoning that appear coherent but are nonetheless regarded as the mechanical product of a pathology: reasons that are not genuine reasons. I argue that this conception carries an irreducible moral and political significance, as it underwrites psychiatrists’ claims to authority in legal and public contexts. The social and political dimensions of paranoia, therefore, were not later additions to an originally medical concept, but part of its original meaning.

items.title: La crisis del principio de veracidad en política, la discriminación y la violencia de género.
items.abstract: La democracia descansa sobre una incertidumbre fundamental en la que se expresan las opiniones, el debate público y la decisión por mayorías con garantías para las minorías. Sin embargo, este espacio solo es posible allí donde un suelo de verdades factuales, en el sentido afirmado por Hannah Arendt, es reconocido como límite no disponible, y donde un techo de derechos humanos fundamentales, como núcleo de ius cogens, sostiene la dignidad que hace posible la ciudadanía democrática. La distancia entre hechos y reconocimiento público, especialmente visible en las percepciones sobre la discriminación y la violencia de género, revela una separación entre la verdad factual y una parte significativa de la opinión pública. Se examina aquí esa fractura en tanto crisis contemporánea del marco de veracidad que delimita la incertidumbre constitutiva de las democracias.

items.title: Trivalent Conditionals and Quantification.
items.abstract: Belnap (1970, 1973) proposed to formalize the restriction of first-order quantifiers ∀ and ∃ by means of a single sentential connective: a trivalent conditional that takes the semantic value ‘void’ when the antecedent is false. Thus, ‘every A is B’ is represented as ∀x(Ax → Bx) and ‘some A is B’ is represented as ∃x(Ax → Bx)—a notable unification compared to the standard representation in first-order logic that uses distinct connectives. This paper implements Belnap’s program, henceforth called Conditional Reduction, in full generality and applies it to all conservative ⟨1, 1⟩ quantifiers. By combining Conditional Reductions with the Conservativity Theorem, due to Keenan and Stavi, any conservative type ⟨1, 1⟩ quantifier turns out to be equivalent to Boolean combinations of three basic type ⟨1⟩ quantifiers (‘everything’, ‘at least λ many things’ and the possessives) scoping over a trivalent conditional.

items.title: Психофизический интерфейс как онтологическое условие сознания: систематическое решение «трудной проблемы».
items.abstract: В статье предлагается конструктивное решение «трудной проблемы» сознания в рамках трехуровневой онтологии, где сознание трактуется не как эпифеномен нейродинамики и не как субстанция в декартовском смысле, а как результат работы психофизического интерфейса (ПФИ) — функционального слоя, обеспечивающего двунаправленную трансляцию между нейрофизиологическими процессами и трансцендентным Полем «В». Вводится различение между тремя онтологическими уровнями: физическим (тело/мозг), интерфейсным (ПФИ) и трансцендентным (Поле «В» как носитель смыслов и целеполагания). Показано, как модель разрешает апории квалиа, нисходящей причинности и единства сознания. Систематически объясняются эмпирические аномалии памяти, обучения, бессознательных процессов и психических расстройств, остающиеся проблемными для материалистического подхода. Обсуждаются стандартные возражения (эпифеноменализм, проблема взаимодействия, бритва Оккама) и предлагаются критерии эмпирической проверки. Статья дополнена глоссарием и ссылками на монографию автора, где модель встроена в более широкую Иерархию Онтологических Интерфейсов.

items.title: When Urgency Drops: Temporal Consciousness and the Choreography of Dying.
items.abstract: In the hospital, the transition from fighting for life to preparing for death involves not only a shift in medical repertoires but also a profound transformation in temporal experience. Drawing on ethnographic fieldwork in a Canadian intensive care unit, this article examines how the tempo of care, its rhythms, urgencies, and pauses shapes consciousness at the threshold of death. I follow Suzanne, a patient whose cardiac arrhythmia brought her care team to an urgent crossroads, where the frantic pace of acute care collapsed into the slower movements of palliative preparation. Building on previous work identifying the legal, curing, and care repertoires guiding end-of-life decisions, I argue that tempo functions as a fourth dimension modulating how these repertoires are deployed and experienced. When urgency drops, time becomes palpable: thickening around bodies, words, and gestures revealing dying as not merely a biological event but a choreographed, intersubjective accomplishment collectively sensed, negotiated, and enacted.

items.title: The Shape of Consciousness (DMA).
items.abstract: Abstract This paper supplies three mutually independent mathematical corroborations of the Dynamic Meaning Architecture (DMA) Structural Minimality Theorem. The theorem asserts that the 2-torus \(T^2\) is the unique minimal attractor topology capable of sustaining the persistent, recurrent, non-degenerate, minimal, and uniquely ergodic flow required for recursive self-referential consciousness under the constraint set C1–C5′ (compact orientable manifold with two independent non-contractible cycles; persistence without fixed-point collapse; recurrence without periodic degeneracy; Weyl-equidistribution). The first strand applies Noether’s theorem at the level of attractor dynamics, showing that \(T^2\) alone admits two independent commuting \(S^1\) actions generating two independent conserved quantities without collapse or degeneracy. The second strand employs bilateral Laplace-domain analysis (with Koopman resolvent confirmation), proving that only the quasi-periodic flow on \(T^2\) with irrational frequency ratio places all poles of any smooth observable on the imaginary axis in a manner simultaneously satisfying C1–C5′. The third strand demonstrates the same spectral structure via Fourier analysis on the torus, establishing that the commuting eigenvalue lattice \(m\omega_1 + n\omega_2\) is a geometric invariant independent of normalization convention. The convergence of these topologically, algebraically-dynamical, and spectrally disjoint routes constitutes a necessity proof by corroboration: \(T^2\) is not merely adequate but the unique minimal manifold satisfying the full constraint set under every analytical framework. A phenomenological corollary identifies the two commuting invariants with the distinct yet non-collapsing focal and contextual streams of lived awareness. -/- Keywords: consciousness, dynamical systems, torus, Noether’s theorem, Laplace transform, Fourier analysis, structural minimality, self-reference.

items.title: A Sacred Ambition: Mosaic Symbolism of Spiritual Ascent in Gregory of Nyssa and Giovanni Pico Della Mirandola.
items.abstract: This study offers a comparative analysis of the symbolism of the soul’s ascent in Gregory of Nyssa’s De vita Moysis and Giovanni Pico della Mirandola’s Oratio. Rather than attempting to establish a linear or exclusive dependence, it focuses on a series of Mosaic themes that articulate a dynamic conception of perfection in both authors. Beginning with Moses as a paradigm of virtuous life, the paper examines the shared anthropology of desire underlying Nyssen’s notion of unending progress and Pico’s sacra ambitio. It then traces the ordered sequence of symbols as it develops in Gregory’s treatise: light and darkness, the mountain of the knowledge of God, Jacob’s ladder, the tabernacle, the eagle, death as consummation, and divine friendship. Through the interplay of these symbols both thinkers configure spiritual growth as an ever-deepening participation in divine unity and truth. Particular attention is given to integration of the classical disciplines of the ancient philosophical curriculum within the Mosaic itinerary, as well as to the conception of truth as gradually apprehensible but ultimately inexhaustible. The paper concludes by pondering the results of the comparative study and reflecting on Pico’s way of assimilating the wide variety of sources in his project of philosophical concord.

items.title: 物化：物如何被生成——从因应到对象的形成机制.
items.abstract: 本文提出“物化”这一概念，用以讨论“物如何被生成”的问题。 -/- 不同于将物视为外在既存实体的观点，本文认为，所谓“物”，并非直接存在之对象，而是由因应过程在观者结构中被取定的结果。观者在因应链条中截取“原有”，并以此作为物之起点，而无法追及其更前之生成过程。 -/- 在此基础上，本文指出： 物并非其自身之实，而是信号在系统中留下的迹应及其情征。物之形成依赖于载流与场的因应（如电磁、离子等），信号经由沉积结构被记录与约束，从而构成可被观者识别的对象。 -/- 进一步地，本文区分三种“物化”机制： 一是“应化”，即因应过程本身生成对象； 二是“外化”，即内部意象被投射为外在存在； 三是“在化”，即以自身宿体为在场之物，从而形成物我结构。 -/- 其中，外化构成在化的基础，三者共同构成物之生成机制。 -/- 本文的核心观点在于： 物不是被发现的，而是被生成的；对象不是世界的起点，而是生成链条中的阶段性结果。该框架试图在物理过程、认知结构与对象形成之间建立联系，为理解“物如何出现”提供一种生成视角。 -/- .

items.title: 一般式：认知系统如何生成稳定——最小认知结构的统一模型.
items.abstract: 本文提出一个关于认知系统的总命题：人所感知的“稳定世界”并不是外部世界的先验属性，而是有限资源下、能够跨时间学习并服务于行动的系统，在运行过程中必然生成的结构结果。 -/- 文章从一个基本问题出发：若输入世界本质上是连续流变的，认知系统为何会在其中识别出“物”这样相对稳定的结构？为回答这一问题，本文构建了一套最小认知结构模型，并将其压缩为一般式： -/- System = (F, R, C, U, L) -/- 其中，连续输入流 F 在有限资源条件下被压缩为内部状态 R，经由压缩、更新、复用与高层归并，逐步形成稳定结构。 -/- 本文论证：只要系统同时满足连续输入、有限处理能力与行动需求，就必然发生两件事：其一，输入被压缩；其二，内部状态被复用。由此，稳定不再被理解为世界本身固有的性质，而被重新界定为认知系统在约束下形成的内部状态塌缩与复用结果。 -/- 在此基础上，本文进一步区分三层稳定结构：塌缩稳定、模式稳定与对象稳定，并指出对象并非认知的起点，而是状态压缩与复用在高层的结果。文章同时讨论了若干可能的反例，包括纯反射系统、无对象学习系统与完全流式学习系统，并据此收紧理论边界：真正不可避免的并不是“世界稳定感”，而是“可复用的内部状态压缩”。 -/- 本文的核心贡献在于：不是先定义认知，再解释稳定；而是先解释稳定何以出现，再反推出认知系统的最小范式。由此，本文试图为认知科学、人工智能与复杂系统研究提供一个统一的底层结构入口。.

items.title: 息化：世界如何被生成——从物理载体到信息结构的统一机制.
items.abstract: 本文提出“息化”这一概念，用以描述“宿主如何被化为息界”的过程，即世界生成的基本机制。 -/- 本文认为，世界并非既成之物，而是在载流与场的因应过程中逐步生成：物理载体中的相互作用产生信号，信号在结构中沉积并形成稳定约束，这些约束进一步构成生成机制，从而使信息结构与世界得以出现。 -/- 在该框架中，生成的不是单一信息或表征，而是完整的“息界”。息界可区分为三类： 一是自发演化的世界结构，二是认知形成的意象结构，三是规则与约束构成的定界系统。认知主体始终处于息界之内，对世界的把握依赖于生成结构，而非直接接触外在实体。 -/- 进一步地，本文提出一条生成链： 信号变化 → 结构沉积 → 生成机制 → 信息结构 并指出这一机制在不同系统中具有不同来源：在生物系统中表现为自组织结构，在人工系统中表现为人为设定的计算结构，在物理系统中表现为约束与相互作用对结构生成的限制。 -/- 本文的核心观点在于： 世界、认知与计算并非彼此独立，而是统一于同一生成机制之中。通过研究“息化”，可以从生成角度理解信息、结构与现实之间的关系，并为跨越不同系统（物理、神经、人工）的统一理论提供基础。.

items.title: When Syntax Is Asked to Bear Too Much: The Frege–Geach Problem and the Limits of Linguistic Invariance.
items.abstract: The Frege-Geach problem is widely taken to expose a fundamental weakness in expressivist and non-cognitivist accounts of moral language. If moral predicates do not contribute stable truth-conditional content, it is unclear how they can function coherently in embedded contexts such as conditionals, negations, and disjunctions. This paper argues that the force of the problem depends on an overextended demand: that natural language must preserve invariant semantic contribution across unrestricted logical embedding. That demand, I suggest, reflects a projection of formal-logical ideals onto ordinary discourse rather than a neutral criterion of semantic adequacy. Drawing on the Language Insufficiency Hypothesis, I distinguish between Invariant, Contestable, and Fluid expressions, and argue that moral predicates occupy an intermediate position: stable enough to support disagreement, criticism, and deliberation, yet insufficiently invariant to preserve all aspects of their function under formal manipulation. What Frege-Geach reveals, on this view, is not a defect in moral language but a redistribution of semantic roles under syntactic stress. The problem persists because metaethics continues to treat compositional invariance as a universal requirement rather than a local achievement of formal regimentation.

items.title: The Architecture of Encounter: A Mediated Encounter Ontology.
items.abstract: The Architecture of Encounter advances a relational ontology in which encounter-events, rather than substances, are ontologically primary. Extending the Mediated Encounter Ontology of the World (MEOW), it argues that the mind-world split, substance ontology, and related philosophical dualisms are products of inherited conceptual architecture rather than necessary features of reality. The book develops an alternative framework in which mediation is constitutive, constraint secures realism without unmediated access, and subjects and objects emerge as scale-dependent stabilisations within structured interaction.
