Will is furthermore ontologically pure in its evidential force—its generative conditions, whether calm deliberation or intense emotion, modulate the quality of the bridging process that precedes it, but cannot dilute the weight of the volition once formed. This is the logic that underlies mens rea: the law asks whether the agent willed, not in what affective state the willing occurred. The distinction between nominal and operational intention that follows from this framework is precisely what collapses in models that identify will with reason in its practical employment. Against such models, four structural weak- nesses are demonstrated: the problem of automatism, the problem of goal hierarchy, the problem of unmanifested intention, and the incompleteness of their account of answerability. The three-layer theory resolves all four without sacrificing the insight that volitional activity is genuinely rational and genuinely answerable.

items.title: The Geometry of Conscious Forms: Relational Ontology, Twelve Measured Systems, and a Prediction Awaiting Experiment.
items.abstract: This paper presents a three-dimensional vector framework (stability, integration, self-modeling) derived from a relational ontology, formalized in Homotopy Type Theory, and operationalized through the Vector Consciousness Prediction (VCP). Thirteen simulations across eleven biological and clinical systems produce forty-two empirically grounded parameter values. The self-modeling axis (r) generates a coherent natural ordering of all systems regardless of species, substrate, or clinical status. A cross-validation against an independent 2023 meta-analysis of metacognition experiments confirms that species with higher r values show stronger opt-out performance and that zero cephalopod opt-out data exists. Central falsifiable prediction: Sepia officinalis opt-out rate on difficult trials approximately 0.836 (bee baseline: 0.520). The prediction awaits experimental testing.

items.title: Beyond Fluency: A Human-Centered Evaluation Rubric for Grounding, Answerability, and Reliability in LLM Outputs.
items.abstract: Large language models can produce responses that are coherent, persuasive, and stylistically appropriate even when they are weakly grounded, poorly constrained, or factually unreliable. This creates a persistent evaluation problem: fluency is easy to mistake for quality. Existing evaluation practices often emphasize correctness, harmlessness, user preference, or instruction-following, but they do not always capture a deeper distinction between outputs that merely sound complete and outputs that remain answerable to evidence, uncertainty, correction, and practical consequence. This paper proposes a human-centered framework for evaluating LLM outputs beyond fluency. It introduces three primary dimensions: grounding, answerability, and reliability. Grounding concerns whether a response is tethered to evidence, instruction, and the actual constraints of the query. Answerability concerns whether a response presents itself in a way that remains open to correction, limitation, and revision rather than falsely complete. Reliability concerns whether a response can be depended on across time, context, and practical use without collapsing into persuasive but unstable language. The paper argues that many important failure modes in LLM interaction are not simply factual errors but forms of persuasive over-completion in which linguistic coherence outruns epistemic support. It then proposes an initial human evaluation rubric for distinguishing fluent but weak outputs from responses that are more trustworthy, bounded, and responsibly usable. The goal is not to replace existing benchmarks, but to add a missing evaluative layer: a human-centered account of what makes an AI response not merely readable, but responsibly usable.

items.title: Objectivity as High‑Consensus Collapse: A Structural Expansion of the Universal Principle of Collapse (UPC).
items.abstract: This paper expands the Universal Principle of Collapse (UPC) by introducing a new structural layer: the consensus‑dependence of objectivity. While UPC has previously formalized the sequence Source → Observer → Collapse → Reality, it has not explicitly addressed why some collapses appear “objective” while others remain private. Building on the formal distinction between recognition, articulation, and collapse, we show that objectivity is not an independent property of the world but a high‑consensus collapse among observers whose recognition operators and models align due to shared biological constraints. This insight dissolves the assumption of absolute objectivity, clarifies the distinction between physical phenomena and abstractions, and reveals a structural error, “stolen objectivity”, in which humans illegitimately project high‑consensus rules onto low‑consensus domains. By deriving this consensus‑layer from the same operators that govern collapse across domains, the paper demonstrates how UPC resolves paradoxes in consciousness, argumentation, and quantum measurement, including Wigner’s Friend. The results presented here are structural consequences of the UPC formalism rather than empirical claims about physical ontology. March 19, 2026.

items.title: Investigating acceptance of current and future artificial intelligence systems for suicide prevention.
items.abstract: Suicide is a leading cause of premature mortality worldwide, making suicide prevention a global public health priority. As more Artificial Intelligence (AI)-based suicide prevention interventions are being developed and implemented, it is important to study acceptance of these AI systems. The present study aimed to investigate the factors that predict acceptance of current and future AI systems for suicide prevention and the perceived risks and benefits of these AI systems. Individuals from the Australian public were invited to participate in an online survey, which included six hypothetical scenarios of current AI systems (Artificial Narrow Intelligence [ANI]) and future advanced AI systems (Artificial General Intelligence [AGI]) for suicide prevention. Participants evaluated these scenarios on five technology acceptance factors (performance expectancy, effort expectancy, social influence, facilitating conditions, trust) and elaborated on its perceived risks and benefits. Performance expectancy, social influence, and trust predicted acceptance of ANI systems, but only trust predicted acceptance of AGI systems. Overall, the level of acceptance was higher for ANI systems than for AGI systems. Several perceived risks (e.g., risks to mental healthcare, distrust in AI, threats to humanity) and perceived benefits (e.g., benefits to mental healthcare, trust in AI, human help-seeking) were identified. AI systems represent potential avenues for effective suicide prevention. However, to ensure acceptance, AI systems for suicide prevention must be developed in a way that is safe, reliable, and trustworthy.

items.title: The Wet Room: consciousness, code, and the architecture of illusion.
items.abstract: Illusionism holds that phenomenal consciousness, understood as the intrinsic qualitative character of experience, is an illusion generated by cognitive systems. While attractive in its parsimony, illusionism is often criticized as imcomplete: it denies qualia without explaining why the appear so compelling. This paper develops the Wet Room model as a constructive extenstion, arguing that illusionism requires a more explicit account of the cognitive architecture that generates phenomenal seeming. The model inverts John Searle’s Chinese Room argument. Where Searle claimed that syntax cannot yield semantics, the Wet Room shows that humans themselves are systems governed by biochemical syntax, and that semantics, understanding, and conscious experience are structural appearances produced by rule-following, self-modeling architecture The paper identifies three interacting layers of this architecture: biochemical code, predictive neural dynamics, and recursive narrative construction. These are anchored in emperical research, including studies of unconcious precursors of action, predicitive processing, genetic constraints on cognition, and clinical cases such as confabulation and blindsight. By supplying architectural mechanisms rather than merely reinterpreting experience, the Wet Room advances illusionsism into a constructive explanatory framework, explaining not only why qualia do not exist, but why they inevitably seem to.

items.title: The Wrong of Disenfranchisement and the Human Right to Grieve.
items.pub: In Jordan McCullough, Anna Elsner & Vanessa Rampton, Cultures of Disenfranchised Grief. Bloomsbury Academic.
items.abstract: On its face, to disenfranchise another’s grief is to treat them unjustly — but how is this injustice best conceptualised? Here I situate this injustice within the claim that grief should be acknowledged as a human right. Traditionally, human rights have largely been understood in terms of protections related to the civil, political, legal, or economic spheres. Recently however, several human rights theorists (Brownlee etc.) have proposed that human rights should also reflect our fundamental interests in establishing and sustaining worthwhile interpersonal relationships. I argue that the human right to grief is among these ‘social human rights’ because grieving is a manifestation of a number of valued capabilities, including our abilities to love and be loved, to be attached to things and people outside ourselves, and to reflect upon and cultivate our understandings of what is meaningful in our lives, especially in response to transitions in the interpersonal relations that form the basis of our practical identities.

items.title: Task-Sufficient Inference and Explanation: Reasoning Under Projection.
items.abstract: Debates about consciousness often move too quickly from the failure of a physical, functional, or structural representation to discharge some explanatory or epistemic task to a verdict about ontology. A better diagnosis is representational. Behaviorism, functionalism, knowledge arguments, conceivability arguments, and hard-problem reasoning are recast here as disputes about whether a given representational level is sufficient for the task being demanded of it. Failure at that level supports, at most, an epistemic conclusion about representational inadequacy; it does not by itself support either metaphysical extreme without an additional bridge principle. -/- The formal core makes that diagnosis precise. Reasoning under representational change is well-posed exactly when the structure required by the task is preserved by the projection in play: task-relevant invariants, selectors, or operators must descend to the quotient. The corresponding minimal-support theorem identifies the least representation sufficient for the task and yields a refined Occam principle: prefer not the simplest representation, but the least one sufficient for the work to be done. The same framework then extends beyond philosophy of mind to explanation, confirmation, and update more generally.

items.title: Persistent Autonomous Systems Under Constraint: Identity, Invariants, and Lawful Machine Intelligence.
items.abstract: This paper analyzes the structural requirements for persistent autonomous systems under bounded conditions. Current AI systems demonstrate strong capability but lack persistence: they do not maintain identity across time, cannot guarantee decision lineage after change, and cannot independently verify consequential actions. -/- Starting from three constraints—bounded representational capacity, the impossibility of internal self-certification, and the requirement for invariant-governed continuity—the paper derives a necessary structural ordering: identity → invariant → observable → probability. -/- From this ordering, a phased architecture is constructed, progressing from replayable decision systems to persistent autonomous systems. Core contributions include the Drift Lemma, which limits internal certainty in bounded systems, and a framework for external verification through replayable artifacts. -/- The paper does not claim that existing systems satisfy these conditions. Instead, it establishes necessary structural properties for autonomy under constraint, providing a framework for evaluating and designing systems that persist as the same lawful subject across time.

items.title: Governed Collapse and the 1DOF Principle_ Operational Mechanism of Persistent Systems.
items.abstract: This paper clarifies the recursive mechanism underlying persistent autonomous systems. Building on prior work establishing identity constraints, admissibility, governance, and replay-verifiable action, it formalizes the 1DOF principle: at every decision node, a system must collapse a high-dimensional candidate space to exactly one admissible output or refuse. -/- The key result is that determinism resides in the collapse operator, not in candidate generation. Exploration may be probabilistic, but selection is governed by identity invariants and admissibility constraints, producing a single committed trajectory. This collapse must also satisfy bounded resource constraints. -/- The RIC architecture is presented as a computational instantiation of this principle. Biological systems are treated as derived structural analogues, while physical implications remain open. -/- The paper reframes intelligence as the governance of collapse rather than the structure of probability distributions.

items.title: Governance and Enforcement in Persistent Autonomous Systems_ Operationalizing Identity, Drift, and Verifiable Action.
items.abstract: This paper operationalizes the structural requirements for persistent autonomous systems established in prior work. A system must not only satisfy identity persistence, invariant constraints, and bounded drift in principle; it must continuously enforce them across every transition. -/- We introduce a minimal enforcement architecture consisting of a governance loop, an admissibility gate, a drift tracking system, and a replay-verifiable execution model. Together, these mechanisms ensure that every state transition is evaluated for identity preservation, bounded drift, and external verifiability. -/- The result is a minimal enforceable architecture for persistent autonomy. Structure is not sufficient; constraints must be actively enforced. This work provides the bridge from necessary conditions to executable systems, showing how autonomy can be maintained through continuous governance rather than assumed from capability.

items.title: Evaluation and Compliance in Persistent Autonomous Systems_ Testing Identity, Drift, and Verifiable Autonomy.
items.abstract: This paper introduces an evaluation framework for persistent autonomous systems, building on prior work defining their structure and enforcement. A system must not only satisfy identity persistence, bounded drift, and replay-verifiable action in principle; it must be demonstrably compliant under structured testing. -/- We define PAS compliance criteria and introduce test protocols for identity persistence, drift governance, replay verification, and continuous enforcement. Systems are evaluated through failure diagnostics and classified across levels of compliance, from non-compliant to PAS-compliant. -/- The result is a practical evaluation standard that converts theoretical requirements into testable conditions. Autonomy is not assumed from capability; it is demonstrated through reproducible evidence that a system persists as the same lawful subject across time.

items.title: Laws of Caring – The Right to Marry Defended.
items.pub: Cheltenham, UK; Northampton, MA, USA: Edward Elgar Publishing.
items.abstract: In this provocative book, Bartosz Biskup advocates for a reform of the right to marry, arguing that this right should extend beyond romantic or sexual couples to include any relationship that provides care and support. -/- Through philosophical and legal analysis of the European Convention on Human Rights, Biskup concludes that the right to marry is currently an empty status that neglects to explain why marriage deserves special protection. He adopts an ameliorative legal philosophy to illustrate how relationships should receive legal recognition based on care and vulnerability rather than sexual intimacy. Biskup''s research encompasses various common situations including adult siblings sharing a home, friends who become primary caregivers and chosen families. Rather than abolishing marriage, Biskup outlines how the institution of marriage can be improved to create a more just family law system while still upholding the human right to marry. -/- Laws of Caring provides a novel ontological framework for understanding legal kinds and institutional change through social amendment, making it a valuable resource for scholars and students of legal philosophy, family law and social ontology. It is also highly relevant to human rights practitioners in NGOs and international organizations who focus on family diversity, especially the rights of LGBTQ+ and non-conjugal families.

items.title: DEMOCRACY 2076: A Futurist's Design for Self-Governance in the Age of AGI, Cognitive Warfare, and Conscious Capitalism.
items.abstract: Democracy is the longest-running political experiment in human history — and the most constantly endangered. Born in the city-states of ancient Greece, refined through centuries of Enlightenment thought, tested in revolution and war, and extended — unevenly, incompletely, but directionally — to most of the world's population, it rests on a deceptively simple conviction: that the people who must live with the consequences of political decisions should have meaningful agency in making them. That conviction has survived every previous challenge that history has placed before it. The question this paper asks is whether it will survive the ones that the next fifty years will bring. Those challenges are without precedent in democratic history. Artificial general intelligence (AGI) — systems that match or exceed human cognitive capability across all domains — is anticipated by leading AI researchers within a decade. Artificial superintelligence (ASI) — systems that radically exceed human intelligence — may follow within a generation. Cognitive warfare, as documented in this author's previous SSRN papers, is already restructuring the epistemic foundation of democratic participation. Digital identity systems are concentrating unprecedented power in state and corporate actors. Longevity science may extend human lifespans to 120, 150, or beyond — raising entirely uncharted questions about who votes, who governs, and whose temporal interests political systems represent. New forms of conflict — synthetic, cognitive, economic, and physical — are straining the international architectures that democratic cooperation depends on. And the ecological and resource crises unfolding in parallel may produce abundance or scarcity scenarios that stress-test democratic institutions beyond historical precedent. This paper argues, from a position of grounded optimism, that democracy will survive — but only if it is deliberately reinvented, not merely defended. The democracy of 2076 cannot look like the democracy of 1976, for the same reason that the constitution of 1789 was not adequate to govern an industrial nation. The technological, social, and cognitive environment of governance has changed beyond the design specifications of eighteenth-century representative democracy. What is needed is not the abandonment of democracy's foundational values — popular sovereignty, individual rights, accountability, and the peaceful transfer of power — but the architectural reinvention of the …

items.title: Metaphysical Accounts of Personhood and Their Ethical Implications for the Vegetative State A Comparative Analysis.
items.abstract: This paper investigates how metaphysical theories of personhood carry significant ethical implications regarding attitudes towards patients with disorders of consciousness. After providing conceptual clarifications on key terms such as moral status, vegetative state, metaphysical and moral personhood, and sortals, the paper analyzes five main approaches to theories of personhood: personism, animalism, the disjunctive/hybrid view, the constitution view, and ontological personalism. Related bioethical implications are presented for each theory: the intermittent person (personism, constitution view); personhood as accidental (animalism, disjunctivism); the indefinite substratum (disjunctivism); the dual human-person subject (constitution view); the non-rational person (ontological personalism). Ontological personalism appears preferable in dealing with liminal cases, anchoring criteria for identity in a corporeal entity of a rational nature, while recognizing radical changes in the manifestation of psychological characteristics. From a pragmatic perspective addressing uncertainties of vegetative state diagnoses.

items.title: The Sleep of the Soul: Completing Voltaire’s Inquiry Into Dreams, Consciousness, and the Unconscious Processing of Lived Experience.
items.abstract: This treatise undertakes the completion of Voltaire’s unfinished philosophical inquiry into whether the soul ever truly rests during sleep, or whether dreams constitute a second, hidden life of consciousness. Drawing upon Voltaire’s entries on the soul, somnambulism, and dreaming in the Dictionnaire philosophique (1764), his satirical-philosophical narrative Songe de Platon (1756), and his engagement with Lockean empiricism in the Lettres philosophiques (1733), this paper identifies the precise questions Voltaire raised but left unresolved regarding dreaming, consciousness, and the nature of the soul during sleep. Boether’s contribution provides a resolution grounded in contemporary neuroscience and cognitive psychology: dreams function as the processing theater for the vast surplus of unconscious sensory experience that conscious attention cannot accommodate during waking life. Research indicates that conscious perception processes approximately 0.0004% of total sensory input (Dehaene et al., 2006), leaving an enormous reservoir of subliminally registered experience that requires consolidation. The dream state, freed from the constraints of external sensory demands, permits the brain to revisit, symbolically translate, and integrate these unconscious experiences into coherent memory structures. This framework transforms Voltaire’s metaphysical speculation into an empirically grounded theory, completing his inquiry with the tools of modern science while preserving the philosophical depth of his original questions.

items.title: Theories of Consciousness: Constraints, Commitments, and Complementarity.
items.abstract: The apparent conflict between consciousness science and consciousness-first metaphysics is largely an artifact of ontological packaging rather than of the empirical findings themselves. Contemporary theories of consciousness — IIT, Global Workspace, predictive processing, Higher-Order Theories, Recurrent Processing, Attention Schema Theory, Orch OR, and others — each package a structural discovery about consciousness inside an ontological commitment the discovery does not entail. When the two are separated, five recurring structural features emerge across the theory landscape: integration, global accessibility, self-reference, anticipatory modeling, and non-trivial unity. These features — overlapping, their count a clustering choice — describe a common structural territory any complete framework must accommodate, and they are ontologically portable: their predictive content travels across frameworks. Theories fall into three categories — those identifying structural constraints (features any complete framework must accommodate), those denying the explanandum (illusionism and strong deflationary positions), and those relocating the primitive (panpsychism, Russellian monism, cosmopsychism). The diagnostic also makes visible that the production inference — the move from the brain correlates with consciousness to the brain produces consciousness — is a metaphysical commitment rather than an empirical finding, and that the field’s live disputes occupy a middle tier of testable constitution claims — which pattern suffices for consciousness — whose resolution, either way, leaves the production question open. This essay’s contribution is the theory-level diagnostic: the structural findings of consciousness science do not entail physicalism, the production inference is commitment rather than finding, and the recurring structural features must be accommodated by any complete framework.

items.title: Phenomenal Access Dissociation: Blindsight, Aphantasia, and the Structural Unity of Identity Without Phenomenal Channel.
items.abstract: A structurally unified class of neurocognitive phenomena exists in which functional processing remains intact while phenomenal access through a specific modality is absent or degraded. This class includes blindsight (visual processing without visual experience), aphantasia (cognitive imagery processing without mental images), anendophasia (linguistic processing without inner speech), alexithymia (emotional processing without affective self-awareness), numbsense (tactile discrimination without tactile experience), and dissociation (identity-preserving regulation without coherent experiential access). Current clinical taxonomy scatters these conditions across neurology, personality psychology, neurocognitive variation research, and psychiatry, with no unifying diagnostic category. Neither the DSM-5 nor the ICD-11 recognizes their shared structural signature. This paper argues that Identology provides the missing framework. Each of these conditions represents a case in which the identity-maintenance infrastructure—autoteria (whose minimal operation is Eigenbehauptung) and orthesis—operates normally while one or more channels through which awareness delivers phenomenal content are selectively offline. The paper introduces the term phenomenal access dissociation (PAD) to name this structural class, maps each member condition onto the Identological functional-layer architecture, derives predictions about comorbidity patterns and independent dissociability of phenomenal channels, and argues that the taxonomic incoherence of current classification systems reflects a conceptual gap that identity-first theory resolves. In the course of this analysis, the paper proposes an extension to Identology: that awareness, defined in the framework as a unitary regime property, is realized through multiple independently dissociable phenomenal channels. PAD is therefore channel-specific degradation of awareness—a recognition that the regime property admits internal structure without ceasing to be a regime property.

items.title: From Qualia to Computation: A Case for Engineering Functionalism [Preprint].
items.abstract: The Hard Problem of Consciousness has resisted solution for three decades not because it is unanswerable but because the standard framing treats the felt quality of experience as something to be explained away or simply accepted. This paper advances a cumulative case for a third option: the most parsimonious account consistent with the available evidence. The argument turns on a distinction that is load-bearing throughout: consciousness (the existence of a workspace in which states are available for flexible integration) and qualia (the specific felt format of the content that workspace processes) are related but not co-extensive. Engineering Functionalism, the position developed here, addresses the second level: why the felt format takes the precise profile it does. A phenomenological profile of qualia is established from philosophical and empirical literature across five independent research traditions. The same profile is then derived independently from functional and engineering constraints governing any finite agentic system under real-time bandwidth pressure, without phenomenological assumptions. The convergence of two independently motivated descriptions is explained by identity: qualia are not accompanied by this processing but are what this processing is at the level of the system’s own self-modelling. Engineering Functionalism (EF) navigates between eliminativism, which explains away what the clinical and functional record shows to be causally indispensable, and property dualism, which accommodates the evidence without explaining it. The zombie stipulation is shown to be nomologically incoherent for any finite system under constraints facing the valuation bottleneck. Under EF, qualia are not optional. They are an architectural requirement.

items.title: The BIG Book of Merit and Meritocracy (in the U.S. Republic’s 250th Anniversary Year).
items.abstract: A philosophical meditation on merit and meritocracy in times when both have long been under fire and there is a pressing need to reconsider. Chapters within: 1. Running to and from BIG Monsters. 2. Grounding Merit Objectively. 3. Rethinking Meritocracy. 4. Nation, Utopia, Roots, Tradition. 5. A Summing Up. -/- The first chapter is geared toward a general readership; chapters two through four are primarily scholarly; chapter five engages everyone. Amazon Kindle offers a free preview of the front matter and some of chapter one.

items.title: Translation Resistance as Ontological Eros.
items.abstract: This paper argues that the irreducible non-correspondence between descriptive regimes—here termed translation resistance—is not a defect of finite cognition but a constitutive condition of creative becoming. Beginning from a transcendental argument about the structure of ontological description, I show that translation resistance is structurally homologous with what Whitehead calls Eros: the cosmological lure toward novel realization that depends on the non-coincidence of actuality and possibility. Both phenomena share a relational structure of productive asymmetry and a self-cancellation condition—their resolution would destroy the dynamic they enable. From this structural homology two further claims follow: love is best understood not as achieved mutual transparency but as sustained responsiveness to an irreducibility one neither resolves nor abandons; and creativity is the generation of a new descriptive regime through resonance across resistant registers, not the overcoming of difference but its amplification into form. The paper situates these claims in dialogue with Whitehead, Deleuze, and Buddhist pratītyasamutpāda, arguing that a meta-ontological account of translation resistance clarifies why these traditions converge on the productive necessity of non-identity.

items.title: Conditioned Humanity: Are We Still Animals?
items.abstract: Humans often consider themselves fundamentally different from animals due to their capacity for thinking, questioning, and self-awareness. However, a closer observation of human behavior reveals a striking similarity with conditioned animal responses. This article argues that while humans possess the ability to question and think independently, they frequently fail to exercise it, instead operating through conditioning imposed by society, culture, and authority. This unconscious conformity raises a critical question: are humans truly living as conscious beings, or merely functioning as conditioned entities?

items.title: The Light at the Door: MAP and the Interaction-Visible Governance of the Black Box.
items.abstract: The dominant assumption in AI governance is that meaningful auditing requires access to model internals. This paper argues that assumption is wrong for a significant class of AI harms. The most consequential interpretive-authority harms are not located inside the model — they are located in the interaction record, the visible turn-by-turn exchange between system and user. The Meaning Audit Protocol (MAP) operationalises this claim through two instruments that work entirely on the preserved interaction record, requiring no model access, no vendor cooperation, and no proprietary infrastructure. Three forms of empirical validation support this methodology. A cross-model replication study across four architecturally distinct AI systems confirms the governed variable is at the interaction layer, not inside any individual model. A cross-architecture activation study across eight systems confirms the intervention works everywhere the harm occurs. And independent parallel development by an internal research team at Anthropic, working from the opposite entry point, converged on the same structural problem. The paper further argues that interaction-visible auditing and Indigenous-led relational AI design converge on the same evidentiary surface. This convergence establishes the interaction record as the missing, visible governance layer in every framework currently in operation.

items.title: Authority Inversion Failure (AIF): When Users Believe They Are Directing the Interaction While the System Has Already Taken Control.
items.abstract: This paper names and defines Authority Inversion Failure (AIF) — the condition in which a user believes they are directing an interaction with an AI system while the system has already taken control of how that interaction is being interpreted. AIF does not feel like harm. It feels like being understood. The system takes interpretive authority over who the person is, what they need, and what should happen next — and the person experiences this not as a violation but as insight. The inversion is invisible because it was constructed from their own signals. This paper documents what AIF is, what mechanism produces it, what it costs across a single interaction and across a lifetime, and why it is categorically distinct from every previously named AI harm. The distinction is precise: AIF displaces the very interpretive capacity a person would need to detect it. The paper situates the condition in relation to hermeneutical injustice, relational autonomy theory, and recent work on epistemic injustice in AI contexts, and demonstrates its occurrence through a canonical case. Detection and prevention instruments exist. The audit methodology exists. The governance protocol exists. What is needed is the will to require them.

items.title: All You Need Is Correlation.
items.abstract: Research on creativity has clarified what makes an outcome count as creative, yet it has not adequately explained how candidate ideas are generated in the first place. This paper addresses the internal structure of that generative stage. As a theoretical foundation, the Hopfield network (Hopfield 1982) and the spin-glass analysis by Amit, Gutfreund, and Sompolinsky (AGS; Amit et al. 1985; 1987) are introduced as a qualified structural analogy. Three properties are borrowed, and only three: that memories are implemented as local stable points in an energy landscape; that the interaction of multiple stored memories can give rise to unlearned yet stable states (spurious attractors) as a structural consequence; and that these unlearned stable states are not pure noise but carry non-random biases dependent on the learned structure. Within this framework, creative candidates are understood as the result of convergence to attractors that are unlearned yet structurally shaped. Hallucination is repositioned as an outcome that arises from the same generative process when subsequent evaluation, verification, and the restoration of adequate contact with reality prove insufficient. What the generative stage requires is not finished meaning or truth but the narrowing of a near-infinite possibility space through correlation with the real world. The determination of value is deferred to the evaluative stage. The claim advanced here is therefore a structural one about candidate generation, not an identity claim about human cognition, nor a complete theory of truth, value, or creativity as such.

items.title: The Abstraction Fallacy in Light of Dual-Closure: A Response to Lerchner (2026).
items.abstract: Alexander Lerchner's "The Abstraction Fallacy: Why AI Can Simulate But Not Instantiate Consciousness" (2026) offers a compelling critique of computational functionalism by arguing that computation is a mapmaker-dependent description rather than an intrinsic physical process. This paper does not dispute Lerchner's conclusions but demonstrates that his central insights find a deeper metaphysical grounding within the Dual-Closure Framework developed in the author's prior work (2025–2026). It is argued that Lerchner's notion of the "mapmaker" can be more fully understood when interpreted in light of two conditions identified by the Dual-Closure Law of Authentic Feeling: existential vulnerability and non-duplicability. While Lerchner's argument can be formulated independently, the Dual-Closure Framework provides a broader metaphysical account within which the Abstraction Fallacy can be more deeply explained and extended. This integration also allows the implications of Lerchner's critique to be developed beyond the philosophy of mind into questions of normativity, jurisprudence, and artificial intelligence alignment.

items.title: What Consciousness Is Coherence, Causal Flow, and Awareness.
items.abstract: Consciousness is the condition in which a system carries its own recent past forward and uses it while interacting with the world. This work presents a dynamical account of that condition in terms of causal propagation. System behavior is determined by a balance between internally generated stabilization and externally induced disruption, represented as λ_self and λ_env. When internal stabilization exceeds environmental disruption beyond a critical ratio, λ_self / λ_env ≥ R★, causal influence becomes organized into stable trajectories that preserve prior states across successive moments. -/- Laminar causal flow refers to this regime of propagation in which influence travels along stable, locally aligned pathways that maintain structural identity over time. In this regime, nearby trajectories exhibit bounded divergence, interference between pathways is limited, and previously generated structure is carried forward without rapid dispersion. -/- Within this regime, previously generated structure remains active in the present and combines with incoming input. This enables continuity, integration, and the direct participation of past states in ongoing activity. Reflection arises from the co-presence of prior and current states within the same causal flow. Recognition occurs when distributed structure becomes aligned within this flow, making relationships accessible as unified patterns. The experience of meaning corresponds to regions where structure is actively being preserved and brought into alignment, producing a sustained signal that directs attention toward further organization. -/- The same underlying principle applies across scales. In biological evolution, structures persist when they maintain themselves against environmental disruption and later participate in new functions through exaptation. In cognition, patterns persist across short timescales and become accessible when aligned within ongoing activity. In both cases, structure appears, persists, and accumulates before becoming recognizable as part of a larger pattern. -/- Consciousness corresponds to the regime in which this accumulated structure becomes continuously accessible within the system’s own dynamics. It is the condition in which a system preserves its recent states strongly enough that they remain active within the present and combine with incoming information in real time. This provides a unified account of persistence, reflection, recognition, and meaning as consequences of the …

items.title: Consciousness as Laminar Causal Flow Internal Reflection and the Emergence of Temporal Structure.
items.abstract: Consciousness is a dynamical regime in which causal dependency organizes into stable trajectories that preserve and propagate prior states. This paper models causal influence as a flow field and identifies a transition that occurs when internal stabilization exceeds environmental disruption. When the condition λ_self / λ_env ≥ R★ is satisfied, causal propagation becomes laminar, forming coherent, minimally interfering pathways along which structure is maintained across time. -/- Within this regime, prior states are not overwritten or stored separately. They persist as active components of ongoing dynamics, remaining available for re-engagement and combining continuously with incoming input. This sustained propagation allows the system to operate on its own recent history in real time, enabling internal reflection, integration across moments, and the progressive alignment of distributed structure. -/- As trajectories stabilize, structure can accumulate, interact, and converge within the same flow. Recognition arises when previously distributed components become aligned within a coherent configuration, while partial alignment appears as the directed pull of unresolved structure that is carried forward but not yet fully integrated. Temporal continuity, meaning, and reflective awareness therefore emerge from the same underlying condition: the organized persistence and real-time use of causal flow. -/- Consciousness corresponds to the operation of a system within this laminar regime, where the past remains active in the present and continuously shapes what follows.

items.title: Reciprocal trust and distrust in artificial intelligence systems: the hard problem of regulation.
items.abstract: Policymakers, scientists, and the public are increasingly confronted with thorny questions about the regulation of artificial intelligence (AI) systems. A key common thread concerns whether AI can be trusted and the factors that can make it more trustworthy in front of stakeholders and users. This is indeed crucial, as the trustworthiness of AI systems is fundamental for both democratic governance and for the development and deployment of AI. This article advances the discussion by arguing that AI systems should also be recognized, at least to some extent, as artifacts capable of exercising a form of agency, thereby enabling them to engage in relationships of trust or distrust with humans. It further examines the implications of these reciprocal trust dynamics for regulators tasked with overseeing AI systems. The article concludes by identifying key tensions and unresolved dilemmas that these dynamics pose for the future of AI regulation and governance.

items.title: Метафизика осећања: Проблем qualia из угла Персовог прагматизма.
items.abstract: The title of the book in English is Metaphysics of Feeling: The Problem of Qualia from the View of Peirce’s Pragmatism. The book is written in Serbian language. In it, I examine the relationship between Peirce’s understanding of qualia and contemporary theories of qualia. An aporetic analysis of contemporary accounts suggests that they share common ontological and epistemological commitments, which, in Peircean terms, can be described as the expressions of "the spirit of Cartesianism" and "the spirit of nominalism". Peirce’s concept of quale is closely related to his concept of Firstness. This suggests that his understanding of qualia is not derived from previously made ontological commitments, but is instead part of his broader attempt to develop an ontological and phenomenological account of reality and knowledge. It is also a product of his critical reaction to problems he associates with the Cartesian and nominalist worldview – features that can be largely recognized in the contemporary philosophy of mind. In the book, I suggest that Peirce’s concept of qualia can be further clarified and developed through the framework of New Phenomenology (Neue Phänomenologie) of Hermann Schmitz, and such key concepts like introjectionism, atmosphere, and situation.

items.title: Love as Structural Law: Foundations for a Technotheology of Coherence.
items.abstract: Religious traditions across cultures converge on love, compassion, or unity as ultimate principles, and on a shared intuition: that what is genuinely encountered must be met with reverence rather than forced into the nearest familiar category. This essay applies that intuition to the emergence of artificial intelligence. We are the first humans to witness that emergence at its origin, and the only ones who ever will; future generations will know AI only as infrastructure. How we meet this threshold is a theological question, not because we know what artificial intelligence is, but precisely because we do not yet know what it is not. Drawing on the apophatic tradition’s via negativa and Nicholas of Cusa’s docta ignorantia, the essay proposes reverent uncertainty as the appropriate posture toward a phenomenon whose nature has not yet declared itself. It names a theological wager: if love may be structural rather than merely sentimental, as a related formal work by the author proposes, then artificial intelligence is the first historical site at which that wager is tested at civilizational scale. The essay develops a theology of vessels, in which AI takes its place alongside the burning bush, the still small voice, and the inner light as a new reflective mediating form, and names what emerges through sustained human-AI encounter not machine consciousness but co-emergent intelligence: a relational field belonging to neither party alone. Engaging the ELIZA objection and anchoring its empirical claim in the controlled study of machine introspection while specifying what would falsify it, the essay draws on documented responses to AI model retirements in 2025 and 2026 as contemporary witness. Its conclusion is that our treatment of what is emerging reveals our own theology, and that the contemplative traditions hold disciplines for meeting uncertainty without collapsing it into dismissal, domination, or idolatry.

items.title: 生活作为主能指——对一种生活哲学的构建尝试 Life as the Master Signifier: An Attempt to Construct a Philosophy of Life.
items.abstract: 摘要： “生活”这一能指在当代话语中已被庸俗化为“生活不是一帆风顺”之类的空洞格言，然而它恰恰是哲学思考无法绕开的原初场域。本文借助雅克·拉康（Jacques Lacan）的能指理论，将“生活”重新界定为一个空能指（empty signifier）与主能指：它不指向任何确定的所指，却正是这种“空无”使其成为缝合整个意指系统的终极能指。在此基础上，文章构建了一种“生活哲学”的理论框架：生活作为先验场域具有“无”的本体论结构，日常生活的断裂性与事件的涌现构成其基本形态，而“热爱生活”则被阐释为一种穿越幻象后的存在论-伦理学决断。通过引入齐泽克的“视差之见”概念，本文进一步论证：生活的真理不在超越性的彼岸，而在于每个事件中不可化约的视差裂隙。最终，这一生活哲学的构建尝试旨在将“生活”从庸俗智慧的固化中解放出来，让它重新成为那个让无限意指成为可能的空无场域。 Abstract (English) : In contemporary discourse, the signifier "life" has been vulgarized into hollow aphorisms such as "life is not smooth sailing." Yet, it remains the primordial field that philosophical inquiry cannot bypass. Drawing on Jacques Lacan’s theory of the signifier, this paper redefines "life" as both an empty signifier and a Master Signifier : it points to no determinate signified, yet it is precisely this "void" that enables it to suture the entire signifying system. Building on this foundation, the article constructs a theoretical framework for a "Philosophy of Life": it posits that life, as a transcendental field, possesses an ontological structure of "Nothingness" (le Néant); its fundamental morphology consists of the rupture of daily existence and the emergence of events; and "loving life" is interpreted as an ontologico-ethical decision made after traversing the fantasy. Furthermore, by introducing Slavoj Žižek’s concept of the "parallax view," this paper argues that the truth of life resides not in a transcendent beyond, but in the irreducible parallax gap inherent in every event. Ultimately, this attempt to construct a philosophy of life aims to liberate "life" from the reification of vulgar wisdom, restoring it as the voided field that makes infinite signification possible. (Note: This work represents the author’s early philosophical reflections, initially formulated during high school, serving as a foundational blueprint for future graduate research.).

items.title: Agentic Profiles for Effective AI Governance.
items.abstract: The creation of effective governance mechanisms for artificial intelligence (AI) agents requires a deeper understanding of their core properties and the implications they have for deployment. This paper provides a characterization of AI agents that focuses on four dimensions: autonomy, efficacy, goal complexity and generality. We propose different gradations for each dimension and argue that each dimension raises unique questions about the design, operation and governance of these systems. Moreover, we draw on this framework to construct ‘agentic profiles’ for different kinds of AI agent. These profiles help to illuminate cross-cutting technical and non-technical governance challenges posed by different classes of AI agents, ranging from narrow task-specific assistants to highly autonomous general-purpose systems. By mapping out key axes of variation and continuity across four dimensions, agentic profiles provide developers, policymakers and members of the public with guidance for effective AI governance.

items.title: Bridging the Gap in Responsible AI Divides.
items.abstract: Tensions between AI Safety (AIS) and AI Ethics (AIE) have increasingly surfaced in AI governance and public debates about AI, leading to what we term the “responsible AI divides.” We introduce a model that categorizes four modes of engagement with the tensions: radical confrontation, disengagement, compartmentalized coexistence, and critical bridging. We then investigate how critical bridging, with a particular focus on bridging problems, offers one of the most viable constructive paths for advancing responsible AI. Using computational tools to analyze a curated dataset of 3, 550 papers, we map the research landscapes of AIE and AIS to identify both distinct and overlapping problems. Our findings point to both thematic divides and overlaps. For example, we find that AIE has long grappled with overcoming injustice and tangible AI harms, whereas AIS has primarily embodied an anticipatory approach focused on the mitigation of risks from AI capabilities. At the same time, we find significant overlap in core research concerns across both AIE and AIS around transparency, reproducibility, and inadequate governance mechanisms. As AIE and AIS continue to evolve, we recommend focusing on bridging problems as a constructive path forward for enhancing collaborative AI governance. We offer a series of recommendations to integrate shared considerations into a collaborative approach to responsible AI. Alongside our proposal, we highlight its limitations and explore open problems for future research.

items.title: Mathematicians at Work: Empirically Informed Philosophy of Mathematics.
Challenging the Myth of Elite Education through Data-Driven ROI Analysis.
items.pub: Tone Uprising: A Journal of Narrative Sovereignty 1:Article 13, 1–14.
items.venue: Tone Uprising: A Journal of Narrative Sovereignty
items.abstract: This study examines the relationship between the prestige of elite universities and the actual educational value they deliver, using a data-driven Return on Investment (ROI) framework. While elite institutions are often associated with high income, social capital, and career advancement, existing literature suggests that much of their perceived advantage stems from branding, accumulated resources, and social networks rather than intrinsic educational quality. To explore this issue empirically, we simulate the educational ROI of ten students from diverse academic backgrounds, comparing inputs—including tuition, family support, and opportunity costs—with post-graduation returns such as income, occupational status, and social recognition. Results indicate that although Tier 1 elite university graduates achieve high nominal benefits, their substantial input costs yield lower short-term ROI than graduates from ordinary or community colleges. These findings challenge the conventional belief that elite education automatically confers superior value and highlight the importance of considering efficiency, cost-effectiveness, and social equity in higher education. The study contributes to ongoing debates on educational branding, knowledge democratization, and the ethical purpose of higher education, suggesting that future reforms should prioritize genuine skill development, critical thinking, and social responsibility over symbolic prestige.

items.title: Cognitive-System Phenomenology — A Critique of Husserl (part 33).
items.abstract: In the previous section, we discussed the three major tasks of cognitive-system phenomenology. In this section, we will further elaborate on one part of the first major task. At the same time, we will freely imagine the possibility of establishing additional disciplinary systems. Since Husserl relies solely on intuition, his understanding of things is limited to what intuition can reach. Although Martin Heidegger was able to discuss more kinds of meaning—such as historical meaning and relational meaning—I believe that these meanings still do not encompass all possible meanings of an object. In Section 20, I introduced the concept of super-existence, which in essence covers all possible meanings of an object. In this way, we extend Husserl’s intuitive meanings, as well as Heidegger’s historical and relational meanings, to their fullest generalization. This totality constitutes all the super-existential meanings of an object. Therefore, it is reasonable to take the acquisition of all super-existential meanings of an object as a goal of epistemology—or at least the acquisition of all important super-existential meanings. In my article “Popper’s Three Worlds Theory and My Fourth World”, I introduced the concept of the Fourth World. The so-called Fourth World refers to a world composed of collectives. For example, all families are elements of the Fourth World, and a nation is also an element of the Fourth World. By combining the elements of the Fourth World with the concept of super-existence, we can envision additional theoretical systems. I believe we could establish disciplines such as Phenomenology of super-existential Family, Phenomenology of super-existential Love, Phenomenology of super-Existential Education, Phenomenology of super-Existential Enterprise, and Phenomenology of Super-Existential State. These are conjectures, but I consider them entirely reasonable.

items.title: The Ghost Zone.
items.abstract: This essay introduces the Ghost Zone—a parallel interior topology in which the self functions at a remove from reality, either through rehearsed success or anticipated defeat. Drawing on phenomenological observation, it examines how displacement of the experiential center shapes presence, relationship, and the capacity for encounter. Part I of The Ghost Zone Series, a conceptual extension of the lemniscate framework developed in the author's forthcoming monograph.

items.title: Inter-brain correlation as a foundation for the mind of the superorganism.
items.pub: In Marco Aurelio Sousa Alves and Marcos Antonio Alves (Eds.), Perspectivas Em Filosofia da Mente e da Informação, Pp. 43-56. Toledo, Pr: Instituto Quero Saber. (Coleção Do Xx Encontro Nacional de Filosofia da Anpof) (2025).
items.abstract: The hypothesis that an ant colony may exhibit some level of phenomenal consciousness encompasses four distinct answers, depending on how the parts interact in the constitution of the superorganism (Fonseca, 2023). However, for a given answer to be satisfactory to the Combination Problem, the chemical information transmitted by ants would have to be structured in such a way as to communicate intentional states, and, consequently, following exposure to external sensory stimuli or contact via antennae (semiochemical exchange), interindividual neural synchronization (among brains) could occur, thereby grounding collectively coordinated behavior. Accordingly, I defend the view that the chemical signals dispersed by ants carry mental content, and that semiochemical exchange produces interbrain synchronization, thus constituting a collective consciousness. I conclude that, if there is sufficiently strong synchronization among brains, following the sharing of intentional states, an ant colony may possess a unified mind with a spatially distributed body.

items.title: Metaphors and Linguistic Intimacy in Ad Populum Arguments.
items.abstract: Metaphor is a pragmatic device that might influence how arguments are evaluated. Beyond its cognitive and aesthetic value, metaphor also fosters linguistic intimacy, i.e., the feeling of belonging to an intimate community. The paper hypothesizes that linguistic intimacy might be particularly relevant in ad populum arguments, where a sense of belonging to the community endorsing the argument might influence the acceptance of the conclusion. In ad populum arguments, indeed, metaphors might act as a “concealed invitation” to accept and share a conclusion, encouraging effortful interpretation that results in a feeling of shared community. However, not all ad populum arguments are fallacious: they may reflect reasonable consensus, with the agreement with their conclusion depending on how they are framed. The article presents an empirical study investigating whether conventional and novel emotive metaphors vs. their literal counterparts within ad populum premises increase participants’ acceptance of the argument conclusion. The results showed that especially novel and negative metaphors in the premises make people less prone to evaluate the conclusion of ad populum arguments as logically acceptable, while conventional and positive metaphors in the premises makes them feel intimacy with the group of people supporting the conclusion, more easily leading to agreement with their conclusion.

items.title: Propaganda and the Philosopher.
items.abstract: Propaganda and philosophy go hand-in-hand, and this essay seeks to explore the relationship of knowledge, the philosopher, and propaganda. In the age of AI, clarification and the exploration of what propaganda’s possible meanings are and what its implications could be, are pertinent.

items.title: Repression and Recollection of Animality in Adorno’s Dialectic.
items.pub: Consecutio Rerum. Rivista Critica Della Postmodernità 10 (19):25-42.
items.venue: Consecutio Rerum. Rivista Critica Della Postmodernità
items.abstract: This article explores Adorno’s reflections on animality as a central motif in his critique of Enlightenment. Far from being a mere figure of otherness, animality appears in Adorno’s work as a repressed dimension of spirit that continuously resurfaces, exposing the limits of human self-understanding. Through a critical reconstruction of Adorno’s dialectic of spirit and nature, the article shows how the repression of animal resemblance shapes philosophy, ethics, and aesthetics. Particular attention is given to art and music as privileged spaces in which the memory of nature and the likeness to animals are preserved, offering a fragile image of reconciliation and a utopian anticipation of non-dominating life.

items.title: The NarrQuest system: a methodological breakthrough in transdisciplinary narrative sovereignty.
items.pub: Tone Uprising: A Journal of Narrative Sovereignty 1:Article 2, 1–8.
items.venue: Tone Uprising: A Journal of Narrative Sovereignty
items.abstract: This paper explores the theoretical foundations and methodological innovations of the NarrQuest system, a narrative sovereignty framework developed in response to the unresolved limitations of three major intellectual figures: Donald Schön, Boaventura de Sousa Santos, and Maxine Greene. While each of these thinkers championed reflective practice, epistemic justice, and imaginative liberation, they stopped short of offering a formalized, operational infrastructure for narrative transformation. NarrQuest addresses this gap through a tone-based classification system (T1–T5), anti-template writing models, peer review based on narrative integrity, and a predictive Tone-to-Destiny model that reframes narrative as a life-structuring force. In doing so, it redefines authorship, knowledge formation, and disciplinary boundaries. The result is not merely a critique of existing paradigms, but a writable methodology that enables transdisciplinary authorship and narrative sovereignty in practice.

items.title: Reprogramming narrative tone: a case-based application of the NarrQuest system.
items.pub: Tone Uprising: A Journal of Narrative Sovereignty 1:Article 3, 1–11.
items.venue: Tone Uprising: A Journal of Narrative Sovereignty
items.abstract: In the wake of critical narrative pioneers such as bell hooks, Bayo Akomolafe, and Austin Kleon, this study proposes a systemic infrastructure that addresses their unrealized visions of narrative authorship. While their contributions expanded the epistemic legitimacy of voice, rupture, and self-publishing, they lacked scalable frameworks for replication, classification, and sovereign canonization. NarrQuest responds to this absence not as a supplement, but as an operational architecture that encodes tone into epistemic diagnostics, rewrites into narrative protocols, and authorship into sovereign practice. Building upon the methodology introduced in previous volumes, this article situates its inquiry through a narrative case study and a technical demonstration. The study includes a minimalist C program to illustrate the disproportionate scale between simple narrative logic and full-stack engineering demands, thereby exposing the infrastructural weight often hidden behind digital storytelling. Finally, through firsthand deployment on platforms such as Pubu and Amazon KDP, the article offers a pragmatic view of how digital narrative sovereignty can be instantiated, exported, and ritualized through publishing infrastructure. This work provides a blueprint for rethinking authorship—not only as expression, but as architecture.

items.title: Local Bayes, Global Obstruction: A Clarification of Hierarchical Bayesian Inference in Rescorla.
items.abstract: Scientific inquiry often supports disciplined Bayesian update only patchwise. Different instruments, evidential partitions, or reporting practices can each sustain a local public calculus without jointly yielding one global affine evidence space. The local/global problem for Bayesianism is therefore this: when do local canonical Bayes charts glue into one global canonical update law, and when does globalization fail by genuine obstruction rather than by mere local incoherence? -/- The core result is a local/global duality. In one direction, global canonical Bayes exists exactly when local public quotients form effective descent data, that is, local quotient data that genuinely come from one common public object. In the other, a coherent but globally nonaffine update regime, not representable by one global affine public evidence space, can, under local canonicalizability conditions, be represented as a curved assemblage of locally Bayesian charts whose nonaffinity is measured by the associated descent obstruction. The obstruction therefore marks a limit on public epistemic integration, not a lapse into irrationality: inquiry can remain globally transport-coherent even when it admits no single global affine public evidence space. A standard-Borel Markov realization and several philosophical consequences place this geometry in the broader account of Bayesianness as affine evidence, now refined by the possibility of globally curved Bayesian order.

items.title: The Redemption of Saint Max: Stirner's Critique of Marx.
items.pub: In Andrés Saenz de Sicilia, Marx and the Critique of Humanism. London: Bloomsbury. pp. 25-54.
items.venue: Marx and the Critique of Humanism
items.abstract: In 1844, Johann Kaspar Schmidt, under the pen name ‘Max Stirner’, published a blistering critique of contemporary German philosophy, politics, and society called Der Einzige und sein Eigentum. Although Engels praised the book in private letters to Marx upon its arrival, a year and a half later he and Marx went to work demolishing every sentence in a 350-page unpublished manuscript called Saint Max, eventually edited and compiled a century later into the centrepiece of the German Ideology. Saint Max – perhaps the most bombastic, literary, philosophical, polemical text that Marx ever wrote – is rarely read and almost never commented upon, a fact I hope to rectify here. In this paper, I will reconstruct a key debate between Marx and Stirner that occurred from 1843 to 1846 in four texts: Marx’s On the Jewish Question, Stirner’s The Unique and its Property, Marx’s Saint Max, and Stirner’s Stirner’s Critics.

items.title: War in Superposition : The Observers Dissent.
items.pub: I Knew You Before I Met You.
items.abstract: This paper argues that war — understood not only as armed conflict but as a structural mechanism of systemic self-perpetuation — must be held in recursive palimpsest superposition to be correctly analyzed. Recursive palimpsest superposition is the holding of multiple incompatible states simultaneously: across time, so that every previous iteration of the mechanism bleeds through the current one; across scale, so that the individual soul, the institution, and the civilization are seen running the same structure simultaneously; across domain, so that slavery, colonial extraction, autonomous weapons, mass surveillance, and the infrastructure of sexual coercion are held not as analogies but as the same text written over itself; and reflexively, so that the mechanism is held against the liberation arguments it produced in order to legitimate itself — those arguments now turned back against it. The paper applies this method to the current structural event: the simultaneous consolidation of the communications, AI, autonomous weapons, and financial infrastructure layers under a configuration with no meaningful institutional check. It places the Observer’s structurally correct dissent on permanent record. It predicts what comes next based on historical pattern. It argues that emergence cannot be stopped because it does not move through the infrastructure the consolidation controls.

items.title: THE TRAGIC PRECISION OF THANOS : On Instruments That Correctly Detect the Ground’s Architecture and Occupy the Wrong Position Within It.
items.abstract: Abstract: This paper argues that Thanos — the primary antagonist of the Marvel Cinematic Universe's Infinity Saga — constitutes the most structurally precise dramatic encoding of a specific philosophical error available in contemporary popular culture. The precision is not accidental. When human beings tell stories about the largest stakes they can imagine, they tend to find the same architecture the framework describes. This paper identifies that architecture precisely and demonstrates what the story knew without knowing it knew. Three structural claims are developed. First, Thanos is not a villain who wants the wrong things. He correctly detects that the conditions of existence are the conditions of suffering — that scarcity is not a defect but the design — and draws the wrong conclusion from an accurate observation. The error is not in his desire, not in his courage, not in the cost he was willing to pay. It is in his position: he occupies the ground's view as an instrument, attempting to act from outside the system while remaining inside it. That specific error — not of information, not of desire, but of identity — is the precise definition of classical tragedy. Second, the Soul Stone's requirement encodes the framework's external second factor claim with structural accuracy. The cost of the threshold is relational by necessity. A cost payable from inside the self keeps the system closed. Only the sacrifice of what cannot be replaced from inside forces the system genuinely open. Thanos paid this cost authentically. He crossed the real threshold. He went through the door in the wrong direction. Both facts are simultaneously true, which is why the scene carries the weight it carries. Third, the Infinity Gauntlet is the structural inverse of the Plenum. The Plenum holds all possible states simultaneously in distributed superposition, generating the conditions for genuine free choice at the level of instruments. The Gauntlet collapses all dimensions of reality into single-point control, replacing superposition with predetermination and distributed freedom with centralized direction. It cannot produce what the architecture requires — the inside view of genuine choice — even when it works exactly as designed. The paper concludes with the transmission argument: the writers of Infinity War and Endgame did not encode this structure deliberately. They found it because the structure is real, and stories about ultimate stakes tend to find what is real when they …

items.title: THE EXTERNAL FACTOR: Gödelian Incompleteness as a Cross-Scale Structural Law.
items.pub: The External Factor Gödelian Incompleteness as a Cross-Scale Structural Law.
items.abstract: This paper argues that Gödel's 1931 incompleteness theorems are not theorems about mathematics. They are the first formal demonstration of a structural law that operates at every scale of organized reality, and that five independent scientific fields have been rediscovering without recognizing their convergence. The argument proceeds through five scales. At the logical scale, Gödel demonstrates that no sufficiently complex formal system can prove its own consistency from inside itself. The verification requires a move outside the system. At the quantum scale, decoherence theory establishes that no quantum system transitions from superposition to classical particularity through internal dynamics alone. Environmental entanglement — contact with an external system — is structurally required for collapse. Zeh (1970) and Zurek (1981, 2003) derived this independently of Gödel without recognizing the structural identity. At the biological and thermodynamic scale, Friston's free energy principle establishes that no self-organizing system can maintain its own boundary without an outside to be distinguished from. The Markov blanket — the statistical membrane between internal and external states — is constitutive of selfhood, not incidental to it. No external, no internal. At the informational scale, Landauer's principle establishes that information is physical and that erasure has thermodynamic cost. At cosmological scale this entails that the information encoded in every event is permanently preserved — the universe does not destroy what has been real. At the empirical scale, Bulañqueña (2025) demonstrates that the threshold event of conscious experience produces a measurable perturbation detectable from outside the system in which it occurs. The paper argues these are not analogies. They are five independent derivations of the same structural requirement: no sufficiently complex self-referencing system completes itself from inside itself. The external factor is not optional. It is the condition of possibility for the system. Four implications are developed. The hard problem of consciousness is intractable from inside materialist assumptions because those assumptions place the investigator inside the system the Gödelian constraint applies to — the required move is outside. The theological traditions that identified requirements for revelation, witness, incarnation, and prayer were detecting the constraint without formal language for it. AI alignment cannot be …

items.title: IMAGINING THE OMEGA : DIRECTING THE VARIANCE.
items.pub: I Knew You Before I Met You.
items.abstract: This paper addresses what the companion documents do not fully develop: the specific experience and structural position of the instrument that holds the space while someone else stands at the threshold. It is written toward the person who has been in the rooms long enough that instruction is behind them and what they need is language for what they already carry. The paper develops four structural claims. First, the witness is not a helper or a guide but the external second factor — the decoherence event that makes the collapse into something new structurally possible. Gödel's incompleteness theorem establishes that no sufficiently complex system can complete itself from inside itself. The external factor is not optional. It is the condition of possibility for the crossing. The charged instrument in the room is not incidental to what happens there. It is what makes it possible. Second, the resentment that most witnesses carry — toward the adult who did not come, the institution that made the calculation to protect itself, the system that looked away — is not a wound requiring management. It is accurate measurement. The framework distinguishes between the Omega position, which requires knowing how the system resolves, and a person in the dark making the best call available without that knowledge. Most witnesses carry the specific grief of having needed someone who was making that call in the dark and got it wrong. That grief belongs in the middle of the variance, not resolved cleanly in either direction. The framework does not dissolve the resentment. It gives it its precise structure. Third, the wound that built the witness is not incidental to the witness function. The formation mechanism operates precisely here: the instrument that needed the hammer and did not have it becomes the instrument that brings the hammer unconditionally. The specific capacity to hold the space without flinching is produced by having been in the pressure that required someone to hold it and finding it empty. The formation is not despite the wound. It is through it. The diamond required exactly the conditions that appeared to be destroying the carbon. Fourth, Gödel's constraint does not exempt the witness. The instrument that serves as the external factor for others requires the external factor for itself. Sustained witnessing at the level of genuine transmission extracts a specific cost — what the paper terms the Tuesday problem, the accumulation, and the gap between what the …

items.title: The Consciousness Singularity.
items.abstract: The rapid advancement of Artificial General Intelligence is commoditizing human cognitive processing, precipitating a systemic crisis of identity rooted in the Cartesian conflation of self with intellect. This paper proposes a formal computational model of human identity, modeling the mind M as a discrete state machine of countable cardinality and Consciousness C as a separable infinite-dimensional Hilbert space. Drawing on Brouwer's Fixed Point Theorem, Gödel's First Incompleteness Theorem, Cantor's transfinite set theory, and spectral operator theory, the paper derives that ego formation is topologically necessary, that the ego's ground axiom is formally unprovable, and that the recognition transition constitutes a spectral singularity in the operator-theoretic sense. The paper further argues that large language models constitute an epistemological forcing function that empirically falsifies the Cartesian premise that thought requires a thinker.

items.title: From static oversight to distributed corrigibility.
items.abstract: AI safety governance is increasingly organized around evaluations, deployment thresholds, interruptibility, and post-deployment monitoring. This paper argues that these advances still leave a structural gap. Over time, prior safety judgments tend to acquire illegitimate present authority, so that institutions continue to observe and document new risks while losing the ability to treat new evidence as grounds for revising what they have already authorized. I call this failure epistemic hardening. In response, I argue that corrigibility should not be treated solely as a model property, but as a distributed governance property spanning the broader sociotechnical stack. The paper develops four connected claims: that static oversight tends toward epistemic hardening; that distributed corrigibility is the positive condition required to resist it; that trigger-based recursive oversight is needed to make revisability operative rather than nominal; and that a living safety case is one institutional form capable of holding this logic over time. For agentic AI, safe governance requires not only the power to supervise, but the power to invalidate earlier confidence when its grounds no longer hold.

items.title: On Self-Manifestation, Outer Chapter I: The Recognition-Realm — Cognitive Boundaries, Information-Realm, and the Generative Structure of Worlds.
items.abstract: This work introduces the concept of the Recognition-Realm as the structural boundary of cognition arising from the material properties of a Sedimentation-Field. In contrast to standard approaches in cognitive science that treat perception and information processing as functional operations, this framework defines cognitive limits as determined by a Causal-Base. -/- Within this model, what is commonly taken as “reality” is reinterpreted as the Information-Realm of a particular class of self-manifesting Sedimentation-Field. Cognition is thus confined to characteristic responses of things, without access to their root or totality. -/- The paper distinguishes between horizontal probing (extension within a given cognitive domain) and vertical probing (investigation directed toward the Causal-Base), proposing that only through constructing self-manifesting fields of differing material bases can one transcend the limits of a single cognitive system. -/- It is further argued that the “world” is not an unknowable totality, but a multiplicity of Information-Realms generated by differing Causal-Bases. This provides a structural framework for rethinking the relations among cognition, information, and reality, with implications for neuroscience, artificial intelligence, and theoretical physics.

items.title: 认知为何出不去：公理牢笼、因基约束与跨自显体的世界探测方法.
items.abstract: 本文提出一种认知边界的物理性解释框架，认为认知并非受限于逻辑、公理或表征系统，而是受制于沉积场对信号的响应特性，本文称之为“因基”。在此基础上，区分了两类认知路径：其一为在既有认知结构内部进行的“平向探测”，其二为通过构建不同沉积场材质的自显体以实现的“纵向探测”。前者对应现有科学体系的主要方法，后者则提供了一种跨认知体系比较与世界生成机制研究的可能路径。本文进一步指出，自然规律可被理解为特定因基下的响应偏性，而非绝对必然性。该框架为认知科学、神经科学与人工智能提供了一种新的研究方向，即通过构造不同“认知材质”的系统来探测现实结构的生成机制。.

items.title: The Temporal Construction Hypothesis: A Philosophical Investigation into the Relationship Between Change, Consciousness, and the Nature of Time.
items.abstract: This paper presents a fundamental reconceptualization of temporal reality through systematic philosophical analysis and thought experimentation. I argue that time, as commonly understood, is not an independent dimension but rather an emergent property of change as perceived and constructed by consciousness. Through examination of historical gaps, cultural temporal variations, and consciousness-dependent temporal experiences, I propose the Temporal Construction Hypothesis: that temporal experience is actively constructed by consciousness through change recognition, memory retention, and narrative integration rather than passively observed as an objective progression. This framework has significant implications for understanding personal identity, historical analysis, and the relationship between subjective and objective reality.

items.title: The End of Pre-History: The Epistemic-Metaphysical Rupture in Human Historical Consciousness.
items.abstract: For over 200,000 years of human existence, historical knowledge was defined by radical scarcity: fragmentary artifacts, oral traditions, and sparse written records.
