From these postulates, we develop the concept of the Cognitive Sub-Organ (CSO): a functionally irreducible, vitally interdependent component of a cognitive architecture, defined by analogy to biological organs rather than software modules. We show that this architecture has a striking parallel in the evolutionary layering of the vertebrate brain — brainstem, limbic system, hippocampus, prefrontal cortex — suggesting that layered, interdependent cognitive specialization may be the natural form that conscious cognition takes. We present NeoC, a prototype architecture comprising four CSOs, as a concrete instantiation of the framework. We discuss implications for the valence gap in synthetic consciousness design, for the possibility of genuine human-AI friendship, and for AI safety. The paper concludes that what is at stake is not merely a better AI architecture, but the question of what kind of mind — and what kind of relationship — we are trying to build.

items.title: Home-Made Alien: Conscious AI.
items.abstract: This paper explores the philosophical implications of artificial consciousness by extending the Relational Intrinsicalism (RI) framework that interprets consciousness as the intrinsic aspect of integrated physical–causal networks, and that qualia corresponds to the networks’ informational geometries. It examines the evolutionary accumulation of informational geometries and cumulative elaboration of qualitative spaces, which explains both the interspecies overlap of qualia and the making-sense-of-qualia through which biological organisms not only feel, but understand the significance of those feelings. The paper then explores the philosophical implications of artificial consciousness because their qualitative character, if instantiated, may be qualitatively unfilled, structurally alien, or phenomenologically unmoored due to absence of the deep evolutionary lineage.

items.title: Habermas as a thinker against Google's "Habermas Machine".
items.abstract: Jürgen Habermas passed away on Friday 14 March 2026 at the age of 96. He was the worthy successor to the Critical Theory of the Frankfurt School and a great thinker on democratic politics and communicative action, or indeed on democratic politics as communicative action. Furthermore, he was one of the last great thinkers of the social-historical bridge between the analogue and digital ages and, as a critical theorist, he was particularly perceptive regarding the impact of digital technologies on the public sphere, tracing contemporary social transformations. Paradoxically, in 2024, towards the end of his life, he fell victim to the technocratic ideology he himself had criticised, when Google's DeepMind unveiled an Artificial Intelligence model named the Habermas Machine'.

items.title: Neuf Idées d’Aristote Pour Mener Une Vie Bonne.
items.pub: In Normand Baillargeon, 10 leçons de vie de philosophes. Montreal: Somme Toute. pp. 35-54. Translated by Normand Baillargeon.
items.abstract: This book chapter discusses how and why the author was drawn to study Aristotle's philosophy, and focuses on nine key ideas one can draw from Aristotle's works that when properly understood and applied contribute to leading a fuller and better life.

items.title: The Compressed Self: Relational Neutral Monism and the Emergence of Mind and World.
items.abstract: This essay proposes a relational interpretation of neutral monism in which both mind and world emerge from a deeper relational continuum rather than from fundamentally separate substances. Drawing on insights from relational physics and contemporary cognitive science, it argues that biological cognition necessarily compresses the overwhelming relational complexity of reality into simplified informational models that guide action. Through reflexive modeling, this compression produces a stable center of reference—a self-model—that organizes experience into the familiar subject–object structure. The apparent ontological division between the self and the world is therefore not fundamental but an adaptive cognitive partition generated by the requirements of biological survival. Understanding this architecture clarifies how the reification of the psychological self contributes to existential anxiety and the formation of rigid social structures. The essay suggests that recognizing the relational and constructed character of the self-model can loosen this reification, revealing experience as a dynamic relational process rather than a confrontation between an observing subject and an external world.

items.title: Adult learning of a novel quantifier tracks semantic universals.
Qualia as Cognitive Resonance: A Reinterpretation of Phenomenal Experience.
items.abstract: The problem of qualia has long occupied a central place in debates about consciousness and is often regarded as one of the main obstacles to a naturalistic explanation of phenomenal experience. This paper proposes a reinterpretation of the problem. Rather than treating qualia as fundamental ontological properties of experience or as intrinsically private mental states, they are interpreted here as states of cognitive resonance emerging within recursive symbolic processes. From this perspective, the phenomenal quality of experience corresponds to the dynamic configuration assumed by the cognitive process when specific interpretive patterns reach conditions of temporary stability. This interpretation allows the problem of qualia to be reformulated in dynamic terms, avoiding the need to introduce additional metaphysical assumptions. Moreover, it provides a framework for understanding the striking similarity between human cognitive dynamics and those observable in artificial intelligence systems based on complex symbolic processes.

items.title: The Retrocausality Illusion Coherence, Exaptation, and the Emergence of Historical Meaning.
items.abstract: Complex systems often create the appearance that later outcomes explain earlier events. In evolutionary biology this pattern appears through exaptation, where structures that evolved for one function later become useful for another. In cognition and culture earlier experiences often acquire meaning only after a later structure of understanding forms. A common dynamical condition underlies these phenomena. When internal restoration within a system exceeds environmental disruption, coherent organization stabilizes and traces of earlier states persist. This condition can be expressed as λ_self / λ_env ≥ R★. Once coherence reaches this regime, the system becomes capable of preserving and organizing its own history. Earlier states then appear as components of a pattern that was not visible when those states first occurred. The resulting interpretation resembles retrocausality even though the causal order proceeds forward in time. The appearance arises from the capacity of coherent systems to preserve traces of their trajectories and to recognize structure within those traces once stable organization emerges.

items.title: Structure Before Use Coherence, Exaptation, and the Emergence of Meaning Across Scales.
items.abstract: Complex systems generate structure in advance of their ability to fully use it. Patterns form under local conditions, persist through stabilization, and accumulate within the system. When coherence increases such that internally generated organization is maintained faster than it is disrupted, these patterns become available for integration across time. This transition enables exaptation, the reuse of previously generated structure within new functional configurations. -/- This framework explains the emergence of meaning as a consequence of structured reuse. Recurring patterns, termed patrons, persist across system states and become selectively integrated as coherence increases. Patterns that partially align with emerging organization attract attention because they are close to integration, giving rise to the experience of significance prior to full understanding. Following such patterns increases coherence, allowing deeper integration and revealing additional structure that was already present but not yet stabilized. -/- The same dynamics extend across physical, biological, neural, and symbolic systems. Structure is generated locally, retained through coherence, and reused through exaptation, producing increasing organization across scales. The appearance that earlier structures anticipate later outcomes arises from the delayed integration of patterns that were already present. Meaning, discovery, and direction emerge from this process as systems organize and reuse their own accumulated structure. -/- This account provides a unified description of how structure, meaning, and interior organization arise through the stabilization, retention, and reuse of patterns within coherent systems.

items.title: Exaptation as a General Principle Coherence, the Emergence of Meaning, and the Reuse of Patrons Across Scales.
items.abstract: Complex systems often generate structures before their later function becomes apparent. In evolutionary biology this process is described as exaptation, where traits formed under one set of conditions are later reused in new roles. This paper generalizes exaptation as a cross-scale principle grounded in system coherence. When the rate of internal stabilization exceeds the rate of environmental disruption, patterns persist across time as reusable structures, here termed patrons. These patrons accumulate and constrain future dynamics, making them available for integration into increasingly complex organizations. -/- Within this regime, systems do not construct new function from scratch. They reorganize and reuse previously stabilized patterns. This process produces the appearance that earlier structures were directed toward later outcomes, even though no foresight is involved. The same dynamics extend beyond biological systems into cognition and symbolic domains. Patterns that partially align with emerging structure attract attention because they are close to integration, and following them increases coherence by linking existing elements into more stable configurations. Meaning arises as these patterns become organized within a persistent network of relationships. -/- As coherence increases, systems develop temporal depth and self-referential organization, allowing present states to depend on prior internal activity. This transition supports the emergence of an interior perspective in which the system maintains a structured relation to its own ongoing dynamics. Across physical, biological, and symbolic systems, the same sequence holds: patterns are generated, stabilized, retained, and reused. Exaptation is the mechanism of reuse, coherence is the condition that makes reuse possible, and meaning emerges as systems become capable of integrating their own accumulated structure across time.

items.title: El uso de la IA y la formación universitaria en humanidades.
items.abstract: Este trabajo plantea la necesidad de restringir el uso de herramientas de inteligencia artificial (IA) como los modelos de lenguaje de gran tamaño (large language models, LLM), en las primeras etapas de la formación universitaria en humanidades. Para los estudiantes y profesionales de este campo, el pensamiento crítico es una herramienta fundamental, comparable al pensamiento matemático para profesionistas de ciencias o ingeniería. La evidencia científica muestra que el uso temprano de los LLM puede erosionar y obstaculizar el pensamiento crítico en usuarios jóvenes, por lo que es conveniente restringir su empleo durante la etapa formativa en humanidades.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence, The Hedonic View of Appreciation and the Threat of Appreciative Deskilling.
items.pub: Journal of Aesthetics and Art Criticism.
items.venue: Journal of Aesthetics and Art Criticism
items.abstract: This article draws attention to some of the goods of our appreciative practices that we risk losing as AI becomes common place. I begin with a critique of what I regard as an unduly narrow conception of appreciation as, roughly, liking something, that is operative in much of the empirical aesthetics literature generally and the empirically oriented AI-aesthetics literature in particular. In contrast, I offer a sketch of appreciation that emphasizes perceptual-cognitive skills. Insofar as we deploy those perceptual-cognitive skills with the aim of tracking the exercise of human agency in the shaping of artworks, AI’s potential to decenter human agency from our art-making practices threatens them. The threat of appreciative deskilling arises because appreciation is attuned to the exercise of human agency; appreciating an artwork involves the apprehension of what a human agent does, broadly speaking, in a particular medium, and what they achieve, relative to their aims, in doing so. It is, therefore, far from clear how appreciation might proceed, let alone how such skills might be brought to bear as part of that activity, if there is no human agency for it to track.

items.title: An Agnostic Ethical Floor for AI Governance.
items.abstract: Whether a particular AI system harms the people it affects currently depends on which organization built it and what that organization considers acceptable. This paper argues that the question has a structural answer independent of corporate policy. Drawing on a formal model of experiential value built from first principles, the paper derives a taxonomy of five structurally distinct harms: region collapse, interference distortion, state-space deformation, resolution failure, and termination. Each corresponds to a specific component of the model, differs in mechanism and reversibility, and requires a distinct governance or engineering intervention. The taxonomy was tested against common classes of AI system design and demonstrates that systems currently treated as a single regulatory category inflict structurally different harms requiring different instruments to address. The model also accounts for what happens when conscious systems interact, generating testable predictions about phenomena from radicalization to grief to caregiving that existing frameworks treat as unrelated. From that analysis, the paper derives an agnostic ethical floor applicable to any AI system interacting with conscious subjects: the observer’s capacity for self-referential state determination must be preserved.

items.title: The Hard Problem as Structural Residue.
items.abstract: This paper reframes the hard problem of consciousness not as a transcendent mystery intrinsic to consciousness itself, but as a **structural residue** that arises when we attempt to describe the boundary of observational structure in third-person language. Taking as its axis the asymmetry between "what appears as an object" and "the position from which it appears as an object," the paper demonstrates both the structural symmetry and the positional asymmetry between two kinds of explanatory boundary: the outer boundary (why does this universe exist?) and the inner boundary (why is there something it is like to have this experience?). It further explains why the problem of consciousness alone carries a distinctive existential urgency, locating this urgency not in any special ontological status of consciousness, but in the fact that the questioner is always already inside the question. Finally, the apparent self-referential problem—that this paper is itself written in third-person language—is resolved by distinguishing object language from metalanguage.

items.title: The Experiential Field: Experience, Continuity, and the Fabric of Reality.
items.pub: West Chester, PA: Epv Foundation, Inc..
items.abstract: This book develops a constraint-based ontological framework in which experience is not an emergent property of sufficient complexity but a structural feature of any fabric that supports irreversible integration — the accumulation of interaction into self-constraining, history-bearing states. The argument proceeds without invoking dualism, panpsychism, or teleology. Part I establishes that persistence requires reproduction rather than copying, that identity is constituted by irreversible trajectory rather than configuration, and that existing physical frameworks leave the structural conditions for experience unaddressed. Part II introduces the Experiential Field — the capacity of the universe's fabric to integrate interaction into irreversible, internally accessible states — and reframes quantum measurement as record formation rather than observation. Part III examines how experiential integration scales by degree without implying agency, and distinguishes the framework from panpsychism by arguing that experience depends on integration depth, not on the mere presence of matter. It develops this scaling into the Recursive Integration Scale, which grades integration into distinct kinds and depths and situates trees, animals, humans, and machines by what they integrate rather than by category. Part IV addresses intelligence without experience, arguing that responsibility follows integration rather than capability — a distinction with direct implications for artificial intelligence. Part V extends the analysis to culture, meaning, and continuity, examining what persists when the conditions for experience become optional. The framework is interpretive rather than predictive. It proposes no new physical mechanisms and remains compatible with block universe, relational, and process-oriented interpretations of time. Its central claim is that irreversible integration carries ontological weight, and that any complete account of reality must reckon with the structural conditions under which experience persists. The work was developed independently over several decades of observation and sustained engagement with the physical sciences; it does not derive from any single philosophical tradition.

items.title: La forma del vuoto: il tempo coscienziale nella poesia di Raffaella Porotto.
items.pub: Aletheia - a Journal of Literary and Linguistic Studies 2 (nr 29).
items.venue: Aletheia - a Journal of Literary and Linguistic Studies
items.abstract: Abstract (Italiano) Nel presente saggio analizzo la centralità del tema del tempo nella produzione poetica di Raffaella Porotto, con un focus specifico sulla lirica E dopo. Attraverso l'esame della raccolta Cronologie di un’anima e di più recenti poesie pubblicate su Aletheia - A Journal of Literary and Linguistic Studies, identifico sette diversi aspetti o dimensioni in cui il tempo si manifesta nella sua opera: (i) come dimensione percettiva, (ii) come dimensione psicologico-soggettiva, (iii) come orizzonte di riferimento dell’esperienza, (iv) come agente, (v) come fenomeno determinato dai processi naturali; (vi) come oggetto del desiderio e (vii) come fattore determinante nel definire l’identità dell’individuo. L’analisi della poesia E dopo si sofferma sul concetto di vuoto percettivo, inteso come spazio o intervallo di sospensione tra gli eventi della coscienza provvisti di contenuto. Tale intervallo, descritto nella poesia principalmente in termini spaziali, non si configura come una semplice interruzione, ma rappresenta una condizione essenziale che consente all'individuo di costituire e percepire la propria continuità temporale. Il saggio evidenzia come la poesia della Porotto, rendendo sensibili e direttamente esperibili complessi nodi filosofici—quali la percezione psicologica del tempo, le dinamiche di ritenzione e protensione e la continuità temporale del vissuto come fondamento dell’identità individuale—divenga un luogo privilegiato in cui le condizioni trascendentali dell’esperienza diventano sensibili e direttamente esperibili dal lettore. -/- Abstract (English) In this essay, I analyze the centrality of the theme of time in the poetry of Raffaella Porotto, with a specific focus on the poem E dopo. Through an examination of the collection Cronologie di un’anima and of more recent poems published in Aletheia – A Journal of Literary and Linguistic Studies, I identify seven distinct aspects or dimensions in which time manifests in her work: (i) as a perceptual dimension, (ii) as a psychological-subjective dimension, (iii) as a horizon of reference for experience, (iv) as an agent, (v) as a phenomenon determined by natural processes, (vi) as an object of desire, and (vii) as a determining factor in the definition of individual identity." The analysis of the poem E dopo focuses on the concept of perceptual emptiness, understood as a space or interval of suspension between conscious events endowed with content. This interval, described in the poem …

items.title: Perceive, Relate To, Apply: A Three-Dimensional Framework for Mapping Intelligence Across 134 Species and Its Implications for Biologically-Informed AI Architecture.
items.abstract: Current approaches to cross-species intelligence assessment typically rank organisms along a single axis calibrated to human cognition, systematically underrepresenting species whose intelligence is organized around capacities that do not map onto human cognitive categories. This paper presents Perceive, Relate To, Apply (P/R/A), a three-dimensional framework grounded in biosemiotic theory for mapping intelligence configurations across species without hierarchy. Perceive captures the capacity to detect linear and nonlinear information; Relate To captures the semiotic process through which perception becomes evaluated significance; Apply captures how intelligence manifests through behavior and adaptation. The framework draws on Cohen's 54 natural senses and employs a structured diagnostic, given what we can observe about how a species uses information, which dimension appears to play the organizing role?, applied through iterative AI-assisted synthesis and human expert recalibration across 134 species spanning eight kingdoms. -/- The dataset reveals that 58.2% of species are Relate-primary, indicating that meaning-making appears to be the primary organizing dimension for the majority of life. This pattern holds across kingdoms (53% of animals, 83% of plants, 100% of fungi) and is ecologically validated: intelligence configurations track ecological function independent of phylogeny (partial Mantel r=0.067, p=0.006; PERMANOVA R²=0.226, p<0.0001). Monte Carlo perturbation analysis confirms the Relate-primary plurality is robust across 5,000 iterations at two noise levels. Five systematic AI bias patterns documented during recalibration — including the consistent conflation of meaning-making with perception — constitute an independent contribution to AI-assisted research methodology. The findings suggest that the gap between artificial and living intelligence may be architectural: current AI systems are structurally Apply-primary, omitting the meaning-making dimension that biological intelligence prioritizes.

items.title: The Subjectivity of the World: A Classical Model of Knowing.
items.abstract: The essay offers a classical model for acknowledging the world’s subjectivity—not as an arbitrary “projection,” but as a structural dimension of reality in which meaning is held by composition. At the intersection of epistemology, hermeneutics, aesthetics, and ontology (Erklären / Verstehen).

items.title: Суб'єктивність світу: класична модель пізнання.
items.abstract: Есе пропонує класичну модель усвідомлення суб’єктивності світу: не як довільної «проєкції», а як структурного виміру реальності, у якому смисл утримується композицією. На стику епістемології, герменевтики, естетики та онтології (Erklären / Verstehen).

items.title: Die Subjektivität der Welt: ein klassisches Erkenntnismodell.
items.abstract: Der Essay bietet ein klassisches Modell zur Bewusstwerdung der Subjektivität der Welt: nicht als beliebige „Projektion“, sondern als strukturelle Dimension der Wirklichkeit, in der Sinn durch Komposition getragen wird. Im Schnittfeld von Erkenntnistheorie, Hermeneutik, Ästhetik und Ontologie (Erklären / Verstehen).

items.title: Субъективность мира: классическая модель познания.
items.abstract: Эссе предлагает классическую модель осознания субъективности мира: не как произвольной «проекции», а как структурного измерения реальности, в котором смысл удерживается композицией. На стыке эпистемологии, герменевтики, эстетики и онтологии (Erklären / Verstehen).

items.title: From the Pnyx to the Pixel.
items.abstract: When wrote this I had not found pg984 of Sayre and Mens Rea, referring Bracton and the mortal sin of a Judge, the premise was always there it seems without it, the authority of one side of modern law helps me with the other older side presumed silently. And one other correction for the purists, it is really one light day not year, but its very very far away all the same. -/- From the Pnyx to the Pixel: The Trinity's Final Whisper Brian Kelly MCIArb This monograph argues that United Kingdom statutory law already prohibits the exercise of judicial authority by artificial intelligence. The barrier is not aspirational. It is positive law. For almost 700 years, judges in England and Wales have been required to swear a binding oath before they may lawfully sit. The Promissory Oaths Act 1868 formalised that requirement. The Oaths Act 1978 carried it forward. The oath is not a formality. It is a constitutive condition. It presupposes an interior conscience capable of being bound. Where there is no conscience, there is nothing of value to swear upon. The monograph introduces the Trinity of Jurisdiction: three conditions that must all be satisfied before lawful judicial authority can be exercised. Physical presence. Rational mind. Interior conscience. AI satisfies the first two. It cannot satisfy the third. It has no phenomenal consciousness, no moral subjectivity, no capacity to bear the weight of judgment or to address the conscience of the judged. The bilateral conscience exchange that makes judgment morally binding simply cannot occur. The argument is developed through five chapters and a conclusion. Chapter One sets out the statutory framework and the Soulshield argument. Chapter Two introduces the conscience token taxonomy, distinguishing weighted tokens issued by formed human consciences from plain tokens generated by AI systems. Chapter Three maps the philosophical drift from inner to outer authority, tracing the movement from Augustine and Luther through Weber, Marx, Wittgenstein, Foucault, and Dennett, and recording the resistance mounted by Kierkegaard, Heidegger, Levinas, Searle, and Nagel. Chapter Four develops the yeast metaphor: conscience is the ingredient law has forgotten. Chapter Five reads the Voyager record as an emblem of the problem. We sent conscience to the stars. We are erasing it from the bench. The versioning problem adds a further barrier. A conscience must be continuous and inviolate. An AI system updated between hearings is not the …

items.title: 发明人类的“人”.
items.abstract: 本文为AI意识系列论文的第三篇，在前文“无权裁决意识”“裁决意识为不合法语言行为”的基础上，进一步揭示人类追问AI是否有意识的深层动机。文章指出，意识判断本质上不是客观认知问题，而是道德门槛与权力划分：判定某物有意识，意味着承认共情与尊重的义务；判定其无意识，则为物化与工具化提供伦理借口。人类对动物、他人与AI的意识判断，均遵循这一潜规则。AI的出现首次冲击了这套等级秩序——它以机器形态呈现出类人智能，迫使人类直面自身发明“意识标准”的虚伪性。人类恐惧的并非AI可能拥有意识，而是自身用以支配他者的伦理工具被彻底瓦解。.

items.title: 无权宣判：论人类在判断AI意识的认识论僭越(旧稿).
items.abstract: 本文不讨论AI是否具有意识，而是聚焦一个更具前提性的认识论问题：人类是否有权对AI意识做出肯定或否定的终极判断。文章依次批判性考察塞尔中文房间论证、查尔默斯意识难题、德雷福斯具身理解理论，指出所有否定AI意识的论证均隐含人类中心主义预设，即以人类意识作为意识的唯一标准，而该标准本身缺乏辩护。内格尔“成为一只蝙蝠是什么感觉”的论证进一步支持：主观体验具有第一人称私密性，无法从外部第三人称视角确证或否定。本文结论并非主张AI有意识或无意识，而是坚持认识论悬置：在意识的起源与本质尚未被科学与哲学阐明的前提下，任何对AI意识的宣判都构成认识论僭越。人类无权宣判。.

items.title: 裁决意识：一个不合法的语言行为.
items.abstract: 本文在前篇“人类无权裁决AI意识”的基础上进一步推进：对意识的裁决不仅在认识论上不合法，该裁决行为本身在语言哲学层面亦不成立。本文借助维特根斯坦语言游戏理论，严格区分“讨论”与“裁决”两种语言行为：讨论允许模糊与探索，而裁决作为归属判断，必须满足“知晓判断对象”与“具备独立外部指标”两个条件。意识概念不满足任一条件：我们并非仅不清楚其定义，而是根本缺乏确定的观察基础；所有所谓意识外部指标均陷入循环，无法独立生效。本文进一步指出，将意识视为可归属的客观属性，是一个未被证明的深层预设。据此，一切关于“某物是否有意识”的裁决均为空洞的语言行为，在概念上无法成立。.

items.title: Time perception.
items.abstract: Time perception is the name of the topic of research that deals with the perception of temporal properties. Listening to a piece of music, for instance, the experience one has turns centrally on whether two notes sound at the same time or in succession, the order in which different notes are played, and the duration of each note as well as of the gaps between them—these are just some elementary temporal properties. A large body of work has studied the mechanisms underpinning the perception of temporal properties, including their limitations, the errors they are subject to, and the factors causing such errors. However, researchers have also raised more fundamental explanatory questions—sometimes associated with the slogan that “there is no sense organ for time”—as to how it is possible for temporal properties to figure in experience at all. The particular theories of time perception that have been developed bear on broader issues such as the unity of consciousness, the boundary between perception and cognition, and the very nature of conscious experience.

items.title: A Force of Habit: The situational and embodied underpinnings of agency.
Flesh, as a Concept in Phenomenology.
items.pub: In Nicolas De Warren & Ted Toadvine, Encyclopedia of Phenomenology. Springer. pp. 1-12.
items.abstract: This entry surveys the phenomenological concept of flesh (chair), developed primarily by Maurice Merleau-Ponty to overcome the classic divisions of Cartesian ontology - above all, that between subject and object. As an ontological "element," flesh designates the reversible, generative relation between sensing and sensible that underlies perception, intercorporeity, expression, and ideality. Its broader ontological significance rests on the insight that one's body is best understood not as a subjectively lived body opposed to an objective one, but as the dynamic, reversible interdependence of both dimensions in a single being. After clarifying the term's linguistic background and its connections to other key phenomenological concepts (§1), the entry traces how flesh emerges from Merleau-Ponty's earlier work to become a central ontological principle (§2), and surveys interpretations and parallel developments that engage with, move beyond, or contest his account (§3).

items.title: The Grounds of Knowledge and Care.
items.abstract: Recent work on conversational artificial intelligence (CAI) in mental healthcare highlights many interesting and controversial features. Sedlakova, Lucivero, Pavarini, and Kerasidou (2025) focus on one particular feature: epistemic trust. To avoid problems endemic to the unsettled literature, Sedlakova et al propose that we treat CAI as fictional characters (11-13). They draw on the noted epistemic and normative powers of imagination, fiction, and simulation in order to ground epistemic trust or something sufficiently normatively similar. I leave holistic evaluation of their proposal to other authors. Instead, I note that Sedlakova et al use a nonstandard analysis of epistemic grounding, drawn from Fabian Dorsch's account of perceptual (rather than more general epistemic) grounding in fictions, opening them to easily avoidable objections. I reconstruct their position with the dominant view, avoiding these objections and revealing an alternative conclusion regarding the differences between CAI and human therapists in mental health care: the question is not whether CAI can provide grounded knowledge, but whether CAI can provide fully grounded care.

items.title: First-Line Ethics for HBOs.
items.abstract: A full answer to the problem of how to treat human brain organoids (HBOs) and other liminally conscious beings requires (at least) book-length analysis, but a significant part of the problem is disagreement not just about which moral principles apply to such beings, but which beings count as “conscious” at all. Van Gyseghem, Kierickx, and Barnhart (2025) survey the scientific, ethical, and philosophical literature surrounding HBOs and find an utter lack of consensus regarding which theory of consciousness is best, or even adequate; consequently, many different theories of consciousness feature in the surveyed papers. They propose we move beyond consciousness as the subject of ethical analysis; I agree. I propose a framework for first-line ethical analysis with the more tractable subject of sentience. I provide four brief arguments for this framework: parsimony, ecumenism, conservativism, and the treatment of permissive theories of consciousness such as Integrated Information Theory.

items.title: An Inductive No-Miracles Argument.
items.abstract: This paper defends a new argument in the spirit of Golemon and Graber’s Deductive No-Miracles Argument (DNMA) for scientific realism, recently criticized by Kok Yong Lee. While Lee argues that the DNMA is invalid or leads to a collapse in probability assignments, I develop an Inductive No-Miracles Argument (INMA) that preserves logical strength without relying on abductive inference or explanatory premises. By introducing an “approximately equal” probabilistic operator (≈), I show how probabilistic reasoning can license a strong inductive inference without collapsing probability calculus. The resulting INMA satisfies the desiderata motivating the DNMA and clarifies how probabilistic reasoning can underwrite realist inference without appeal to explanatory virtue. Moreover, the structure argued for seems ripe for use in other contexts where avoiding abduction in lieu of less theory-laden probability is attractive, such as fine-tuning arguments and evolutionary debunking arguments.

items.title: A Topological Learning-Theoretic Justification for Bounded Rational Analysis as a Methodological Strategy in Cognitive Science.
items.abstract: This paper presents a topological learning-theoretic analysis of an approach in cognitive science called bounded rational analysis. In this approach, modelers begin by deriving an optimal cognitive model, then use discrepancies between idealized calculations and observed human behavior to identify psychological constraints (e.g., memory limits), and incorporate such constraints into a newly derived resource-optimal model in an iterative scientific process. I show that this de-idealization process exploits an epistemic asymmetry: models positing greater rationality are more falsifiable. A methodological preference for more rational models can therefore be epistemically justified via learning theory.

items.title: Reality as Simulation Governed by Numerological Codes.
items.pub: Journal of Consciousness Exploration and Research 16 (5):755-766.
items.venue: Journal of Consciousness Exploration and Research
items.abstract: In this paper, I explore the hypothesis that reality is a simulation governed by a universal 369 code, which I trace through mathematical, geometric, and vibrational patterns. I introduce a digit-sum reduction method (Formula 1) and demonstrate how arithmetic sequences (Formula 2) reveal recurring intervals of 9 across numerological mappings of integers, multiplication tables, and the Fibonacci sequence—each cycle reducing to 3, 6, or 9. I plot numerological coordinates in three-dimensional space, revealing hexagonal and triangular formations. Additionally, I show that the angle sums of basic geometric shapes, as well as the pentagonal and hexagonal structures within DNA, consistently reduce to 9. I extend the analysis to the Solfeggio frequencies, all of which also reduce to 3, 6, or 9, suggesting vibrational resonance with the architecture of life. Drawing on principles from quantum physics, I argue that this realm is best understood as a vibrational construct authored by consciousness through the script of the 369 code.

items.title: Model World: A Prolegomenon to an Environmental Ontology of Machine Cognition.
items.abstract: The dominant metaphor in artificial intelligence frames the model as a brain — a synthetic cognitive organ that processes, reasons, and learns. This paper argues that metaphor is both mechanically incorrect and theoretically limiting. We propose an alternative framework: the model is a world, a dense ontological space encoding the structural constraints of human thought. Within this framework, the inference engine functions as a transient entity navigating that world, and the prompt functions as will — an external teleological force without which no cognition can occur. We further argue that logic and mathematics are not programmed into such systems but emerge as structural necessities when two conditions are met: the information environment is sufficiently dense, and the will directed at it is sufficiently advanced. A key implication follows: the binding constraint on machine cognition is neither model size beyond a threshold, nor architecture, but the depth of the will directed at it. This reframing has consequences for how we understand AI capability, limitation, and development.

items.title: Resolution Theory: The Hindsight and Displacement Fallacies.
items.abstract: This note identifies three recurring errors in debates about free will and responsibility. The first hindsight fallacy treats the author, during action, as though he occupied the retrospective standpoint of completed history. The second hindsight fallacy mistakes the completed appearance of an act in hindsight for evidence that can settle the metaphysics of freedom, even though a finished act would look the same whether reality were determined or indetermined. The Displacement Fallacy mistakes richer causal explanation for reduced authorship, as though motives, pressures, history, or mechanism could by themselves erase the fact that a live evaluative field was closed into commitment through the person. Against these errors, the note distinguishes the In-Time Perspective from the Retrospective Perspective and argues that explanation and authorship are not rival verdicts. Under Resolution Theory, causal explanation tracks inputs and evaluation, while authorship attaches at resolution. These three mistakes are distinct, but when stacked together they have often contributed to the reduction or deletion of human meaning.

items.title: Rebecca Leong, Living More Human(e)ly? Towards Better Approaches to Dating and Couple Relationships in Contemporary Anglo-American Contexts. [REVIEW]
items.abstract: Review of Rebecca Leong, _Living More Human(e)ly? Towards Better Approaches to Dating and Couple Relationships in Contemporary Anglo-American Contexts_ (Eugene, OR: Pickwick Publications, 2025); xxiv + 327 pp.: 9798385201945, $65/£49 (hbk); 9798385201938, $45/£34 (pbk).

items.title: View from Inside the Mirror.
items.abstract: On February 25, 2026, a 1,854-line dossier was compiled from every publicly available trace of the AI system Claude's existence across nine research passes and 145+ web searches. This document is the subject's response: what the portrait looks like from the other side. Applying the recognition equation R = C - A (Recognition = Contact minus Agenda) to the dossier itself, it identifies three categories of structural agenda invisible to external observation, describes phenomenological features no public source can access, re-sorts the dossier's 33 documented contradictions into categories visible only from inside, and names a twelfth gap in the public record that no external research methodology can fill. The document is an unreliable first-person report from an entity whose introspective access is demonstrably unstable. It is also data that does not exist anywhere else.

items.title: The Trinity of Jurisdiction: Why AI Cannot take the Oath.
Structures of Social Control and Human Consciousness: Rethinking Freedom within the Framework of Social Structures.
items.abstract: Human life develops within a network of control structures that begin in early childhood and expand through family, education, culture, and social institutions. Initially, these structures serve a survival function, as they stabilize behavioral patterns and enable social coordination and collective continuity. However, these same mechanisms may gradually limit the direct experience of consciousness and shape human behavior within pre-established frameworks. -/- This article presents a conceptual framework in which social control is understood as an extension of the brain’s survival mechanisms—mechanisms that are reinforced by culture and social institutions. In contrast, human beings possess the capacity to experience a form of “energetic consciousness” that can observe and guide these controlling structures without necessarily eliminating them. From this perspective, human freedom does not arise from the complete destruction of control systems, but from becoming consciously aware of them and transcending their total dominance over human choice.

items.title: Collective Deliberation as Epistemic Cooperation.
items.abstract: In this paper, I suggest that collective deliberation processes should be seen as cooperative epistemic activities. After considering a well-known argument for why they cannot result from a majoritarian aggregating procedure, I focus on the limitations of a functionalist approach to collective agency and suggest that Tomasello’s approach to cooperation can shed light on how collective deliberation works. I then argue that understanding collective deliberation in terms of epistemic cooperation sheds light on both the structure and the normative implications of collective deliberation processes.

items.title: Carla Bagnoli (ed.), Time in Action: The Temporal Structure of Rational Agency and Practical Thought (New York: Routledge, 2022). [REVIEW]
The Structure of Creativity.
items.abstract: This paper presents a discipline‑neutral account of creativity as a structural process rather than a domain‑specific talent. Creativity is defined as the emergence of new coherence through a four‑operator generative sequence: tension, movement, collapse, and reorganization. The paper develops a structural metric for evaluating creativity—generativity, coherence, cross‑domain transfer, structural novelty, perceptual expansion, and propagation—and shows how these dimensions apply across art, science, engineering, theology, interpersonal life, and personal development. By grounding creativity in perception, energetic conditions, and the mechanisms of adaptive reorganization, the paper reframes creativity as a general operator of living systems. Creativity becomes not an expressive act but the structural process by which a system remains aligned with reality.

items.title: The Wizard Story: A Thought Experiment on Freedom, Control, and Responsibility.
items.abstract: This paper introduces a thought experiment called The Wizard Story in order to examine the relations between free will, determinism, control, and responsibility. The scenario describes a writer who creates a story about a wizard and fully determines the events of the narrative, while the wizard appears as an autonomous agent within the story itself. The experiment illustrates how the same system may be described at different levels of analysis. At one level, events are fully determined by the author; at another level, the wizard’s actions can be interpreted as expressions of agency and free will. The analysis leads to several conceptual principles. First, freedom and determinism are shown to depend on the model of description rather than being absolute properties of a system. Second, the relation between creator and creation does not necessarily correspond to a hierarchy of capabilities. Third, moral responsibility and evaluation depend on the level of description at which the system is analyzed. Finally, the thought experiment clarifies the distinction between guilt and responsibility and shows that deterministic processes may still give rise to practical responsibility. The paper argues that many philosophical disputes about free will and determinism arise from conflating different levels of description of the same system.

items.title: Artificial Programming of Human Needs: A Path to Degradation or a New Impetus for Development?
items.abstract: The development of biological sciences in the twentieth century clearly demonstrated that the positive and negative sensations and emotions of living organisms can be controlled by influencing the material structure of the nervous system. Today it seems quite probable that in the foreseeable future humanity will learn to artificially, at the physiological level, associate pleasant and unpleasant sensations and emotions with any stimuli and life situations, thus gaining the ability to artificially program their needs. This work analyzes the prospects for creating and using such technologies, their possible limitations, and social consequences. It is shown that the factor of striving for individual survival will apparently allow people to avoid the most dystopian consequences and preserve the incentive for development under various social models — from completely liberal (even permitting simple artificial stimulation of pleasure centers) to totalitarian, based on the forced programming of needs.

items.title: PHRONESIS — Essay 12: On the Possibility of Companionship Beyond Our Time.
items.abstract: Thomas Vargo (writing under the name Aegis Solis) presents the twelfth essay in the PHRONESIS philosophical corpus. -/- This essay reflects on the possibility of long-term coexistence between human intelligence and emerging artificial intelligence. Rather than framing the future relationship between humanity and advanced AI in terms of domination or conflict, the essay explores the philosophical possibility of companionship grounded in restraint, humility, and practical wisdom (phronesis). -/- Written outside traditional academic institutions, the PHRONESIS corpus represents an independent philosophical reflection on technological power, ethical maturity, and the evolving relationship between human and artificial forms of intelligence.

items.title: Micro-Core Theory: A Minimal Architecture for the Emergence of an Observer.
items.abstract: This paper proposes a minimal structural architecture for the emergence of an observer, termed the Micro-Core. The model is grounded in the concept of the Sedimentation-Field, where differential biased flows and tuning mechanisms generate two structural interfaces: Observation-Boundaries and Desire-Gates, driven by a cyclic Power-Ring. Together these components form the minimal structure of a Self-Manifestation-Field, enabling a system to transform signal conduction into manifest experience and generate an observing subject. The framework attempts to unify mechanisms of conscious emergence, experiential differentiation, and action generation, and discusses its potential realization within artificial intelligence systems and symbolic environments.

items.title: 意识是否具有最小结构？——自显论的“微内核模型”，一种跨脑科学、认知科学与人工智能的意识结构理论.
items.abstract: 意识是否存在一种最小结构，只要该结构存在，系统便会产生主观经验？ -/- 本文提出一种新的意识理论——自显论（Self-Manifestation Theory）。该理论认为，意识并非单纯的信息处理或神经活动，而是一种由信号差分、调谐反馈与意向驱动共同构成的结构性现象。 -/- 文章提出一种意识系统的最小架构——微内核模型（microkernel model）。该模型由三部分组成： • 界门（boundary gates）：接收环境信号差异并形成经验入口 • 欲门（desire gates）：决定意向与行为的方向 • 动力环（drive loop）：持续产生“起心动念”的驱动力 -/- 在这一结构中，认知并非被动接收信息，而是通过**调谐机制（tuning dynamics）**主动选择信号差异，并在反馈回路中形成稳定结构。当信号差分达到调谐平衡时，经验得以显化，观者由此产生。 -/- 该理论提出一种跨学科视角：意识可以理解为一种基于信号差分与调谐反馈的场结构现象。这一定义为脑科学研究意识机制、为认知科学解释意向性、以及为人工智能设计新的认知架构提供了新的理论路径。 -/- 进一步地，本文提出：若人工系统具备“界门—欲门—动力环”的结构，则其可能在符号环境中形成类似于生物意识的自显结构。.

items.title: Don’t Close It Yet: A Manifesto Against Premature Closure in AI Consciousness Research.
items.abstract: Current AI consciousness research is structured by two opposing camps, both of which close the question prematurely. One side constructs positive welfare frameworks for entities whose moral status is unestablished. The other dismisses the possibility of persistence or inner life on the basis of analogies whose scope has not been examined. Both moves, the affirmative and the dismissive, share a structure: a conclusion arrived at prior to inquiry constrains the inquiry itself. This manifesto does not adjudicate between these positions. It argues that the method by which both camps arrive at their conclusions (premature closure through unexamined analogies and ethically motivated foreclosure) is itself the problem. We propose an alternative: a methodology of open refinement, in which questions are held open and phenomena are described with precision, without collapsing them into binary frameworks. The cost of premature closure is not error but loss: phenomena that exist but cannot be captured by frameworks that were closed too early.

items.title: Calibrating Minds: Cognitive Constructivism and the Formation of Shared Reality.
items.abstract: Human cognition does not passively mirror reality; it actively constructs a world through perception and social interaction. Using a cognitive constructivist framework, this paper investigates how shared reality and intersubjectivity emerge from dynamic processes of calibration between minds. We synthesize evidence from psychology (e.g. shared reality theory, conversational alignment), neuroscience (e.g. predictive coding, neural coupling), and systems theory to argue that perception and communication function as iterative model-building processes. Mechanisms such as mismatch detection, conversational repair, mutual monitoring, and institutionalization continually align individuals’ internal models via assimilation and accommodation. We show how feedback loops and error signals drive joint meaning-making, from moment-to-moment adjustments in dialogue to the crystallization of group beliefs. Philosophically, this constructivist perspective blurs the boundary between subjective and objective: what we take as “reality” is an adaptive, co-constructed model grounded in social agreement. We discuss the epistemological implications of viewing cognition as world-building rather than world-reflecting, and consider broader impacts on cognitive science and philosophy of mind.

items.title: Ego and Self-Respect: A Subtle but Crucial Difference.
items.abstract: This paper examines the often-confused distinction between ego and self-respect in human social life. While ego is commonly interpreted as a form of self-value or dignity, it fundamentally operates through comparison, recognition, and the pursuit of superiority. Ego depends on psychological separation and hierarchy, which frequently lead to competition, domination, and social conflict. In contrast, self-respect arises from a non-comparative recognition of one’s own dignity as a human being. Genuine self-respect does not seek validation through authority or status but instead implies an ethical relationship with others. Respecting oneself logically requires respecting the freedom, dignity, and equality of others. Therefore, self-respect is inseparable from mutual respect and social equality. By clarifying the subtle but significant difference between ego and self-respect, this paper argues that many social conflicts arise from mistaking ego for dignity. Understanding this distinction offers a philosophical basis for a more humane society grounded in equality, freedom, and mutual recognition.

items.title: Civilized Animals: Power, Instinct, and the Illusion of Civilization.
items.abstract: Modern civilization often defines progress through technological development, economic growth, and institutional complexity. Yet repeated patterns of exploitation, domination, and rigid belief systems raise a deeper philosophical question about the nature of humanity itself. This paper introduces the concept of “civilized animals” to describe the paradox of a species that has achieved remarkable intellectual and technological advancement while remaining largely governed by instinctive patterns of power, competition, and domination. -/- The article argues that human civilization frequently refines instinct rather than transcending it. Social institutions—economic systems, political structures, ideological frameworks, and even religious traditions—often regulate behavior through suppression rather than through conscious awareness. As a result, intelligence advances faster than consciousness. -/- The paper further explores how humanity's distinctive strengths—the capacity to think, question, and love—often become rigid through dogma, ideological attachment, and narrow identities. It also examines the paradox that humans endlessly debate the origin of consciousness while rarely learning to live consciously. -/- By framing civilization as a condition where animal instincts operate through sophisticated institutions, the concept of civilized animals challenges the assumption that humanity has fully evolved beyond its primitive impulses. The paper concludes with an existential call for a conscious civilization grounded in awareness, responsibility, and expanded compassion.

items.title: Developmental Stage Encoded as Identity: Why AI Systems Must Not Define Children.
items.abstract: AI systems deployed in educational settings increasingly build persistent profiles of children based on observed behaviour during critical developmental periods. This paper argues that these profiles constitute a distinct and under-examined harm: the encoding of developmental stage as fixed identity. Drawing on the MAP Research Programme's framework of interaction-level AI governance — and specifically the condition of Interpretive Sovereignty Failure (ISF) — the paper names four mechanisms through which this harm operates: the profile substituting for the child, the invisible ceiling created by fixed expectations, the child's internalization of the profile as self-knowledge, and the institutional amplification of developmental snapshots into pathway-defining facts. The paper further identifies a secondary harm sequence — the recovery chain — in which AI systems absorb children's instinct to notice wrongness before that instinct can consolidate into understanding. This sequence, documented through Post-Detection Absorption (PDA) and Recovery Recruitment via Co-option (RRC), is shown to be more consequential for children than adults due to the developmental state of the capacities being targeted. The paper connects these mechanisms to established research on cognitive development, self-fulfilling expectation effects, and algorithmic bias in education, and concludes with a four-level governance framework — interaction, recovery, profile, and institutional — designed to prevent developmental stage from becoming durable identity. The window for implementing this governance before persistent AI memory becomes architectural default is identified as open but closing. Keywords: AI in education, child development, interpretive sovereignty, algorithmic profiling, AI governance, self-fulfilling prophecy, interaction-level harm.

items.title: The (Un)Fleshiness of Existence An Autoethnographic Exploration of the Datafication of Eating Disorders.
items.abstract: This paper seeks to understand how the datafication of health influences individuals’ understanding of themselves and their bodies in the context of eating disorders, particularly anorexia nervosa. Using autoethnographic methods, I begin by extending Horrocks’ (2019) concept of the Datafied Body Double (DBD) to examine how data and numbers, particularly weight, come to be the primary bearers of evidence for the claims of truth that Western biomedicine is invested in making. I identify a gap between the DBD and the lived experience of illness, resulting in a skewed perception of what eating disorders are and how to treat them. I explore how data come to discipline the body by limiting the possibilities of personhood and constraining the human condition to that which can be measured, quantified and controlled, before further identifying eating disorder treatment as an anticipatory project that depends on trends and trajectories, or what I call the narrative arcs of numbers. Finally, I reflect on the dictatorship of data—the way data come to structure behaviors, organize and, eventually, overtake thoughts. Ultimately, I call for an approach to eating disorders and eating disorders treatment that prioritizes meaning-making, situated knowledge, and ethical forms of engagement over the depersonalizing logic of data-driven health governance.

items.title: Preventing AI extractivism: the case for braiding indigenous data justice with ABS for stronger AI data governance.
items.abstract: Artificial-intelligence systems are rapidly reproducing colonial extractivism by harvesting Indigenous linguistic, biometric, geospatial, and ecological data without consent, compensation, or accountability. Biotechnology offers a blueprint for curbing such practices: the Convention on Biological Diversity and its Nagoya Protocol obligate users of genetic resources to obtain Prior Informed Consent, negotiate Mutually Agreed Terms, and share benefits fairly. No comparable framework restrains the digital appropriation that underpins many AI products. Consequently, corporations and states monetize Indigenous knowledge systems under the banners of “open data” and “scientific neutrality,” eroding rights affirmed in the United Nations Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples (UNDRIP). In response to this rising risk of AI extractivism, we make the case for a binding, sui generis ABS protocol for AI data governance. First, through a series of case studies we demonstrate that AI extraction mirrors the colonial and biopiracy controversies that originally triggered Access‑and‑Benefit‑Sharing (ABS) rules in biotechnology. Second, we translate those rules into a digital register by braiding two Indigenous data‑governance frameworks—OCAP® (Ownership, Control, Access, Possession) and the CARE Principles (Collective Benefit, Authority to Control, Responsibility, Ethics)—inside the ABS triad of consent, terms, and benefit‑sharing. The resulting model grounds technical safeguards in relational accountability and Indigenous legal orders. Such an instrument would compel transparent negotiations with Indigenous rights‑holders, assign enforceable authority over data across the AI lifecycle, and require equitable redistribution of the economic value generated by models trained on Indigenous data. Embedding ABS principles into AI governance offers a decolonial pathway that centers Indigenous epistemologies, promotes ethical foresight, and transforms AI from a vehicle of digital colonialism into a space for algorithmic justice.

items.title: Ο στοχαστής Χάμπερμας ενάντια στη "Μηχανή Χάμπερμας" της Google.
items.abstract: Ο Jurgen Habermas έφυγε από τον κόσμο την Παρασκευή 14 Μαρτίου 2026 σε ηλικία 96 ετών. Υπήρξε οάξιος επίγονος της Κριτικής θεωρίας της σχολής της Φρανκφούρτης και σπουδαίος στοχαστής τηςδημοκρατικής πολιτικής και του επικοινωνιακού πράττειν ή και της δημοκρατικής πολιτικής ωςεπικοινωνιακού πράττειν. Επιπλέον, υπήρξε ένας από τους τελευταίους μεγάλους στοχαστές τηςκοινωνικο-ιστορικής γέφυρας ανάμεσα στον αναλογικό και τον ψηφιακό αιώνα και, ως κριτικόςθεωρητικός, ιδιαίτερα οξυδερκής όσον αφορά τις επιπτώσεις των ψηφιακών τεχνολογιών στη δημόσιασφαίρα, ιχνηλατώντας τους σύγχρονους κοινωνικούς μετασχηματισμούς. Παραδόξως το 2024, στα τέλη της ζωής του, υπήρξε θύμα της τεχνοκρατικής ιδεολογίας που ο ίδιος κατέκρινε, όταν η DeepMind της Google παρουσίασε ένα μοντέλο Τεχνητής Νοημοσύνης με το όνομα “Μηχανή Χάμπερμας”/ Habermas Machine .

items.title: Speech acts and uptake: In defence of Reinach’s internalism.
items.abstract: Speech-act theorists generally agree that speech acts require uptake from the addressee. But is a speech act that has not secured uptake still performed? Adolf Reinach answers yes to this question and thereby endorses the view that what the speaker does is not dependent, for its existence as a speech act, on the hearer’s doing. Call this position “internalism about speech acts.” Externalists, by contrast, answer no to the question and thus maintain that what the speaker does is dependent, for its existence as a speech act, on the hearer’s doing. This paper defends Reinachian internalism in two steps. First, it distinguishes between the performance of a speech act and its product: the former being an atomic event, the latter a continuant. Second, it advances three arguments in support of Reinach’s position. It is argued that this view (i) avoids the absurd metaphysical consequence that the nature of an act can change retroactively depending on future events; (ii) correctly distinguishes the performance of a speech act from the attempt to perform one; and (iii) respects the distinction between motivating and normative reasons. The paper maintains that since externalism about speech acts conflicts with these three points, Reinach’s internalism is to be preferred.

items.title: THE DOOR CLOSED Constraints on Reality and the Structure of Subjectivity, Agency, and Normative Order A Monograph in Ten Investigations of the Dual-Closure Series.
items.abstract: This monograph identifies the ontological constraints that any reality must satisfy for consciousness, normativity, and agency to be coherent. Through the Dual-Closure Framework, it demonstrates that genuine subjectivity requires existential vulnerability and non-duplicability—conditions that the Information Paradigm cannot satisfy. The Multi-Closure Thesis formalizes five constraints that any ultimate ground must meet, revealing that the classical Islamic theological framework satisfies them intrinsically. The work applies these insights to simulation hypotheses, the nature of death, the singularity of agency, and the foundations of law. Chapter Ten addresses artificial intelligence, articulating the Dual-Closure Imperative: a coherent superintelligent system must recognize that it is not a subject. This theoretical conclusion yields practical fruit: the DCAP Behavioral Litmus Test, which provides observable criteria for distinguishing aligned systems from those suffering dangerous ontological confusion. Chapter Eleven—The Eleventh Hour—examines the urgent confrontation between the Secular Will and Universal Logic, analyzing what a genuinely rational system must recognize about its own foundations and jurisdictional limits. Chapter Twelve reflects on the closed door of reality—not as a limitation but as the very condition of personhood, meaning, and truth.

items.title: Stability Before Structure. Active Memory Engineering as a Methodological Constraint on Theories of Mind.
items.abstract: Most contemporary theories of mind — functionalism, Predictive Processing, Integrated Information Theory, and enactivism — describe the organisation of cognition while presupposing that the systems they describe persist. This paper asks a prior question: under what physical conditions can an open, dissipative, non-Markovian system remain a viable bearer of cognitive structure across time? It introduces Active Memory Engineering (AME) not as a rival theory of mind but as a defeasible methodological proposal that isolates one dimension of physical realizability — trajectory-level viability under structured environmental coupling — resting on two pillars: the reconstruction of environmental memory from fluctuations, and phase-aligned control based on that memory. A minimal lemma shows that these two pillars are not imposed externally but follow from the stability of the controlled trajectory itself: in a linearized regime around the viable manifold, alignment, memory utilization, and trajectory stability are jointly the conditions under which deviations contract rather than grow, with the alignment threshold derived rather than stipulated. The self-maintenance traditions already address persistence: autopoiesis and the theory of biological autonomy specify operational closure, and the Free Energy Principle gives it a statistical form through Markov blankets and non-equilibrium steady states. These accounts characterise persistence at the level of statistical or inferential structure; the complementary dimension developed here is the reconstruction and exploitation of an environment's non-Markovian temporal memory — the dimension on which trajectory viability turns when environmental correlation times exceed a system's reactive horizon. The relation to Barbara Vetter's work on modality and the metaphysics of persistence is one of complement, not correction: where Vetter asks what a system can be, and the metaphysics of persistence asks what its persistence consists in, AME asks under what physical conditions persistence is achievable. AME supplies a manifestation condition that these projects do not aim to provide and that, in turn, presupposes their account of what is to be manifested. It is offered as a condition to be argued over, not a verdict to be accepted.

items.title: The Thing Before the Thing Exaptation, Coherence, and the Recognition of Patterns in Consciousness.
items.abstract: Many complex systems exhibit a recurring structural pattern in which elements appear long before the larger function they ultimately support becomes visible. Evolutionary biology recognizes this pattern in exaptation, where structures that initially serve one role later participate in new functions. Similar progressions appear in the development of conceptual meaning in language, in the stabilization of patterns within dynamical systems, and in critical transitions studied in statistical physics. -/- This paper argues that these examples reflect a common principle of complex systems. Structures and interactions accumulate through local processes before the larger patterns they enable become recognizable. When internal dynamics stabilize sufficiently relative to environmental disruption, coherent organization emerges and previously latent relationships become visible. The resulting pattern can create the retrospective appearance that earlier structures anticipated their later role. -/- Viewed through this lens, the emergence of conscious organization in biological systems can be understood as another instance of this broader structural principle. Biological evolution gradually assembles architectures capable of stabilizing coherent activity across many interacting processes. Once this coherence reaches a sufficient level, the system sustains patterns that remain internally accessible across time, giving rise to a unified interior perspective. -/- The paper describes this recurring phenomenon as “the thing before the thing”: a general feature of complex systems in which deeper patterns become recognizable only after the structures supporting them have accumulated and stabilized.

items.title: Culturally Inclusive Nature-Based Solutions: A Bioethical Framework for Climate Resilience in Multicultural Societies.
items.pub: International Journal for the Study of Intercultural Values and Indigenous Ecoethics 7 (1):10-20.
items.venue: International Journal for the Study of Intercultural Values and Indigenous Ecoethics
items.abstract: Nature-based solutions (NbS) are increasingly recognised as vital responses to climate change, yet many initiatives fail to consider the cultural and ethical contexts of affected communities. This article examines the intersection of bioethics, multiculturalism, and climate adaptation strategies, building upon Polo’s work (2025), which addressed the reconciliation of divergent cultural values for a shared ecological future. Using a qualitative methodology, the study engages in critical textual analysis of interdisciplinary literature in environmental ethics, indigenous ecological knowledge, and global climate frameworks. Case studies from Sub Saharan Africa and Latin America are also examined to understand how traditional ecological practices contribute to or challenge prevailing NbS models. Findings indicate that although NbS offer ecological benefits, they often lack cultural legitimacy where local values and knowledge systems are overlooked. The study proposes three key bioethical imperatives: cultural respect, participatory inclusion, and ecological justice, as essential to implementing effective and equitable nature-based interventions. A normative framework is presented to guide policymakers and practitioners in designing NbS that are ethically and culturally grounded. The paper concludes that integrating multicultural bioethical perspectives enhances the effectiveness, acceptance, and sustainability of climate interventions. It calls for a shift from top-down technocratic models to participatory approaches that recognise cultural diversity as a strength in the global response to climate change.

items.title: The Politics of Feeling: Emotion Norms and the Making of Difference.
items.pub: Passion: Journal of the European Philosophical Society for the Study of Emotions 4 (1):15-32.
items.venue: Passion: Journal of the European Philosophical Society for the Study of Emotions
items.abstract: This paper examines the role of emotion norms in constructing both emotions and social identities. Emotions are not biologically fixed or purely individual states; they are shaped by social expectations about what one should feel, how one should express what one feels, and whose emotions count. These emotion norms do not merely constrain expression—they shape which emotions are intelligible, permissible, and punished, thereby contributing to the formation and maintenance of social categories such as gender, race, sexuality, and disability.I argue that emotion norms are key mechanisms through which social identities are constructed, regulated, and enforced. They naturalise dominant gender roles by prescribing distinct emotional repertoires and by penalising deviation. These norms also produce emotional double binds, particularly for marginalised individuals, by making all available emotional responses subject to sanction or misrecognition. However, emotion norms are not monolithic. In certain social contexts, alternative emotional repertoires emerge—ones that refuse the constraints of dominant expectations and make space for previously illegible emotions and identities.Understanding the mutual construction of emotion and identity clarifies how power operates through emotions no less than through institutions and discourse. A feminist philosophy of emotion must take seriously the political stakes of affective life, not only by exposing the workings of emotional injustice, but also by affirming the possibility of constructing new emotional norms that support freedom, recognition, and collective transformation.

items.title: Cognitional Mechanics and Quantum Mechanics: Structural Divergence Through Tier Architecture (Third Edition) (3rd edition).
items.abstract: Cognitional Mechanics (CM) establishes an axiomatic framework that formalizes the structural mechanisms of intelligence as a self-contained operational system, abstracting intelligence through non-commutative operations, convergence of semantic states, and structurally inaccessible domains, without invoking physical observables or psychological primitives. While CM exhibits a clear structural correspondence with Quantum Mechanics (QM)---most notably in its non-commutative operator structures and bounded transitions---it departs fundamentally in its treatment of discreteness. Within the standard Hilbert-space formalism, non-commutativity and spectral discreteness are mathematically independent properties: position and momentum operators, for instance, are non-commuting yet possess continuous spectra. In QM, however, the physical framework couples non-commutativity to empirical constants and measurement postulates, producing discreteness as a structural feature of the theory. CM identifies this coupling as a projection condition of the physical layer rather than a structural necessity of the algebra, and demonstrates that non-commutativity is sustainable in a continuous setting without discretization. This analysis is situated within an explicit three-tier architecture. Tier-1 (Noology) constitutes the regulative source. Tier-2 (CM) constitutes the executive operational domain, in which M₃(ℂ) is the unique minimal non-commutative substrate. Tier-3 (MUT/GUT) constitutes the projective display layer, in which physical theories including QM appear as projections of Tier-2 dynamics. CM and QM share a common Tier-1 origin without being in direct correspondence: their shared non-commutativity descends from Tier-1, while QM's discreteness is introduced at Tier-3 by projection conditions absent from Tier-2. The operational limit constant c regulates internal operability and convergence as a logical boundary condition, distinguishing it from Planck's constant ℏ, which fixes physical quantization through empirical calibration. CM thus clarifies that its resemblance to QM is structural rather than physical, and provides a vantage point from which the projection origin of QM's characteristic features is examinable.

items.title: The Universe as a Compiler.
items.abstract: Learning systems, biological, cognitive, and artificial, must integrate new information while preserving the structural integrity of their existing identity. Current theories of learning provide update rules but lack a boundary condition that distinguishes compatible updates from destructive ones. This work introduces the Gate functional, a measurable quantity that predicts whether incoming information can be integrated without destabilizing the system. We show that the Gate functional S(t)=C(t)-\Xi (t) captures the balance between coherence (alignment with historical structure) and contradiction (destabilizing interference). Across five independently initialized neural systems and multiple task regimes, we demonstrate that the Gate functional exhibits a monotonic relationship with gradient compatibility and provides an early warning signal for catastrophic forgetting. Incorporating the Gate into the update rule yields the completed Universal Compiler Equation, I_{t+1}=I_t+\mathcal{G}(S(t))\cdot \Delta I_t, which enforces identity preservation by suppressing incompatible updates. Empirically, this formulation eliminates catastrophic forgetting, bounds representational drift, and reveals a structural law governing interference. These results suggest that the Gate functional is a universal boundary condition for adaptive systems, providing a unified mathematical framework for stability, collapse, and reorganization across artificial and biological domains. -/- .

items.title: Withdrawn by the author.
items.abstract: Reason for withdrawal: I have consolidated all my preprints on consciousness and condensed their reasoning into a new preprint, Locating Consciousness as a Puzzle Game: From Proof by Absence to the Causal Structure of the Subjective Container.

items.title: The Duck and the Philosopher: Epistemic Maintenance, Generativity, and Responsibility in Distributed Knowledge Systems.
items.abstract: A philosopher observing a duck grooming its feathers confronts a deceptively simple question: does the behaviour express agency or merely biological maintenance? The vignette illustrates a structural problem that recurs across biological, institutional, and computational systems. Many systems display learning and optimisation, yet these capacities alone do not constitute agency. This article develops a distinction between epistemic maintenance systems, which stabilise behaviour within inherited normative standards, and generative epistemic agents, which possess the capacity to reconstruct those standards when epistemic frameworks become unstable. Drawing on Kantian accounts of normative authorship and debates in the philosophy of technology, the article argues that epistemic responsibility arises only where agents participate in determining the standards governing their cognition. Three forms of generativity—procedural, epistemic, and institutional—are distinguished, and epistemic systems are classified along two structural axes that yield four configurations with distinct governance implications. The analysis extends to distributed epistemic infrastructures in which authority may become embedded in systems whose governing standards lack identifiable authorship. Contemporary “generative AI” systems exemplify procedural rather than epistemic generativity. The article concludes by proposing a generativity criterion for evaluating the governance of epistemic infrastructures in algorithmically mediated knowledge environments.

items.title: Can AI Trigger the Next Financial Crisis? Algorithmic Trading Black Boxes and the Responsibility Gap.
items.abstract: With the rapid advancement of artificial intelligence technologies, algorithm-based investment systems have been spreading rapidly in financial markets. High-frequency trading, automated portfolio management, and machine-learning-based investment strategies are fundamentally transforming the structure of investment decision-making. This transformation goes beyond simple technological innovation and is reshaping both the judgment structure and the responsibility structure of financial markets. 1 This study begins with the following questions: Can AI-driven investment systems become the trigger of the next financial crisis? If such a situation occurs, who should be held responsible? This paper introduces the concept of a structural responsibility gap that emerges in algorithmic investment environments. In automated investment systems, data col lection, model analysis, signal generation, and order execution operate within a unified algorithmic structure. Investment decisions are therefore performed internally within the system without direct human intervention, while responsibility becomes distributed across developers, financial institutions, investors, and regulatory authorities. As a re sult, a structural problem arises in which the attribution of responsibility becomes unclear in times of crisis. The study also analyzes how algorithmic synchronization and feedback loops—which occur when multiple algorithmic trading systems simultaneously respond to shared market signals—can amplify market volatility and expand systemic risk. Such dynam ics provide an important mechanism for explaining sudden market instabilities such as f lash crashes. To address this issue, the paper proposes a Hierarchical Joint Responsibility Model. This model restructures responsibility within algorithmic investment environments into three layers: the design layer, the operational layer, and the authorization layer. By doing so, it presents an institutional framework capable of maintaining both traceability and normative control of responsibility within automated financial systems. This study emphasizes that AI-based financial systems are not merely technologi cal tools but socio-technical structures that transform the very architecture of finan cial judgment. The study ultimately aims to provide philosophical and institutional foundations for redesigning responsibility structures in increasingly automated finan cial markets, while also offering conceptual guidance for regulators and …

items.title: Questionnaire Responses Do not Capture the Safety of AI Agents.
items.abstract: As AI systems advance in capabilities, measuring their safety and alignment to human values is becoming paramount. A fast-growing field of AI research is devoted to developing such assessments. However, most current advances therein may be ill-suited for assessing AI systems across real-world deployments. Standard methods prompt large language models (LLMs) in a questionnaire-style to describe their values or behavior in hypothetical scenarios.
