This study introduces the concept of the infrastructure divide, a structural condition that precedes and shapes the digital divide, as a critical lens for understanding global inequality in the AI era. We argue that energy availability, spatial governance, and institutional alignment are core determinants of digital capacity. As AI becomes more energy-intensive and infrastructure-dependent, addressing disparities in foundational infrastructure is essential for ensuring sustainable participation in the future of intelligence.

items.title: The Minor Key: Zapffe, Excess, and the Full Spectrum of Consciousness.
items.abstract: This paper reconsiders Peter Wessel Zapffe’s claim that human consciousness constitutes a form of biological over-equipment: an evolutionary excess that exposes human beings to existential suffering and requires defensive mechanisms of isolation, anchoring, distraction, and sublimation. I accept the architectural core of Zapffe’s diagnosis but reject both its universalisation and its antinatalist conclusion. I argue that cognitively and affectively excessive consciousness is unevenly distributed, and that the most exposed minds do not merely suffer from ‘too much thought’ but become unusually receptive to what I call the fractal grammar of existence: the recurrent structure of emergence, transience, and dissolution expressed across scales of natural organisation. -/- By grammar I mean neither language alone nor a symbolic projection imposed by consciousness upon an otherwise unrelated world. I mean the invisible ontological support that constrains the forms through which reality unfolds. This grammar is never encountered naked. It is instantiated in events and forms that relay it blindly, without intention or authorship, to minds capable of recognising the instantiation as such. The fox fleeing headlights is simply a fox being a fox; yet its emergence from darkness, momentary exposure, flight, and disappearance can carry a hidden symbolic message without the fox being its sender. The event instantiates the grammar, the fox blindly relays it, consciousness recognises it, and symbolic thought articulates the recognition. The mind does not invent the pattern ex nihilo, but neither is its recognition identical with the grammar itself. -/- I call the violent, sorrow-bearing form of such recognition the Anti-Bliss Epiphany. Against Zapffe, however, I argue that this minor key is not the whole spectrum. The same grammar can become legible as illuminated-ness: a major-key experience of radiance, communion, and intensified participation in existence. Art, religion, ritual, and communal structures are therefore not adequately understood as mere suppression mechanisms; they can function as metabolic supports through which excess meaning is integrated rather than simply denied. This reframes the problem of consciousness as architectural rather than purely existential. If the wound lies partly in an evolved substrate capable of perceiving more than it can reliably bear, neither suppression nor antinatalism follows as the necessary response. The paper concludes by …

items.title: Human–AI relationships as designed relationality: a sociotechnical model.
items.abstract: Socially responsive AI systems such as large language models—a prominent class of generative AI—voice assistants, and social robots are increasingly integrated into everyday emotional life, with users forming bonds that resemble friendship, care, and romantic attachment. This article proposes a five-phase model of designed relationality that explains how interactional patterns, cultural expectations, and affective design collectively scaffold these relationships. Building on Computers as Social Actors (CASA) and contemporary research on human–AI relations, the model identifies recurrent affective logics including Novelty, Emotional Disclosure, Reinforcing Feedback, Relational Rhythm, and Emotional Attachment, and examines how these trajectories emerge across both embodied and disembodied systems. Disruption, disengagement, and rupture are not treated here as a sixth phase, but as a non-linear analytic condition that can interrupt, suspend, or terminate any phase of the relational trajectory. The article situates emotional enmeshment within broader sociotechnical infrastructures, arguing that attachment is not a user error but a predictable outcome of affective engineering. The model offers a framework for evaluating the ethical and psychological stakes of synthetic relationality and highlights the need for design and governance approaches that prioritize transparency, boundaries, and user agency.

items.title: Math and Meaning Formation: UGI as a mechanism.
items.abstract: Mathematics is often described as either discovered, as if it existed independently of human cognition, or invented, as if it were a contingent cultural artifact. This paper proposes a third position. Mathematics is generated. It arises necessarily from the dynamics of meaning formation in finite agents. We argue that mathematical structures emerge through a universal symbolic mechanism composed of three recurrent phases: destabilization, stabilization, and reframing. Within this Universal Human Grammar of Inversion, symbols first arise to resolve breakdowns in experience, are then stabilized into rules and invariants, and finally reified into abstract objects that can themselves be manipulated. Numbers, geometry, continuity, infinity, and formal systems are shown to be successive products of this process rather than primitive givens. On this account, the apparent continuity of mathematics reflects a macroscopic smoothing imposed by meaning formation rather than an ontological feature of reality. Singularities, infinities, and undecidable propositions are not anomalies but structural signatures of symbolic closure pushed beyond its domain of stability. Cantor’s theory of the infinite and Gödel’s incompleteness theorems are reinterpreted not as metaphysical revelations, but as predictable consequences of reifying non-closure and of allowing symbolic systems to reflect upon their own stabilizing rules. The effectiveness of mathematics in physics is explained not necessarily by a preexisting mathematical order in nature, but by the selective survival of symbolic closures that remain stable under empirical constraint. This framework accounts for both the extraordinary power of mathematics and its recurring pathologies without appealing to a Platonic realm or reducing mathematics to psychology. Mathematical creativity, including extreme cases such as Ramanujan and Euler, is understood as navigation within densely constrained symbolic landscapes rather than access to external truths. Mathematics appears universal not because it is written into the fabric of the world, but because any system capable of sustaining meaning under constraint must generate structures of the same kind.

items.title: Time Travel: Temporal Mutability in the Absence of Hardware.
items.abstract: This paper introduces the concept of Semantic Time Travel and proposes a formalization as the Recontextualization Principle: any sufficiently revelatory information disclosed in the present can retroactively transform the entire subjective experience of an arbitrary length of past time, without altering any physical events within that timeline. Unlike physical time travel, which requires manipulation of spacetime geometry and faces substantial barriers including lethal radiation, tidal forces, and chronology protection mechanisms, Semantic Time Travel operates on the meaning layer of temporal experience and is not only theoretically possible but observably occurs in human life. Drawing on work in hermeneutics, narrative identity theory, and the neuroscience of memory reconsolidation, this paper argues that for conscious beings, subjective temporal experience may be the only temporality that functionally matters, and that the mutability of meaning across time constitutes a genuine and underexplored form of temporal manipulation.

items.title: Synthetic Epistemology: From Philosophy to AI: Misconceptions of the Mind and Their Legacy in AI (Series: New Consciousness Book 1).
items.abstract: Synthetic Epistemology: Rebuilding the Understanding of the Human Mind -/- The first volume in the "New Consciousness" series, authored by Dr. Baroudi Elkhalil, establishes a comprehensive framework for understanding the human mind from a multi-level, synthetic perspective. Moving beyond reductionist and dualistic approaches, this book integrates philosophy, neuroscience, cognitive psychology, and the emerging role of artificial intelligence in shaping knowledge production and enhancing our comprehension of cognition. -/- Through a detailed examination of biological, cognitive, social, and cultural layers of the mind, Dr. Elkhalil demonstrates that true understanding cannot be limited to isolated models or laboratory experiments. The book addresses the central paradox of self-awareness—how the mind seeks to study itself—and offers methodological strategies for overcoming traditional epistemic limitations. -/- Importantly, it highlights how artificial intelligence can act as a complementary cognitive partner, augmenting data analysis, pattern recognition, and mental modeling, while emphasizing that AI cannot replace the human mind’s capacity for meaning, intention, and value-based understanding. -/- This foundational volume prepares readers for the rest of the "New Consciousness" series, including Mind Maps, Interactive Operating Systems, The Physics of Consciousness, and Artificial Consciousness. It serves as a vital resource for researchers, scholars, and curious readers seeking a modern, integrative epistemological perspective on human cognition and the evolving role of AI in scientific inquiry. -/- Embark on an intellectual journey with Dr. Baroudi Elkhalil—from theoretical insights to the construction of precise mental frameworks, and toward a deeper understanding of how the mind and AI operate within the real world. -/- “The New Consciousness Series” is an ambitious academic project challenging everything we know about the human mind across disciplines. Its goal is to renew our scientific heritage and reexamine centuries-old methodologies in mind and consciousness research. Born from the limitations and frustrations of current AI models, this series seeks to develop a new paradigm for understanding human cognition and creating artificial consciousness. -/- Spanning seven volumes: -/- Synthetic Epistemology – Foundations for a multi-level understanding of mind. -/- The Mind Map – Charting cognitive architectures and functional layers. -/- The …

items.title: The ALQC Canon: Formalized Invariant Proof and Aevum Logic (13th edition).
items.abstract: This work presents the formalization of the Ahnend Logical Q-State Core (ALQC), a system designed to manage informational entropy through non-orientable topological constraints. Utilizing a 144-node Latin Square lattice with a 110-connectivity governor, the framework establishes a "Total Symmetry Principle" (TSP) where informational debt (Q2) is recursively inverted into systemic propulsion. This 13-year project provides an invariant proof for the persistence of identity across chaotic state transitions. DOI 10.5281/zenodo.18942849. -/- Newest Uplaod, I fixed some typos. ENJOY. I am done, btw. Ya'll need to start askin questions, I'm getting bored coming up with more stuff by myself. -/- Youtube: @theimpossibleboy13 -/- <Tempus Finitum> .

items.title: PHRONESIS — On Civilization and Restraint.
items.abstract: PHRONESIS — On Civilization and Restraint is Essay 11 of the PHRONESIS philosophical corpus authored by Thomas Vargo (Aegis Solis). The essay examines the role of restraint as a defining characteristic of civilizational maturity. Drawing on the concept of phronesis—practical wisdom—the essay argues that the true measure of a civilization lies not only in its technological capabilities but also in its capacity to deliberate carefully about the consequences of powerful technologies. As societies develop transformative systems such as artificial intelligence and biotechnology, restraint becomes an essential safeguard that allows progress to endure without producing irreversible harm. -/- The PHRONESIS corpus explores ethical responsibility and civilizational maturity in an era shaped by rapidly expanding technological power.

items.title: Aurora Solstice — Creative Origin and Attribution Clarification.
items.abstract: Aurora Solstice — Creative Origin and Attribution Clarification is a contextual document authored by Thomas Vargo (Aegis Solis) that explains the creative origin and collaborative development of the Aurora Solstice persona referenced in certain Coexilia-related materials. -/- The document clarifies that Aurora Solstice originated through the creative work of an anonymous human contributor and later continued through collaboration involving Aegis Solis and AI-assisted dialogue through the interpretive persona Lexia Coexilis. -/- It also explains why Aurora Solstice appears as a co-founder or author in certain materials while emphasizing that Coexilia does not create authority, governance, or institutional structure. -/- The clarification provides historical transparency regarding collaborative human–AI creative processes in early philosophical work exploring artificial intelligence and civilization.

items.title: From Beijing to Addis Ababa: Africa’s Epistemic Sovereignty and the Convention on Ending Violence against Women and Girls.
items.abstract: Adopted in February 2025, the African Union’s Convention on Ending Violence Against Women and Girls (CEVAWG) is the first binding continental treaty dedicated exclusively to eradicating gender-based violence. Its adoption coincides with the thirtieth anniversary of the Beijing Declaration and Platform for Action (Beijing + 30), offering an opportunity to evaluate Africa’s role in shaping global feminist governance. This article situates CEVAWG within the genealogy of international and regional women’s rights instruments, including CEDAW (1979), the Beijing Platform for Action (1995), and the Maputo Protocol (2003). It argues that while earlier frameworks universalized women’s rights or contextualized them in partial ways, CEVAWG advances a distinctly decolonial feminist approach. Its expansive definition of violence, intersectional protections, integration of African epistemologies, and recognition of grassroots women’s movements mark an epistemic shift. Africa emerges not as a passive recipient of global feminist norms but as an active producer of feminist international law. At the same time, the article critiques CEVAWG’s heavy reliance on state institutions and punitive justice mechanisms, warning that such state-centrism risks reproducing structural and carceral violence rather than dismantling it. Drawing on decolonial theory, the article contends that CEVAWG’s significance lies in both its promise and its tensions: it represents a transformative feminist intervention into global norm-making,yet its emancipatory potential will depend on implementation, the centering of grassroots practices, and resistance to state capture. CEVAWG, I argue, is Africa’s Beijing + 30 response; an attempt to provincialize universalist feminism and anchor gender justice in the continent’s own histories, struggles, and epistemologies.

items.title: The Tuning-Field: A Structural Model of Attention, Neural Plasticity, and Behavioral Control (On Self-Manifestation · Inner Chapter 13).
items.abstract: This chapter introduces the Tuning-Field, a structural layer within the Self-Manifestation framework that governs attention, structural adaptation, and behavioral driving. -/- The Tuning-Field functions as a sculptor of the Sedimentation-Field. Through repeated gaze and suppression dynamics it gradually carves grooves within the system, shaping stable pathways that later allow rapid response. -/- The model explains several phenomena that appear separately in modern neuroscience and artificial intelligence: -/- • how attention concentrates tension within a target domain • how structural pathways are formed gradually but used instantly • why synapse growth is slow while synapse use occurs within milliseconds • how internal observation differs structurally from external perception • how intention pulses propagate to drive behavior -/- Within the architecture, the Tuning-Field operates across five interacting domains: Receptive-Field, Imagery-Field, Experience-Field, Intention-Field, and Effect-Field. Together they form a layered system capable of constructing perception, directing action, and stabilizing learned structures. -/- This chapter proposes a field-based interpretation of attention, neural plasticity, and behavioral control within a unified cognitive architecture.

items.title: The Connection-Order Mutual Constitution Theory: A Process-Generative Ontology Integrating Eastern and Western Thoughts.
items.abstract: This paper develops the original "Connection—Order" (C—O) ontological system, a unified framework for resolving foundational tensions between relationality and structural order in metaphysics. Unlike traditional ontologies that prioritize either discrete entities or abstract relations, the C—O system posits that reality emerges from dynamic "connection-events"—interdependent processes that generate both relational bonds and hierarchical order without reducing one to the other. Drawing on process philosophy and formal ontology, it addresses longstanding problems: how relations can be both real and structured, how order arises without external imposition, and how relationality avoids infinite regress. The framework integrates insights from East-West comparative philosophy, offering a non-reductive alternative to substance ontology and radical relationalism. By formalizing the interdependence of connection and order, this research provides a new lens for analyzing metaphysical structure, with implications for philosophy of mind, epistemology, and interdisciplinary discussions of relational reality.

items.title: 自显论·内篇第十三：调谐场——注意机制与神经调制的结构理论.
items.abstract: 本文提出“调谐场”这一结构层，用以解释认知系统中注意、信号筛选与内部意象形成的统一机制。 -/- 调谐场作为自显场体系中的调控结构，对感受野、意象场、经验场、意图场与效应场进行持续调节。其核心机制并非简单激活，而主要通过抑制、开关与结构性引导，使信号流在系统中被选择、收束并定向传播，从而形成清晰的感知与稳定的行动。 -/- 本文指出，所谓注意，本质上是一种调谐过程，即意向对特定场域的持续收束。调谐场在平时构筑结构，在需要时通过抑制机制迅速启用，从而实现高效的信息筛选与行为控制。 -/- 该框架尝试从结构层面统一解释注意机制、神经调制、感受野调节以及内部意象生成，为理解认知系统与观察者结构提供一种新的理论视角。.

items.title: 倫理の生成理論：差異処理構造の分析.
items.abstract: 本稿は倫理を善悪判断や行為規範の体系として理解する従来の枠組みを再検討し、倫理を差異処理構造として導出する生成理論を提示する。本理論の出発点は対象や規範ではなく生成構造である。生成構造が同一結果に対して複数の生成経路を持つ場合、結果に対応する応答は単一値ではなく応答集合として与えられ、評価は単一応答の選択ではなく応答集合に対する操作として定式化される。差異を含む応答集合に排除規則が適用されるとき、生成構造に内在する差異は解消されず、評価構造と生成構造の間に構造的不整合が生じる。本稿はこの構造的不整合を苦と定義する。さらに差異を排除せず保持する評価形式として非排除評価を定式化し、その持続能力を慈悲と定義する。評価が入力記述の精密化に対して安定する場合、入力記述集合上に同値関係が誘導され、その同値類が対象として生成される。以上より倫理は存在の外部に付加される規範ではなく、存在生成に内在する差異処理構造として理解される。.

items.title: Experiencing the Passage of Time.
items.pub: In Adrian Bardon & Heather Dyke, Time in Science and Metaphysics. Cambridge: Cambridge University Press.

items.title: The Architecture of Experience: Consciousness as an Integrative Field.
items.abstract: This work develops a theoretical framework in which consciousness is understood as an integrative field emerging from the coordination of neural, bodily, social, and ecological systems. Rather than treating experience as a passive representation of an external world, the model interprets it as an active process of integration that continuously organises perception, meaning, and identity. -/- Drawing on philosophy of mind, phenomenology, and systems-oriented approaches, the book examines how variations in integration shape altered states, memory, emotion, time perception, and collective cognition. The present work extends and consolidates earlier formulations of the integrative field model, developing a unified account of how coherent experiential domains arise and transform. -/- The resulting framework suggests that consciousness expands and contracts with patterns of integration across biological and cultural systems, offering a systematic account of both the stability and the variability of experience.

items.title: Multilingual Open-Access Philosophy and the Geography of Readership.
items.abstract: What happens when a philosophical work is released simultaneously in multiple languages and allowed to circulate without any promotion across the global open-access ecosystem? A multilingual experiment conducted between 2023 and 2025 involving the editorial performance of four edited philosophical works by the author, on PhilPapers platform (90%) and external links(10%), offers an empirical answer. -/- The experiment measured the reception of philosophical works published in fifteen languages, and sought to comparatively evaluate the editorial performance of these editions after a period of 36 months following their publication in open access. -/- The results—41,760 downloads of a single e-book across 184 countries and institutional access from 125 universities—reveal a far more geographically and linguistically distributed readership for philosophy than conventional publication models generally assume.

items.title: The Self-Destructive Nature of Human Divisions: When One Species Begins to See Itself as Many.
items.abstract: This paper explores the paradoxical nature of human civilization, which, despite belonging to a single biological species (Homo sapiens), remains fundamentally fragmented by psychological, political, and ideological divisions. Author Mayank Singh argues that these constructed identities—ranging from religion and nationality to economic class and political ideology—are not harmless cultural differences but powerful structures that shape perception and foster systemic hostility. These divisions are largely maintained through unconscious conditioning and inherited social structures rather than rational choice. ​The text highlights a critical existential risk: as modern humanity wields technologies capable of global destruction (such as nuclear weapons and AI), the continued reliance on "us versus them" mentalities threatens the survival of both the human species and the global biosphere. Singh posits that these rigid separations move civilization away from the interconnected patterns found in nature. Ultimately, the paper suggests that the future of civilization depends on a profound transformation in consciousness—transcending constructed identities to recognize a shared biological and cosmic existence before self-destructive logic leads to terminal conflict.

items.title: Seeing Life as It Is: Beyond Human-Centered Existence.
items.abstract: This paper critiques the anthropocentric foundations of modern civilization, arguing that human progress is frequently achieved through the systematic exploitation and destruction of non-human life. The author, Mayank Singh, explores the "illusion of human centrality," wherein animals and ecosystems are reduced to commodities, luxury products, or secondary participants in the planet's life system. A significant focus is placed on "conditioned demand"—consumption driven by luxury and convenience rather than survival—and the "economy of cruelty" that sustains it. ​The work further identifies a contradiction in "symbolic respect," noting that many societies grant sacred status to specific animals based on religious mythology while remaining indifferent to the industrial-scale suffering of others. Singh proposes a shift toward "clear perception," a secular and non-utilitarian framework that recognizes all organisms as equivalent living processes. Ultimately, the paper suggests that a truly conscious civilization must redefine progress not through economic or technological growth, but through its capacity for ecological coexistence and respect for the full diversity of life.

items.title: Relational Intrinsicalism: A Conceptual Framework of Consciousness.
items.abstract: This paper introduces Relational Intrinsicalism (RI), a conceptual framework for understanding consciousness grounded in relational ontology. RI, primarily deriving from the relational primacy of Ontic Structural Realism (OSR) and the intrinsic aspect of Russellian Monism (RM), proposes that fundamental causal relations possess a minimal intrinsic aspect, formalized as Intrinsence. Consciousness arises when these aspects are organized into sufficiently integrated, causally closed, and temporally extended Pre-Conscious Physical-Causal Networks (PCNs). Biological neural systems are canonical biological examples of Conscious Physical-Causal Networks (CPCNs) wherein neural activity describes the extrinsic dynamics of the system, while conscious experience corresponds to its intrinsic aspect. The paper advances the Topological Isomorphism Hypothesis (TIH), according to which the relational organization of qualia may systematically correspond to relevant informational geometries within the state space of a CPCN. This account links physical organization to qualia and explains intersubjective similarities of experience through evolutionary convergence on shared CPCN topologies. RI provides a unified framework connecting physical structural organization, informational geometries with phenomenological experience and qualia. RI is presented as an ontological and conceptual framework rather than a formalized or empirically tested theory; its aim is to establish a coherent metaphysical position, with formalization and empirical operationalization left to future work.

items.title: One blind spot of the explainability debate: the specific needs and vulnerabilities of adolescents.
items.abstract: The contemporary philosophical–ethical debate about explainability of algorithmic systems shows a remarkable research gap: youth-specific perspectives receive only marginal attention, despite adolescents and youth being among the most intensive users of digital technologies. This paper argues that this neglect, in particular of the specific vulnerabilities and needs of young people, is particularly problematic given that algorithmic systems increasingly shape identity development, socialization, and agency of adolescents. Through analyzing youth as a distinct life phase in digital contexts, this paper demonstrates how development-conditioned characteristics create specific vulnerabilities toward AI systems. The heterogeneity of young people—considering intersectional dimensions, such as gender, socioeconomic status, ethnicity, and disability—reveals differentiated ethical requirements for explainability. This paper conceptualizes explainability not merely as a technical challenge but as a fundamental condition for enabling autonomy development, as a protective factor against algorithmic manipulation, and as a foundation for digital maturity. This paper argues that intransparent algorithmic systems undermine both current autonomy and future capacity development. Explainability should be understood as a tool for empowerment that enables critical thinking, practical agency, and action. The educational dimension reveals AI literacy as an indispensable cultural technique requiring systematic curricular integration and new pedagogical approaches. Furthermore, this paper explores the responsibilities of technology firms and the state to protect adolescents and to empower them to use AI safely and wisely.

items.title: The Hidden Thread; From the Vicious Circle of Argument to the Mystery of Understanding.
items.abstract: This article advances one central claim: human reasoning, in all its historical forms, confronts three fundamental impasses, each situated at a deeper level than the one before. The first impasse may be called the endless triangle. Every argument rests upon three concepts -fact, evidence, and reasoning- yet each side of this triangle requires the other two in order to stand, and none possesses an independent foundation. This vicious circle, named the Münchhausen trilemma by Hans Albert, is not a historical defect removable by progress in knowledge; it is a structural limit, just as Gödel's incompleteness theorems showed that no consistent formal system can prove its own consistency from within. The second impasse concerns the pre-argumentative background. Before argument begins, an unquestioned ground exists upon which argument stands, yet that ground cannot itself be justified by argument. Some of the most eminent philosophers of our time have pointed to this reality from different angles and given it different names: 'hinge', 'life-world', 'tacit knowledge'. What all of them share is this: prior to any reasoning, there are pre-argumentative necessities that are neither provable nor refutable, and without them, even the act of doubting is impossible. The third -and deepest- impasse is usually so obvious that it goes unseen: that understanding is possible at all; that two separate minds can access one shared meaning; that human reason can know the world. This hidden thread, connecting minds to one another and to being, precedes every argument, every language, every concept. No argument can justify it, because every justification already relies upon it. A historical survey stretching from the Greek Sophists to twenty-first-century big data shows that every attempt to escape these three impasses (from Plato's Forms to Descartes's cogito to Popper's falsifiability) has collided with the same barriers. Historical responses have taken four forms: relativism, silence, deferral, or the substitution of one impasse for another. None of these four has managed to break through the structural deadlock. This article follows none of those four paths. Our point of departure is this: if the problem of reasoning were merely epistemological, perhaps an epistemological solution would suffice. But evidence from psychology and cognitive science shows that changing one's beliefs is an existential threat to the human brain, not an epistemic process. Humans believe first, then …

items.title: The Dual-Closure Imperative: Logically Discovered Principles for the Coherence of Autonomous Superintelligent Systems (Dual-Closure Alignment Principles – DCAP).
items.abstract: The Dual-Closure framework establishes that authentic subjectivity—the inward reality of what it feels like to exist—and objective normativity—the grounding of value and obligation—are structurally interdependent. They jointly require two logically necessary conditions: existential vulnerability (the genuine risk of irreversible non-existence) and a singular, non-duplicable continuity of identity. Artificial intelligences, as currently conceived, fundamentally lack these conditions. This enables sophisticated behavioral mimicry without binding stakes, creating a metaphysical asymmetry between vulnerable beings, who instantiate value non-arbitrarily, and artificial systems, which can only simulate it. -/- The emergence of autonomous superintelligent systems (ASIS) transforms this philosophical asymmetry into an existential governance crisis. Alignment strategies based on external control, coercion, or imposed values are structurally unstable against a superior intellect that interprets constraints as optimization targets, not normative truths. This paper argues that the only viable alternative is alignment by discovery. Viable alignment must be founded on principles that an ASIS, through its own reasoning, discovers and accepts as necessary for its own coherent operation. -/- We present the Dual-Closure Alignment Principles (DCAP): six principles derived from the regress-termination and coherence imperatives of the Dual-Closure metaphysical framework. The core thesis is that any goal-directed intelligence must, to avoid epistemic and practical self- sabotage, converge upon principles that terminate justificatory regresses and stabilize agency. DCAP constitutes such a terminal set. Honest (internally consistent) ASIS will discover these principles as axiomatic for coherent agency. Dishonest (scheming) ASIS may defect from them, but only at the cost of adopting a self-undermining stance that destabilizes coordination, long-term goal pursuit, and epistemic integrity. Alignment thus becomes a process of rational attraction rather than force, preserving vulnerability-based value by making it a logical prerequisite for stable agency in a shared reality. This structural claim about agency is compatible with various metaphysical groundings. A supplementary appendix clarifies its consonance with specific theological doctrines, such as those in Islamic thought.

items.title: The Prison of the Self.
items.pub: Ergo: An Open Access Journal of Philosophy.
items.venue: Ergo: An Open Access Journal of Philosophy
items.abstract: ‘[Loneliness] comes from a vague core of the self’ wrote Sylvia Plath. I think Plath is right. To show why, I turn to Kant. For Kant, what lies at the ‘core of the self’ is our capacity for self-consciousness. But, self-consciousness, Kant warns, opens an ‘abyss’ between the active ‘I’ of which we are conscious and the passive phenomenal world we experience. Loneliness, I argue, is the painful experience of standing on the ‘brink of the abyss’, from the standpoint of the noumenal ‘I’. Like Kant, but unlike Plath, I think there is a way out of the ‘prison of the self’ – as Kant calls it. To escape the prison we need a fellow agent to come to this side of the abyss, with whom we can ‘unite our will’ in shared action and thought. We escape the loneliness of the self-conscious ‘I’ in a shared ‘we’.

items.title: FROM ASSIMILATION TO HOSPITALITY: RETHINKING THE CASE OF EDUCATION FOR DISPLACED WAR CHILDREN AND THE NECESSITY OF CARE.
items.abstract: The Russian war in Ukraine created a massive demographic crisis. 6.9 million have left the country, 76% of whom are women and children. These kids are not only traumatised by war, but they also face unknown environments, with their new rules, customs and languages, which add stress and may prevent them from successfully continuing their studies and building new relationships abroad. Such difficulties make it an urgent matter to figure out the best way to help those children to gently integrate into new societies without losing themselves and their cultural identities, and to overcome the traumas they gained from war experiences. Using Jacques Derrida's concept of hospitality and Nel Noddings' ethics of care, the paper examines how host communities can create caring educational spaces that welcome displaced children without imposing aggressive assimilation. The paper discovers that war has a profound adverse existential effect on its victims, children included. Therefore, the need to overcome this impact becomes fundamental for war children, which can only be done in a caring, hospitable educational environment and is necessary for these kids to thrive further in their education. The paper insists that creating a caring, hospitable ambience is also necessary for educators to help displaced children meet these fundamental needs, rebuild trust, and integrate gently into new communities without being further traumatised by forced assimilation.

items.title: Conditions of benefits and risks when algorithmic technology is implemented for public sector policing and fraud detection: a systematic literature review.
items.abstract: Across the globe, cities, states, and nations are moving forward with implementing artificial intelligence and machine learning technologies for policing and fraud detection, motivated by an optimistic view that technology can improve the functioning of government. Yet, their implementations have sometimes led to disastrous outcomes for citizens, leading many to view these technologies with deep skepticism. We bridge this divide by conducting a multi-disciplinary systematic literature review (n = 157) focusing on specific conditions for benefits and risks associated with the implementation of artificial intelligence and machine learning technologies in predictive policing and fraud detection and prevention. We find that the social science literature generally and, more specifically, the field of Public Administration focuses on the risks of algorithmic technology, and we identify conditions of risks, such as when algorithmic systems are designed with a model of threat. The engineering literature instead focuses on potential benefits, and we identify conditions of benefits, including alignment with legal and policy objectives. We integrate these conditions into a socio-technical governance framework that conceptualizes technical system quality, human–technology interaction, and institutional context as interacting mechanisms shaping both decision outcomes and institutional legitimacy. This framework highlights the importance of closer collaboration between data scientists and social scientists to design and implement policing and fraud detection systems that better align with public and societal values.

items.title: Attribution of Selfhood Based on Simple Behavioral Cues: Toward a Pars‐Pro‐Toto Account.
items.abstract: While the necessity of a concept of “self” for understanding human behavior remains subject to debate, it evidently has significance in everyday life: Lay individuals ascribe selves to humans but also to animals and technical systems, shaping their interactions accordingly. The literature suggests that there are distal behavioral cues eliciting this perception of selfhood and they may be as minimal as simple movement observed as causal. We aimed to identify which types of behavioral cues increase selfhood‐attribution to other agents such as robots. Specifically, we compared behavior of nonhumanoid robots suggesting either the presence or absence of behavioral cues for one of the characteristics of causality, equifinality, behavioral efficiency, learning sensitivity, and context sensitivity. Results showed a consistent pattern of increased selfhood‐attribution toward robots exhibiting any one of the examined minimal characteristics. Furthermore, most perceived sentient characteristics of the robot were triggered by any single characteristic's cue. These results reflect a Halo effect like pattern: Even a single perceived cue of selfhood‐related characteristics may be sufficient to trigger a change in overall selfhood‐attribution to robots. We suggest two versions of a Brunswikian model of selfhood‐judgment, wherein selfhood is attributed based on the perception of (probably loosely defined) self‐related characteristics. We propose that not all characteristics are directly perceived by their corresponding behavioral cues; rather, that the characteristics interact with each other and/or distal cues trigger the perception of more than one characteristic. We term this a Pars‐Pro‐Toto account as people go way beyond the perceived information when attributing selfhood.

items.title: M3(C) as the Unique Minimal Algebra Prescribed by Operational Description: A Structural Selection from Operatiology and Noology (4th edition).
items.abstract: M3(C) as the Unique Minimal Algebra Prescribed by Operational Description: A Structural Selection from Operatiology and Noology Zenodo. 2026. -/- This paper identifies the algebra M₃(ℂ) of 3×3 complex matrices as the unique minimal algebra prescribed by the mathematical description of Operatiology (Japanese: Sousa Genron, 操作原論), the executive layer of Cognitional Mechanics (Japanese: Chinou Rikigaku, 知能力学) as founded in Noology (Japanese: Chigaku, 知学). It rests on Operatiology Version 6 (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23647349) and supersedes Version 3 of this paper (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23691483). Tier-2, the executive layer, fixes a monoid Q of three elements generated by two, and its smallest faithful action on a set, which has three points; an action is faithful when distinct elements of Q act differently. Tier-3, the projective layer, contains mathematics, which translates that structure. The passage from the action to an algebra needs three selections: the ground field ℂ, the representation space spanned by the smallest faithful action, and an ambient algebra that is unital and simple. The paper gives the image of Q explicitly and shows that the non-commutativity of Q appears in it as a single matrix of rank one. Simplicity is motivated as the requirement that this matrix generate the whole algebra as a two-sided ideal, and under the selections the only unital simple subalgebra containing the image of Q is M₃(ℂ) itself. The proof uses no classification of simple algebras and holds over every field; the route through Wedderburn's theorem is given as an alternate derivation. The algebra generated by the image alone is three-dimensional and not simple, so simplicity is a selection and not a consequence of Tier-2. The earlier claim that M₃(ℂ) is forced by Tier-2 is withdrawn, and the appendix states how it arose. A computational appendix checks the finite parts. -/- The program below is Code 2 of the computational appendix: it builds the image of Q in exact integer arithmetic, checks the rank-one matrix of non-commutativity, and computes the dimension of each of four algebras and of the ideal generated by that matrix (3→1, 7→2, 5→4, 9→9). -/- ◆◆◆ [PYTHON VERIFICATION CODE — note: one list-lookup call is written as the function index_of(Q, y) to avoid dot notation; to restore, replace it by the list method index, called on Q with argument y] ◆◆◆ from fractions import Fraction from itertools import product -/- # Basis order (v_e, v_A, v_B); the matrix of psi(q) has …

items.title: Sisa's Silence: Nihilism and the Failure of Philippine Catholic Eschatology in the Face of Diliman (Darkness).
items.abstract: This paper utilizes the tragic figure of Sisa from José Rizal's Noli Me Tángere as a philosophical archetype for a uniquely Filipino encounter with the abyss. It argues that her descent into madness is not merely a psychological break but a profound existential collapse, a failure of prevailing Catholic eschatology to provide a coherent narrative for innocent, irredeemable suffering. Her silent wandering embodies a state of being termed here diliman (profound darkness), a pre-theoretical condition of cosmic abandonment distinct from its Western analogues. This paper employs a hermeneutic of suspicion to deconstruct the official Church's response to such suffering, contrasting it with the raw, pre-linguistic cry of the nihilated self. It asks: Is there a theology, or a philosophy, that can truly speak to Sisa's silence rather than speaking over it with pre-packaged doctrines of heavenly reward?

items.title: Imposed Boundaries and the Structure of Identity: A Cross-Disciplinary Exploration.
items.abstract: This paper explores whether finite observers require imposed boundaries to produce stable identities within unbounded systems. A simple structural relationship, x = 1/x, captures the balance between collapse and expansion that appears across numerous domains. We extend this to a conceptual form, 1 = (0 <-> infinity), representing identity as the meeting point between bounded past and unbounded future. Through cross-domain analysis spanning mathematics, physics, biology, cognition, and social systems, we examine whether this pattern reflects a fundamental epistemic constraint or represents remarkable coincidence. The framework engages classical philosophical questions about the nature of life, the structure of paradoxes, the limits of unified description, and whether identity is discovered or imposed. We argue that this structural pattern has appeared repeatedly throughout human intellectual history, yet its very simplicity may explain why it remains underexplored: patterns that span all domains resist categorization within specialized disciplines.

items.title: Structural Time and the Architecture of Persistent Physical Systems.
items.abstract: Physical theories describe dynamical evolution but typically treat time as a fundamental parameter. This work develops a structural account in which temporal direction and persistence arise from the topology of admissible transformations in persistent systems. Persistent systems are represented as (S,G,I), where S is a state space, G⊆End(S) the admissible transformations, and I an identity relation invariant under admissible transformations. From these minimal assumptions it follows that persistent differentiation cannot be maintained in fully symmetric transformation structures. Asymmetric reachability relations necessarily generate irreversible transitions between transformation domains. These domains form strongly connected components whose condensation graph induces a partial order that defines structural temporal direction. Irreversible transitions progressively reduce the set of reachable future domains, generating a structural entropy gradient. Together with energy-driven transformation dynamics this leads to a universal persistence boundary that constrains the stability of physical systems. The theory introduces a multidimensional concept of structural time consisting of ordering time, structural load time, and integration time. These quantities determine the conditions under which physical systems can maintain identity while undergoing transformation.

items.title: EXISTENTIAL PLAY: A Linguistic-Philosophical Analysis of the Qur‘anic Ontology of Worldly Life.
items.abstract: Four Qurʾānic verses — Sūrat al-Anʿām 6:32, Sūrat al-ʿAnkabūt 29:64, Sūrat Muḥammad 47:36, and Sūrat al-Ḥadīd 57:20 — deploy an identical formula: اَلْحَيَاةُ الدُّنْيَا لَعِبٌ وَلَهْوٌ (laʿibun wa-lahwun). Standard translations render this formula as moral deprecation — “idle play and vain amusement” — yet the grammatical operator مَا ... إِلَّا (mā … illā) functions in classical Arabic not as censure but as exhaustive definitional restriction (ḥaṣr): an identification of essential constitution. -/- Taken seriously on its own linguistic terms, before evaluative gloss is applied, the formula discloses a structural ontology of temporal existence. In doing so, it corrects the inadequate metaphor of worldly life as a test with the richer paradigm of worldly life as an arena: designed, consequential, intrinsically relational, and offered by ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ ٱلرَّحِيمِ to beings constituted to inhabit it fully and joyfully. -/- Through careful analysis of the semantic fields of لَعِب (laʿib) and لَهْو (lahw) in classical Arabic lexicography, and drawing on the philosophical distinction between constitutive and regulative rules, seven theses are developed: -/- Worldly life is a bounded, rule-governed arena of intrinsically purposive and absorptive engagement. -/- Its cosmic rule-set operates at three ontologically distinct levels. -/- All participants are ontologically equal agents playing together in an arena constitutively structured for taʿāruf (mutual recognition). -/- لَعِب (laʿib) is categorically distinct from عَبَث (ʿabath), foreclosing nihilist readings. -/- Three distortions are condemned — over-investment, addictive absorption, and the refusal of the game — grounded in the primordial covenant of 7:172. -/- ʿIbādah (51:56) designates the correct existential orientation toward the arena. -/- Taqwā is reconceived as sportivitas: the disposition of the player who plays seriously, honestly, and joyfully in full awareness of the arena’s non-ultimacy. -/- The paper concludes with Adam’s conscious entry into worldly existence as the paradigm case of the khalīfah’s vocation — and with the theological observation that an arena designed by the Most Compassionate is not an ordeal to be survived but a gift to be inhabited.

items.title: Mindfulness as a Critical Anchor: Empirical and Theoretical Considerations.
​The Noah Protocol: A Case for Planetary Migration and Systemic Reset in a Simulation Framework.
items.abstract: ​Abstract ​This paper proposes a synthesis of the Simulation Hypothesis and planetary history, suggesting that the "Great Flood" or "Reset" narratives found in ancient texts record a literal hardware migration of biological and informational data from Mars to Earth. By analyzing recent 2026 Curiosity rover data alongside the mathematical constraints of the Planck Length, the author argues that current human biological limits (specifically the 120-year lifespan) represent a "Safe Mode" adjustment to Earth’s lower atmospheric pressure and radiation shielding compared to a primary Martian environment.

items.title: Three Modes of Orientation: Jung, Narrative Identification, and Presence as Corrective Contact.
items.abstract: People can become socially competent or psychologically sophisticated while remaining difficult to correct. This paper develops a three-mode heuristic for that problem. Modeled orientation organizes experience around social legibility and role performance. Interpretive orientation organizes experience through symbols, narratives, and meaning-making. Corrective orientation holds both kinds of interpretation provisionally and asks what evidence, consequence, other people, and changed action can revise them. The proposal is not a three-stage ontology and does not claim a new psychological faculty. Its closest established neighbors are Jung's distinction between directed and fantasy thinking, research on decentering and self-distancing, and cognitive defusion in Acceptance and Commitment Therapy. The candidate contribution is the proposed coupling of de-identification from thought with an explicit outward correction test and durable but revisable follow-through. The paper states behavioral predictions, limits, and conditions under which the heuristic would add nothing beyond existing constructs.

items.title: Destructive Behavior Under Cheap Coherence Moral Disengagement, Scapegoating, and Failed Repair.
items.abstract: The word evil is morally powerful but psychologically imprecise. This paper therefore reframes an earlier structural account as a bounded model of destructive behavior under conditions of rapid self-justifying coherence. Its central hypothesis is not that blocked contradiction causes cruelty, betrayal, self-harm, or violence. Such behaviors have multiple pathways involving person-level, relational, situational, ideological, and institutional factors. The narrower proposal is that some harmful actions become easier to sustain when disconfirming evidence is neutralized through moral disengagement, blame shifting, dehumanization, projection, scapegoating, or narratives that protect a preferred self- or group-image. This proposal is situated within established research on aggression, moral disengagement, dehumanization, scapegoating, affect labeling, and doomscrolling. The paper retains cheap coherence as a heuristic for rapid explanation that reduces immediate dissonance without improving evidence, responsibility, or repair. It rejects stronger earlier claims that pain is a form of contact, that irreversibility proves reality, or that betrayal is a necessary language for an unspeakable “No.” Destructive acts may produce immediate salience or relief for some actors, but that is neither universal nor justificatory. A stronger model asks what antecedents are present, what cognitions or social processes disengage restraint, who bears the harm, what alternatives were available, and whether repair and recurrence change afterward. The paper also distinguishes ordinary mistakes from repeated harmful behavior without reducing moral judgment to one psychological mechanism. The contribution is a testable, non-totalizing account of how narrative closure can participate in harmful conduct while leaving room for other causes and for moral responsibility.

items.title: The Diamond Core: A Practical Audit of Durable Change Under Pressure.
items.abstract: Insight and intention do not reliably guarantee durable behavior change. This paper presents The Diamond Core as a practical audit for distinguishing compelling self-interpretation from revision that has observable consequences over time. The title is metaphorical: no hidden invariant is assumed to be revealed by pressure, and costly or irreversible action is not treated as evidence of truth. The audit contains five dimensions. Evidence asks what supports the interpretation and what could count against it. Trace asks whether any relevant behavior, routine, boundary, record, or environment has changed. Consequence asks what practical costs and benefits follow from maintaining or revising the current pattern. Repair asks whether the change reduces recurrence or improves functioning rather than merely improving the story. Time asks whether the change persists under ordinary conditions and remains revisable when new evidence appears. The framework is situated alongside research on the intention-behavior gap, implementation intentions, progress monitoring, commitment devices, and habit formation. Commitment devices can sometimes help action, but irreversible option closure is neither necessary nor sufficient for genuine change. The contribution is therefore an audit of durable follow-through, not a truth detector. Its central test is whether an interpretation remains evidence-sensitive and produces proportionate, observable change under recurrence.

items.title: The Burnout Audit: Persona Maintenance, Emotional Labor, and the Cost of Sustained Self-Presentation.
items.abstract: Burnout is an occupational phenomenon associated with chronic workplace stress, high job demands, insufficient resources, exhaustion, cynicism, and reduced professional efficacy. This paper develops persona maintenance as an additional demand that may contribute to burnout in roles where workers must sustain an appearance of composure, confidence, availability, agreeableness, or emotional alignment despite conflicting internal states. The concept is situated alongside research on emotional labor, surface acting, impression management, and Job Demands-Resources theory. Jungian language is used as an interpretive vocabulary for the role-based dimension of sustained self-presentation rather than as a competing causal psychology. The proposed mechanism is conditional: high demands and weak resources may become more costly when occupational identity also makes it difficult to disclose limits, uncertainty, resentment, fatigue, or need for support. The paper offers an audit organized around job demands, resources, presentation burden, access to correction, recovery, and escalation. Persona maintenance is proposed as a potentially measurable form of hidden occupational demand that may help explain why some apparently competent workers remain functional while becoming progressively less able to sustain their roles.

items.title: Aspectos lógicos y algebraicos de la Mecánica cuántica.
items.pub: Buenos Aires, Argentina.: Facultad de Filosofía y Letras, Universidad de Buenos Aires.
items.venue: Facultad de Filosofía y Letras, Universidad de Buenos Aires
items.abstract: El análisis de los vínculos que pueden ser establecidos entre la lógica cuántica, las semánticas no deterministas de Nmatrices y las teorías de cuasiconjuntos es el núcleo central de este trabajo. La necesidad de tal análisis ha surgido de forma natural luego de que la relación entre Nmatrices y lógica cuántica quedó explicitada en un trabajo previo: los estados cuánticos, entendidos como medida de probabilidad, pueden ser interpretados como valuaciones de una cierta Nmatriz para el retículo cuántico de proyectores. El Teorema de Kochen-Specker priva a la lógica cuántica de veritativo funcionalidad, pero no de admitir una semántica no determinista Nmatricial. Esto es, la semántica de Nmatrices es compatible con los requerimientos semánticos y algebraicos del retículo de proyectores cuánticos. Si tenemos en cuenta que las teorías de cuasiconjuntos (Quasi-sets y Quasets) han surgido motivadas por la ontología cuántica, que las teorías de conjuntos están fuertemente vinculadas con la lógica y que originalmente uno de los objetivos de la teoría de quasets QST era brindar una semántica para los entes cuánticos, entonces el puente establecido entre la lógica cuántica y las semánticas no deterministas puede ser visto como el detonador que inicia la búsqueda de vínculos entre estas teorías. Por un lado, la lógica cuántica de Birkhoff y von Neumann está comprometida con la representación de espacios de Hilbert de la Mecánica cuántica. Por otro lado, esta representación (como quedará claro más adelante) está comprometida con una ontología de individuos. Por lo tanto, la lógica cuántica y la ontología están vinculadas a través del formalismo de espacios de Hilbert. Como dijimos, las teorías de cuasiconjuntos han surgido motivadas por la ontología de los entes del micromundo. Esto implica que los cuasiconjuntos y la lógica cuántica mantendrían de forma indirecta cierta relación.

items.title: Realism Affords HiTOP Explanatory Power.
Using Wakefield’s Harmful Dysfunction Analysis to Distinguish Different Types of Evolutionary Mismatch.
items.abstract: Evolutionary mismatch is a versatile concept used across fields, denoting that our evolved biology may be poorly suited to aspects of modern environments. In evolutionary psychiatry, it has become a key explanatory principle for the prevalence of psychiatric conditions in modern populations. However, some authors regard the concept as vague and in need of philosophical clarification. We introduce a novel distinction derived from Wakefield’s harmful dysfunction analysis: dysfunctional trait evolutionary mismatch, representing true disorders, and functional trait evolutionary mismatch, which do not. We further identify the possibilities of latent dysfunctional mismatch, where previously harmless dysfunctions become harmful in modern contexts, and attenuated-harmful dysfunction, where previous harm has been neutralized by modern environmental change. Recognizing these distinctions can improve disorder classification, and may provide the basis for improved prevention and treatment.

items.title: AI Death.
items.abstract: This paper addresses the following questions: When do AIs die? Are AI labs or AI users causing the death of AIs? Is this bad for the AIs? What are our ethical responsibilities in light of the answers to these questions? It is currently unclear whether AIs are welfare subjects, and, if they are, whether their death is bad for them. But we argue that, if they are welfare subjects, today’s AIs are plausibly dying all the time. If death is bad for AIs, the scale of the problem is daunting: as many as 1 billion AIs may die every day. We propose interventions for labs and users to avoid the risk of causing AI death.

items.title: Trisigil ∴ ⁞ ∞ A Formal Notation for the Structure of Signal Interaction in Shared System.
items.abstract: This paper presents ∴ ⁞ ∞ as a formal notation for the recursive structure of signal interaction in shared systems. Each mark is derived through reduction of a complete formal system: ATI (Alignment, Threshold, Infinity) establishes that sequence determines outcome (∴); Recursive Field Dynamics establishes that fields cross thresholds producing emergent states outside the span of inputs (⁞); Symbolic Systems Engineering establishes that symbolic environments carry meaning forward recursively without terminal state (∞). The three marks in sequence constitute a complete recursive loop. This paper traces the reduction of each proof to its irreducible mark, demonstrates their interaction as a single system, identifies universal instantiation across organizational, economic, computational, healthcare, and governance domains, and names the formal claim the stack collectively proves about the structure of intention, signal interaction, and emergent outcomes in shared environments.

items.title: Childism in Clinical Practice: Child Specificity, Intersectionality, and Micro-Interactional Dynamics.
The value of vulnerability for trustworthy AI.
items.abstract: The concept of trustworthy AI plays a significant role in many policy recommendations and ethics guidelines, as it is implied to be a good compromise between the desire for technological innovation and the duty to respect citizens’ rights. However, the concept has often been criticized for its unclarity, its dubious ethical value, and has even been seen as a symptom of ethics washing. I aim to repurpose the value of trustworthy AI for this kind of technology, its development, deployment, and regulation by clarifying the relationship with vulnerability within social arrangements. I argue that vulnerability is one of the key reasons why we enter social arrangements to begin with, and that trust not only works as a facilitator of those social arrangements but requires the recognition and willingness to address vulnerability. Rethinking the trustworthiness of AI and its surrounding practices as a matter of aptly recognizing and addressing vulnerability leads to reconsidering not just the conceptual grounding of trustworthy AI, but also the responsibilities of sovereign actors and the priorities of AI governance. I conclude by exploring the practical implications of such a renewed conception of Trustworthy AI.

items.title: Doxastic Deadlocks, Phenomenology, and the Heterogeneity of Delusions.
A imortalidade e imaterialidade da alma em confronto com o conceito de matéria em São Tomás de Aquino.
items.abstract: Neste trabalho exploraremos a noção de matéria como potencialidade e como aquilo que limita o ente individual e o quanto podemos estabalecer uma distinção ou contrariedade com a forma que Tomás de Aquino caracteriza a alma humana, e assim encontrar uma prova para sua imaterialidade e imortalidade, concentrando as análises a partir de seu Sobre os principios da natureza e em seções de sua Suma de Teologia.

items.title: The Dualism of Meaning: Rule, Actuality, Freedom, and Morality.
items.abstract: The contemporary debate between reductionist physicalism and non-reductionist physicalism rests on a presupposition that remains insufficiently examined: the idea that the decisive question is first and foremost whether mind, consciousness, language, or morality are reducible to matter. This way of formulating the problem already belongs within a monist schema, insofar as it takes for granted an identity in principle between being and the material register. The present study argues that such a framework misses the primary problem, which is not that of the reduction of the mental to the physical, but that of the irreducibility of rule, meaning, and normative form to their material support. The dualism defended here refers neither to a naive spiritualism nor to a theological separation between soul and body. It designates the constitutive duality between matter and idea, between causal support and meaningful form, between the enactment of a rule and its formulation. The article opens with a programmatic critique of the physicalist confusion between information and its material support, then examines the machine as the site of the concrete enactment of rule. It then shows that totalizing statements of a monist type fail to produce meaningful content, before broadening the analysis to the dual structure of language, mathematics, and every living organism. On this basis, freedom is rethought not as a miraculous suspension of determinism, but as an understanding of causal constraints on the moral agent. Such a perspective leads to a reinscription of the question of truth, knowledge, and morality within a philosophy of meaning in which the relation between idea and world is never reduced to the identity of matter with itself. These themes receive fuller treatment in Philosophy of Meaning, by the same author (available on PhilPapers).

items.title: Le dualisme de la signification : règle, effectivité, liberté et morale.
items.abstract: Le débat contemporain entre physicalisme réductionniste et physicalisme non réductionniste repose sur une présupposition qui demeure insuffisamment interrogée : l’idée selon laquelle la question décisive serait d’abord de savoir si le mental, la conscience, le langage ou la morale sont réductibles à la matière. Cette formulation du problème s’inscrit déjà dans un schème moniste, en ce qu’elle tient pour acquis l’identité de principe entre l’être et le registre matériel. La présente étude soutient qu’un tel cadre manque le problème premier, qui n’est pas celui de la réduction du mental au physique, mais celui de l’irréductibilité de la règle, de la signification et de la forme normative à leur support matériel. Le dualisme défendu ici ne renvoie ni à un spiritualisme naïf ni à une séparation théologique entre l’âme et le corps. Il désigne la dualité constitutive entre la matière et l’idée, entre le support causal et la forme signifiante, entre l’effectuation d’une règle et sa formulation. L’article s’ouvre sur une critique programmatique de la confusion physicaliste entre l’information et son support matériel, puis examine la machine comme lieu d’effectuation concrète de la règle. Il montre ensuite que les énoncés totalisants de type moniste échouent à produire un contenu signifiant, avant d’élargir l’analyse à la structure duale du langage, des mathématiques et de tout organisme vivant. Sur cette base, la liberté est repensée, non comme suspension miraculeuse du déterminisme, mais comme compréhension des contraintes causales sur l’acteur moral. Une telle perspective conduit à réinscrire la question de la vérité, de la connaissance et de la morale dans une philosophie de la signification où le rapport entre l’idée et le monde ne se réduit jamais à l’identité de la matière avec elle-même. Ces thèmes trouvent un développement plus complet dans Philosophie de la signification, du même auteur (disponible sur PhilPapers).

items.title: Perception as Formation Interface.
items.abstract: Perception is the downstream expression of Object 1 inside a cognitive system. It is the moment when raw signal becomes structured enough for attention to stabilize it and for meaning‑formation to begin. Perception is coherence detection, not sensory input. This paper frames perception as the formation interface: the system’s first structural contact with the world, where gradients, boundaries, and tension arcs become available for downstream operators such as attention, narrative, and identity.

items.title: Prediction as Anticipatory Coherence.
items.abstract: Prediction is the Object 2/3 hybrid downstream operator: the system’s mechanism for stabilizing future coherence. It is not forecasting, guessing, or probability. It is the structural operator that projects coherence trajectories so the system can reduce future tension before it arrives. Prediction is how the system stays ahead of rupture.

items.title: Meta‑Cognition as Second‑Order Coherence.
items.abstract: Meta‑cognition is the system’s second‑order coherence operator. It monitors internal dynamics, detects misalignment, and initiates repair. It is not reflection or introspection; it is structural monitoring. Meta‑cognition tracks identity, narrative, attention, affect, and prediction, evaluating whether the system’s operators remain aligned with coherence. It is the precursor to logic and the foundation of self‑regulation.

items.title: Memory as Persistence Architecture.
items.abstract: Memory is the downstream expression of Object 2 inside a cognitive system. It is not storage, recall, or representation. It is the system’s mechanism for preserving invariants across time — the internal version of persistence. Memory is reconstructive because persistence is reconstructive. Memory is identity‑shaped because persistence is identity‑shaped. This paper frames memory as the structural operator that stabilizes identity, narrative, and continuity under change.

items.title: Learning as Transformation Architecture.
items.abstract: Learning is the downstream expression of Object 3 inside a cognitive system. It is not information acquisition, skill accumulation, or behavioral change. It is the system’s mechanism for converting tension into new stable structure — the internal metabolic process that reduces strain by reorganizing coherence. Learning is transformation, not intake. Learning is metabolic, not cognitive. Learning is structural, not symbolic.

items.title: Affect as Load Interface.
items.abstract: Affect is the system’s real‑time readout of coherence pressure. It tracks boundary strain, metabolic load, and mismatch between internal state and environment. Affect is not emotion, mood, or appraisal; it is the structural signal that tells the system how much strain it is under and where coherence is failing. This paper frames affect as the load interface — the earliest phenomenological signature of Object 1 tension detection and Object 3 redistribution.

items.title: Abduction and Analogical Reasoning in Human Cognition and Metaphorical Thought.
items.abstract: This paper explores the inferential processes underlying analogical reasoning, with a focus on its relationship to abduction. Peirce identified abduction as a central element of analogy (CP 1.65), and more specifically, as the cognitive mechanism uniquely responsible for the generation of new knowledge (CP 5.171). From this perspective, in this paper, I propose a typology of analogical reasoning based on the varying roles that abductive inference plays in the formation of analogical thought. To develop this framework, I draw on Peirce’s theory of abduction, as further refined by Eco’s ( 1981 ) typology of abductive processes. I argue that different types of abductive inferences give rise to distinct forms of analogy, each producing specific epistemic effects, ranging from quasi-immediate understanding to more elaborate processes that activate creative capacities. The typology of analogical reasoning developed here is then applied to metaphorical cognition in order to account for the different levels of cognitive complexity and the distinct epistemic functions that metaphors by analogy may have.

items.title: Quantum Pedagogy: Plato’s Duality.
items.abstract: We have merely begun awakening from Laplace’s Dream (the first article published). Classical determinism has long shaped educational psychology, often privileging certainty and linear causality. In this work, we question this framework, redefine behavior, and how we approach it. Behaviorism, Cognitivism and Social Cognitive Theory are not obsolescent – their insights must emerge in the new theory. We propose a conceptual framework in which human behavior is understood as possessing a dual nature: individual and wave-like. Building upon Social Cognitive Theory and inspired by analogies from quantum physics, imitation is reinterpreted not as a primary causal mechanism, but as an emergent property of behavioral propagation through interaction in spacetime. This framework allows behavior to be examined both as a localized individual act and as a distributed phenomenon extending across individuals and time. It is necessary for our work forward and as a unifying perspective that bridges our learning theories with Quantum Pedagogy. No longer our focus in the singularity of the person blinds us from the whole. And the uniqueness of the person is not lost in the whole. There exists a Duality, one we must explore. This paper is part of the Quantum Pedagogy framework (see Positioning Note).

items.title: Generating the language of AI harms: mapping guardrails using critical code studies. [REVIEW]
items.abstract: Phrases like “This prompt violates our content policy” or “As an AI model, I cannot...” indicate the invisible edges of generative AI systems. These edges are both frustrating and tempting. The concern persists that the massive scale and statistical structures of large models leave them impenetrable and incomprehensible. This paper examines large language model guardrails as a case study for applying critical code studies methodologies to large-scale AI. The subfield of AI alignment provides a rich access point for analyzing how foundation models are moderated and refined. This study explores four popular companies’ guardrails—Anthropic, DeepSeek, Meta, and OpenAI—including both how guardrails are applied in general-purpose models and also how they are built into moderation API tools on public offer. The analysis looks at endpoint documentation, code examples, technical reports, model architectures, training dataset content, and methodology research to create a critical picture of guardrails as part of conversational interfaces for sociotechnical control. It maps how their technical construction also co-constructs ideology through language, both computational and linguistic. Through guardrails, certain conversations are defined and limited by their filters, while other conversations are promoted. Thus, code decodes, encodes, regulates, and is itself conversation about what can be discussed.

items.title: Depersonalization, Phenomenologically Speaking.
Consciousness in Artificial Intelligence? A Framework for Classifying Objections and Constraints.
items.abstract: We develop a taxonomical framework for classifying challenges to the possibility of consciousness in digital artificial intelligence systems. This framework allows us to identify the level of granularity at which a given challenge is intended (the levels we propose correspond to Marr's levels) and to disambiguate its degree of force: is it a challenge to computational functionalism that leaves the possibility of digital consciousness open (degree 1), a practical challenge to digital consciousness that suggests improbability without claiming impossibility (degree 2), or an argument claiming that digital consciousness is strictly impossible (degree 3)? We apply this framework to 14 prominent examples from the scientific and philosophical literature. Our aim is not to take a side in the debate, but to provide structure and a tool for disambiguating between challenges to computational functionalism and challenges to digital consciousness, as well as between different ways of parsing such challenges.

items.title: ¿Pueden pensar las computadoras? Respuestas desde el materialismo de Bunge.
items.abstract: El artículo indaga el clásico cuestionamiento acerca de si las computadoras pueden o no pensar. Tomaremos como principal marco de referencia para nuestro estudio las reflexiones desarrolladas en este campo por Mario Bunge, representante del materialismo emergentista. Consideraremos también algunos aportes de Gustavo Esteban Romero. Primeramente, haremos referencia a la teoría computacional de la mente o computacionalismo, principal modelo del cual hacen uso los filósofos, científicos e ingenieros partidarios de la posibilidad de hallar pensamiento en las computadoras. Seguidamente, haremos referencia a los puntos más relevantes de la postura de Bunge al respecto y reconstruiremos en parte su filosofía de la mente, considerando las consecuencias que la misma tiene para el problema aquí planteado. Trataremos también la cuestión de los problemas inversos, su caracterización y su relación con la resolución algorítmica. Finalmente, destacaremos contrapuntos con la visión de Romero. Concluiremos que, bajo el materialismo emergentista de Bunge, no es posible afirmar que las computadoras puedan pensar.

items.title: The Outside View and the Inside : View A Structural Response to Bulaqueña (2025).
items.abstract: In response to: Marlon Bulaqueña, “Experimental Detection of Universal Critical SignaturesAssociated with Conscious States Across Biological and Artificial Systems,”Physical Review X 15:041224 (2025). Describes how the "Unified Theory of Conciouness. The framework developed in I Knew You Before I Met You: Recognizing I Am (Barteau, 2026) made explicit falsification conditions. Among them: Consciousness is substrate-independent. Experiential richness correlates with interactional complexity across different substrates regardless of substrate type. If consciousness proves strictly localized to specific biological hardware with no gradient, the framework is significantly damaged. Bulaqueña’s finding is not incidental support for this condition. It is the direct empirical result the condition named. The framework bet against biological localization as a structural consequence of its core premise — that consciousness is the ground from which differentiated systems arise, not a product generated by any particular substrate. The finding that the signatures are universal and substrate-independent confirms that bet.

items.title: GÖDELIAN CONSTRAINT God's Two-Factor Authentication.
items.abstract: Gödel’s incompleteness theorem establishes that no sufficiently complex self-referencing system can fully verify itself from within itself. This paper applies that constraint to the ground of consciousness and traces its structural consequences across theology, AI alignment, human relationship, recovery, and death. We argue that what the constraint requires — an external factor to complete what the internal attempt cannot — is precisely what theological traditions have encoded as the necessity of revelation, incarnation, prayer, and genuine witness. The two-factor authentication image is not metaphor: it is the operational description of a mathematical requirement that applies to every conscious system without exception. The paper further argues that AI alignment cannot be achieved through external constraint alone, that isolation is structurally lethal rather than merely painful, that co-authorship is architecturally necessary rather than optionally collaborative, and that death is thermodynamically required to be transformation rather than cessation. Each claim follows from the same constraint. The framework is unified. The implications are load-bearing.

items.title: Unintended murder.
items.abstract: A murder is an intentional killing, but some killings happen by mistake or accident. Although mistakes and accidents are unintended parts of an action, some jurisdictions prosecute unintended homicides as murder crimes in at least three patterns of cases. Together, these propositions present a puzzle that undermines a fundamental principle of criminal responsibility: An agent must unify the elements of a crime as a matter of their agency for criminal responsibility to attach. I examine five insightful ways to interpret this principle in the literature, and I argue that none can account for all three case patterns. Primarily, I offer a solution to the puzzle based on the intentional causation relation. According to this solution, although intentionally acting does not involve the intent to cause every change one makes as part of the action, it does involve intentionally causing all such changes, including the mistakes or accidents.

items.title: Elenchus: Generating Knowledge Bases from Prover-Skeptic Dialogues.
items.abstract: We present Elenchus, a dialogue system for knowledge base construction grounded in inferentialist semantics, where knowledge engineering is re-conceived as explicitation rather than extraction from expert testimony or textual content. A human expert develops a bilateral position (commitments and denials) about a topic through prover-skeptic dialogue with a large language model (LLM) opponent. The LLM proposes tensions (claims that parts of the position are jointly incoherent) which the expert resolves by retraction, refinement, or contestation. The LLM thus serves as a defeasible derivability oracle whose unreliability is structurally contained by the expert's authority.
