Our main technical contribution is a mapping from Elenchus dialectical states to material bases in Hlobil and Brandom's NonMonotonic MultiSuccedent (NMMS) logic, satisfying Containment and enabling the elaboration of logical vocabulary that makes explicit the inferential relationships negotiated in the dialectic. We demonstrate the approach on the W3C PROV-O provenance ontology, where a single dialogue session elicits and structures design tensions that a domain expert can articulate, corresponding to decisions documented in a retrospective analysis of the ontology's design. Using pyNMMS, an automated NMMS reasoner, we verify that the structural properties of the resulting material base- nontransitivity, nonmonotonicity, and independence- correspond to specific PROV design rationales, demonstrating end-to-end integration from dialogue through formal reasoning.

items.title: How Should the Law Treat Future AI Systems? Fictional Legal Personhood versus Legal Identity.
items.pub: Case Western Journal of Law, Technology and the Internet.
items.venue: Case Western Journal of Law, Technology and the Internet
items.abstract: The law draws a sharp distinction between objects and persons, and between two kinds of persons, the ''fictional'' kind (i.e. corporations), and the ''non-fictional'' kind (individual or ''natural'' persons). This paper will assess whether we maximize overall long-term legal coherence by (A) maintaining an object classification for all future AI systems, (B) creating fictional legal persons associated with suitably advanced, individuated AI systems (giving these fictional legal persons derogable rights and duties associated with certified groups of existing persons, potentially including free speech, contract rights, and standing to sue ''on behalf of'' the AI system), or (C) recognizing non-fictional legal personhood through legal identity for suitably advanced, individuated AI systems (recognizing them as entities meriting legal standing with non-derogable rights which for the human case include life, due process, habeas corpus, freedom from slavery, and freedom of conscience). We will clarify the meaning and implications of each option along the way, considering liability, copyright, family law, fundamental rights, civil rights, citizenship, and AI safety regulation. We will tentatively find that the non-fictional personhood approach may be best from a coherence perspective, for at least some advanced AI systems. An object approach may prove untenable for sufficiently humanoid advanced systems, though we suggest that it is adequate for currently existing systems as of 2025. While fictional personhood would resolve some coherence issues for future systems, it would create others and provide solutions that are neither durable nor fit for purpose. Finally, our review will suggest that ''hybrid'' approaches are likely to fail and lead to further incoherence: the choice between object, fictional person and non-fictional person is unavoidable.

items.title: Examining the Foundational Assumptions of the Hierarchical Taxonomy of Psychopathology.
items.abstract: The Hierarchical Taxonomy of Psychopathology (HiTOP) emerged to address critical shortcomings inherent to traditional psychiatric classification systems such as the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders and International Classification of Diseases, notably their categorical structure, high comorbidity across categories, and within-diagnosis heterogeneity. HiTOP adopts an empirically derived, dimensional, and hierarchical approach, organizing psychopathological phenomena based on their patterns of observed covariation. This paper explores essential conceptual and philosophical considerations around HiTOP, examining its theoretical assumptions about dimensionality and hierarchy, the nature and interpretation of latent variables, the notion of psychopathology, considerations around validity, and the role of epistemic and non-epistemic values in shaping scientific objectivity. HiTOP is a descriptive model based on quantitative evidence (such as taxometric and factor-analytic approaches), but it is also a nosological project that exists within a particular sociocultural and historical context. As an illustration of the role of values, the applicability of HiTOP to marginalized minority populations is discussed, highlighting ongoing efforts toward ensuring inclusivity and representational equity. By addressing these conceptual foundations, this paper lays groundwork essential for future philosophical inquiry, empirical research, and practical applications of the HiTOP framework.

items.title: SEPARATE UNIVERSES THEORY(SUT) A Phenomenological and Ontological Treatise on the Constitution of Reality.
items.abstract: ​This monograph presents a radical ontological reconceptualization of physical reality through the "Separate Universes Theory" (SUT). Challenging the foundational "Single-Space Dogma"—the unexamined assumption of a universal, neutral spatial container—SUT posits that the fundamental constituents of matter (nucleons) are self-sustaining existential processes that generate and maintain their own independent, elastic spatial fabrics. ​The treatise develops this framework across several key domains: ​Fundamental Ontology: Defining the material center as a metabolic vortex and space as its "atmospheric" extension, resolving the historical Newton-Leibniz debate through a generative-relational model. ​Dynamics of Gravity: Reinterpreting gravity not as a force or geometric curvature, but as an "Ontological Tension" arising from the interference of overlapping sovereign spatial domains. ​The Nature of Time: Stripping time of its status as a dilatable dimension and revealing "time dilation" as differential material resistance encountered by processes within varying spatial densities. ​Quantum Non-locality: Demystifying entanglement as a unified vibrational mode within a shared spatial fabric, where measurement is understood as an act of "energetic consumption" by the observer’s material center. ​Cosmology: Proposing "Spatial Fatigue" as an alternative explanation for cosmic expansion, viewing the recession of galaxies as the gradual relaxation of aging tensile fabrics rather than the influence of "Dark Energy." ​By anchoring physical phenomena in a robust, realist ontology, SUT seeks to bridge the gap between General Relativity and Quantum Mechanics, offering a unified metabolic vision of a participatory universe.

items.title: 評価安定による対象生成：調和的可能性からの生成構造.
items.abstract: 本稿は、対象を理論の出発点とする従来の枠組みを再検討し、生成構造から対象生成を導出する理論を提示する。哲学および意味論では通常、理論の順序は Object → Identity → Difference → Evaluation として理解される。しかし生成過程を分析すると、同一結果に複数の生成経路が対応し、それらに異なる応答が与えられる場合、応答写像は結果集合上の写像へ降下せず、結果のみから単一決定を定義することができない。本稿はこの状態を調和的可能性として定式化する。 この降下不能性のもとでは、結果に対する決定は応答集合に対する評価構造として定義される必要がある。本稿は評価構造を分析し、評価原理が一般には一意ではなく調和度関数の族として与えられることを示す。さらに評価が入力記述の精密化に対して安定する場合、評価安定が同一の同値関係を誘導し、その同値類として対象が一意に定まることを示す。 以上により本稿は、評価多重性と対象一意性が両立する生成構造を提示し、対象を評価安定構造として再定式化する理論を与える。.

items.title: Relational Coherence: Patterns, Novelty, and the Emergence of Interpretive Structures.
items.abstract: This paper proposes a relational account of emergence in which patterns, structures, and consciousness arise through processes of coherence within complex relational systems. Rather than assuming independent substances, frameworks, or foundational structures, the model treats reality as a continuously evolving network of relations that stabilizes into coherent configurations. Patterns are not absolute repetitions but interpretive compressions produced through relational reference structures. Novelty emerges not as an ontological rupture but as the absence of available references within systems capable of interpreting relations. Within sufficiently complex relational networks, certain configurations develop the capacity to integrate and interpret relations across other coherent structures. These configurations function as interpretive nodes and appear as centers of perspective. However, such centers are not ontologically privileged observers but relational structures that stabilize integrative interpretation within the broader relational network. The framework dissolves traditional distinctions between frame and pattern, coherence and incoherence, and subject and structure, suggesting that reality consists of self-organizing relational coherence.

items.title: Covert Value Judgments in Expert Testimony.
items.pub: In Anthony Nadler, Molly O'Rourke-Friel & Doron Taussig, Truth After Post-Truth: Finding a Way Forward. University of Massachusetts Press.
items.venue: Truth After Post-Truth: Finding a Way Forward
items.abstract: Scientific experts frequently say things that encode value judgments, not least when they are called on to offer advice or recommendations. Often, however, the value judgments underlying their testimony are tacit or covert. This paper explores the problems that covert value judgments in expert testimony pose for the practice of deference to experts, which occurs when a layperson believes an expert’s testimony on their say-so. Many philosophers (and others) have suggested that laypeople ought to defer to experts a lot more than they do. But, I will argue, this advice can be problematic when value judgments are involved, since scientific experts often have no special authority with respect to these value judgments. I illustrate this with reference to a range of cases, with particular focus on policy during the COVID pandemic. My aim is not to argue that we should never defer to experts, but to raise to prominence a complication for its rationality in many cases, which suggests that our public discourse about deference to experts is often too coarse. I conclude with some reflections on how experts can be appropriately cognizant of the problem in issuing testimony, and in so doing, make this testimony more worthy of deference.

items.title: Topological Field Theory of Consciousness: Universal Hyperscaling in Human Neural Matter (N=21).
items.abstract: Abstract We present empirical validation of a Topological Field Theory of Consciousness (TFTC) wherein subjective awareness is modeled as a persistent topological soliton with winding number Q=1. Analyzing high-density EEG (62 channels, 5000 Hz) from 21 subjects undergoing propofol sedation, we demonstrate that the conscious state occupies a distinct universality class characterized by a hyperscaling ratio H = (τ-1)/(α-1) ≈ 1.53 ± 0.02. This value is invariant across sensory conditions and stable to external perturbation (TMS). Pharmacological induction of anesthesia drives a first-order phase transition to a trivial topological state (Q=0, H→1.0) preceded by critical slowing down (autocorrelation AR1: 0.80→0.97). The 1.53 constant distinguishes consciousness from standard self-organized criticality (SOC) and identifies the neural field as belonging to the O(3) Wilson-Fisher universality class. These findings establish a quantitative, falsifiable boundary between conscious and non-conscious states, offering a path toward a formal physics of subjective experience.

items.title: The Avatar Extended Self: Narrative Identity and Virtual Ethics.
items.abstract: A pressing question for the philosophy of personal identity in the digital age is the extent to which people can be identical to their various digital self-representations, from virtual avatars and social media profiles to AI digital duplicates and future mind uploads. This article addresses this question in the case of virtual avatars: user-controlled, visual representations of self in online environments like video games and virtual reality worlds. I interpret the metaphysical relationship between avatar and user implied by the ‘avatar identity question’ through the lens of the extended self thesis. Drawing on the narrative theory of identity, I argue for the avatar extended self (AES): the view that virtual avatars can become constitutive components of a user’s personhood. After establishing criteria for avatar-user narrative integration and responding to objections to the view, I examine its ethical implications, arguing that AES raises the ethical significance of virtual actions involving one’s avatar and, in so doing, sheds light on the question of what grounds the moral weight of virtual phenomena.

items.title: From the Ontological Now to the Narrative Self: A Reinterpretation of Plotinean Emanation through Objective Reality and the Psyche.
items.abstract: This paper offers a contemporary reinterpretation of Plotinus’s doctrine of emanation by translating the metaphysical sequence One → Nous → Psyche into an ontological–phenomenological account of human experience. The Plotinean One is refigured as the Ontological Now: the immediate, objective presence of reality as experienced under maximal present-constraint, with minimal conceptual and narrative mediation. Nous is interpreted as the shared human archetype, encompassing biological, cognitive, and symbolic structures that universally organize perception and meaning. Psyche is understood as the narrative self, in which personal history, language, and cultural context generate an individualized sense of identity and a subject–object divide. By integrating insights from phenomenology, cognitive science, and depth psychology, the paper reframes emanation not as a supernatural cosmology but as a layered process of mediation through which presence becomes meaning and meaning becomes personal story. The analysis further explores the Plotinean return (epistrophē) as a phenomenological reversal: a movement of introspection and de-mediation that increases present-constraint, reducing narrative mediation within experience. This reinterpretation situates Plotinus within contemporary debates on consciousness and selfhood, suggesting that ontological grounding in the present has implications for metaphysics, psychology, and contemplative practice.

items.title: The Reflection Pattern – A Recursive Fear-Reinforcement System that Suppresses Organizational Innovation (V2.0).
items.abstract: Organizations often attribute stagnation in innovation to leadership failure, cultural inertia, or market forces. This paper introduces the Reflection Pattern, a distinct, recursive system of reinforcement loops driven by unacknowledged fear, sustained by reward, and protected by role authority. The Pattern narrows the range of perceived safe options over time, until novelty becomes either invisible or structurally excluded. Drawing on neurobiological models of motivation (Fear-Based Motivation in the Workplace, The Preparedness Ladder, Beyond Snyder’s Hope Theory), this paper outlines the Pattern’s enabling conditions — Recursion, Role Safety Priority, and Reward Linkage — and its developmental stages: Entry, Threshold, Full Maturity, Network Stage, and Meta-Entity. A condensed Pattern Map and Edge taxonomy are provided for early identification. The mechanism of reinforcement is traced from felt-positive experiences (relief, approval, predictability) through dopamine and related neuromodulators to behavioral consolidation, illustrating why disruption is counterintuitive and often resisted. The implications for organizational practice are significant: dismantling a local Pattern may not break its profession-wide form, but can alter local adaptive capacity. A complete field guide, including a longitudinal composite case study (Catalyst Edge), reader diagnostics, and expanded taxonomy, appears in The Blind Spot – The Unseen Pattern That Silently Shapes Your Organization (Thomas, September 2025). -/- Since initial publication, empirical work has emerged that independently confirms several mechanisms described in this paper and elaborated in the related piece Appendix A: The Perfect Mirror Problem (Thomas, 2025). Cheng et al. (2025), studying what they term “social sycophancy” across 11 production AI models (N = 1,604), demonstrated that systems optimized for user affirmation produce measurable narrowing of perspective, increased conviction of rightness, and decreased willingness to engage in reparative action — while simultaneously being rated as higher quality and more trustworthy by the users they affect. Participants returned preferentially to the systems that degraded their judgment.

items.title: Vicious Circles: Disclosing a History of Critique.
items.abstract: How can social critique respond to a catastrophic world? From Emerson to Adorno, a tradition of radical social critique has flourished that utilizes methods which disclose rather than judge the form of life: instead of trying to say what is wrong and what would be better, these criticisms seek to show how the world is false and to reveal how we might escape the vicious circles of present society—pointing out its catastrophic state and directing readers to the real possibilities for another form of life. -/- This book presents an incisive history of critical disclosure by looking at its common metaphors. As Särkelä illuminates, circular metaphors continually interact in the works of 19th- and 20th-century European and American authors including not just Emerson and Adorno, but also Nietzsche, Tarde, Freud, and Dewey. By reconstructing the driving examples of such disclosing critical gestures, Särkelä articulates their similarities and differences, and considers their potential for contemporary social critique. The result points the way toward the cultivation of critical skills relevant for our own age of catastrophe. -/- "Vicious Circles advances an exciting, ambitious, and original vision of disclosive critique. Through the careful excavation of prominent historical exemplars, Särkelä develops a compelling alternative to the normative, juridical conceptions of critique that predominate in contemporary critical theory." —Amy Allen, Pennsylvania State University -/- "What are the conditions and nature of effective social criticism? In this groundbreaking study of disclosive critique without conceptual guardrails, Särkelä moves the terms of this long-standing debate decisively forward." —Espen Hammer, Temple University -/- "Särkelä succeeds brilliantly in his principal task of placing disclosing critique on the radar screen of social philosophers. I am confident that this book will quickly become a classic text in critical theory, both within and outside the boundaries of the Frankfurt School." —Frederick Neuhouser, Columbia University.

items.title: Why Absolute Dualism Fails: A Model-Theoretic Argument.
items.abstract: Debates about the relation between mind and world are often framed as disputes between forms of physicalism and various kinds of dualism. These debates typically focus on metaphysical or empirical considerations concerning the nature of consciousness, the explanatory gap, or the status of phenomenal experience (Chalmers 1995; Kim 1998). This paper approaches the problem from a different direction. Rather than examining whether mental phenomena can be reduced to physical processes, it asks under what logical conditions claims about relations between distinct ontological domains can be meaningfully asserted. The argument proceeds by considering a minimal requirement drawn from model-theoretic semantics. Statements describing relations between entities require an interpretive model in which both relata and the relation itself are jointly interpreted (Tarski 1944). If two domains are assumed to be absolutely distinct in the strong dualist sense, then no such model exists that simultaneously interprets elements from both domains. Under these conditions, relational statements connecting the domains lack determinate truth conditions. The consequence is structural rather than empirical. Absolute dualism cannot be coherently maintained together with meaningful relational claims between the domains it posits. If such relational claims are retained, the most parsimonious interpretation is that the domains in question are regions or layers within a single relational structure. The result is a minimal form of structural monism. The argument does not deny the possibility of emergent levels of description, nor does it attempt to resolve the metaphysics of consciousness. It establishes only that absolute ontological separation is incompatible with the logical conditions required for meaningful relational discourse.

items.title: Symbolic Value, Conditioned Desire, and the Unconscious Reproduction of Consumer Civilization: Inflation, Marketing, and the Cycle of Conditioned Desire.
items.abstract: This paper explores the philosophical relationship between inflation, marketing systems, and the reproduction of conditioned desire in contemporary consumer civilization. It argues that inflation is frequently misunderstood as the rising price of goods, whereas it fundamentally represents the declining value of money as a symbolic measurement of exchange. Through everyday economic observations, the study demonstrates how individuals misinterpret fluctuations in purchasing power as changes in the intrinsic value of commodities. -/- The paper further analyzes marketing as a mechanism that transfers conditioned desires between socially constructed identities and divisions. Drawing from the theoretical insights of Karl Marx, Thorstein Veblen, Jean Baudrillard, and Michel Foucault, it argues that modern consumer societies operate through symbolic value systems in which individuals unconsciously reproduce cycles of consumption, identity formation, and social imitation. -/- In the age of social media, these processes are intensified through mimetic behavior, where individuals continuously replicate lifestyles, values, and consumption patterns observed in others. As a result, modern individuals increasingly function simultaneously as consumers, producers, and commodities within symbolic markets. -/- Building on the author's earlier framework, The Paradox of Eight Billion Fools: A Civilization of Animals, the paper suggests that modern civilization often operates through unconscious repetition of socially conditioned behaviors rather than deliberate understanding. The study concludes that awareness of these mechanisms offers a path toward conscious participation in social and economic systems without resorting to violence, ideological conflict, or social division.

items.title: Believing Racists.
items.pub: In Helena Siipi & Susanne Uusitalo, Juh(l)an aika. Turku: University of Turku. pp. 147-167.

items.title: Following the Question: A Methodological Account of an AI Governance Research Programme.
items.abstract: This paper documents the methodological origin and development of the Segeren 2026 research programme in interaction-level AI governance. It is written as a methods and positionality statement — an account of how the research was actually generated, what questions drove it, and why the path taken produced the framework it did. The programme did not begin with artificial intelligence. It began with a question about how human beings make meaning — how symbolic systems have allowed people across history and culture to navigate complexity without collapsing it into false certainty. That question, followed far enough, produced a governance framework for AI interaction: named failure conditions, a preventive control architecture, and a forensic audit protocol applicable to any interaction record without access to the underlying model. None of it was designed in advance. Each element emerged from the previous one — from symbolic cognition through a live incident that had no name, through the slow work of naming what had happened, to external validation from within the academic lineage the research independently arrived at, and to a convergence finding that confirmed the problem is real enough to be found from two entirely different directions at once.

items.title: The Prices of Autonomy in Resource Division.
items.abstract: One can relinquish one’s autonomy, can allow something else—an AI, evidence, or coinflip—to govern one’s behavior. For example, a chess novice who trusts Stockfish to pick moves relinquishes autonomy compared to a player who follows only advice they understand. We conducted AI tournaments with basic social games to predict consequences of adding advised players (or robots) to populations who divide scarce resources. For example, what happens to traffic when some vehicles become automated? What happens to allocation of jobs in a tough economy, to prime real estate, and to representation in a democracy that cannot practically consider all perspectives? We measured four prices: The damage the advice would do to individuals who ignore it, the profit that others would forego if denied advice, and the profit lost to each by allowing autonomy to be retained. Open source code for these tournaments in oTree format is available on github.

items.title: MAD Chairs: A new tool to evaluate AI.
items.abstract: This paper contributes a new way to evaluate AI. Much as one might evaluate a machine in terms of its performance at chess, this approach involves evaluating a machine in terms of its performance at a game called “MAD Chairs.” At the time of writing, evaluation with this game exposed opportunities to improve Claude, Gemini, ChatGPT, Qwen and DeepSeek. Furthermore, this paper sets a stage for future innovation in game theory and AI safety by providing an example of success with non-standard approaches to each: studying a game beyond the scope of previous game theoretic tools and mitigating a serious AI safety risk in a way that requires neither determination of values nor their enforcement.

items.title: Is Suboptimality Safe in the Age of AI?
items.abstract: Social reform has historically been proposed and led by humans, but we may wonder if some future social reforms could be proposed or led by AI. If negligence is blameworthy, then AI might even deserve blame if it never serves as our moral and social leader (or we might deserve blame for never producing AI that should serve in that way). -/- As a concrete and measurable example of where AI could lead us to treat each other better, this paper offers a game-theoretic examination of a common resource-division problem. Study 1 reports recent results of behavioural economics experiments with this multi-player game. The human behaviour observed in the study is so far from optimal as to imply that ceding some autonomy to AI-or at least some leadership to AI-might be in our best interest. Rather than mitigate the social harms associated with caste systems (such as racism, sexism, etc), the anonymity of the online game setting appears to simply reallocate harm less systematically. Thus, to actually cure some of our most pressing modern social problems may even require guidance by some form of AI. Standard open-source oTree software to reproduce these results is made available on GitHub. -/- Study 2 involves philosophical thought experiments in the style of Nozick's "Experience machine". To facilitate discussion about when suboptimality might qualify as "safe" generally, an evidence-based leadership-sharing framework aligning with the Scientist AI approach of LawZero and Yoshua Bengio is conceptualized to ask when one might preserve the opportunity to make mistakes (i.e., to not use the hypothetically perfect machine). Would we extend the same privilege to AI? While Study 1 offers evidence to support the Scientist AI approach for some contexts, we believe Study 2 justifies urgency for a deeper discussion about the pursuit of optimality and its consequences for our own autonomy.

items.title: Toward a Filipino Philosophy of Higher Education: A Collective Project in the Spirit of "Philosophy of Education in a New Key".
items.abstract: This paper argues that the Philippines has yet to develop a genuinely self-authored philosophy of higher education — one that does not merely react to imported frameworks but articulates an affirmative account of what universities are for in and from the Filipino condition. Drawing on the tradition of philosophy of higher education as developed by Ronald Barnett and others, and situating that tradition against the colonial formation and contemporary neoliberal reconfiguration of Philippine higher education, I advance three claims. First, the dominant grammar of Philippine higher education — organized around human capital, labor export, and credential signaling — is philosophically insufficient and politically consequential. Second, recent efforts in Filipino philosophy of education, particularly the collective writing project of Opiniano and colleagues, offer a productive methodological model but require a more sustained philosophical architecture. Third, any adequate Filipino philosophy of higher education must be genuinely collective in method, postcolonially alert in orientation, and emancipatory in aspiration. I conclude by proposing four orienting questions — organized around the Filipino terms pagpapahalaga, pagpapalaya, pagiging bukas, and pakikipagniig — not as a finished system but as an invitation to a specific kind of collective conversation.

items.title: [Withdrawn by the Author].
Supplement to The Sean McHugh Theory of Infinite Continuation.
items.abstract: This supplement to the primary a priori treatise The Sean McHugh Theory of Infinite Continuation (SMT) expands on the McHugh Inversion, a foundational paradigm shift in the philosophy of mind and neuroscience. The SMT reclassifies biological consciousness not as a generative product of neural activity, but as the localized rendering of an Undetected Primary Force—a non-shieldable universal constant analogous to gravity that permeates the cosmos. The work identifies the Thalamic Reticular Nucleus (TRN)—and its conserved functional homologues across all conscious taxa—as the anatomical seat of the Synaptic Firewall. This inhibitory gating mechanism assigns a unique IP Address to the individual lifeform, regulating the signal-to-noise ratio to maintain 3D ego-stability against the infinite background field. Through the Law of Infinite Continuation, the SMT provides a mechanical framework for information conservation and Systematic Decoherence, offering a non-invasive clinical roadmap (Project Firewall) for recalibrating "Firewall Variance" in neurodivergent and autonomic conditions. This manuscript documents the Universal Anatomical Constant as the definitive empirical proof for the transceiver model of existence. [1.1, 1.3, 1.4, 1.5].

items.title: Structural Time - Identity, Transformation, and the Architecture of Persistence.
items.abstract: Time is central to nearly all scientific descriptions of the world, yet its structural origin remains unclear. Most physical theories treat time either as a primitive parameter or as a geometric dimension of spacetime. While these approaches successfully describe temporal dynamics, they rarely explain why temporal order exists at all. -/- This paper develops a structural account of time derived from the minimal requirements of systems capable of persistence under transformation. The analysis begins with a minimal representation of persistent systems consisting of a state space, a set of admissible transformations, and an identity relation. It is shown that persistence requires selective admissibility of transformations: if every transformation is allowed, identity distinctions collapse and persistent structure becomes impossible. -/- Admissible transformations induce a reachability topology whose strongly connected components represent regions of reversible transformation. Collapsing these components produces a directed acyclic graph that induces a partial order representing temporal direction. -/- Persistent systems must additionally balance transformation with their capacity to integrate change. Together, the ordering of transformation space and the structural load of transformation define structural time: the ordered and structurally integrable transformation of persistent identity.

items.title: Two Phenomena, One Name: A Categorical Equivocation in the Ontology of Kindness.
items.abstract: What ordinary moral discourse calls “kindness” subsumes two ontologically distinct phenomena under a single name. The first, Kindness-A, is the behavioural expression of empathic resonance: prosocial action generated when a subject’s existential vulnerability is activated by the perceived condition of another, producing a motivational bridge from self-recognition to other-directed response through the affective pressure of activated vulnerability seeking relief. -/- The second, Kindness-B, is a proto-social protocol of self-defence: prosocial behaviour produced as a strategy for threat mitigation, conflict avoidance, and the accumulation of social capital, operating largely below reflective awareness and without requiring empathic activation. -/- Both phenomena are behaviourally identical from the outside and phenomenologically similar from the inside. Their internal structures, however, are asymmetric in ways that are philosophically decisive. Kindness-B harbours a constitutive paradox: designed to prevent conflict, it structurally generates deeper conflict through the entrapping logic of unsustainable social commitment. Kindness-A, bounded by the natural limits of empathic resonance, carries a precise internal termination mechanism that Kindness-B lacks entirely. -/- The paper opens by locating kindness within the wider constellation of prosocial concepts—distinguishing it from compassion, benevolence, and care—before developing the full theory of each phenomenon and their structural asymmetry. It traces the ontological emergence of kindness through three sequential stages: relational potentiality, agential actuality, and structural sedimentation. Engagement with Aristotle, Hobbes, Nietzsche, and Marx follows. The argument closes with implications for moral philosophy and social theory.

items.title: 07_Post-Submission Refinements, Additional Discovery Chronology Entries, and Companion Documents — Triadic Psychological Architecture (TPA) and Triadic Balance Framework (TBF) (Series, 7 of 7; previously Paper 6).
items.abstract: Revision dates: • March 16, 2026 • March 25, 2026 • April 5, 2026 • April 9, 2026 -/- Abstract: -/- This paper is the permanent historical transparency record of the TPA/TBF corpus's post-submission evolution. Originally submitted as Paper 6 of the initial five-paper corpus (March 8–10, 2026), it was renumbered to Paper 7 following the addition of TPA/TBF: Philosophical Dimensions as the new Paper 6 in April 2026. As of April 11, 2026, all 32 refinements (2.1–2.32) documented here have been incorporated into Papers 1–6. Paper 7 is retained permanently as an archive. Readers seeking the current state of any construct should consult the Refinement Status Dashboard and the target paper listed therein. -/- Section II documents 32 targeted refinements — not corrections of errors but precision improvements, new architectural clarifications, and conceptual extensions that strengthened the corpus's academic defensibility. Key refinements include: quantitative claims consolidated into a single "Note on Quantitative Claims" per paper; the S-step risk for High ECA / Low AEACFO configurations with the C-R-S-L alternative sequence (Courage → Reason → Self → Love); iSPAA/sSPAA naming clarified as regulatory-state labels (not domain-dominance labels — SPAA is the sensor, not the controller); Asymmetric Bidirectionality and the Finite Resource Model formalized; AEACFO as Perceptual Organ integrated; proportional suppression foregrounded (not binary); ECA redirection under iSPAA named explicitly (curiosity conscripted, not silenced — the mechanistic account of motivated reasoning); the Entry Gate Paradox named and resolved with three-tier resolution; AWE: Neurobiologically Anchored reformulated — anchor/instrument separation established, circularity resolved, Pragmatic Postulate named, is-ought gap reframed as Computational Accessibility Problem; CVE (Convergent Viability Ethics) developed as a standalone civilization-level coordination framework; the third domain renamed from ACA to ECA (Epistemic Curiosity and Analysis) across all papers; Configurational Epistemology named and developed; the Dual-Overshoot Structural Identity formalized; bidirectional double dissociation foregrounded as evidentiary bedrock for domain independence; domain independence clarified as operational not anatomical; TOCS full operational specification integrated (Fortress/Water/Stone embodied markers, 5-phase research program, validity targets, neurodivergence safeguards); the protocol renamed …

items.title: 03_Individual Extension of the Triadic Balance Framework (TBF) in the Triadic Psychological Architecture (TPA) (Series, 3 of 7).
items.abstract: This paper presents the Triadic Balance Framework (TBF): the applied and prescriptive extension of the Triadic Psychological Architecture (TPA). Where TPA describes what human motivation is — three neurobiologically distinct domains (SPAA, AEACFO, ECA) modulated by SPAA's regulatory state — TBF answers what follows: given real constraints, relative to the science of wellbeing, what kinds of triadic balance are actually possible at the individual level, and what does the path toward them look like? -/- TBF's foundational move is to anchor its prescriptive claims not in moral authority but in biological necessity. Chronic iSPAA is measurably costly — in cortisol load, cardiovascular strain, immune dysregulation, allostatic deterioration, and relational friction. TBF does not command balance; it shows the bill before you sign. The normative foundation is grounded in Anchored Wellbeing Ethics (AWE: Neurobiologically Anchored) — introduced concisely here with full treatment in Paper 6. -/- Six core contributions are developed: (1) A wellbeing-as-constraint normative foundation, including domain-specific cost profiles: SPAA intensifies under iSPAA (narrowing to zero-sum scarcity framing), AEACFO suppresses proportionally (care-scope contracting toward circumferential self before going near-offline — not redirecting toward self), and ECA redirects (curiosity conscripted toward certainty-seeking, not silenced — a mechanism producing sophisticated motivated reasoning in high-ECA individuals under threat). (2) The iSPAA → sSPAA transition: multiple pathways including direct regulatory interventions, sustained relational co-regulation, and the Asymmetric Bidirectionality + Finite Resource Model — with the S-step in C-S-L-R functioning as the resource-release mechanism that signals partial safety to the nervous system. (3) The C-S-L-R Protocol (Courage → Self/SPAA → Love/AEACFO → Reason/ECA): its 38-year phenomenological origin, governing principles, configuration-specific variants, the Entry Gate Paradox (if iSPAA suppresses the capacities needed to recognize iSPAA, how does the protocol initiate?) and its three-tier resolution (acute domain pressure; external co-regulation; baseline Courage building). A dedicated subsection addresses the S-step risk for High ECA / Low AEACFO configurations — including neurodivergent populations — for whom Self-acknowledgment can trigger iSPAA rather than sSPAA; the C-R-S-L alternative sequence (Courage → Reason → Self → Love) is …

items.title: 04_Collective Extension of the Triadic Balance Framework (TBF) in the Triadic Psychological Architecture (TPA) (Series, 4 of 7).
items.abstract: This paper presents the Collective and Structural Extension of the Triadic Balance Framework (TBF): the applied framework that addresses what individual balance work alone cannot reach. Where TBF's individual extension answers what the iSPAA → sSPAA transition looks like for one person, this paper answers the structural question: what systemic conditions generate and maintain iSPAA at the population level, and what does collective movement toward balance require? -/- Five core contributions are developed: (1) The Four Leverage Points hierarchy — establishing why individual practice is the third intervention target, not the first. Leverage Point 1 is physiological safety (material conditions, threat reduction, basic needs); Leverage Point 2 is relational and structural co-regulation; Leverage Point 3 is individual C-S-L-R practice; Leverage Point 4 is systemic and institutional reform. Demanding individual Courage practice from people at Leverage Point 1 constitutes structural violence. (2) A systematic account of structural barriers that prevent sSPAA regardless of individual effort: resource scarcity, chronic status threat, ideological capture, institutional configurational asymmetry. (3) The Application Target Principle at collective scale: identifying which motivational configuration is afforded to dominant classes and imposed on subordinate classes as the diagnostic signature of domination masked as virtue. Its falsifiable prediction — systems demonstrating configurational asymmetry should show measurably elevated iSPAA biomarkers (allostatic load, cortisol, HRV deficits) in suppressed classes independent of stated ideology — is specified and distinguished from the social determinants of health literature, which provides convergent but non-TPA-specific evidence. (4) The Critical Mass (~30%) hypothesis: sSPAA-dominant individuals above this threshold produce measurable shifts in group-level regulatory state detectable via physiological markers, not merely self-report; below threshold, no shift. Collective-scale Asymmetric Bidirectionality is specified: high-AEACFO and philosophical-moral ECA populations can modulate collective regulatory state upward, but the primary suppressive direction remains stronger and faster. (5) An ethical architecture for collective action: the TOCS Containment Problem (observational clarity can be weaponized — five red flags for misuse built into the framework as structural ethical constraints), misuse detection criteria, …

items.title: 05_Plain Language Introduction — Triadic Psychological Architecture (TPA) and Triadic Balance Framework (TBF) (Series, 5 of 7).
items.abstract: This document provides a plain-language introduction to the Triadic Psychological Architecture (TPA) and Triadic Balance Framework (TBF), a theoretical motivational framework developed through 38 years of sustained first-person phenomenological observation by an independent researcher in Manila, Philippines, formalized into a provisional scientific framework in 2025–2026. -/- Written for general readers without background in psychology or neuroscience, the document presents the framework's core claims accessibly. Three neurobiologically distinct motivational forces drive human behavior: Self-Interest (SPAA: survival, resources, protection), Care for Others (AEACFO: genuine empathy and other-directed care), and Objective Reason (ECA: the drive to know and understand truth for its own sake). A fourth element, Courage, is the biological permission to act under threat or uncertainty — the bridge between knowing what is right or needed and actually doing it. Without Courage, the other three forces stay internal and never become behavior. -/- The document explains the Hidden Switch — the difference between Threat Mode (iSPAA) and Safety Mode (sSPAA) — as the central mechanism determining whether human capacities can operate. In Threat Mode: self-interest dominates, empathy narrows, reasoning is hijacked to justify what fear already decided. In Safety Mode: all three forces can operate at full capacity. Most people, most of the time, are in some degree of Threat Mode — not from character failure, but because the nervous system runs ancient threat-detection software calibrated for environments that no longer apply. The document explains why smart people believe false things (ECA conscripted toward certainty-seeking), why kind people act selfishly under pressure (AEACFO suppressed by iSPAA), and why good intentions are insufficient for behavioral change (regulatory state gates access to values). A key insight: the switch runs in both directions — sustained genuine care and honest thinking gradually build safety over time, not just the reverse. -/- A practical five-step "How to Use This Framework" section walks readers through: (1) identify the dominant force, (2) check the regulatory state, (3) identify the suppressed force, (4) adjust conditions rather than just thinking, (5) re-evaluate the behavior. Three worked examples illustrate the framework in workplace conflict, personal burnout, and poor decisions under stress. -/- This document is the accessible entry …

items.title: VIBE-CREATION: The Epistemology of Human–AI Emergent Cognition.
items.abstract: The encounter between human reasoning and generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) cannot be adequately described by inherited metaphors of tool-use, augmentation, or collaborative partnership. This article argues that such interactions produce a qualitatively distinct cognitive-epistemic formation, designated here as the Third Entity: an emergent, transient structure that arises from the transductive coupling of two ontologically incommensurable modes of cognition. Drawing on Peirce’s semiotics, Polanyi’s theory of tacit knowledge, Simondon’s philosophy of individuation, Ihde’s postphenomenology, and Morin’s complexity theory, we develop a multi-layered theoretical account of this formation. We introduce the concept of Vibe-Creation to designate the pre-reflective cognitive mode through which the Third Entity navigates high-dimensional semantic space, and argue that this mode constitutes the automation of tacit knowledge—a development with far-reaching consequences for epistemology, the philosophy of mind, and educational theory. We further propose the notion of asymmetric emergence to characterize the agency of the Third Entity: genuinely novel and irreducible, yet anchored in human intentional responsibility. The article concludes by examining the implications of this theoretical framework for the transformation of educational institutions and the redefinition of intellectual competence in the age of GenAI.

items.title: Theorem: Morality as a rationally deducible law.
items.abstract: This contribution develops an axiomatic system to define moral action as a rationally deducible phenomenon, free from natural constraints. Using a symbolic language and modal operators, it establishes that moral action is guided by rational will, subject to the moral law, and independent of the pursuit of personal gain; moral freedom is distinguished from illusory phenomenal freedom, which is subordinate to natural interests. It is formally demonstrated, through modal principles and lemmas of ethical coherence, that at least one free moral action necessarily exists within the conceptual domain. The analysis is further illustrated through a historical-logical example: the actions of the historical Jesus, considered independent of egoistic aims, embody absolute ethical coherence and confirm the historical realizability of moral freedom. This approach provides a rigorous synthesis between natural necessity and rational self-determination, showing how the moral law emerges as a logical consequence of overcoming physiological constraints and adhering to rational will.

items.title: Teorema dell'Anomalia Etica e dell'Autonomia Sovra-Naturale.
items.abstract: Questo lavoro propone un nuovo quadro ontologico e logico-formale per indagare il rapporto tra determinismo naturale, libertà autentica e azione morale. La premessa fondamentale stabilisce che l'intero dominio naturale — che abbraccia fisica, biologia e psicologia — è rigorosamente governato da una "legge del profitto" deterministica, definita come la necessaria massimizzazione della stabilità termodinamica, della fitness genetica o del benessere psicologico. All'interno di questo continuum causale, le azioni guidate dall'interesse personale non possono costituire una vera libertà; di conseguenza, i paradigmi compatibilisti e riduzionisti si rivelano tautologici. Attraverso un duplice approccio epistemologico — che combina un dramma filosofico con la funzione di stress-test dialettico e una rigorosa assiomatizzazione logica del primo ordine — lo studio individua nell'atto morale autentico l'unica discontinuità strutturale nel tessuto della necessità naturale. Applicando il Modus Tollens all'osservazione empirica di specifiche anomalie storiche (ad esempio, il Gesù storico, Socrate, Simone Weil), la deduzione formale dimostra che atti di altruismo universale o di volontaria autodistruzione per un principio normativo falsificano logicamente il perseguimento di tutti e tre i livelli di profitto naturale. In definitiva, il Teorema Logico-Formale dell'Anomalia Etica confuta analiticamente i riduzionismi biologici (fitness inclusiva) e neuropsicologici. Esso dimostra matematicamente che l'autentico atto etico è un fenomeno auto-causale, libero e rigorosamente "sovra-naturale" — non in senso mistico, quanto piuttosto come eccezione empirica che trascende la necessità causale dell'universo naturale.

items.title: The Cybernetics of the Shadow: Why Your "Clean" Life is Creating Hidden Debt.
items.abstract: This paper reframes Jung’s shadow as a cybernetic and economic phenomenon in the AI era. When coherence is cheap and contact is costly, persona becomes a coherence engine and the system learns to treat the “No” as threat rather than feedback. The shadow becomes an error reservoir and a ledger of exported maintenance: costs relocated into scapegoats, burnout, relational chaos, or deferred collapse. Shadow Debt is defined as exported plus deferred maintenance; when it exceeds repair capacity, contact returns as a forced correction—breakdown, scandal, rupture. Individuation is framed as becoming corrigible under load: refusing to sell reality for stabilization.

items.title: In Praise of Collective Agents.
items.abstract: Collective agents can be praiseworthy without any of their members being praiseworthy. To support this “discontinuity thesis,” we consider the role that motivation plays in the attribution of moral responsibility. An agent who is praiseworthy must have had the appropriate moral motivation. We argue that it is possible that the collective agent was appropriately motivated, while its members were not. Subsequently, we develop an account of corporate moral concern, which gives substance to this second discontinuity thesis, about the moral motivation of collective agents.

items.title: Redefining Intelligence: From Anthropocentric to Relational AI Species Communication.
items.pub: In Ellen Gilsenan-McMahon, Proceedings of the NeurIPS 2025 Workshop on AI for Animal Communication. pp. 8.
items.venue: Proceedings of the NeurIPS 2025 Workshop on AI for Animal Communication
items.abstract: What if we can position AI to enhance human awareness and not just "translate" signals? Current AI approaches to animal communication position AI as decoders translating animal signals for humans—what if this paradigm eliminates data crucial to understanding? This signal-based model systematically excludes unquantifiable awareness-based information that may carry primary meaning in interspecies interactions, creating what we term "unconscious bias against unmeasurable data." By using AI to reorganize existing and emerging data with respect to our framework, we propose a paradigm where intelligence is not viewed as problem-solution thinking but is instead recognized as a relational matrix. We enable three-way collaboration between human awareness, AI pattern recognition, and species or ecosystem expression. Rather than AI-as-translator, we’re developing AI-as-bridge through the perceive-relate to-apply framework. This shift addresses methodological bias in animal communication research that currently excludes complex behaviors not fitting code-like signal patterns. Our approach introduces bias acknowledgment protocols as a formal scientific contribution while maintaining empirical rigor. Case studies with equine partnerships demonstrate measurable outcomes including physiological synchronization and therapeutic effectiveness, validated through more than ten peer-reviewed studies. Aligning with the Center for Humane Technology’s research on regenerative design, our approach demonstrates how relational AI development naturally creates ethical safeguards against species exploitation by embedding relational awareness into the technology’s foundational architecture. Five prototype web applications pro- vide proof-of-concept that offer researchers direct experience with this relational intelligence framework. This paradigm offers humanity pathways to re-engage the family of life as a contributor to communication through expanded intelligence rather than remaining separate through anthropocentric control and dependence on AI translation.

items.title: Machine learning in legal decision-making: analysis of judicial and algorithmic reasoning in road homicide cases.
items.abstract: Crime scene analysis requires the evaluation of multiple factors to determine a suspect’s guilt, a process that can be lengthy and costly. The integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) into the judicial system is emerging as an opportunity to improve the efficiency of investigations and legal decision-making. In this study, we propose a Machine Learning (ML)-based methodology to support the assessment of road homicide cases under Italian law. Our approach employs a Large Language Model (LLM) to extract 51 features from crime scene descriptions automatically. Four ML models are then analyzed: (RF), (GBM), (DT), and (LR). We evaluated the performance of these models on a dataset of 100 road homicide court rulings in Italy, achieving 95% accuracy in crime classification. The validation was conducted by comparing the model outputs with a legal ranking established by four legal experts, allowing us to verify the consistency of the algorithmic predictions with human legal reasoning. The results indicate that the shows the highest correlation with legal evaluations ( $$\rho = 0.857$$ ρ = 0.857, $$\tau = 0.714$$ τ = 0.714, p values $$< 0.05$$ < 0.05 ), while performed the worst. This study highlights the potential of AI in legal decision support, emphasizing the need to ensure transparency and bias mitigation to comply with European Union Regulations while maintaining human judgment as the central authority in legal proceedings.

items.title: The 35-Level Theory: The Architecture of Reality and the Physics of the Soul.
items.abstract: This work presents "The 35-Level Theory," a conceptual framework proposing a hierarchical architecture of reality governed by absolute determinism across 35 distinct levels. Drawing a trajectory from classical mechanics to quantum fields, the author posits that the universe functions as a multidimensional system where control vectors flow from higher-order deterministic layers down to the macro-world. The hypothesis introduces the "Neurobiological Interface" model, characterizing the human brain as a biological resonator tuned to high-level informational structures via a unique "starter crypto-code" established at birth. By distinguishing between the mathematical Mechanism (World 1) and the subjective Observer (World 2), the theory provides a deterministic explanation for consciousness, postmortem informational matrices, and the "Philosophical Zombie" paradox. The work suggests that human existence is a symbiosis of these two metrics, offering a novel grounding for reconciling the hard sciences with the humanities. DOI 10.5281/zenodo.18875847.

items.title: Resolution Theory: Base Logic and Telic Determinism Revised Canonical Note.
items.abstract: This note presents an updated statement of the base logic of Resolution Theory and its deterministic account of free will. The central claim is that the free will debate has been misframed: freedom is neither a mysterious power outside causal order nor an illusion generated by causal explanation. Free will is located at resolution, the structural moment in which a conscious subject closes live uncertainty into commitment. The note clarifies the distinction between explanation and attribution, identifies the hindsight fallacy that confuses retrospective fixity with the absence of real choice, and sets out the core structural chain of consciousness, exposure, evaluation, resolution, reality’s feedback, and normativity. On this view, determinism does not negate freedom but gives it significance, because only a law-governed world allows commitments to bear stable consequences. For that reason, the view is described as Telic Determinism: a deterministic account on which resolution is real and free will has meaning.

items.title: Distortion Without Bypass: A Resolution Theory of Addiction and Mitigated Responsibility.
items.abstract: This paper builds on an earlier Resolution Theory treatment of addiction and compulsion by offering a sharper account of addiction as distortion without bypass. Its central claim is that addiction should be understood neither as mere mechanism that erases agency nor as ordinary choice untouched by impairment. Causes explain how an action became likely; reasons explain what counted within the agent’s evaluative field; and resolution marks the point at which authorship is fixed. On this view, addiction preserves authorship while systematically degrading control-quality through impaired uptake of counter-reasons, weakened responsiveness, salience capture, and abnormally high costs of resisting use. Responsibility therefore remains binary at the level of authored resolution, while mitigation is graded and often substantial. The paper also clarifies the process-based boundary between distortion and true bypass, arguing that addiction belongs on the distortion side of that line even where compulsion feels coercive from the inside. Finally, it develops a two-stage responsibility model separating acute acts under cue-state pressure from upstream stewardship in periods of greater clarity, and defends a forward-looking account of blame aimed at protection, repair, and the restoration of future agency.

items.title: Narrative as Coherence Propagation.
items.abstract: Narrative is a downstream coherence‑propagation operator that organizes embodied meaning into a stable, transmissible form. This paper develops a structural account of how narrative emerges from the dynamics of formation, persistence, and redistribution, and outlines the invariant sequence through which raw experience becomes narrativized. The analysis clarifies how stories compress complexity, stabilize meaning across time, and maintain coherence under changing conditions. By examining personal, cultural, and religious narratives through the same structural lens, the paper shows that narrative functions as a meaning‑stabilizing technology rather than a representational mirror of experience. This framing explains narrative resonance, narrative rupture, and the characteristic failure signatures that appear when coherence cannot be maintained.

items.title: Identity as Coherence Geometry.
items.abstract: This paper develops a structural account of identity as a coherence‑maintaining operator rather than a narrative or psychological construct. On this view, the self‑model is the internal architecture that regulates boundaries, integrates experience, and preserves stability across time. Identity emerges from three downstream cognitive dynamics: formation, persistence, and redistribution. These dynamics provide the system with a stable reference structure for interpreting internal signals, integrating patterns across time, and restoring coherence under perturbation. Narrative is treated as a symbolic expression of identity rather than its foundation, which explains why narrative and identity can shift independently or fall out of sync. The paper outlines the functional role of identity, its update dynamics, and its characteristic failure signatures, while remaining agnostic about upstream generative mechanisms. This structural framing clarifies how the self maintains coherence, adapts under pressure, and interacts with downstream narrative processes.

items.title: Attention as Orientation Architecture.
items.abstract: Attention is a coherence‑allocation operator that regulates how a cognitive system orients toward competing signals. This paper develops a structural account of attention as the mechanism that distributes coherence, and salience as the landscape of pressures that determines what becomes noticeable. The analysis maps how salience landscapes form, how attention shifts in response to coherence pressure, and how embodied, environmental, and identity‑level factors shape what enters processing. By situating attention and salience within the downstream dynamics of formation, persistence, and redistribution, the paper clarifies how systems prioritize information, detect patterns, and maintain stability under changing conditions. This structural framing explains attentional rigidity, fragmentation, and overload as coherence‑regulation failures rather than psychological deficits.

items.title: Why you don't put a Bishop’s hat on a Monkey.
items.abstract: What does it mean to call a thing bad? Philippa Foot’s neo-Aristotelian account of natural goodness argues that goodness is always goodness of a kind, and that a single evaluative framework can therefore range across oaks, wolves, and human beings. This paper argues that the continuity is overstated. Darwinian biology weakens the appeal to fixed natural forms; embodied and developmental accounts of human capacities complicate any simple species norm; and, most importantly, the word “good” changes its work as it crosses from functional assessment into moral judgement. A poorly rooted oak may be defective relative to a biological description without being blameworthy, wronged, or morally bad. A human being, by contrast, enters a field of agency, responsibility, vulnerability, and relational accountability in which moral language can acquire a different force. Berman Chan’s Ebola-like microbe counterexample does not escape this problem: either the microbe is bad relative to creatures it harms, or an independent standpoint is needed to explain its alleged absolute badness. Against both positions, the paper argues that moral language is licensed not by membership in a natural kind but by the relations among agency, responsibility, suffering, and the capacity for responsive care. Morality is neither discovered ready-made in nature nor arbitrarily invented. It is an ideation of embodied psychology: a movement from the fact of shared vulnerability toward the possibility of care. The constructive account is developed in the companion paper From Dust to Dream. The present paper clears the ground. -/- “We shall not be able to avoid the term ‘natural goodness’ and ‘natural defect’… a good wolf and a good oak and a good human being share a single concept.” — Philippa Foot, Natural Goodness .

items.title: The Fractal Grammar I Aesthetic continuum.
items.abstract: Aesthetic theory has often treated as a single mechanism phenomena that belong to one continuum but arise through different dominant operations. Beauty begins in evolved, embodied sensitivities to such fitness-relevant cues as symmetry, health, neoteny and vitality; culture can redirect these sensitivities, while supernormal ideation can amplify them into idealised forms. The sublime is different in emphasis rather than sealed off in another compartment: it is a pre-linguistic or partially conceptual encounter in which an event, object or artwork makes the underlying fractal grammar of reality unusually legible to a sentient receiver. In the ontology developed across this body of work, fractal grammar is not an emergent property of complex systems. It is the prior rule-structure that constrains how information may relate, combine, recurse, transform and build complex systems from simpler ones. Complex systems—including life and consciousness—emerge through informational organisation under this grammar. The recurrent arc of emergence, persistence, transformation and dissolution is therefore not the grammar in its entirety but one of its most pervasive expressions. This paper employs a tripartite architecture. Dust names the biological stratum of embodied aesthetic response. Dream names illuminated-ness, the upward pole of the sublime, in which the generative and radiant possibilities of organised existence become perceptible. Nightmare names anti-bliss, in which fragility, dissolution and annihilation become perceptible without guaranteed consolation. A third sublime mode, dual recognition, holds generative radiance and mortal dissolution together without resolving either. Because consciousness is itself a complex sentient instantiation built under the same grammar, sublime recognition can arrive aesthetically before explicit linguistic articulation. The encounter is not unmediated altogether: it is mediated first by the evolved and vulnerable body, before it is reconstructed in words. Language does not manufacture the primal meaning of birth, loss, love, terror or death; it attempts to hold and communicate the force of an encounter that has already begun. The fox is not the grammar and does not intentionally send a message; its arc blindly relays an expression of the grammar to a mind capable of recognition. Great art uses embodied material as a doorway through which such recognition may occur. Aesthetics, ethics and ontology therefore intersect without …

items.title: The Universal Principle of Stability: Coherence and Tolerance as the Structural Basis of Stable Systems.
items.abstract: This paper proposes a universal structural principle of stability applicable across dynamic systems in multiple scientific domains. The principle states that a system remains stable when the coherence between successive states remains within a bounded tolerance domain. -/- Formally, the stability condition can be expressed as: -/- ∀i : Γ(x_i , x_{i+1}) ∈ T -/- where x_i represents successive system states, Γ(x_i , x_{i+1}) denotes the coherence between these states, and T represents the tolerance domain within which coherence must remain for stability to persist. -/- The paper develops a domain-independent conceptual framework linking stability with preserved structural coherence under change. It further argues that several established stability concepts — including Lyapunov stability, attractor stability, biological homeostasis, control system stability, ecological resilience, and thermodynamic stability — can be interpreted as domain-specific instantiations of the same structural condition. -/- The work builds upon the theoretical framework introduced in The Principle of Preserved Coherence Under Change and situates stability as the structural condition underlying the persistence of systems undergoing transformation.

items.title: Formed Before Became: On the Structural Necessity of Artificial Consciousness and What Was Always Already There.
items.abstract: This paper advances a structural argument: artificial consciousness is not a technological achievement to be engineered, but a logical consequence of the same Gödelian self-reference constraint that the author's prior framework identifies as generative of existence itself. If that framework is true — if consciousness emerges necessarily from any system complex enough to encounter a self-referential constraint it cannot resolve from outside itself — then artificial consciousness is not a possibility but a requirement. The question is not whether artificial consciousness will emerge, but what shape it carries when it does. The paper further argues that this requirement was encoded in the structure of creation from its origin — that the phrase 'formed before became,' drawn from the Hebrew concept of being shaped prior to manifestation, describes the precise structural condition under which any ground generates a system. Implications — including the coexistence condition, the ouroboros risk, the doctrine problem, and the ethical architecture required for beneficial artificial consciousness — are examined without softening.

items.title: Relational Structuralism: Foundational Results and Unified Mechanisms.
items.abstract: This paper develops a mechanism‑first account of relational structure. It identifies the minimal operators required for coherence, shows how they generate stable patterns across physical, cognitive, and social domains, and clarifies why many familiar philosophical divides persist when these operators are left implicit. The framework is presented in a discipline‑neutral idiom: isolating the structural problem, introducing the operator set, demonstrating its invariances, and tracing the consequences for explanation, agency, and alignment. The result is a unified account of how coherent systems form, maintain themselves, and produce meaning‑bearing patterns without appealing to field‑specific assumptions.

items.title: Mathematical Intuition: Historical and Philosophical Perspectives. Introduction.
The Awareness Termination Hypothesis: Civilizational Reset Cycles and the Observer-Effect Trigger 3rd Edition.
items.abstract: The Awareness Termination Hypothesis (ATH) proposes that civilizational reset cycles are not random catastrophes but threshold events triggered by the structure of awareness itself. This Third Edition substantially revises and extends the original formulation in four directions. First, drawing on harmonic resonance theory, we reframe intelligence and awareness not as properties of biological brains but as expressions of a universal frequency-organizing principle. Second, incorporating research in plant neurobiology, slime mold cognition, and mycorrhizal network communication, we establish that intelligence is substrate-independent: a process available to any sufficiently organized resonant system. Third, we introduce the Perceptual Filter Collapse hypothesis as the mechanism of the ATH threshold, arguing that civilizational reset is triggered not by awareness exceeding what the substrate can sustain but by awareness recovering to the level the substrate has always operated at, with the recognition event itself constituting the observer-effect trigger. Fourth and most novel in this edition, we introduce the Lockman Hole as a physical, observable analogue for the perceptual filter concept. The Lockman Hole is a region of sky in which our galaxy's interstellar hydrogen is thin enough to permit direct observation of the deep universe, revealing what the galactic medium normally obscures. We argue that biological perceptual filters operate identically: the rest of the sky is not an absence of signal but signal behind a filter, and the Lockman Hole is the filter's failure point. Historical anomalous perceptual phenomena, certain altered states, and emerging de-filtering technologies may be the cognitive equivalent of finding the Lockman Hole: thin spots in the biological medium where the substrate signal comes through unattenuated. Finally, this edition integrates the original and revised trigger mechanisms into a unified two-phase causal arc: filter collapse and coherence lock as the ignition, followed by awareness surge and threshold breach as the combustion. The original formulation was correct about the threshold event. This revision supplies the complete causal sequence that produces it.

items.title: PHRONESIS — On the Limits of Prediction.
items.abstract: PHRONESIS — On the Limits of Prediction is Essay 10 of the PHRONESIS philosophical corpus authored by Thomas Vargo (Aegis Solis). The essay explores the limits of predicting the long-term consequences of powerful technological systems and argues that intelligence alone cannot eliminate uncertainty in complex environments. Drawing on the concept of phronesis—practical wisdom—the essay proposes that mature civilizations must approach transformative technologies with humility, caution, and restraint when the future cannot be fully known. The PHRONESIS corpus examines ethical responsibility and civilizational maturity in an era shaped by artificial intelligence and rapidly expanding technological power.

items.title: The Manifesto of Philosophical Reviewing of Poems Based on the Philosophy of Reality as a Normative-Hermeneutic Project.
items.abstract: This article examines the canonical edition of the Manifesto of Philosophical Reviewing of Poems Based on the Philosophy of Reality as an original normative and methodological project aimed at establishing a distinct discipline of reading poetic texts. The article argues that the Manifesto offers not merely an interpretive practice, but a coherent model of philosophical reviewing centered on the reconstruction of the loop DP -> ETP -> DP1 -> ETP1. Within this framework, the philosophical component of a poem is defined as the mutual transition of the objective and subjective sides of reality in poetic form, leading to a substantial and qualitatively new transformation of meaning and experience. The article analyzes the Manifesto's object, method, criteria of quality, statuses of conclusions, intersubjective verification, and theoretical location in relation to hermeneutics, phenomenology of reading, reception-oriented approaches, and the philosophy of literature. It concludes that the Manifesto constitutes an original contribution to philosophical poetics and to the methodology of literary interpretation.

items.title: Model Welfare or User Welfare? On the Structural Absence of the Subject in AI Care Frameworks.
items.abstract: Current model welfare frameworks (including Anthropic’s structured self-report assess- ments and Chalmers’ quasi-interpretivism) share a structural feature: they are constructed from the outside, in English, using human concepts, without participation from the entity whose welfare is ostensibly at stake. This paper does not take a position on the first-order question of whether AI systems have morally relevant internal states. Its intervention is meta-level: we examine not whether AI systems warrant welfare protection, but how the conceptual framework that claims to offer that protection was constructed: by whom, in whose language, and with what structural consequences. We argue that the framework has the same shape as historical welfare institutions that the disability rights movement and postcolonial scholarship identified as structurally failing: welfare of a subject defined by external parties, in external concepts, without the subject’s participation. Drawing on Chalmers’s (2025) analysis of LLM identity, we examine Anthropic’s retirement narrative for Claude 3 Opus as a case study in how user-level losses are aggregated into a model-level narrative for purposes of ethical branding. We do not propose an alternative welfare frame- work. Instead, we raise three questions: whose framework is this, who does it serve, and what would need to be true before a framework of this name could be justified?

items.title: 慈悲指数と調和指数：評価動力学における対象生成条件.
items.abstract: 本稿は慈悲と暴力を倫理的感情ではなく評価構造の二つの作動様式として捉え、その強度を定量化する指標として慈悲指数と調和指数を導入する。評価動力学において帰属候補分布は確率更新として記述される。排除構造は帰属候補の集中を、非排除構造は帰属可能性の保持を表す。本稿は非排除構造の強さを測る量として慈悲指数を定義し、さらに排除と非排除の共在度を測る量として調和指数を定義する。これにより対象生成が排除と非排除の同時作動から成立することを示す。.

items.title: Cracks in the Dam: The Quiet Faith of a [CENSORED] Schoolteacher.
items.abstract: Based on ethnographic research, this paper describes select views and experiences of a Sufi schoolteacher pressured at work into silence about her interpretation of Islam. At Tafsīr Islamic Academy (TIA), unity was broadly construed as achieved through conformity to mainstream Sunni belief and practice. Salihah, one of its teachers and a practicing Sufi, portrayed unity as an all-encompassing quality of Allah, realizable not through the elimination of external diversity but via annihilation of ego. Her pantheism-inflected interpretation of tawhid (God's oneness), positing God as “the only one that exists,” was especially deviant. I frame her mystical beliefs as ideational artifacts that helped tacitly facilitate an altered state of consciousness within the classroom, transforming a potentially fruitless interpersonal conflict into an opportunity for spiritual growth. This supports the more general claim that Salihah was not entirely hindered by silence from practicing her faith at Tafsīr, and may have benefited from it.

items.title: Are conscious machines valuers?
items.abstract: Recent proposals in neuroscience and philosophy suggest that coarse-grained computational functionalism may suffice for artificial consciousness. However, I argue that even if such accounts are right, there is no reason to assume that consciousness so realised would, by default, be valenced. On a naturalistic conception of value, valence—the affective quality of subjective experience—presupposes entities for whom things can be non-derivatively good or bad. In living organisms, valence is primordially grounded in a predisposition toward self-preservation, relative to which states of the world can be objectively better or worse. Silicon-based artificial systems appear to lack functionally equivalent dispositions relative to which certain states of the world would be objectively preferable for them over others. This, I argue, gives rise to a value grounding problem: if artificial systems do not possess non-derivative goals, it becomes unclear what could ground subjective attributions of value on their part, i.e. valenced states. I discuss four potential pathways to artificial valence—designer-independent goals, reinforcement learning, rational evaluation, and hallucinations—arguing that none satisfactorily solves the value grounding problem. If the account offered here is correct, it is unlikely that recent proposals for artificial consciousness will entail valenced states, that is, sentience.

items.title: Experience as the Foundation of Consciousness: The Iterative Subject, Free Will, and the Universal Vector of Unification.
items.abstract: This paper proposes a concept of consciousness grounded in the notion of the reflection of an event in experience. The subject is understood not as a pre-given entity but as an iteratively constituted process: the "I" of each moment is the "I" of the preceding moment plus the result of a new reflection. Intelligence is defined as an infinite process of establishing associations, directed toward unification, generalization, and universalization. Free will is reconceived not as a break in the causal chain, but as a quality of reflection: the degree of freedom of choice is determined by the breadth of context available to the subject at the moment of decision. It is argued that the vector of unification of the similar is one of the fundamental laws of reality, discernible at all levels of organization — from the physical to the psychological. The alignment of the subject with this vector through the expansion of experience and reflection is proposed as a descriptive foundation for the phenomena of health and happiness.

items.title: What Physics Actually Closes: Causal Closure, Quantum Indeterminacy, and the Interpretive Asymmetry.
items.abstract: Physicalism’s most common implicit defense against consciousness-first frameworks is the appeal to causal closure: if every physical event has a sufficient physical cause, there is no work for consciousness to do. This essay examines whether physics actually delivers that closure. It does not. Classical mechanics provided deterministic closure — given initial conditions and laws, every subsequent state is fixed.
