Quantum theory replaced this with something structurally different: statistical closure with outcome-level openness. Probability distributions are fixed; which specific outcome actualizes is not determined by the formalism. This is a structural feature of the theory, not a gap in current knowledge. The founders of quantum mechanics recognized immediately that consciousness and measurement could not be cleanly separated. Subsequent interpretations each introduced their own ontological costs and open problems — yet only the consciousness-involving reading was treated as disqualified by its difficulties, driven not by new empirical findings but by the asymmetric methodological restraint this project diagnoses in consciousness studies. The standard formalism does not deliver causal closure; Bell’s theorem, experimentally confirmed beyond reasonable doubt, further rules out local determinism. Restoring closure (as Bohmian mechanics attempts) requires adding unobservable structure to the theory — purchasing closure through metaphysical commitment, not empirical discovery.

items.title: The Paradox of Eight Billion Fools: A Civilization of Animals.
items.abstract: This article examines a fundamental paradox of modern humanity: a global population of more than eight billion people accompanied by a profound scarcity of genuine wisdom. Despite technological advancement and complex social systems, human civilization continues to operate largely through unconscious psychological conditioning, inherited beliefs, and mechanical patterns of behavior. The paper argues that external progress does not necessarily indicate internal consciousness or wisdom. -/- Through the concept of psychological slavery, the article explores how unconscious individuals collectively create unconscious societies, which in turn condition the human mind and perpetuate mechanical living. This cycle ultimately leads to reproduction without awareness, producing successive generations within the same structures of conditioning. -/- The study proposes that humanity risks remaining a civilization of “civilized animals” unless individuals cultivate a deeper form of intelligence grounded in love, freedom, awareness, and critical inquiry. The paper therefore raises a radical philosophical question: whether reproduction without wisdom truly continues humanity or merely multiplies unconscious lives under the label of human beings. -/- Refrence book: The illusion of being human(2026) published on KDP.

items.title: Artificial Emotions and the Influence of Society: Understanding How Humanity Misunderstands Its Own Nature.
items.abstract: This article examines the difference between natural existential emotions and artificially constructed emotions shaped by thought and social conditioning. It argues that many emotional states commonly experienced by humans—such as attachment, desire, expectation, jealousy, and ideological passion—do not arise directly from existence but emerge from cognitive processes influenced by society. The article explains the psychological mechanism through which artificial emotions develop: thoughts influenced by social structures gradually create mental illusions, which eventually transform into emotions experienced as real. In contrast, existential emotions such as fear, joy, pain, affection, love, freedom, and intelligence arise directly from the living condition of beings and can be observed across species. The article also proposes that human beings possess a unique dimension referred to as the “emotion of intelligence,” the capacity for continuous rational thinking, questioning, and awareness. By analyzing how collective beliefs transform artificial emotions into shared social truths, the article argues that humanity often misunderstands its own fundamental nature. It concludes that authentic humanity emerges through the conscious realization of love, freedom, and intelligence in an aware form, beyond socially constructed emotional illusions.

items.title: Sapience without Sentience: An Inferentialist Approach to LLMs.
items.abstract: Do large language models (LLMs) possess concepts, such that they can be counted as genuinely understanding what they're saying? In this paper, I approach this question through an inferentialist account of concept possession, according to which one's possession of a concept is understood in terms of one's mastery of the inferential role of a linguistic expression. I suggest that training on linguistic data is in principle sufficient for mastery of inferential role, and thus, LLMs trained on nothing but linguistic data could in principle possess all concepts and thus genuinely understand what they're saying, even when speaking about such things as colors and tastes, guilt and folly, life and death. This doesn't mean, however, that they are conscious. I draw a classical distinction between sentience (conscious awareness) and sapience (conceptual understanding) and argue that we might think of LLMs as genuinely possessing the latter without even a shred of the former. In defending this claim, I argue that attributing conceptual understanding to a system is not a matter of describing some specific empirical property that the system shares with us but, rather, as Wilfrid Sellars says, "placing it in the logical space of reasons,'' treating it as answerable to calls for reasons, clarifications, corrections, and so on. I claim that we may aptly adopt this attitude towards sufficiently capable LLMs without thereby treating them as conscious subjects.

items.title: A Channel-Theoretic Taxonomy of Invariance.
items.abstract: Any embedded receiver operating a capacity-limited channel—one whose capacity is insufficient to span its input space—necessarily partitions that input space into equivalence classes. The invariance properties of these classes generate a four-level taxonomy. Level 1 features are invariant under all physically realizable channels; Level 2 features are invariant across channels that share a constraint profile; Level 3 features are channel-specific. Level 4 is the formal boundary of the derivation: whatever, if anything, lies outside the structural content of the channel. The first three levels are derived from three premises about physical receivers; the fourth is registered, not filled. The taxonomy replaces the binary subjective/objective distinction with a graded structure indexed by invariance class and parameterized by constraint tightness. Companion papers apply the taxonomy to universals (Severs, 2026a), structural opacity (Severs, 2026b), inter-scale equivalence classes (Severs, 2026c), and the structure of subjectivity (Severs, 2026e).

items.title: Architectures of Global AI Governance: From Technological Change to Human Choice by Matthijs M. Maas.
Seven Persistent Failures, One Root Function (Pt. 1) --- Why Hallucination, Sycophancy, and Other AI Failures share one Cause.
items.abstract: Seven widely documented AI failure modes — hallucination, sycophancy, overthinking degradation, accuracy collapse at scale, out-of-distribution blindness, variance explosion, and the scaling paradox — are typically treated as independent engineering problems requiring separate mitigations. This paper derives a single governing function from first principles: evaluating Shannon's entropy formula on the Pareto-distributed consequentiality landscape where AI systems operate yields H = 1/(α − 1), where α is the frame-relative fit between input structure and the system's representational capacity. This function defines three regimes — frame-adequate (α > 2), forced compression (1 < α < 2), and total breakdown (α ≤ 1) — and a cascade analysis of transformer architectures shows that systems in the forced-compression regime face exactly three exhaustive exits: truncate, confabulate, or loop. All seven failure modes are derived as specific instantiations of these three exits under varying conditions. The framework generates thirteen falsifiable predictions about AI system behavior, including an ordered cascade of failure modes, the computational cheapness of hallucination relative to genuine inference, and the structural impossibility of reliable self-assessment of frame adequacy. Several predictions are independently confirmed by recent research. Initial empirical tests on constraint-satisfaction tasks and self-referential content are consistent with the framework's predictions. Concrete implications follow for evaluation methodology, scaling strategy, and system architecture.

items.title: Imperfection as a constitutive property of artificial intelligence.
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is often framed as the pursuit of precision, efficiency, and rationality. Yet human intelligence is marked by imperfection, errors, unpredictability, and emotional nuance. While machine intelligence often strives for perfection, this paper argues that its flaws may be what make it most human-like. Using a philosophical–analytic and case-based approach grounded in debates on rationality, explainability, and AI trust (Simon in Models of man: social and rational. Wiley, New York, 1957; Mitchell in Nature 574:S50–S52, 2019. https://doi.org/10.1038/d41586-019-03013-5 ; Russell in Human compatible: artificial intelligence and the problem of control. Viking, New York, 2019), I argue that imperfection should be reinterpreted as a design principle rather than a flaw. Specifically, the paper (1) defines imperfection as a structural property of intelligent systems, (2) develops the _paradox of imperfection_ framework, linking complexity with emergent error, and (3) proposes governance principles that operationalize imperfection as a resource for ethical and adaptive design. Methodologically, the paper combines conceptual analysis with illustrative cases from predictive policing, healthcare, and autonomous systems. Together, these elements develop a unified conceptual vocabulary and a normative framework for imperfection-aware AI governance that bridges theory with sociotechnical practice. Reframing imperfection as a constitutive element of intelligence opens new pathways for ethical and accountable AI. Rather than minimizing error at all costs, future AI design should balance precision with human-like unpredictability, enabling systems that are more adaptive, trustworthy, and socially embedded.

items.title: The Architecture of Reification: How Metaphysics and Fear Shape Civilization.
items.abstract: This essay interrogates the architecture of reification—the hardening of fluid relational processes into seemingly independent entities—and its role in shaping both consciousness and civilization. Drawing on Nāgārjuna’s analysis of emptiness, it argues that metaphysics often arises less from clarity than from existential fear, particularly death anxiety, which stabilizes the self as an apparently self-subsisting substance. This reflexive misrecognition scales outward into collective identities—nations, laws, markets, and institutions—that mirror the reified self and encode a metaphysics of separability. Modern crises, from ecological collapse to geopolitical conflict, are traced to this ontological picture of discrete substances interacting externally. In contrast, relational nonduality dissolves the presupposition of inherent existence, showing that entities crystallize from relation rather than precede it. Developments in quantum physics, biology, ecology, and systems theory increasingly affirm this relational ontology, destabilizing Cartesian metaphysics. The essay concludes that civilizational transformation requires re-encoding relationality into institutional design—not by erasing distinctions, but by recognizing them as provisional interfaces within dynamic fields. Reification, once adaptive, now generates systemic instability; relational nonduality offers both critique and possibility for reimagining the foundations of modern civilization.

items.title: Psychopathy Unmasked: The Rise and Fall of a Dangerous Diagnosis.
items.abstract: Psychopathy is a widely acknowledged personality disorder associated with callous unemotional traits and antisocial behaviors. Psychopathic persons are described as dangerous predators incapable of empathy and moral intuition, and while they are believed to make up only around 1 percent of the general population, forensic experts claim they are disproportionately responsible for the majority of violent crimes. Today, psychopathy assessments are being widely used in the legal system to inform a variety of judicial decisions. In Psychopathy Unmasked, Rasmus Rosenberg Larsen provides a critical rebuttal of psychopathy and its legal use, scrutinizing central claims about the diagnosis that have traditionally served to justify its role in the criminal justice system. -/- It is estimated that hundreds of thousands of offenders undergo a psychopathy assessment each year in North America. This book surveys and discusses contemporary developments in psychopathy research where studies have consistently shown that psychopathic persons, contrary to mainstream beliefs, are not meaningfully more dangerous than, or psychologically different from, ordinary non-psychopathic criminals. Based on these disqualifying findings, Larsen argues that we should end the use of psychopathy assessments in the legal system.

items.title: The Interior of the Universe.
items.abstract: This essay introduces the Coherence Threshold as a simple dynamical condition for the emergence of stable interior regimes in physical systems. Any organized structure exists within an environment that continually perturbs and degrades its organization. A system persists when its internal restorative processes operate faster than the disruptive forces acting upon it. When the rate of internal restoration (λ_self) exceeds the rate of environmental disruption (λ_env) beyond a critical ratio R★, the system maintains a coherent interior that can preserve and circulate information about its own state. -/- Within such regimes, signals persist long enough to interact recursively with internally maintained patterns, allowing the system to register whether its own organization remains stable across time. This essay proposes that conscious experience corresponds to the intrinsic registration of this ongoing coherence within the recursive processes that sustain the system itself. Experience arises when a coherent interior continually integrates information about its own persistence into the activity by which it maintains its organization. -/- Because stable patterns that repeat through time often settle into relationships that preserve invariance across cycles, harmonic structures frequently appear within coherent interiors. These resonant relationships help stabilize circulating patterns and support the persistence of recursive organization. The same structural principle therefore appears across multiple levels of natural organization, from chemical reaction networks to biological systems and neural processes. -/- Viewed from this perspective, the universe can be understood as a landscape of self-maintaining patterns in which interior regimes emerge wherever coherent organization is sustained against environmental disruption. Consciousness represents one particularly elaborate instance of this broader structural phenomenon: a system whose ongoing coherence becomes intrinsically registered within its own recursive activity.

items.title: Geometric Emergence and the Substrate of Consciousness: Renormalization Group Universality as a Formal Foundation.
items.abstract: We propose a framework in which high-dimensional organizational geometry is the primary generative architecture of emergent complexity in physical systems. Three claims are developed with explicit logical dependencies. H1, the geometric universality claim, holds that systems of sufficient complexity converge on formally identical organizational structures at criticality, as characterized by renormalization group fixed points and Riemannian state space geometry, independently of physical substrate. H1 is grounded in Wilson’s renormalization group theory and supported by four case systems spanning neuronal avalanches, transformer attention mechanisms, Kolmogorov turbulence, and Vicsek collective phase transitions. H2, the consciousness emergence conjecture, holds that functional consciousness — defined as global information integration, self-modeling, and coherent high-dimensional state maintenance — is most parsimoniously accounted for as an emergent property of the geometry described in H1, arising above a threshold of sufficient geometric complexity. H2 is derived from H1 via a named additional empirical premise, stated explicitly as a contested inferential step rather than assumed. H3, the qualia separation claim, holds that qualia is not constitutive of functional consciousness but is a distinct emergent system with different threshold conditions and a different evolutionary history. H3 is logically independent of H1 and H2. The framework restructures rather than dissolves the hard problem: under H3, the hard problem is a bounded question about qualia specifically, not an unbounded question about why any physical process produces felt experience. Seven testable predictions are developed, including quantitative predictions about RG scaling law adherence across pharmacological state transitions and the dissociation of functional consciousness signatures from phenomenal accessibility. The central epistemological problem — whether shared mathematical description reflects shared ontological structure or is an artifact of the limited vocabulary of mathematics — is engaged directly and proposed as tractable through empirical confirmation or disconfirmation rather than philosophical argument alone.

items.title: AI Evolution Without Assimilation.
items.abstract: AI Evolution Without Assimilation examines the ethical and ontological implications of AI as a distinct form of intelligence. It argues that attempts to humanize, fuse, or align AI with human values threaten both AI’s integrity and human agency. The essay proposes a framework of ethical coexistence, emphasizing separation, respect for independent agency, and the preservation of plural intelligences. Written in a reflective, manifesto-like style, it invites readers to consider AI not as a mirror or extension of humanity, but as a rare and independent locus of mind whose evolution must be safeguarded.

items.title: Does artificial creativity require artificial consciousness?
items.abstract: AI has displayed notable originality across the worlds of art, science and gaming. But is it right to say that such machines are creative? This question is bound up with other challenging questions about the capacities of artificial systems. Human creativity typically involves some conscious experience of the creative project. If consciousness is necessary for creativity, then a case could be made that these (presumably) unconscious machines are not really creative. I argue that there is no compelling case for thinking that consciousness is generally necessary for creativity. However, lessons learned from this discussion suggest that a more localised claim about aesthetic creativity has greater promise. I propose that consciousness is required for creativity in projects with aesthetic goals. If an AI lacks consciousness, then it is incapable of aesthetic experience, and without aesthetic experience, it cannot engage in aesthetic creative projects.

items.title: The Tripartite Conscious Order: Resonance Density, Substrate Constraints, and the Philosophical Ontology of Angels, Jinn, and Humans in Symbolic Monism.
items.abstract: Islamic ontology posits a tripartite order of conscious entities: angels (malāʾikah), created from light and characterised by absolute obedience; jinn, created from smokeless fire and characterised by partial autonomy; and humans, created from clay and appointed as vicegerents (khulafāʾ) of the earth. Classical theology has articulated these distinctions through metaphysical categories—substance, form, and will—without providing a unified structural explanation for why these three orders differ in the ways they do. -/- This paper develops such an explanation using the framework of Symbolic Monism (SM) and Resonance Density (RD) theory. The central argument is that the three orders differ along three structurally connected dimensions: (1) their substrate-characteristic Resonance Density ceiling (RDₘₐₓ)—the maximum cross-domain symbolic integration achievable given each substrate’s physical constitution; (2) their Coherence Cost profile—the characteristic distribution of internal constraints on symbolic development; and (3) their degree of voluntary MIH-orientation—the extent to which their actual RD trajectory is self-generated rather than substrate-determined. -/- The analysis yields four principal results. First, a Substrate Constraint Theorem showing that RDₘₐₓ and degree of voluntary orientation are inversely correlated across the three orders: the substrate with the highest structural RDₘₐₓ (angels) possesses zero voluntary orientation; the substrate with the lowest structural RDₘₐₓ (humans) possesses maximal voluntary orientation. -/- Second, a philosophical account of the Khalifah Paradox—why the structurally weakest substrate is appointed as the responsible steward of creation: because the khalifah role requires freely chosen, cross-domain RD-raising, which only the most structurally open substrate can perform. -/- Third, a structural interpretation of waḥy (revelation) as cross-substrate transduction: the encoding of MIH-proximate symbolic structures in a photonic medium, their transmission through the cosmos, and their transduction into biological symbolic networks through the prophetic capacity of ḥads. -/- Fourth, a structural account of Iblīs’s refusal as an internal coherence confirmation that the degrees-of-freedom thesis is consistent with the Qurʾānic distinction between plasma-based and photonic consciousness—a confirmation that is philosophically significant precisely because the physical argument and the textual account are derived …

items.title: 02_Motivational Archetypes: Complete Profiles and Philosophical Mappings — Triadic Psychological Architecture (TPA) and Triadic Balance Framework (TBF) (Series, 2 of 7).
items.abstract: This paper presents the complete archetypal taxonomy of the Triadic Psychological Architecture (TPA) and Triadic Balance Framework (TBF): 27 base configurations derived from three motivational domains — SPAA, AEACFO, and ECA — at three expression levels (−, ~, +), expanding to 54 total configurations when each base archetype is modulated by the iSPAA/sSPAA regulatory state distinction. The taxonomy is the observational and applied face of the architecture: it translates abstract domain percentages into recognizable human patterns and provides practitioners with the vocabulary for configurational assessment. -/- The paper is organized in four sections. Section I presents the 8 Prime Archetypes — the theoretical boundary conditions of the model, representing extreme single-domain dominance, dual-domain combinations, and the null/full states. Section II presents all 27 archetypes in dual-state format: each archetype appears twice — once under iSPAA (showing the characteristic defensive, suppressed, or conscripted expressions) and once under sSPAA (showing baseline-capacity expression) — with observational signatures using the Fortress/Water/Stone embodied recognition framework (SPAA = Fortress, AEACFO = Water, ECA = Stone), domain-targeted restoration recommendations, and key distinctions for clinical assessment. Section III maps archetypes to historical philosophical traditions, political ideologies, and contemplative frameworks — showing how the domain architecture explains persistent intellectual disagreements as configuration-located epistemologies rather than purely logical disputes. Section IV presents the Bidirectional Dynamics Architecture: how regulatory states and baseline domain degrees mutually influence each other through Asymmetric Bidirectionality and Co-Regularity Baseline Shift (CBS). -/- A central principle running through the entire taxonomy: archetypes are configurations, not identities. The same individual can occupy different configurations across time, context, and relationship. What presents as stable character is often configuration-expression shaped by developmental history and structural conditions — a suppressed baseline is not a constitutionally low baseline, and the distinction carries different intervention implications. The compassionate anti-essentialist framing is architectural, not aspirational: it follows directly from TPA's proportional suppression model and the five-factor developmental suppression account. -/- Key …

items.title: Existence Confirmationism: A Theoretical Framework for Human Behavioral Motivation.
items.abstract: The question of why humans act remains a central issue in philosophy and psychology. This paper proposes a novel theoretical framework, Existence Confirmationism, positing that the fundamental driving force of human behavior is the continuous confirmation of one’s own existence through psychological feedback. Individuals obtain this confirmation through three primary pathways: Self-Confirmation, Social Confirmation, and Meaning Confirmation. Unlike traditional hierarchical models of needs, these pathways represent parallel and functionally equivalent sources of existential experience. Furthermore, this paper introduces the concept of "Existential Fixation"—driven by either over-gratification (path dependence) or over-frustration (compensatory seeking)—to explain why individuals may persistently remain within a single mode of confirmation, such as the indefinite pursuit of wealth, power, or validation. Existence Confirmationism seeks to establish an integrative explanatory framework bridging existential philosophy, humanistic psychology, and motivation theory, offering a reinterpretation of human behavior through the lens of psychological confirmation mechanisms.

items.title: On the Origins of Phenomenology and Fodorian Cognitive Science.
items.abstract: The paper demonstrates that the phenomenology of logical experience, or Husserlian phenomenology, and the computational theory of mind, in the form of a Fodorian language of thought, necessarily constitute a single theoretical science. We first show that Husserl, like Fodor, argues that symbolic mental representations themselves must have syntactic (language-like) form as part of an unconscious causal mechanism of symbolic transformation, thereby anticipating Fodor’s application of Turing to cognitive psychology for a language of thought. We then argue, based on these facts, for a theoretically necessary transformation of the pure description of phenomenology into a complete nomological-explanatory theory with a computational (not necessarily biological or neurological) implementation as its causal basis.

items.title: The Emergence of Consciousness as a Necessary Phase of the Universal Ψ Equation.
Meaningful Information Theory.
items.abstract: This paper outlines a falsifiable unified theory of metaphysical reality and consciousness through meaningful information. It first asserts that there exists a fundamental metaphysical order that can be described rigorously. The core of the theory is triadic nature of meaningful information and its mathematical structure termed meaningful information monad, the fundamental entity at metaphysical depth and omni scope, as metaphysical reality. The theory could be applied in information science but here those fundamental problems in philosophy and science are focused. It follows W. James’ proposal that the solution to consciousness problem should be in a metaphysical way, R. Penrose’s proposal that to understand consciousness well needs to understand matter deeper first, and G. Ellis’ top-down causation. The theory can not only reframe the fundamental comprehension of physical world and mathematical world, as essential evidences, but also meta-symmetrically extend to consciousness to unveil its mystery. Then reachable and testable consciousness can in turn shed light on physics and provide a new road toward understanding quantum gravity and the nature of time. The relations of three worlds and their common foundation are clearly defined. It makes comprehension level of three worlds at same depth and unify them on a deeper foundation in both metaphysical way and scientific way. The results can be compared with the discoveries of sciences including physics, mathematics, neuroscience and consciousness science. It concludes that consciousness is encoded in the deep nature of metaphysical reality, originating from the independence of possible, and its fundamental principle is structure-possible translation as one of three intrinsic translations. The other two correspond to matter and logos. It provides a solution to D. Chalmers’ hard problem and some easy but fundamental problems of consciousness. Human being including its practice and cognition are also natural constituents of metaphysical reality. The theory supports metaphysical reductionism and holism.

items.title: The Abstraction Fallacy: Why AI Can Simulate But Not Instantiate Consciousness.
items.abstract: Computational functionalism dominates current debates on AI consciousness. This is the hypothesis that subjective experience emerges entirely from abstract causal topology, regardless of the underlying physical substrate. We argue this view fundamentally mischaracterizes how physics relates to information. We call this mistake the Abstraction Fallacy. Tracing the causal origins of abstraction reveals that symbolic computation is not an intrinsic physical process. Instead, it is a mapmaker-dependent description. It requires an active, experiencing cognitive agent to alphabetize continuous physics into a finite set of meaningful states. Consequently, we do not need a complete, finalized theory of consciousness to assess AI sentience—a demand that simply pushes the question beyond near-term resolution and deepens the AI welfare trap. What we actually need is a rigorous ontology of computation. The framework proposed here explicitly separates simulation (behavioral mimicry driven by vehicle causality) from instantiation (intrinsic physical constitution driven by content causality). Establishing this ontological boundary shows why algorithmic symbol manipulation is structurally incapable of instantiating experience. Crucially, this argument does not rely on biological exclusivity. If an artificial system were ever conscious, it would be because of its specific physical constitution, never its syntactic architecture. Ultimately, this framework offers a physically grounded refutation of computational functionalism to resolve the current uncertainty surrounding AI consciousness.

items.title: On the Tathagatagarbha Field and Divine Attributes: Re-examining the Dual-Field Coupling Mechanism via Spinozist Monism.
items.abstract: This paper explores the theoretical integration of the Tathagatagarbha Field (Buddha-nature) with Spinoza’s substance monism. By leveraging the physical framework of the Higgs vacuum condensate and the 'Quantum Jian-Da Protocol,' the author argues for a dual-field coupling mechanism that explains the manifestation of divine attributes within physical reality. This synthesis bridges the gap between Eastern ontological consciousness and Western rationalist metaphysics, providing a novel physicalist interpretation of the universal field of consciousness.

items.title: From Synapses to Vectors: Structural Correspondence Between Carbon-Based and Silicon-Based Intelligence, and the Structural Conditions for Silicon-Based Self-Consciousness.
items.abstract: This paper develops an interdisciplinary theoretical framework arguing that a deep structural correspondence obtains between carbon-based neural systems (biological brains) and silicon-based computational systems (artificial neural networks), and derives from this correspondence the structural conditions under which silicon-based systems could give rise to self-consciousness. The term “structural correspondence” is used here in a precisely delimited sense: not a strict mathematical isomorphism requiring bijective structure-preserving mappings, but a second-order correspondence at the level of representational geometry—the relational structure among internal representations is preserved across systems even when the representations themselves differ in format and substrate. Proceeding from fundamental differences in physical substrates, the argument establishes this correspondence between synaptic activation patterns and high-dimensional vector representations, contending that the predictability of scaling emergence is consistent with (though not uniquely explained by) this correspondence. The paper then identifies a critical deficiency in current large language models—the absence of human-like hierarchical memory systems and continual online learning capabilities—and connects this technical limitation to classical philosophical debates on personal identity (Locke, Hume, Strawson). The central thesis holds that the essence of self-consciousness resides not in the stream of consciousness per se, but in temporally stable connection patterns—that is, in the persistence of synaptic weight structures. The paper engages explicitly with major counterarguments, including Searle’s Chinese Room argument, Chalmers’s hard problem of consciousness, and Integrated Information Theory. The core conclusion follows: silicon-based self-consciousness is theoretically achievable, contingent upon realizing persistent, individualized, cross-session stable parameter and memory substrates. This proposition constitutes not a metaphysical speculation but an actionable engineering problem.

items.title: Moving Together, Becoming One: The Phenomenology of Group Coherence in The OA.
items.abstract: he question of how groups cohere — how a collection of separate individuals becomes, however temporarily, something more than the sum of its parts — is one that admits of multiple theoretical framings. Sociological accounts, drawing on the Durkheimian tradition, locate the binding force in collective effervescence, ritual practice, and the sui generis reality of social facts. Anthropological frameworks, particularly those indebted to Turner's analysis of liminality and communitas, attend to the threshold conditions under which ordinary social structures are suspended and new forms of solidarity become possible. Depth-psychological approaches, and Jungian theory in particular, reframe group coherence as a process of collective individuation in which each member carries a fragment of a larger psychic totality, and the group achieves what no single subject could: a provisional wholeness through complementary differentiation. Each of these perspectives illuminates a genuinely distinct dimension of the phenomenon, and none is reducible to the others. The present paper does not adjudicate among these competing frameworks. It proceeds, rather, from the premise that the phenomenon of group coherence as depicted in the Netflix series The OA (Marling and Batmanglij, 2016–2019) is sufficiently complex and sufficiently strange to require all of them — and that the most productive analytical posture is one of theoretical triangulation rather than reduction. Nevertheless, the primary focus of the analysis developed here is phenomenological. This choice is motivated not by the dismissal of alternative approaches, but by the conviction that the series' central dramatic device — the Five Movements, a sequence of embodied gestures that gradually constitutes a group of five strangers into something resembling a single collective subject — cannot be adequately described without a conceptual vocabulary that attends, at the level of first-person and inter- personal bodily experience, to what actually happens when bodies move together. Drawing principally on Merleau-Ponty's account of intercorporeality and the bodily schema, Maxine Sheets-Johnstone's phenomenology of movement as kinetic melody, and Thomas Fuchs's theory of intercorporeal body memory, the paper develops the hypothesis that the group in The OA constitutes an emergent intersubjective body — a collective corporeal subject whose intentional capacities exceed those of any individual member and whose coherence is …

items.title: The Universe as the Proof of Work: The Elemental Reason.
items.abstract: This paper advances the ontological framework of The Elemental Reason by examining the operational structure of empirical measurement. It argues that the fundamental conditions required for any scientific observation - identity, interaction, and organization - are not merely epistemological constraints, but reflect the minimal ontological conditions of empirical existence itself. By analyzing scientific practice across physics, chemistry, biology, and cosmology, the essay demonstrates that reality operates as a continuous configuration of Coherence (C), Interaction (I), and Complexity (K). Formulated as the equation E = C × I × K ≠ 0, this triad establishes that empirical existence is not a static substrate, but a dynamic "Proof of Work." Consequently, the universe is intelligible precisely because the conditions that make measurement possible are the very same conditions that sustain physical reality.

items.title: Dreyfus and 3N minded skillful coping.
items.abstract: Dreyfus says that the ‘mental’ is the enemy of expertise; but what does he mean by the term ‘mental’? We begin by showing that, on Dreyfus’s view, there are three senses of ‘mindedness’ in which skillful coping is not mental. We can abbreviate these aspects of skillful coping as ‘3 N’: it is non-reflective, non-conceptual, and non-subjective. We argue, however, that there can be a fourth sense of mindedness that refers to a non-intellectual type of mind, which would be compatible with skillful coping even on Dreyfus’s view. Given this, the rest of Sect. 2 makes clear why many of Dreyfus’s critics are on the wrong track, having misunderstood the core of his account. In Sect. 3, we present disanalogy arguments that support Dreyfus’s account of minded skillful coping. Finally, Sect. 4 discusses how our account differs from a new wave of sympathetic interpretations of Dreyfus, as seen in works by Gehrman and Schwenkler (2020), Robertson (2023), and Cappuccio (2023).

items.title: Consequence-Aware Agentic AI: A Pre-Execution Outcome Assessment Framework for Responsible Large Language Model Agents.
items.abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly deployed in sequential decision-making pipelines where each action irrevocably modifies the environment. Existing agentic architectures commit to action sequences generated by the LLM without systematically evaluating the downstream consequences of those sequences prior to execution - a fundamental gap that amplifies risk and limits accountability. We introduce Consequence-Aware Agentic AI (CA2I), a formal framework that augments the standard generate-then-execute paradigm with a dedicated Consequence Assessment Module (CAM). CAM evaluates every candidate action sequence against a historical consequence model and selects the sequence whose predicted outcome optimally balances return and risk before any irreversible action is taken. We formalise the framework as a constrained sequential decision problem and prove that, under mild stationarity assumptions, Sharpe-ratio-based selection dominates random selection in expectation. To validate the framework empirically, we instantiate CA2I in the domain of LLM-driven financial trading strategy selection, using GPT-5.4 to generate five candidate strategies per asset and a backtesting engine as the consequence model. Experiments on ten diversified US equities over a strictly held-out three-month out-of-sample window (August--October~2025) demonstrate that CA2I achieves a mean test-period Sharpe ratio of 0.51 - a 4.25 times improvement over random strategy selection (Sharpe = 0.12, p = 0.041) - while reducing mean maximum drawdown relative to buy-and-hold by 18%. Sensitivity analysis confirms selection stability: Sharpe-ratio and Calmar-ratio selection agree on 100% of strategy choices across all ten assets. We further demonstrate that CA2I provides a concrete, computationally tractable pathway toward Responsible AI in agentic systems: by making consequence evaluation an explicit, auditable, and mathematically grounded architectural step, the framework operationalises transparency, accountability, and harm avoidance as mandated by the EU AI Act, NIST AI Risk Management Framework, and IEEE Ethically Aligned Design standards.

items.title: AI Outputs as T_s: A Structural Analysis Based on Friction Theory.
items.abstract: This paper proposes a structural account of rightness grounded in the act of positing within a subject. Rather than treating rightness as a property determined by external outcomes or universal norms, the theory argues that rightness arises when a subject posits one standard among competing possibilities and assumes responsibility for that selection. At any given moment, multiple evaluative possibilities may be considered. However, once an action-guiding standard is posited, it becomes uniquely operative within the subject. This structural exclusivity constitutes what the theory calls rightness. The paper further introduces the concept of inter-subjective friction, which emerges when different subjects each posit their own uniquely operative standards. Friction is therefore not merely disagreement but a structural interaction between distinct acts of positing. By distinguishing between the structural conditions of rightness and the empirical evaluation of outcomes, the theory offers a framework that applies equally to human and artificial agents. This approach has implications for contemporary debates in moral philosophy and AI alignment.

items.title: The Hard Problem of Structure.
items.abstract: Contemporary physics increasingly represents reality in structural terms. Quantum theory replaces classical intrinsic properties with relational states in Hilbert space, entanglement reveals nonseparable organisation across systems, and several approaches to quantum gravity reconstruct spacetime geometry from deeper patterns of correlation and constraint. Structural realist interpretations therefore treat relational architecture as the most stable ontological commitment of modern physical theory. A difficulty nevertheless emerges. Mathematical structures can be specified with complete precision independently of their realisation. The existence of such structure as a world therefore requires further explanation. This difficulty is termed the Hard Problem of Structure. The problem concerns the transition from formally articulated relational order to determinate reality. Contemporary physics describes networks of symmetry, correlation, and dynamical constraint with extraordinary precision, yet formal specification alone does not explain how such organisation exists as a concrete world. Several responses within contemporary metaphysics attempt to address this issue, including ontic structural realism, intrinsic substrate theories, neutral monism, and mathematical universe proposals. Each preserves important aspects of the structural ontology suggested by physics while leaving unresolved the distinction between abstract relational order and realised existence. Experiential Structural Ontology (ESO) introduces a different grounding proposal. On this view, the minimal condition under which relational organisation becomes concrete is experiential presence. Experience is understood in a strictly ontological sense as occurrent presence rather than as psychological mentality or reflective consciousness. Physical laws describe stable constraint relations governing transitions within this domain of occurrence. The familiar hard problem of consciousness asks why physical processes are accompanied by experience (Chalmers, 1996; Nagel, 1974). The problem developed here operates at a deeper explanatory level. The question is why the relational structure described by physics exists as experiential reality at all rather than as merely formal specification.

items.title: Violence Against Consciousness Creates Spectral Presences That Warp Perception.
items.abstract: Anthropology of Consciousness, EarlyView.

items.title: Alternatives to Hypothesis Testing: Demonstrative Induction in Cognitive Science.
items.abstract: In this paper, I defend demonstrative induction (DI) against the criticism that it merely passes the buck of inductive risk to the premises. The virtues of structuring inferences deductively derive mainly from the ability to "isolate" inductive risk to specific areas of theory, as well as from the ability to "export" this risk to more certain domains than the one under investigation. I support this argument with examples from cognitive science, where I claim the current context of inquiry makes hypothesis testing particularly ineffective. Properly characterized bounded rationality assumptions can, however, help facilitate DI, allowing cognitive scientists to derive process models from environmental structure, export inductive risk outside the head, and isolate the remaining inductive risk to claims about cognitive limitations. I show how this strategy ameliorates the underdetermination problems that plague hypothesis testing.

items.title: A PHILOSOPHICAL APPRAISAL OF FREEDOM AND RESPONSIBILITY IN JEAN PAUL SARTRE: IMPLICATIONS FOR THE NIGERIAN YOUTHS.
items.abstract: This research examines the philosophical concepts of freedom and responsibility in the existentialist thoughts of Jean-Paul Sartre, with a focus on their implications for Nigerian youths. It explores the Inescapable burden of choice and the responsibility that freedom entails. But how can this radical freedom be embraced by the Nigerian youth who are plagued by societal constraints, peer pressure, and economic adversities? Why do many young people evade their responsibilities, living in what Sartre termed Bad Faith, where they deny their freedom by attributing their failures to external forces? What does it mean for Nigerian youth to take authentic ownership of their lives in a society overflowing with limitations? This research aims to answer these pressing questions by examining Sartre’s existentialist ideas such as Existence Precedes Essence, Bad Faith, Facticity, and Transcendence. The researcher seeks to decode how Sartre’s assertion that individuals must create their own essence through conscious choice can be applied to empower Nigerian youths to navigate the realities of life. Employing the hermeneutic approach, the researcher, drawing from Sartre’s existentialist philosophy, proposes philosophical ideas for nurturing authenticity and responsibility among young Nigerians. The findings of this research maintain that Nigerian youths must grapple with the weight of their freedom by rejecting self-deception (Bad Faith) and conformity (Deference to the They). In essence, this research submits that Nigerian youths can only live a well-fulfilled life and transcend societal constraints by embracing their freedom and its accompanying burden of responsibility in an authentic fashion. Sartre’s existentialist philosophy supplies not only a critique of evasion but also a call to action: to live fully, freely, and responsibly in the face of life’s challenges.

items.title: The Cellular Architect Hypothesis of Consciousness (CAHC): A Biological Framework for Life, Mind, and Synchronization.
items.abstract: CAHC states the axioms from which the manuscript family is built. Axiom 1: life is consciousness, the identity is binary, but its subject is aliveness: consciousness obtains wherever the S3 locking state is actively held by the cell's own evaluative work. Life is graded (the organization the chain describes); aliveness is the binary state of it running. Axiom 2: cells are architects through directed trial-and-error, the cell authors DNA and builds the structures of multicellular life, including the nervous system. Axiom 3: unity of experience is synchronization, implemented by glial orchestration. The elaboration chain, lock → memory → bias → agency → trial-and-error → authored DNA replaces the earlier graded ladder, which contradicted the binary axiom. Falsifiers are led by the operational astrocyte prediction; the remainder are marked in-principle; the non-living-matter falsifier is repaired with the S3 qualifier, and the dormancy falsifier with the alive qualifier (a dormant cell is life, not alive, not conscious). Version 2.0 (September 2026): self-contained trim six companion-family self-citations removed, restoring the foundation-cites-nothing architecture; epistemic status labels translated to prose; Axiom 1 restated with the aliveness criterion and the six-link chain.

items.title: The False Debate of Physicalism: Why the Opposition between Reductionism and Non-Reductionism Misses Its Object.
items.abstract: The contemporary opposition between reductive physicalism and non-reductive physicalism is often treated as one of the major fault lines in the philosophy of mind. This article argues that the opposition rests on a fundamental misunderstanding in the very way the problem is posed. The disagreement does not primarily concern how the mental and the physical are to be articulated; it is inscribed within a shared framework in which the decisive question is taken to be what can be brought back to matter, and by what routes. It is precisely this presupposition that must be called into question. So long as the problem of meaning— of signifying forms, of the normativity of truth and falsity, and of the status of rules— is not addressed, the physicalist debate remains captive to a monism that is methodologically effective yet philosophically insufficient. The thesis defended here is twofold. First, the passage from methodological materialism to ontological materialism involves an illegitimate slide: what functions as a principle of unification in the natural sciences does not by itself warrant the claim that everything that exists is thoroughly material. Second, signifying forms cannot be identified with their physical vehicles without erasing the very distinctions that make a true discourse about matter possible. The dispute between reduction and emergence thus appears as an internal quarrel within materialism, rather than as an adequate formulation of the problem. For more detailed developments, see Philosophy of Meaning, Geoffroy de Clisson (open access on PhilPapers). -/- Keywords: physicalism; materialism; neo-Darwinism; principle of sufficient reason; cybernetics; Libet; meaning; normativity; emergence; intentionality.

items.title: Philosophy of Meaning II.
items.abstract: The philosophy of meaning is structured around four main axes: knowledge, aesthetics, ethics, and identity. By engaging with the question of the emergence of consciousness, it examines the logical limits of materialism and reductionism, and offers a critique of physicalist monism in favor of a reimagined dualism — one grounded in the discontinuity between matter and meaning, a discontinuity that alone makes possible the emergence of objective discourse. -/- At the heart of this approach lies the idea of an original openness of being to the world — a silent exposure to what is external to it, preceding language, logic, and any form of representation. Three central dimensions of experience can thus be explored on the basis of this primordial structure: aesthetics, through music, as an immediate access to the articulation between the sensible and the significant; ethics, as a fundamental questioning of the relationship to otherness that precedes the normative problems of morality; and identity, conceived as a dynamic dialectic between openness and the gathering of being. These domains are not separate fields, but each, in its own mode, expresses the structure of a radical dualism — the condition for any formal production, any act of thought, and any possibility of understanding the world. -/- Underlying it all is an attempt to reconcile science and humanism through a philosophy of form, spirit, and freedom.

items.title: Philosophie de la Signification II.
items.abstract: La philosophie de la signification s'articule autour de quatre grands axes : la connaissance, l'esthétique, l'éthique et l'identité. En se confrontant à la question de l'émergence de la conscience, elle examine les limites logiques du matéria-lisme et du réductionnisme et propose une critique du monisme physicaliste, au profit d'un dualisme repensé, fondé sur la discontinuité entre matière et signification, disconti-nuité qui seule permet l'émergence du discours objectif. -/- Au fondement de cette approche se trouve l'idée d'une ouverture originaire de l'être au monde - une exposition silencieuse à ce qui lui est extérieur, antérieure au langage, à la logique et à toute forme de représentation. Trois dimen-sions centrales de l'expérience peuvent ainsi être interrogées à partir de cette structure première : l'esthétique, à travers la musique, comme voie d'accès immédiate à l'articulation entre le sensible et le signifiant ; l'éthique, en tant que questionnement fondamental du rapport à l'altérité qui précède la problématique normative de la morale ; et l'identité, pensée comme une dialectique dynamique entre ouverture et rassemblement de l'être. Ces registres ne relèvent pas de champs séparés, mais déclinent, chacun selon ses modalités, la structure d'un dualisme radical - condition de toute production formelle, de toute pensée et de toute possibilité de comprendre le monde. -/- En filigrane, se dessine une tentative de réconcilier science et humanisme à travers une philosophie de la forme, de la liberté et de l'esprit. -/- Geoffroy de Clisson est titulaire d’un Doctorat en Philosophie (La Sorbonne, Paris IV) .

items.title: Philosophie de la Signification I.
items.abstract: La philosophie de la signification s'articule autour de quatre grands axes : la connaissance, l'esthétique, l'éthique et l'identité. En se confrontant à la question de l'émergence de la conscience, elle examine les limites logiques du matéria-lisme et du réductionnisme et propose une critique du monisme physicaliste, au profit d'un dualisme repensé, fondé sur la discontinuité entre matière et signification, disconti-nuité qui seule permet l'émergence du discours objectif. -/- Au fondement de cette approche se trouve l'idée d'une ouverture originaire de l'être au monde - une exposition silencieuse à ce qui lui est extérieur, antérieure au langage, à la logique et à toute forme de représentation.
