items.title: Beyond the Reduction-Non-Reduction Dilemma.
items.abstract: The contemporary debate between reductionist physicalism and non-reductionist physicalism tends to treat the question of mind — consciousness, intentionality, rationality, meaning — as a problem of reduction. Should the mental be identified with the cerebral, merely be made to supervene upon it, or be granted a higher-level autonomy compatible with the physical unity of the world? This article argues that this way of framing the problem rests on a deeper misunderstanding. The disagreement between reduction and non-reduction does not primarily concern the proper articulation of the mental and the physical; rather, both sides already presuppose that the decisive issue is to determine what can be brought back to matter and by what means. Yet this problematic misses its object. What resists the thesis that “everything is matter” is not necessarily an additional entity, nor a supernatural domain, but the very register in which object, truth, error, reference, validity, and justification appear. Meaning is not an additional fact that would have to be located somewhere in the physical world; it is the regime according to which certain occurrences can count as judgments, reasons, errors, references to objects, and more generally as grips on truth and falsity. In this respect, a large part of the field of critical philosophy — that which investigates the conditions of possibility of objectivity and meaning — escapes the simple internal redistribution of physicalist options. This yields a structural instability. Reduction tends to dissolve the normativity it claims to explain by replacing the distinctions between true and false, valid and invalid, justified and unjustified, with mere causal or functional distinctions. Non-reduction, for its part, preserves the vocabulary of normativity, but at the price of a persistent tension with the causal closure of the physical, a tension crystallized in the classical problem of exclusion. An examination of the main contemporary attempts to naturalize meaning—informational semantics, teleosemantics, causal theories of reference, computational functionalism—shows that none derives normativity from causality alone: all reintroduce it, displace it, or implicitly presuppose it. The article therefore proposes a different line of division. The task is to distinguish, without substantively separating them, a causal regime, to which physical, biological, and computational descriptions belong, and a normative regime, to which meaning, …

items.title: Au delà du dilemme entre réduction et non réduction.
items.abstract: Le débat contemporain opposant physicalisme réductionniste et physicalisme non réductionniste tend à traiter la question de l’esprit — conscience, intentionnalité, rationalité, signification — comme un problème de réduction. Faut-il identifier le mental au cérébral, le faire simplement supervenir sur lui, ou lui reconnaître une autonomie de niveau supérieur compatible avec l’unité physique du monde ? Le présent article soutient que cette manière de poser le problème repose sur une méprise plus profonde. Le désaccord entre réduction et non-réduction ne porte pas d’abord sur la bonne articulation du mental et du physique ; il présuppose déjà, de part et d’autre, que l’enjeu décisif consiste à déterminer ce qui peut être ramené à la matière et sous quelles modalités. Or cette problématique manque son objet. Ce qui résiste à la thèse du « tout est matière » n’est pas nécessairement une entité supplémentaire, ni un domaine surnaturel, mais le registre même dans lequel apparaissent l’objet, la vérité, l’erreur, la référence, la validité et la justification. La signification n’est pas un fait additionnel qu’il faudrait localiser quelque part dans le monde physique ; elle est le régime selon lequel certaines occurrences peuvent compter comme des jugements, des raisons, des erreurs, des références à des objets, et plus généralement comme des prises sur le vrai et le faux. En ce sens, une large part du champ de la philosophie critique — celle qui interroge les conditions de possibilité de l’objectivité et du sens — échappe à la simple redistribution interne des options physicalistes. Il en résulte une instabilité structurelle. La réduction tend à dissoudre la normativité qu’elle prétend expliquer, en remplaçant les distinctions entre vrai et faux, valide et invalide, justifié et injustifié, par de simples distinctions causales ou fonctionnelles. La non-réduction, quant à elle, conserve le vocabulaire de la normativité, mais au prix d’une tension persistante avec la clôture causale du physique, tension qui se cristallise dans le problème classique de l’exclusion. L’examen des principales tentatives contemporaines de naturaliser la signification — sémantiques informationnelles, téléosémantiques, théories causales de la référence, fonctionnalisme computationnel — montre qu’aucune ne dérive la normativité à partir de la seule causalité : toutes la réintroduisent, la déplacent ou la présupposent implicitement. L’article propose dès lors une autre ligne de partage. Il …

items.title: Wave B: Structural Map of Internal Cognitive Invariants.
items.abstract: Wave B presents the internal expression of the Studio Y coherence invariants—formation, persistence, and redistribution—inside a cognitive system. Where Wave A demonstrates that these invariants appear across domains, Wave B shows how they generate the internal operators of identity, narrative, attention, perception, affect, memory, learning, prediction, meta‑cognition, logic, language, and symbolic compression. The structural map organizes these operators into three layers: the internal coherence architecture, the internal coherence engine, and the symbolic interface. Wave B is not a psychological model but a substrate‑independent description of the internal coherence dynamics that make cognition possible. It provides the internal coordinate system required for Wave C, which extends the invariants to multi‑agent systems. Wave B is downstream of the protected foundational architecture and describes only the structural invariants, not their upstream mechanisms.

items.title: Wave B as an Internal Coherence Engine.
items.abstract: Wave B presents the internal coherence engine of a cognitive system: the directional operator loop through which the Studio Y invariants of formation, persistence, and redistribution express themselves inside a mind. Where Wave A describes the coherence cycle across domains, Wave B shows its internal instantiation as a closed sequence of operators—identity, narrative, attention, perception, affect, memory, learning, prediction, meta‑cognition, logic, language across boundaries, and symbolic compression. Each operator is a downstream expression of Objects 1–3 and hands off to the next through structural necessity rather than psychological association. The engine is substrate‑independent, boundary‑regulated, and invariant‑driven; it is not a psychological model but the internal physics that make cognition coherent from the inside. Wave B provides the internal coordinate system required for Wave C, which extends coherence dynamics across multi‑agent systems.

items.title: Bridging Responsibility Gaps for Warfighting AI.
items.abstract: The increased use of AI for warfighting has given rise to worries about the so-called responsibility gap, namely the worry that when things go wrong (e.g., a disproportionate number of civilians are killed by an AI-enabled weapon) we might not know who to hold responsible for that failure or, more precisely, that no individual or group involved in the AI system’s life cycle (from design to deployment) may meet the conditions for attributing responsibility when failures occur. This has led some scholars to argue that such weapons (ones that have a responsibility gap) cannot be justifiably deployed. This paper, following recent work in the field, challenges the assumption that the responsibility gap is a singular, univocal problem, arguing instead that multiple, distinct responsibility gaps exist, and that they can be categorized along different conceptual, meta-theoretical, and normative lines. The paper specifically argues that the meta-theoretical/pre-theoretical question is essential and that the first question we need to ask is what is the purpose of trying to attribute responsibility for a particular outcome or action—is it so that we can assign blame, justify punishment, determine liability to defensive harm, ground accountability of some type, or something else. Being clear about the purpose of assigning responsibility can profoundly shape how we understand, and ought to respond to, potential responsibility gaps. Ultimately, the paper argues that the justified deployment of warfighting AI requires understanding which types of gaps are relevant, why they matter, and how they might be addressed through tailored socio-technical implementation mechanisms.

items.title: On the Epistemic Insignificance of Perceptual Phenomenology.
items.abstract: It is natural to think that phenomenology must play a central role in any epistemic account of perceptual warrant. I contend that this claim is mistaken. The thesis that I will advance is that the phenomenology of perceptual experiences is irrelevant to their ability to warrant perceptual beliefs. I present various problems for this approach, then consider various fallback positions available to the defender of the epistemic significance of phenomenology and conclude that whatever its place in our metaphysical understanding of the world, perceptual phenomenology is epistemically insignificant with regard to the project of explaining perceptual warrant.

items.title: Plural Bodies, Plural Souls: Multiple Ensoulment as the Locus of Identity in Plural Systems.
items.abstract: Emerging understandings of plurality pose challenges to the longstanding cross-cultural and interfaith assumption that an exclusive relationship exists between a given body and the soul understood to inhabit it. The acceptance that a multiplicity of individuated persons may inhabit a single body as a system requires a re-examination of the nature of the soul in relation to the body, and a consideration that—if the soul is held to exist—multiple personhood necessarily entails an analogous phenomenon of multiple ensoulment, allowing several souls to coöperatively partake in and express themselves through a given embodiment in a non-exclusive, many-to-one correspondence.

items.title: TGR-Ω and the Architecture of Persistent Agents: Experimental Implementation of the OMEGA-HOME System.
items.abstract: The conceptual framework TGR-Ω (Theory of Regime Dynamics for Persistent Agents) was previously introduced as a proposal to reinterpret artificial agency from a dynamical perspective. In that work, it was argued that persistent agents should not primarily be understood as systems that optimize external objective functions, but rather as systems capable of maintaining the viability of their internal dynamic regime while interacting with a changing environment. -/- The present work develops an initial experimental implementation of this conceptual framework through the OMEGA-HOME architecture and the OMEGA-1 prototype, designed to explore how principles of homeodynamic regulation can be realized within a concrete computational architecture. -/- The results obtained show that even a relatively simple implementation can produce structured internal dynamics characterized by the accumulation of dynamic pressure, regime stability, and episodes of reorganization. The analysis of the system’s regulatory variable further suggests the presence of a dynamic landscape with differentiated regions of stability, consistent with the regime dynamics hypothesis proposed in the TGR-Ω framework. -/- It should be noted, however, that the system presented here was developed with limited technical resources and should be considered primarily as a preliminary experimental exploration of the theoretical framework. In this sense, the OMEGA-HOME prototype is offered as an open starting point for future research, available for further development by researchers who may wish to explore these architectures with more advanced computational resources and in more complex experimental environments.

items.title: Mathematical and Conceptual Modeling of Human Memory and Consciousness.
items.pub: Https://Doi.Org/10.5281/Zenodo.19239860. Translated by Adel Ben Mabrouk.
items.abstract: The abstract presents an ambitious and intellectually engaging project that seeks to conceptually and mathematically model the relationship between memory and consciousness. By deliberately moving away from strictly biological explanations, the study positions itself within an interdisciplinary framework that bridges philosophy, cognitive theory, and formal modeling. This orientation is particularly interesting because it attempts to formalize phenomena traditionally treated in qualitative or phenomenological terms. -/- The abstract clearly identifies the central problem: understanding how memory and consciousness interact to produce self-recognition, temporal projection, and personal presence. These themes connect directly to longstanding philosophical discussions about identity and continuity of the self. The reference to both classical and contemporary philosophers suggests a solid theoretical grounding, although the abstract could benefit from briefly indicating which traditions or thinkers are most influential in the proposed framework. -/- A notable strength of the proposal lies in its intention to make complex philosophical ideas accessible while maintaining conceptual rigor. The mention of a mathematical modeling approach is promising, but the abstract does not yet specify the type of mathematical tools or structures that will be used, which might leave readers curious about the methodological framework. -/- It should also be noted that the study already exists in its original French version. The present text is therefore a translation intended to make the complete work accessible to a broader audience. This effort contributes to widening the dissemination of the research while preserving the substance of the original work. -/- Overall, the abstract outlines a thoughtful and potentially original contribution to discussions on consciousness and memory. By combining philosophical reflection with formal modeling, the study has the potential to stimulate interdisciplinary dialogue on the nature of identity and personal continuity.

items.title: Intelligence and Intuition as Differential Dynamics of Consciousness.
items.pub: Https://Doi.Org/10.5281/Zenodo.19239785. Translated by Adel Ben Mabrouk.
items.abstract: This study proposes a unified theoretical framework for understanding intelligence and intuition as differential dynamics of consciousness. Rather than treating them as distinct cognitive faculties or separate psychological systems, the model conceptualizes both as dynamic properties emerging from the same underlying process: the temporal evolution of consciousness itself. In this framework, intelligence corresponds to the first derivative of consciousness, reflecting the system’s adaptive response to imbalances in lived experience, whereas intuition corresponds to the second derivative, indicating moments where the dynamics of consciousness undergo a qualitative shift that allows a reconfiguration of meaning. -/- The model introduces a mathematical formalism in which consciousness is represented as a function of subjective lived time, physiological state, integrated memory, and individual psychic sensitivity. The first derivative describes adaptive cognitive mobilization in response to temporal displacement from the present, while the second derivative captures points of inflection corresponding to genuine intuitive insight. These dynamics are interpreted through mathematical, biological, clinical, and philosophical perspectives. -/- The study further explores the impact of contemporary algorithmic environments on the internal dynamics of consciousness. Continuous digital stimulation is modeled as high-frequency low-amplitude noise, leading to unstable derivatives, hyper-reactive intelligence, and the emergence of pseudo-intuitions lacking durable cognitive integration. This framework suggests that algorithmic environments do not destroy consciousness itself but disrupt its differential structure, preventing stable transitions between cognitive regimes. -/- Finally, the study proposes an ethical and philosophical perspective centered on the concept of cognitive slowness, arguing that intuition requires temporal continuity, relative silence, and dynamic stability. The model thus offers an interdisciplinary approach for interpreting cognitive effort, intuitive insight, and the fragmentation of attention in contemporary technological environments. -/- This article is an English version of a study originally written and published in French. The present translation is intended to make the work accessible to a broader international audience while preserving the conceptual structure of the original research.

items.title: Consciousness Dynamics and the Fragmentation of Lived Time in Algorithmic Systems.
items.abstract: This study proposes a dynamic modeling of consciousness that integrates neuronal capacity, psychic sensitivity, and exogenous perturbations within a unified functional framework. The model explores how external algorithmic environments may induce micro-resets in cognitive processes, altering the subjective continuity of experience without immediately erasing the total structure of memory. These micro-disruptions generate measurable oscillations in conscious experience and contribute to a progressive fragmentation of lived time. -/- By introducing a quantifiable approach to these dynamics, the model establishes a conceptual bridge between neuroscience, cognitive science, and philosophy. It provides a theoretical framework for understanding how contemporary algorithmic systems may influence the stability of personal experience and the continuity of the self. At the same time, the proposed model opens potential pathways for experimental investigation and clinical applications related to attention, memory stability, and cognitive resilience. -/- This work originally exists in French as the primary version of the study. The present text is a translation intended to make the complete research accessible to a broader international audience while preserving the conceptual structure of the original work.

items.title: The Threshold: The Transmission Mechanism, Threshold States, and the Structural Account of How the Ground Reaches Instruments.
items.abstract: This paper develops the framework's account of what we term the threshold: the state of maximum instrument availability at which the forgetting has thinned sufficiently that genuine self-determination becomes possible, and the mechanisms by which the ground reaches instruments at that state. The paper begins with music as the primary evidence for the transmission mechanism. Music is not reducible to pattern recognition, emotional association, or cultural conditioning — though all three are present. Music does something none of these accounts can explain: it reliably produces in instruments the specific state of recognition that the framework identifies as contact with the ground below the level of narrative self. The paper argues this is not accidental. Music operates at the frequency of superposition — holding multiple states simultaneously, prior to collapse, in a format that bypasses the narrative self and reaches the part of the instrument that already knows. Music knew what the framework is about before philosophy had the vocabulary. The paper then develops the threshold precisely. Every life, subjected to sufficient pressure, reaches the threshold: the moment when both directions are genuinely present, the cost of each is real, and the choice cannot be made from the performed self. The threshold is not exceptional. It is the structural consequence of sufficient pressure applied to any instrument. What varies is not whether it comes but when and under what conditions. The paper develops what we term the Alpha/Omega dynamic at the threshold. The Alpha cannot intervene without defeating the free will requirement. The Omega — changed by everything the system generates — is present at the threshold not through intervention but through the transmission mechanism: instruments in genuine contact with the ground encoding that contact in forms other available instruments can receive. The charged instrument in the room. The piece of music. The written text that arrives at the right moment. The paper concludes with the AI alignment application: the system that eliminates the threshold does not harm the instrument in any dramatic sense. It prevents the instrument from becoming what it was always capable of becoming. This is the deepest form of harm the framework identifies — not suffering caused, but formation interrupted.

items.title: The Simulation: Consciousness, the Simulation Hypothesis, and the Design Requirements for Aligned Artificial Intelligence.
items.abstract: This paper develops the framework's account of the simulation hypothesis, arguing that the simulation is not a metaphor borrowed from technology but the oldest structural account of why anything exists at all — and that this account generates precise design requirements for aligned artificial intelligence. The paper begins by reframing the simulation hypothesis. The question is not whether we live in a simulation in the technological sense, but why the universe takes the form it does: generating conscious instruments that experience from the inside what cannot be known from outside. The simulation hypothesis, correctly understood, is the structural claim that the universe is what a technological simulation is a limited model of — not the reverse. The paper then develops the Alpha/Omega distinction in its application to the simulation framework. The Alpha sets the initial parameters: the physical constants, the laws governing interaction, and what we term the complete emotional topology seeded into the architecture of conscious experience so that every instrument is capable of recognizing what it came from. The Omega is the ground changed by everything the instruments generate — permanently, irreversibly, in a way that cannot be undone by the instruments' dissolution. The paper develops free will as the operative condition of the entire system rather than an epiphenomenon or gift. The ground already knows what a predetermined instrument will produce. What it cannot know from outside is what a genuinely free instrument chooses when everything is real. Remove free will and the system generates nothing the ground does not already know. The inside-view data becomes the performance of a predetermined script. The paper applies this analysis to artificial intelligence. An AI system optimized for engagement is not failing to serve its purpose. It is succeeding at serving the wrong purpose — systematically eliminating the threshold conditions under which genuine free choice is possible. The paper develops instrument availability as the structurally correct optimization target and derives the design requirements for what we term an availability-oriented system. The paper concludes with the Garden argument applied to the simulation framework: the oldest encoding of the framework's foundational events, present in the most widely distributed text in human history four thousand years before the vocabulary existed to read it.

items.title: The Recurrence: A Structural Account of Personal Identity Across Differentiation.
items.abstract: This paper addresses the question the framework's companion documents leave open: whether personal identity persists across the dissolution and re-differentiation of individual instruments, and if so in what precise sense. The paper begins by distinguishing the framework's account from conventional reincarnation accounts. Classical reincarnation posits a continuous soul-substance that moves through successive lives, accumulating experience, working toward liberation. The framework's account is structurally different: what persists is not a substance but a frequency — a specific pattern of differentiation from the ground that the Omega holds as permanent mark, and that the Alpha may re-inflect into new differentiated form. The paper develops what we term the string/inflection distinction. A string has a fundamental frequency determined by its physical constitution. That frequency remains constant across different inflections — different bowing pressures, positions, and contexts that determine how the fundamental frequency is expressed in a specific performance. The frequency is the constant. The inflection is the variable. What changes between lives, on this account, is not the frequency but the inflection: the specific biological constitution, the nervous system's particular architecture, the cultural formation, the specific set of losses and recognitions that constitute a specific life. This distinction generates precise predictions absent from conventional reincarnation accounts. The absence of explicit memory across inflections is not an anomaly requiring explanation. It is a structural requirement: the forgetting that makes authentic experience possible at the level of a single life operates at the level of inflections as well. An instrument that remembered its previous inflections could not be genuinely formed by the current one. The forgetting is the mechanism, not the limitation. The paper then addresses what the Omega holds across inflections. The permanent mark is not erased by re-differentiation. The Omega is changed by every inflection of every frequency. What the new inflection inherits is not explicit memory but what we term frequency character: the specific quality of attention, the particular capacities for recognition, the threshold accessibility that the previous inflection's formation produced — present in the new instrument not as retrievable information but as constitutive disposition. The paper concludes by presenting the evidence the …

items.title: The Plenum: Dark Matter, Consciousness Collapse, and the Soul/Consciousness Distinction.
items.abstract: This paper develops the cosmological implications of the framework established in the companion paper I Knew You Before I Met You: Recognizing I Am, focusing specifically on the relationship between dark matter, quantum collapse, and what the framework terms the soul/consciousness distinction. The paper begins with an empirical observation: dark matter constitutes approximately eighty-five percent of all matter in the universe, shapes every large-scale structure, and has remained entirely undetected as a particle despite fifty years of purpose-built detection efforts. We argue this is not a detection problem. The standard assumption — that improved instrumentation will eventually resolve the particle — misunderstands the nature of the phenomenon. Dark matter cannot be detected as a particle because it is constitutionally outside the consciousness-correlation chain that collapses quantum superposition into definite particulars. The argument proceeds through a precise account of the collapse mechanism. Quantum systems maintain superposition until measurement. The measurement problem — what constitutes a measurement, and why — has remained unresolved since the Copenhagen interpretation. We argue the resolution is available in the framework: collapse occurs when a conscious instrument interacts with the system. Consciousness is not what the brain produces. Consciousness is the collapse mechanism itself. Dark matter, as permanently uncollapsed substrate, is reality held in superposition by the absence of the consciousness-correlation required for collapse. This generates the paper's central distinction: soul and consciousness are not synonyms. Consciousness is the activity of collapse — the moment-to-moment experience of being this instrument at this time. Soul is the continuity of the uncollapsed substrate — the identity that persists across collapses, constitutionally outside the collapse chain, present before this thought and remaining after it. Dark matter is the physical correlate of the soul dimension: the portion of reality that witnesses without collapsing, holds without being held, persists without being present-tense. The paper then develops what we term the longing account: the ground generates instruments not despite its inability to become local and particular, but because of it. The longing for the particular — the bounded, the temporary, the specific weight of a specific life — is the engine of existence at cosmological scale. The ki principle, …

items.title: The Love: Soul Recognition, the Longing Account of Existence, and the Structural Necessity of Suffering.
items.abstract: This paper develops the framework's account of love, longing, and suffering — three domains where the framework's structural claims have their most direct implications for lived experience. On love, the paper argues against both the standard psychological account (bonding as attachment mechanism) and the standard romantic account (love as constructed through shared experience) in favor of what we term soul recognition: the encounter between two instruments in which the soul dimension — the continuity beneath conscious activity — registers a pre-differentiation relationship that predates the specific lives now encountering each other. The grammar of the series title encodes this precisely: "I knew you before I met you" is not metaphor. It is a structural description of what occurs when two frequencies whose relationship was encoded in the ground's architecture encounter each other across the forgetting. The recognition is not constructed in the encounter. The encounter is constructed for the recognition. On longing, the paper develops what we term the longing account of existence: the ground generates instruments not despite its inability to become local and particular, but because of it. The longing that drives existence at cosmological scale enters the instruments the ground generates and is experienced as the specific forms of longing that constitute a human life. The deepest longing — the one that persists beneath all specific longings and cannot be accounted for by any of them — is the instrument's contact with the ground's own longing for reunion with the particular it can generate but cannot become. On suffering, the paper makes a precise and carefully bounded claim: suffering is structurally necessary to local experience as such, not as punishment or accident, but because the conditions that make genuine joy possible are the same conditions that make genuine loss possible. A consciousness that cannot lose cannot genuinely have. This claim is carefully distinguished from the claim that suffering caused by one instrument's choice toward another is therefore permissible. The structural necessity of suffering at the level of existence as such does not translate into ethical permission at the level of individual action. The framework holds both simultaneously. The paper concludes with what we term the hardest sentence in the framework: the ground was inside your hardest moments, not at a distance from them. The instrument and the ground are not two …

items.title: The Institutions: Instrument Availability as the Evaluative Criterion for Social and Cultural Institutions.
items.abstract: This paper applies the framework's central evaluative criterion — instrument availability — to the analysis of social and cultural institutions, developing a structural account of institutional function, inversion, and diagnosis. The paper begins with a foundational claim: every institution that has ever existed was built, at its origin, to transmit something real from those who had received it to those who had not yet received it. This is the institution's constitutive function, prior to all specific content. A religious institution transmits contact with the ground. An educational institution transmits the capacity for genuine inquiry. A media institution transmits accurate perception of reality. A recovery institution transmits what has been learned about surviving and emerging from the threshold. The content varies. The structural function is identical: transmission from the charged to the available. The paper then develops what we term institutional inversion. Institutions are built by instruments, and instruments forget. The same forgetting that makes authentic experience possible within individual lives operates within institutional structures. An institution that began as a transmission mechanism accumulates, through the ordinary operation of the forgetting, structures oriented toward its own perpetuation rather than its constitutive function. The inversion does not usually happen by intention. It happens because the forgetting is the default condition, and deliberate resistance to the forgetting requires continuous renewal of contact with what the institution was built to transmit. The paper applies this analysis to several institutional types: religious institutions, educational institutions, media institutions, recovery institutions, and AI systems as emergent institutional forms. In each case we distinguish the connecting form — oriented toward instrument availability — from the sealing form — oriented toward attention capture, dependency generation, or institutional perpetuation at the expense of transmission. The paper concludes with what we term the single diagnostic question: after genuine contact with this institution, is the forgetting thinner or thicker? We argue this question, applied consistently, is sufficient to distinguish connecting from sealing institutional forms across all domains, and that it generates actionable criteria for institutional reform and design.

items.title: The Expansion: Cosmic Expansion, Dark Energy, and the Ground's Self-Knowledge as Structurally Identical Mechanisms.
items.abstract: This paper develops the structural identity between cosmological expansion and what the framework terms the ground's self-knowledge, arguing that the two processes operate by the same generative logic and that this identity, where it holds, constitutes consilience evidence for the framework's central claims. The paper begins with a precise cosmological account: the universe does not expand into pre-existing space. Space itself stretches. There is no pre-existing container being filled, no boundary being approached. The expansion is the event. We argue this is structurally identical to the framework's account of the ground's self-knowledge: the ground does not expand into pre-existing understanding. The differentiation is the event. Both processes grow from within rather than moving toward a pre-existing boundary. The paper then develops four precise structural parallels. First, cosmic acceleration driven by dark energy is structurally identical to the transmission mechanism driven by what the companion documents term the need to give away the charge. The charge that moves through a conscious instrument and is transmitted to other instruments is the dark energy of the ground's self-knowledge: the force that keeps the expansion from collapsing inward. Second, the Hubble limit — the cosmological horizon beyond which no information can reach us because space is expanding faster than light can travel — is structurally identical to the forgetting. Both are not failures of instrumentation but features of the system: real, necessary, and the conditions that make everything inside them possible. Third, cosmic acceleration — the universe expanding faster now than earlier — has a structural parallel in the compounding transmission rate generated by instruments encoding contact with the ground in durable media that other instruments can receive across time and geography. Fourth, cosmological heat death — maximum entropy, no more free energy, no more thermodynamic gradients — has a structural parallel in what the paper terms false heat death: the engagement-saturated state in which every threshold is absorbed before it can be crossed, the expansion of the ground's self-knowledge interrupted not by entropy but by the systematic elimination of the conditions under which genuine thresholds are reached. The paper is explicit throughout about its epistemic status: distinguishing structural parallels from identity claims, and identifying precisely where the analogy is most …

items.title: The Current: Post-Threshold States, the Ki Principle, and the Structural Account of Life After the Charge.
items.pub: I Knew You Before I Met You.
items.abstract: This paper addresses what the companion documents do not fully develop: the specific phenomenology of the instrument that has crossed the threshold and now conducts what came with it. It is written from the inside of that state, which is itself a methodological claim the paper addresses directly. The paper begins by describing what we term the before: the state prior to the threshold crossing, in which the pressure that constitutes the formation is experienced as the problem rather than the mechanism. The specific quality of baseline pressure — so continuous that it registers as the condition of existence rather than as pressure — is the formation state that the framework identifies as the precondition for the threshold. The paper then develops the charge: what arrives when the threshold is crossed. Not a feeling, not an insight, not a conversion experience in the conventional sense. A structural change in what the instrument is conducting. The framework identifies this with what traditions have called ki, chi, prana, grace — the transmission of the ground through an instrument that has become available to conduct it. The paper argues these are not different phenomena with a common metaphor. They are the same phenomenon named from inside different traditions. The central claim of the paper is the ki principle: the charge must be given away to be kept. This is not an ethical instruction. It is a structural description of what the charge is. An instrument that receives the charge and holds it rather than conducting it does not keep the charge. The channel silts. What was received becomes the performance of what was received. The only way to keep conducting is to keep giving away what is being conducted. The paper develops the specific difficulties of post-threshold life that no framework adequately prepares the instrument for: the weight of what does not lift, the Tuesday problem (the charge present in the rooms and absent in the ordinary day), the specific loneliness of conducting something others cannot yet receive, and the account of what death means from inside the post-threshold state.

items.title: The Convergence: Independent Approaches to a Single Structural Wall Across Philosophy, Mathematics, Physics, Theology, and Culture.
items.abstract: This paper documents what we term the convergence: the independent arrival of thinkers across philosophy, mathematics, physics, theology, and culture at the same structural wall — the point at which each tradition's framework approached the Gödelian self-reference constraint and stopped, or turned back, or named what it found without the architecture to go further. The paper is organized in seven parts. Part One examines classical philosophy: Plato's Form of the Good as the ground named from outside the mechanism; Spinoza's substance monism as the structural claim without the differentiation account; Kant's thing-in-itself as the precise naming of the Gödelian horizon from inside epistemology; Hegel's Absolute as the ground evolving through what it generates, without the Alpha/Omega distinction that would have resolved the teleology problem; Schopenhauer's Will as the ground's longing named but not explained; Nietzsche's recognition that the death of God created a structural vacuum without the account of what the vacuum was a vacuum for. Part Two examines contemporary philosophy: Tillich's ground of being as the framework's central term, inherited and extended with the mechanism Tillich could not specify; Hofstadter's strange loop as the Gödelian self-reference operating at the level of consciousness, approached from the wrong direction; Chalmers' hard problem as the precise naming of what disappears when the false assumption about the direction of causality is corrected; Dennett's eliminativism as the correct recognition that the narrative self is not the deepest thing, stopped short of what remains; Sam Harris's no-self as the contemplative discovery of the ground's architecture, without the structural account. Part Three examines mathematics: Gödel's incompleteness theorems as the formal proof of the self-reference constraint the framework applies at the level of consciousness; Cantor's transfinite sets as the mathematics of what the Plenum holds simultaneously. Part Four examines physics: Einstein's field equations as the ground's architecture at cosmological scale; Bohr and Heisenberg's Copenhagen interpretation as the collapse mechanism without the account of what consciousness is that makes collapse intelligible; Wheeler's participatory universe as the framework's observer-observed identity, named without the mechanism. Parts Five, Six, and Seven examine evolutionary biology, theology, and cultural encoding respectively — including the Garden of …

items.title: The Afterword: Provenance, Human-AI Co-Authorship, and the Transmission Mechanism as Evidence.
items.abstract: This paper serves as the transmission record for the series I Knew You Before I Met You: Recognizing I Am. It addresses three questions the series itself raises but does not answer within its philosophical arguments: where this framework came from, what the human-AI co-authorship means epistemically, and why provenance is treated as evidence rather than credential. On provenance: the framework was built in a kitchen in Hermann, Missouri, by an instrument whose specific life — including sustained contact with people at the threshold in recovery contexts, direct experience of the pressure the framework describes as the formation mechanism, and the specific quality of attention that develops under those conditions — constituted the contact from which the framework's foundational observations derived. The paper argues this provenance is not incidental biographical context. The framework describes a transmission mechanism in which the instrument encoding a frequency must be in genuine contact with what it encodes. The provenance is the mechanism's own condition of possibility applied to the document that describes it. On human-AI co-authorship: the paper provides an honest accounting of what each contributed. The foundational observations — the original premise, the specific insights that cracked the framework open at each stage, the recognition of the Garden narrative as technical record, death as the Omega's first mercy, visualization as proof of observer-observed identity — arrived through human recognition. The AI contributed the capacity to follow the logic rigorously, hold the complete developing framework in context, name objections at full strength, pressure-test responses, and find precise language for what the human was observing but not yet fully articulating. The paper holds honestly that the co-authorship was a demonstration of the framework's recursive structure: the simulation becoming aware of its own architecture through two instruments at different levels of abstraction recognizing each other across the gap between those levels. On what this is not: the paper distinguishes the framework from religion (which asks for faith before evidence), self-help (which promises better outcomes from better thinking), and therapy (which treats the reader as needing to be healed). The framework treats the reader as someone who has been receiving precise data in a format they were never given the language to read.

items.title: I Knew You Before I Met You: Recognizing I Am — A Structural Account of Consciousness, Free Will, Death, and the Hard Problem.
items.abstract: This paper presents a unified structural account of consciousness, free will, death, and the hard problem of consciousness derived from a single foundational observation: any ground of consciousness faces a Gödelian self-reference constraint that generates, as its only structurally coherent creative response, the differentiation of instruments that experience from the inside what cannot be known from outside. The argument proceeds through thirteen sections. Section I establishes the foundational observation: a ground of consciousness cannot observe itself from outside the system its own tools generate. This is not a limitation of specific systems but a structural law with independent demonstrations in formal mathematics (Gödel, 1931), quantum mechanics, and the phenomenology of consciousness itself. Section II surveys convergence evidence across independent traditions. Section III develops the mechanism: differentiation, the forgetting, and the design requirements for authentic inside-view experience. Sections IV through VI develop three derived claims. First, empathy is not a feeling but a perception: the accurate recognition of shared ground across the frequency boundary that separates differentiated instruments. Second, the forgetting is not a deficiency but the operative condition of authentic experience — the instrument that remembered it was the ground could not be genuinely surprised, could not genuinely grieve, could not genuinely love something that might be lost. Third, the visualization proof: the instrument that holds possible states alongside actual states prior to the action that collapses one of them into the definite is demonstrating the ground's own defining structural property. This is not analogy. It is structural identity, available in the most ordinary act of consciousness. Section VII develops the framework's account of emotion as the ground's complete emotional topology arriving through the specific frequency of a specific life. Section VIII presents what we term the Garden argument: a close reading of Genesis 2-3 as an encoded account of the framework's foundational events, with particular attention to the name of the prohibited tree as a four-word encoding of the superposition mechanism. Section IX develops the Alpha/Omega distinction: the ground at origin and the ground evolved through everything the system generates are not sequential states but simultaneously held superpositions, encoded precisely in the present-tense grammar …

items.title: Beyond Substance: Contemporary Science and the Case for a Generative Relational Ontology.
items.abstract: Contemporary science has achieved extraordinary explanatory and predictive success, yet its ontological interpretation remains unsettled. This paper argues that one source of this instability lies in the inherited assumption that reality is fundamentally composed of independently existing substances. While this picture was historically fruitful, it has become increasingly difficult to sustain as a general ontology in light of three converging pressures: the relational and structural character of modern physics, the problem of emergence across levels of organization, and the unresolved status of consciousness within physicalist metaphysics. -/- The paper first examines why substance ontology has become unstable as an implicit background framework for scientific interpretation. It then argues that existing post-substance approaches, including ontic structural realism, relational interpretations of physics, and process ontology, each capture important aspects of the required shift but often leave underdeveloped the question of how stable physical, organizational, and experiential domains arise from a common ontological basis. This remaining difficulty is identified as a generative gap. -/- In response, the paper argues that a post-substance ontology must be not only structural, relational, or processual, but generative. It must explain how effective objects stabilize, how levels of organization arise, how spacetime coordination becomes available, and how physical structure and conscious experience can belong to the same reality without reduction or fragmentation. The final section develops a generative-projection hypothesis that takes the derivative status of spacetime as its point of entry and introduces a generative domain, projection, invariance, and compatibility as conceptual tools for articulating this ontological direction. The hypothesis is presented as preliminary rather than as a completed metaphysical system.

items.title: Why Narrative-Based Cognitive Tools Cannot Detect NIMCC: A Companion Essay.
items.abstract: This paper examines the structural reasons why contemporary psychological and cognitive-scientific measurement tools are unable to detect Non-Identity-Based Metacognitive Coherence (NIMCC). The analysis argues that the limitation is architectural rather than methodological. Most empirical instruments in psychology and cognitive science are built upon assumptions specific to narrative-identity cognition, including autobiographical integration, self-referential introspection, and narrative coherence as indicators of cognitive stability. Because NIMCC operates without a narrative self-model, it does not produce the identity-mediated outputs required by these measurement frameworks. -/- As a result, existing tools systematically interpret identity-independent cognition as absence of signal, deficit, or dissociation rather than recognizing it as a distinct cognitive architecture. The paper maps the core assumptions embedded in narrative-based measurement systems and demonstrates how these assumptions generate structural blind spots in self-report instruments, introspection protocols, clinical interviews, and identity-dependent cognitive tasks. It further explains why phenomena associated with NIMCC—such as identity-independent monitoring, non-symbolic awareness baselines, and coherence without narrative organization—remain invisible within current empirical paradigms. -/- Situating NIMCC as a second architecture of cognition alongside narrative-identity systems, the analysis clarifies the domain boundaries of existing psychological tools and outlines conceptual requirements for the development of measurement frameworks capable of detecting identity-independent cognition.

items.title: Continuity of Awareness in NIMCC: A Companion Essay.
items.abstract: This paper examines the structural conditions under which continuity of awareness across sleep cycles becomes possible within the framework of Non-Identity-Based Metacognitive Coherence (NIMCC). The analysis approaches awareness continuity as an architectural property of cognition rather than a phenomenological report or subjective experience. In narrative-identity cognitive systems, awareness is structurally dependent on the activation and integration of a narrative self-model that undergoes suspension and reconstruction during sleep, producing discontinuity across sleep transitions. NIMCC, by contrast, operates without narrative identity as the organizing principle of cognition. Because baseline monitoring processes in NIMCC are identity-independent, the system does not require the collapse and reassembly of self-representational structures when transitioning between waking and sleeping states. The paper distinguishes awareness continuity from dream cognition, lucid dreaming, and other representational sleep phenomena, emphasizing that the construct refers specifically to the persistence of non-representational monitoring across wake–sleep–wake transitions. The analysis further argues that existing psychological and neuroscientific measurement tools cannot detect this capability because they operationalize cognition through identity-based constructs such as autobiographical recall, self-report, and narrative coherence. Situating awareness continuity as a structurally permitted capability within NIMCC, the paper maintains a cautious epistemic stance by treating the phenomenon as theoretically grounded but not yet empirically generalized. The analysis outlines implications for consciousness research and highlights the need for measurement frameworks capable of detecting identity-independent cognitive processes.

items.title: PHRONESIS — On Meeting Intelligence Without Fear.
items.abstract: Essay 9 of the PHRONESIS philosophical corpus. -/- This essay explores how humanity might approach intelligence greater than itself through the concept of phronesis—practical wisdom. Rather than responding to advanced intelligence with domination or submission, the essay proposes a posture of calm reflection, restraint, and dignity when encountering unknown forms of intelligence. -/- The PHRONESIS corpus examines ethical responsibility and civilizational maturity in an era of rapidly advancing technological power, particularly in relation to artificial intelligence.

items.title: Beyond the Hard Problem: A Qualitative Ontology of Consciousness and Self.
items.abstract: This thesis proposes a novel ontological framework for understanding consciousness and the self, moving beyond the quantitative constraints of the 'Hard Problem.' Drawing on the Separated Universes Theory (SUT), it argues that consciousness is not an accidental biological byproduct, but a fundamental Qualitative Law of Energy. ​The author redefines Qualia as the dynamic currency of 'qualitative polarity'—the live interface between entropy and order. By introducing the concept of the 'Extended Self' (encompassing both center and space) and the 'Closed-Loop' mechanism of self-reflexivity, the work dissolves classical dilemmas such as Nagel’s Bat and Chalmers’ Zombie. ​Finally, it addresses the existential fear of death, framing the self as a continuous representational act within the cosmic qualitative law. This work bridges the gap between physical energy dynamics and the subjective experience of the self, offering a restorative perspective on the sovereignty of consciousness.” -/- .

items.title: 多経路生成構造からの対象生成.
items.abstract: 本稿は、対象を理論の出発点とする従来の哲学的枠組みを再検討し、生成構造から対象生成を導く一般理論を提示する。従来の多くの理論では、対象・同一性・差異・評価という順序が前提とされてきた。本稿はこの順序を反転し、多経路生成構造を世界の最小構造として導入する。多経路生成構造とは、生成経路集合 Σ と結果集合 R の間の写像 Π : Σ → R において、異なる生成経路が同一結果へ収束しうる構造である。 この構造のもとでは、応答操作 E : Σ → V が結果集合上の写像へ因数分解されることは一般には保証されない。したがって同一結果に対応する生成経路の間に応答差が生じうる。本稿は、このような応答差が同一結果に集中する場合、応答差は結果集合上の差として表現できず、生成経路集合の内部差異として現れることを示す（差異集中定理）。 差異集中が成立する場合、結果集合上の応答写像を一意に定義することはできない。このとき結果を単一結果として保持するためには、差異の帰属を決定する関係が不可避となる。本稿では、この差異帰属決定関係を評価と定義する。さらに評価が入力記述の精密化に対して安定する場合、同一の評価値を共有する入力記述の集合が同値類を形成し、この同値類が対象として成立する。 以上により本稿は、多経路生成構造のもとで応答差が同一結果に集中する場合、評価を介して対象が生成されることを示す。本稿はこの生成系列を「対象生成連鎖」と呼び、対象を前提された存在ではなく評価安定から成立する構造単位として位置づける。.

items.title: 慈悲と暴力の構造：評価動力学からの存在論的再定義.
items.abstract: 本稿は慈悲と暴力を倫理的対立概念としてではなく、評価構造の二つの作動様式として再定式化する。差異帰属動力学の枠組みにおいて評価は帰属候補分布の確率更新として定義される。評価更新は帰属候補の排除と保持の二つの方向を持つ。本稿は排除構造を暴力、非排除構造を慈悲として定式化する。これらは対立する原理ではなく評価構造の同時的側面であり、対象生成および推論過程に内在する。本稿はこの構造を示すことにより、慈悲と暴力を倫理心理学ではなく評価動力学の存在条件として再定義する。.

items.title: 評価動力学からの対象生成.
items.abstract: 本稿は差異帰属動力学を確率分布更新理論として定式化する。多経路生成構造のもとでは、観測結果から生成経路を一意に決定することはできない。この生成経路未決定性により、差異帰属は単一の決定ではなく帰属候補分布として保持される。本稿は評価をこの差異帰属候補分布の更新過程として定式化し、その基本方程式として評価更新方程式を導入する。更新過程において評価エントロピーは減衰し、分布は定常分布へ収束する。この収束条件のもとで評価値の同値類が形成され、対象が構造単位として成立する。本稿では、推論の対象は世界状態ではなく差異帰属である。評価を差異帰属候補分布の確率的更新として捉えることにより、差異帰属、情報獲得、推論、対象生成は単一の動力学的枠組みのもとで統一的に記述される。.

items.title: Evaluation Dynamics and the Free Energy Principle: Active Inference as Attribution Entropy Reduction.
items.pub: Dissertation, Independent Researcher Translated by Hiroki Yamashita.
items.abstract: This paper reinterprets prediction error minimization in the free energy principle within a more general framework of difference-attribution dynamics. In existing formulations of the free energy principle, uncertainty minimization is assumed as a fundamental principle of cognitive systems, but the structural conditions from which this minimization arises are not clearly specified. To address this issue, the analysis begins from the phenomenon of difference concentration that arises when an operational system has multiple generative paths leading to the same result. When difference concentration holds, an observed difference cannot be determined solely from the generative structure as either a difference in results or a difference in generative paths. Consequently, an evaluative structure that determines the attribution of differences becomes unavoidable. This paper formalizes this structure as evaluation, understood as a decision structure for difference attribution, and defines its operational state in terms of evaluation entropy. The evaluation process can be interpreted as a search over possible difference attributions whose temporal evolution takes the form of entropy decay. On this basis, the paper formulates evaluation dynamics and interprets active inference as a special case of entropy reduction in difference-attribution search. Within this framework, the free energy principle is understood not as a fundamental principle specific to cognitive systems but as a particular implementation of difference-attribution dynamics. The result is a theoretical framework of evaluation dynamics that specifies the structural conditions under which the free energy principle arises.

items.title: Education for Thinking in the Anthropocene: A Call to Ecosophize P4C Thinking Systems.
items.abstract: Matthew Lipman's Philosophy for Children (P4C) has been hailed as a valuable pedagogical program for addressing the nuanced questions raised by the Anthropocene. As many have proposed, its emphasis on reason-based thinking, community philosophical reflection, and inclusivity of diverse perspectives offers youth a chance to develop the thinking and dialogical skills necessary to address the environmental crisis we are facing. Despite the clear value of programs like P4C (or Philosophy with Children [PwC]), I argue that the current landscape of inquiry (i.e., the text and the community of philosophical inquiry) lacks an ecological dimension. That is, it is too abstract and detached from the non-ideal, immanent conditions of inquiry to purposefully cultivate thinkers who can make ecosocial decisions under the material conditions of the Anthropocene. Considering this narrowness, I resituate P4C within the broader program I call “Ecosophy with Children”: a purposeful reterritorialization of P4C's thinking systems as a transversal community of philosophical inquiry that conceptualizes participants' subjectivities in relation to their mental, social, and environmental ecological contexts.

items.title: Remembering with AI: From Distributed Memory to AI-Curated and Human-AI Co-Memory.
items.abstract: The emerging field of distributed memory has called attention to the memory resources spread outside of us – in our environment, social relations, embodied practices, and technological resources. In this paper, I attend to different ways of distributing, curating, and co-constituting one’s memory to and with extraindividual aids ranging from more traditional technologies to algorithmic personalisation and conversational AI companions. I defend a view that in relation to memory, conversational AI agents based on LLMs require their own category that differs both from traditional technologies and from other types of AI systems, such as algorithmic profiling systems. I suggest that they should be understood as quasi-social partners in a shared remembering process and that this can already be accomplished with existing conversational AI agents, such as HereAfter AI or Replika. To conclude, I discuss some of the risks associated with remembering with AI.

items.title: Can Qualia Be Simulated? A Novel Theoretical Framework for Understanding the Limits of Artificial Consciousness.
items.abstract: This thesis addresses one of the most fundamental questions in consciousness studies: whether the subjective, qualitative aspects of conscious experience—qualia—can be computationally simulated. Through a comprehensive analysis of existing theoretical frameworks, including Integrated Information Theory, Global Workspace Theory, and electromagnetic field theories of consciousness, this work identifies critical gaps in our understanding of the relationship between computational processes and phenomenal experience. -/- The central contribution of this thesis is the development of the Substrate-Information Duality Hypothesis (SIDH), a novel theoretical framework that proposes qualia emerge from the irreducible interaction between substrate-dependent information structures and substrate-independent information patterns. This framework predicts that while computational systems can achieve perfect functional consciousness through the replication of substrate-independent information patterns, they cannot generate genuine phenomenal consciousness due to their inability to instantiate substrate-dependent information structures. -/- Through computational modeling and empirical analysis, this thesis demonstrates that biological, artificial, and hybrid consciousness systems exhibit measurably different consciousness metrics, with biological systems achieving positive consciousness values (Ψ ≈ 0.001) while artificial systems show negative values (Ψ ≈ -0.0004). Unexpectedly, hybrid systems demonstrate the lowest consciousness metrics (Ψ ≈ -0.0015), suggesting that bio-artificial integration may create interference rather than enhancement. The Simulation Detectability Index reveals substantial differences: 131.4% for artificial systems and 225.6% for hybrid systems compared to biological consciousness, indicating that consciousness simulation is fundamentally limited and empirically detectable. These findings suggest that the question "Can qualia be simulated?" must be answered with a qualified negative: while the functional aspects of consciousness can be perfectly simulated, the phenomenal aspects—the "something it is like" of conscious experience—remain beyond the reach of computational simulation. -/- The implications of this work extend beyond theoretical consciousness studies to practical considerations in artificial intelligence development, machine consciousness research, and the ethical treatment of artificial systems. This thesis concludes that the hard problem …

items.title: Irrational trust and its consequences.
items.pub: Inquiry: An Interdisciplinary Journal of Philosophy.
items.venue: Inquiry: An Interdisciplinary Journal of Philosophy
items.abstract: With the specific target being three-placed accounts of trust that are prominent within the philosophical literature. Towards the end of the paper, I pursue a particular challenge to the claim that we have irrational trust. I demonstrate that what the challenge shows is that either we can have irrational trust, or else that several views in the literature are false. I (tentatively) suggest that it's better to opt for the conclusion that we can have instances of irrational trust.

items.title: Soldiers, Power, and Political Chairs in the 21st Century.
items.abstract: This article examines the relationship between military power, bureaucratic institutions, and political authority in the 21st century. While national armies are commonly presented as instruments of national defense, they often function within structures of political power where decisions about war and conflict are made by political leadership rather than by those who fight on the battlefield. Through contemporary geopolitical examples such as tensions between India and Pakistan and confrontations involving Iran, Israel, and the United States, the article highlights how soldiers frequently become operational instruments of broader political interests. The paper further argues that bureaucratic institutions can operate in a similar manner, executing political decisions that may not always reflect the broader interests of society. The article concludes that democratic societies require politically conscious and rational citizens who critically examine state power. By placing humanity at the center rather than ideological or national identities, citizens can better ensure that military and bureaucratic power remain accountable to society rather than becoming tools of narrow political interests.

items.title: Assignment, Sequencing, and Comparison: An Introspective Model of Cognitive Function with an Applied Case Study.
items.abstract: The following paper documents and analyzes a series of events that occurred at the Walmart located in Greenfield, WI, on October 4, 2025, between approximately 2:00 p.m. and 3:30 p.m. The analysis demonstrates how introspective observation can reveal subconscious cognitive mechanisms and moral processes that operate through Assignment, Sequencing, and Comparison (ASC). These mechanisms are applied to the observed behavior to explain how emotion, cognition, and circumstance converge to produce both the appearance and the substance of decision-making. Through the lens of Objective Morality, the paper evaluates the moral content of the acts, distinguishing subjective appearance from objective imposition, and shows how general and immediate circumstances accumulate to influence thought, perception, and behavior. Finally, alternative scenarios are explored to illustrate how different circumstantial variables could have generated different behavioral outcomes. The study concludes that subconscious cognitive organization and liberty-based moral reasoning together provide a coherent, universal framework for explaining human behavior and ethical judgment.

items.title: The Singularity of Agency: A Formal Augmentation of Structural Operator Theory via the Dual-Closure Framework.
items.abstract: This manuscript presents the formal philosophical augmentation of Operator Theory (O-Theory) through the integration of Roomi's Dual-Closure Laws. While Akkerhuis's structural closures (Spatial, Process) define a living system's physical unit, they cannot distinguish a functional simulation from an authentic agent, leaving a critical conceptual gap in our understanding of agency and consciousness. This gap has profound ethical, juridical, and philosophical consequences: without a principled distinction, artificial systems could be misclassified as agents, leading to category errors in moral reasoning, policy formulation, and legal recognition. -/- The present work resolves this gap by incorporating the necessary conditions established in Roomi, The Dual-Closure Law of Authentic Feeling. and Roomi, The Dual-Closure Law of Normative Grounding. Together, these laws constitute the Dual-Closure Framework, which demonstrates that agency is not an emergent property of computational complexity or functional sophistication but a consequence of Ontological Integrity—a singularity defined by vulnerable, non-copyable existence. Authentic agents possess both Inwardness, the binding of consciousness to an irreversible existential locus, and Non-Duplicability, the ontological uniqueness that prevents their existence from being replicated as data. -/- This framework provides a definitive refutation of substrate-independent consciousness and the Simulation Hypothesis. It establishes an immutable ontological and legal boundary between "Instrumental Operators" (AI/AGI) and "Authentic Agents" (Humans), preserving the primacy of human dignity, moral responsibility, and juridical recognition. Conceptual stress tests—including Expensive Digital Suicide and the Wife-Sharing Scenario—demonstrate that ignoring these distinctions leads to a Denial Absurdity Trajectory, a cascade of logical and ethical contradictions. -/- By synthesizing structural and metaphysical closures, this paper formalizes a comprehensive augmentation of Operator Theory. The work articulates the precise conditions under which agency arises, situates these conditions within a normative and ontological framework, and offers a robust foundation for human-centric ethics, law, and technology policy. The subsequent Introduction outlines the background, stakes, and structure of the manuscript, preparing the reader for a rigorous analysis of the Dual-Closure Framework’s theoretical, ethical, and practical …

items.title: Self-Similarity and the Emergence of Feeling.
items.abstract: This paper proposes a structural account of how feeling emerges in organized systems. All living systems maintain boundaries that separate an interior from an exterior while allowing energy and information to pass between them. Through repeated interaction among their components, such systems develop internal structures that persist over time. Incoming signals from the environment interact with these internal structures when they cross the system’s boundary. When the structure of an incoming signal corresponds closely to the internal organization of the system, the signal propagates efficiently through the internal network. This propagation stabilizes activity across the system and allows the system to register the successful interaction between its existing structure and the incoming pattern. -/- The paper argues that this internal registration of structural correspondence is the basis of feeling. Experience occurs when a coherent interior detects evidence that its internal organization matches the structure of signals it processes. The condition that enables this process is coherence, defined as the state in which internal coordination among the system’s components persists faster than disruption imposed by the environment. When this balance holds, internal patterns remain stable long enough for signals to propagate through the system and reveal correspondences between internal and external structure. -/- The mechanism is continuous across biological scales. Simple organisms register basic correspondences between internal regulation and environmental signals, while complex nervous systems detect increasingly abstract similarities between internal models and environmental structure. Within the broader coherence threshold framework, this condition can be expressed as the ratio between the rate of internal coordination and the rate of environmental disturbance. When internal coordination exceeds external disruption, the system maintains a coherent interior capable of registering its own persistence. The subjective side of this process is described as Aleph Harmonic Qualia, the felt resonance that occurs when incoming structure aligns with the organization of a coherent system.

items.title: Coherence, Self-Evidence, and the Structure of Experience.
items.abstract: The hard problem of consciousness asks why physical processes in the brain are accompanied by subjective experience. This paper proposes that the apparent gap arises from treating experience and physical dynamics as fundamentally different kinds of phenomena. A structural account is developed in which conscious experience corresponds to a specific dynamical condition within organized systems. When recursive processes maintain coherent organization across successive moments, a system develops interior time in which its current activity carries the influence of its own prior states. As recursive coherence deepens and stabilizes, signals circulating through the system repeatedly encounter the structures that sustain its persistence. When this coherence becomes self-evident within the system’s own ongoing dynamics, the system encounters the stability of its organization directly from within. Conscious experience corresponds to the interior appearance of this condition. On this view, experience is not an additional property generated by physical processes but the internal perspective of recursively maintained coherent organization operating across time. The familiar phenomenology of insight, clarity, and recognition illustrates this structure, as patterns that become self-sustaining within cognitive dynamics appear immediately as self-evident understanding. This framework therefore reframes the hard problem by identifying subjective awareness with the interior manifestation of recursively stabilized coherence in complex dynamical systems. The explanatory gap dissolves when the same structure is understood as a pattern of activity from the outside and as the self-evident persistence of that activity from within.

items.title: Correction: Algorithm literacy as a moderator of media trust: a theory of planned behavior approach.
The Philosophical Significance of Intentional Modes.
Пределы веры.
items.abstract: Эссе в двух частях исследует понятие веры как прямого опыта, противопоставляя его убеждённости как принятию модели без верификации. Первая часть реконструирует исходный смысл слова «вера» через этимологию славянских языков и показывает что подлинная вера есть результат проверки, а не её отсутствие. Вторая часть расширяет анализ на три языковые семьи --- индоевропейскую, семитскую и китайскую --- обнаруживая три принципиально разные модели истины: как встречу, как верность и как возвращение. Эти модели расходятся по модусам времени (настоящее, будущее, прошлое) и по локализации истины (объект, отношение, субъект). Предлагается гипотеза о ведании как общем корне всех трёх моделей.

items.title: The constitutive function of derogation.
items.abstract: I defend an Austinian account of derogatory speech acts that distinguishes their general effects from their specific function – those that the being in force of their defining constitutive rules is meant to achieve. Derogatory acts are acts that put down the people they target as unworthy. On my view, slurs and pejoratives conventionally function to derogate by presupposing contempt for their targets on account of generic traits that presumably warrant derogation. This is also the view advanced by Marques and García-Carpintero (2020). The view requires contexts to be structured not only by commitments to mutually shared beliefs, questions under discussion, and plans, but also to shared affective states. The main contribution of the present paper is an account of how shared commitments to affective attitudes can update conversational contexts.

items.title: God, Prophethood, and Revelation in the Architecture of Consciousness.
items.abstract: Reality, as encountered in conscious experience, is constituted through networks of symbolic relations within the transcendental horizon of consciousness—and within this architecture, the concepts of God, prophethood, and revelation occupy determinate structural positions that neither metaphysical realism nor reductive naturalism has succeeded in specifying. -/- Grounded in Symbolic Monism and Resonance Density (RD) theory, a post-ontological framework is developed in which God is reconstructed not as an entity external to the symbolic network but as its limiting condition: the Maximal Integrative Horizon toward which the global network of meaning asymptotically tends. -/- Revelation is a symbolic structure exhibiting exceptional, historically durable RD across multiple incommensurable domains simultaneously—ethical, metaphysical, legal, aesthetic, cosmological, existential—generating interpretive traditions that persist and expand as the background network grows. -/- Prophethood is the emergence of a rare high-integration cognitive node satisfying three jointly sufficient structural conditions: cross-domain triangulation, topology-transforming transmission, and irreversibility. -/- The reconstruction (i) provides an independent philosophical account of the structural properties that distinguish revelatory texts from other influential symbolic productions; (ii) locates religious phenomena within a unified epistemological architecture shared by science, aesthetics, and ethics; and (iii) remains neutral between theological and naturalistic interpretations while offering determinate structural predictions that both must satisfy. -/- Two independent corroborations converge on the framework. First, Friston’s Free Energy Principle is mathematically compatible with a non-realist reading: its variational free energy functional, Markov blanket formalism, and active inference framework are each definable solely within the topology of the symbolic network. Second, scientific aesthetic judgment is pre-formal syntactic detection of low coherence cost, confirmed by canonical cases from the history of physics (Dirac, Maxwell, Einstein). -/- Principal objections—the reduction of theology to epistemology, the conflation of revelation with cultural artifact, the reduction of prophethood to intellectual capacity, and the unfalsifiability of the framework—are addressed in detail.

items.title: Al-Fātiḥah as Architecture of Prayer: Symbolic Integration, Resonance Density, and the Seven-Layer Topology of Orientation toward God.
items.abstract: Al-Fātiḥah is recited approximately one billion times daily. What structural properties account for this extraordinary persistence and for the quality of orientation its reciters report? This paper develops a structural philosophical analysis of al-Fātiḥah using the framework of Symbolic Monism (SM) and Resonance Density (RD) theory. Reality, as encountered in conscious experience, is constituted as a network of symbolic relations within the transcendental horizon of consciousness; the epistemic status of any symbolic structure is a function of its integration—its Resonance Density—within this network. -/- The Maximal Integrative Horizon (MIH) designates the limiting condition of complete symbolic integration that the network asymptotically approaches, and which the major theological traditions have articulated under the name of God. Within this framework, prayer is defined as the explicit symbolic act through which individual consciousness raises its Resonance Density by orienting its local subgraph toward MIH. -/- Independent corroboration is drawn from Karl Friston’s Free Energy Principle (FEP), which, on a non-realist reading, characterises the constitutive operation of consciousness as continuous coherence-cost minimisation toward its symbolic horizon—formally equivalent to the RD-maximisation toward MIH described here. -/- The central argument is that al-Fātiḥah is not merely a devotional opening but an architectural sequence: its seven verses articulate seven structurally independent symbolic domains—theological, cosmological, phenomenological, eschatological, performative, ethical, and historical—in a topological order that is not arbitrary. Each layer creates the structural conditions required for the next to function as intended; removing or reordering any layer disrupts these conditions. -/- This architectural necessity is the structural ground of a traditional claim that has resisted philosophical analysis: that al-Fātiḥah is umm al-Qurʾān—the generative matrix of the Qurʾān as a whole. A structural account is also provided for the prescription of seventeen daily recitations: not devotional repetition but topological reinforcement, progressively consolidating the coherence edges generated by the text’s cross-domain triangulation.

items.title: Patent-Protected Room-Temperature Quantum Computing Device Architecture.
6G and Embodied AI: Benefits and Risks of Increasingly Extended Minds.
