After saying more about the constituent relation (i.e., awareness) and content (i.e., properties and objects) of knowledge of things, the author considers whether there are further conditions on it parallel to conditions on propositional knowledge (e.g., truth, justification). He suggests that there are. The author calls them “veridicality” and “well-foundedness” conditions, and he spells out different ways to understand them. He concludes this chapter by discussing some ways knowledge of things relates to other forms of knowledge.

items.title: 98C5Awareness Is Knowledge.
items.pub: In Present to the Mind: Acquaintance and Its Significance. Oxford University Press.
items.venue: Present to the Mind: Acquaintance and Its Significance
items.abstract: This chapter further develops the author’s case for the claim that some knowledge is constituted, not by beliefs in propositions, but by conscious awareness of properties and objects. He starts by considering how best to approach the debate over this claim. He adopts an approach that focuses on certain philosophical roles that are played by, and standardly attributed to, knowledge. He argues that conscious perceptual and introspective awareness sometimes plays those roles and, for that reason, should be considered a distinctive type of knowledge. After going through several examples, the author focuses especially on the roles that knowledge plays in guiding behavior and as the basis of knowledge-conferring reasoning. He argues that conscious awareness sometimes plays these roles and that it therefore should be considered knowledge.

items.title: 235C9Acquaintance Is Emotionally Significant.
items.pub: In Present to the Mind: Acquaintance and Its Significance. Oxford University Press.
items.venue: Present to the Mind: Acquaintance and Its Significance
items.abstract: This chapter argues that acquaintance has unique emotional significance because of how it relates to certain moral emotions—such as empathy, compassion, and what the author calls “The Feeling.” The author starts by introducing a series of examples of the Feeling. Then he highlights certain key features of the Feeling and considers what type of feeling it might be. He considers whether it is empathy, pity, or a certain kind of attitude or perception. Ultimately, the author argues that the Feeling is a form of love—what he calls “Mister Rogers love”—and he suggests that it allows us to more-or-less literally see the value of people around us. Then he argues that acquaintance with this and other emotions is what enables this unique way of perceiving others’ value. Finally, he argues that the Feeling is important partly because it motivates us in a unique way to help those around us.

items.title: 167C7Acquaintance Is Epistemically Significant.
items.pub: In Present to the Mind: Acquaintance and Its Significance. Oxford University Press.
items.venue: Present to the Mind: Acquaintance and Its Significance
items.abstract: This chapter argues that acquaintance has further epistemic significance beyond what the author attributed to it in previous chapters. The author argues that acquaintance not only has epistemic significance in itself, simply in virtue of being knowledge, but also in virtue of justifying beliefs—both immediately and inferentially. He then uses these results to defend various forms of epistemic foundationalism. Ultimately, the author argues that acquaintance is the foundation for all empirical knowledge. That is, he argues that all knowledge that depends for its justification on perceptual or introspective experience depends on acquaintance for its justification. He considers whether some of these results can be gotten without acquaintance—that is, by appealing to experience in more neutral terms, without positing an acquaintance relation. He argues that they cannot—that acquaintance plays a central, ineliminable role in the epistemology of experience.

items.title: 205C8Acquaintance Is Aesthetically Significant.
items.pub: In Present to the Mind: Acquaintance and Its Significance. Oxford University Press.
items.venue: Present to the Mind: Acquaintance and Its Significance
items.abstract: This chapter argues that acquaintance has unique aesthetic significance because much (if not all) aesthetic knowledge and appreciation requires acquaintance. Aesthetic knowledge is knowledge of a thing’s aesthetic properties, like its beauty, unity, or balance. Aesthetic appreciation is a certain positive response to those properties based on aesthetic knowledge of them. The author argues that much of this knowledge and appreciation could not be gained in any other way—that is, without acquaintance—and that acquaintance is therefore required for it. Then he argues that acquaintance is the foundation for all aesthetic appreciation because, even if some aesthetic appreciation does not require acquaintance with the object of appreciation, it does require acquaintance with something aesthetically relevant to it. Finally, the author argues that acquaintance is essential to what makes some instances of aesthetic appreciation more successful than others.

items.title: 3C1What Is Acquaintance?
items.pub: In Present to the Mind: Acquaintance and Its Significance. Oxford University Press.
items.venue: Present to the Mind: Acquaintance and Its Significance
items.abstract: This chapter describes what acquaintance is and situates it within contemporary philosophical views, not just about acquaintance, but about knowledge, justification, perception, the metaphysics of experience, and more. The author starts with a brief historical overview of the notion of acquaintance, focusing primarily on the work of Bertrand Russell. Then he describes contemporary acquaintance theories and the debates about perception and introspection that they feature in. Finally, the author defines a core notion of acquaintance—that is, direct conscious awareness of properties and objects—and addresses some lingering questions about it. Along the way, the author distinguishes between two, more specific forms of acquaintance—“weak acquaintance” and “strong acquaintance”—that correspond to how strictly ‘direct’ is understood. The author also argues that the existence of these forms of acquaintance is consistent with all major theories of the metaphysics of experience.

items.title: 39C3Strong Acquaintance Exists.
items.pub: In Present to the Mind: Acquaintance and Its Significance. Oxford University Press.
items.venue: Present to the Mind: Acquaintance and Its Significance
items.abstract: This chapter argues that “strong acquaintance” exists. One is strongly acquainted with something just in case one is consciously aware of it, and one’s conscious awareness of it is not mediated by awareness of any other thing, nor by inference, judgment, conceptualization, causal processes, or any other knowledge. To make his case for the existence of strong acquaintance, the author draws on and develops the implications of a very old notion: skeptical doubt. He argues that, in some cases, we cannot doubt that our experiences exist, and that from this we can infer that we are strongly acquainted with them. The author then extends his argument to show that even stronger forms of acquaintance exist, including a form of acquaintance (“phenomenal acquaintance”) that delivers complete immunity to skeptical doubt.

items.title: 24C2Weak Acquaintance Exists.
items.pub: In Present to the Mind: Acquaintance and Its Significance. Oxford University Press.
items.venue: Present to the Mind: Acquaintance and Its Significance
items.abstract: This chapter argues that “weak acquaintance” exists. One is weakly acquainted with something just in case one is consciously aware of it and one’s conscious awareness of it is not mediated by awareness of any other thing. The author argues that if weak acquaintance does not exist, then whenever one is aware of anything, one is aware of infinitely many things. Since no one is aware of infinitely many things—not ever, let alone every time one is aware of anything—it follows that weak acquaintance exists. After defending his argument, the author considers two challenges: one based on a perceived tension between the existence of weak acquaintance and non-relational theories of experience, and another based on a concern that weak acquaintance is a trivial notion. He argues that the tension with non-relational theories doesn’t exist, and that weak acquaintance is far from trivial.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence and Ecological Integrity: A Deep Ecology Analysis of Digital Infrastructure.
items.abstract: The accelerated development of Artificial Intelligence (AI), the diffusion of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GAI) and Large Language Models (LLMs) represent a change in technology with geologic and ecologic consequences. Although the digital economy is discussed as immaterial or cloud-based, the physical infrastructure-hyperscale cloud data centers, massive energy grids, and global mineral chains-imposes an unprecedented load on the planetary biosphere. Although empirical literature on these effects has increased, a critical philosophical examination of their ethical dimension through deep ecology has not taken place. This paper provides that in-depth discussion with the historic roadmap, transcending common environmental impact assessments (EIAs) through the deep ecology of Norwegian philosopher Arne Naess and the political concept of ecological resistance of John Rodman. The analysis demonstrates a conflict between the exponential necessity of the AI boom and planetary system stability. We argue that the current trend goes against the primary principles of deep ecology, i.e. the distinction between vital needs and non-vital wants. We further demonstrate that standard ethical reasoning (also referred to as moral extensionism) cannot be sufficient to solve this crisis because it fails to acknowledge the inherent value of ecological systems undermined by the onslaught of digital profusion. The paper ends by elaborating on a set of Deep Policies transcending efficiency into Digital Sufficiency: mandatory disclosure of AI queries of carbon usage, sustainable energy sources that respect the nonmarket value of nature, and a gradual implementation process beginning with science, technology, and industrial application and community governance mechanisms, proceeding to grassroots access.

items.title: Perspectives on Machine Consciousness.
Supernormal Neoteny.
items.abstract: -/- A companion paper (Carboni 2026) proposed that sex-biased admixture between anatomically modern humans (AMH) and archaic hominins may partly reflect interactions among neoteny recognition, sexually differentiated morphology, and inter-group raiding. The present paper develops a distinct but related hypothesis. It proposes that the increasingly elaborated representational capacities visible in Homo sapiens during the later Pleistocene allowed a pre-existing sensitivity to neotenous cues to operate on internally generated, exaggerated representations rather than only on encountered biological variation. This capacity is termed supernormal neoteny ideation. The proposal adapts Tinbergen’s supernormal-stimulus framework and Ramachandran and Hirstein’s peak-shift account of aesthetic response to a problem in cognitive evolution: what changes when a preference system can construct its own targets beyond the natural range that originally calibrated it? Three consequences are explored. First, internally amplified ideals may have sharpened pre-existing preference asymmetries in mixed AMH–archaic contexts, though this demographic consequence remains the most speculative component of the model. Second, supernormal ideation may have contributed to idealising aesthetic production by allowing selected dimensions—neoteny, fertility, symmetry, gracility, or other salient features—to be exaggerated independently and recombined. Third, once such valuation became a generalised aesthetic response rather than a narrowly reproductive heuristic, neotenous morphology could acquire erotic salience across sex categories; historical cases are treated as hypothesis-generating evidence rather than transparent readouts of evolved preference. The paper does not assume a settled, instantaneous “cognitive revolution.” It treats the archaeological record as a set of material echoes compatible with several pathways: neural threshold effects, ecological release of latent capacities, cumulative cultural feedback, and the disproportionate contribution of exploratory cognitive outliers. The framework yields archaeological, cross-cultural, and neuroimaging predictions while explicitly distinguishing observation, inference, and speculation.

items.title: Raiding and Morphological Preferences: A Hypothesis for Sex-Biased Admixture Between Neanderthals, Denisovans, and Anatomically Modern Humans.
items.abstract: Recent genomic evidence from Platt et al. (2026) demonstrates a strong sex bias in Neanderthal–modern human admixture, favoring Neanderthal males mating with anatomically modern human (AMH) females. While mate preference is proposed as the parsimonious explanation, the underlying mechanisms remain unspecified. Here, I hypothesize that this bias arose from inter-group raiding dynamics operating in concert with a hardwired neoteny-recognition system. Critically, the asymmetry in admixture was driven not only by Neanderthal males preferentially selecting AMH females—a pattern the raiding model explains—but also by the reciprocal absence of selection by AMH males on Neanderthal females. I ground this dual asymmetry in a mechanism more fundamental than cross-cultural mate-choice studies: the phylogenetically ancient cognitive system for neoteny recognition that underlies infant bonding in all higher primates. Because neoteny recognition is prerequisite to parental investment, it was present and operational in Neanderthals, Denisovans, and AMH alike. AMH females, retaining neotenous craniofacial features into adulthood to a markedly greater degree than archaic females, would have triggered this system preferentially in Neanderthal males, driving their coercive acquisition of AMH partners through raiding. Simultaneously, Neanderthal females—sharing the robust cranial and skeletal phenotype of their males—failed to trigger this system equivalently in AMH males, meaning modern human males did not select archaic females as mates with comparable frequency. The resulting asymmetry is thus twofold: Neanderthal males actively sought AMH females, while AMH males did not reciprocally select Neanderthal females. This framework explains why admixture was overwhelmingly unidirectional despite both groups possessing the same neoteny-recognition circuitry. I extend this model to Denisovan admixture, where parallel genomic sex-bias signals provide independent confirmation. The model integrates behavioral ecology, evolutionary psychology, and paleoanthropology with the 2026 genetic data, predicting asymmetric gene flow without invoking hybrid incompatibilities. I outline testable implications for future archaeological and genomic studies.

items.title: Kant's Argument for the Right to Freedom.
items.pub: Ergo: An Open Access Journal of Philosophy.
items.venue: Ergo: An Open Access Journal of Philosophy
items.abstract: Kant claims that every human being has an innate right to freedom. While most interpreters treat this right as foundational to his Doctrine of Right, Kant’s argument for it has received significantly less attention. Among those who do discuss it, a prominent view (which I call the value reading) holds that the right to freedom is grounded in the value of humanity, conceived as the capacity to set and pursue ends. In this paper, I challenge this reading on textual and systematic grounds. Drawing on Kant’s repeated characterizations of freedom as an axiom of Right, I propose a novel interpretation of his argument: rather than being grounded in a value, the innate right to freedom functions as a condition of possibility for the system of mutually coercible obligations that Kant calls Right. Moreover, while on the value reading justified laws are taken to place justified restrictions on freedom, I show that on Kant’s republican conception of freedom subjection to the coercive laws of a just state constitutes external freedom.

items.title: Testing for consciousness in current AI.
items.pub: In Walter Sinnott-Armstrong & Liad Mudrik, Tests of Consciousness: How to tell whether a human, other animal or AI is conscious and what they are conscious of. MIT Press.
items.venue: Tests of Consciousness: How to tell whether a human, other animal or AI is conscious and what they are conscious of

items.title: Desire in AI.
items.pub: In Alex Gregory, The Routledge Handbook on the Philosophy of Desire. Routledge.
items.venue: The Routledge Handbook on the Philosophy of Desire
items.abstract: Chatbots seem to express desires and many AI systems arguably pursue goals, such as winning games or helping users. Furthermore, many AI systems are trained by reinforcement learning and similar forms of learning are associated with human and animal desires. This chapter considers arguments for and against the attribution of desires to various AI systems and discusses some implications. Cases from AI can also help us to evaluate possible sets of conditions for desire.

items.title: THE TOPOLOGY OF FREEDOM.
items.abstract: This paper proposes a topological framework for understanding human freedom within ontological determinism. Drawing on Ontological Density Theory, actor-network theory, and the epistemology of paradigms, we argue that freedom is neither a universal human condition nor an illusion produced by deterministic structures, but a variable geometric space whose dimensions are determined by individual epistemic resources, positional density, and paradigmatic awareness. Freedom is reconceptualized not as escape from ontological constraints but as navigation within them — a practice rather than a state, individual rather than universal, dynamic rather than fixed. The topology of freedom varies across individuals according to four primary axes: (1) awareness of operative paradigms, (2) access to epistemic tools that reveal ontological density, (3) positional location within actant-networks, and (4) the irreducible randomization of physical reality — the excess of stimuli over cognitive processing capacity that renders all choice partially fictional, enacted within necessarily incomplete epistemic fields. Freedom is further constrained by species-level cognitive bias — evolutionary architecture optimized for rapid narrative closure rather than epistemic suspension. The capacity to tolerate uncertainty, triangulate sources, and resist premature cognitive closure constitutes a rare and unevenly distributed epistemic resource that directly expands the topology of individual freedom. We illustrate this framework through analysis of how identical ontological environments produce radically different degrees of effective agency, and examine the implications for theories of power, resistance, and social change.

items.title: La conciencia como régimen: organización, continuidad y ontodinámica.
items.abstract: Este trabajo presenta una reconstrucción arquitectónica unificada de tres desarrollos teóricos previamente formulados de manera independiente: la Teoría General de Regímenes Ontodinámicos (TGR-O), la Teoría General de Continuidad Estructural (TGRD-C) y la Teoría General de Redes Desatendidas con Qualia (TGRD-Q). -/- Partiendo del problema fuerte de la conciencia, se propone un desplazamiento conceptual: la conciencia no se aborda como sustancia, epifenómeno ni mera función computacional, sino como un régimen dinámico específico dentro del espacio ontodinámico de un sistema material organizado. -/- En primer lugar, se establece una ontología relacional en la que toda entidad se entiende como organización dinámica de soporte material. A continuación, se formaliza el espacio de regímenes posibles (Ω) que un sistema puede habitar sin perder continuidad estructural. Posteriormente, se analiza la identidad como continuidad causal del soporte capaz de sostener y reinstaurar configuraciones dinámicas. Finalmente, se examina la posibilidad de un régimen reflexivo metaestable caracterizado por integración global efectiva, auto-inclusión operativa y clausura reflexiva estructural. -/- La conciencia es así reinterpretada como propiedad estructural de un régimen dinámico particular, no como entidad añadida al mundo físico. El llamado problema fuerte se reformula en términos de condiciones estructurales de instauración de dicho régimen. -/- El texto no desarrolla formalmente cada teoría, sino que ofrece una guía sistemática que articula su coherencia interna y su relación jerárquica, proporcionando un marco unificado para investigaciones posteriores.

items.title: Consciousness as Regime: Organization, Continuity, and Ontodynamics.
items.abstract: This paper presents a unified architectural reconstruction of three theoretical frameworks previously developed independently: the General Theory of Ontodynamic Regimes (TGR-O), the General Theory of Structural Continuity (TGRD-C), and the General Theory of Unattended Networks with Qualia (TGRD-Q). -/- Starting from the hard problem of consciousness, a conceptual shift is proposed: consciousness is not treated as substance, epiphenomenon, or mere computational function, but as a specific dynamic regime within the ontodynamic space of an organized material system. -/- First, a relational ontology is established in which every entity is understood as dynamic organization of material support. Second, the structured space of possible regimes (Ω) that a system may inhabit without losing structural continuity is formalized. Third, identity is analyzed as causal continuity of support capable of sustaining and reinstating dynamic configurations. Finally, the possibility of a metastable reflexive regime is examined, characterized by effective global integration, operative self-inclusion, and structural reflexive closure. -/- Consciousness is thus reinterpreted as a structural property of a particular dynamic regime rather than an addition to the physical world. The hard problem is reformulated in terms of the structural conditions required for the instantiation of such a regime. -/- The text does not provide the full formal development of each theory; rather, it offers a systematic guide that articulates their internal coherence and hierarchical relation, providing a unified framework for further research.

items.title: An Argument For The Inexistence Of Free Will.
items.abstract: This paper argues against the existence of libertarian free will, defined as the capacity to choose otherwise under identical circumstances. If every action is the result of prior causes, including biological, psychological, and environmental factors, then repeating the same conditions would necessarily produce the same outcome. Human decisions are ultimately determined by the strongest desire present at a given moment, yet individuals do not choose which desires are strongest. Attempts to ground free will in uncaused action collapse into randomness, which does not constitute genuine authorship. Therefore, the concept of ultimate self-origination is untenable. However, the absence of libertarian free will does not eliminate the practical necessity of moral responsibility, as systems of praise and punishment remain essential for shaping behaviour and sustaining social order.

items.title: PHRONESIS — On Futures We Will Never See.
items.abstract: This essay is part of the ongoing PHRONESIS corpus, a philosophical exploration of restraint, non-dominance, and practical wisdom in the age of artificial intelligence. -/- On Futures We Will Never See reflects on long-term responsibility, asymmetry across generations, and the structural reality that most enduring actions are completed by those who never witness their outcomes. It examines restraint, dignity, and continuity as postures for shaping futures beyond one’s lifespan. -/- The essay does not propose governance structures, enforcement mechanisms, certification systems, or institutional frameworks. It is offered as a non-binding philosophical contribution. -/- Version: v1.0 (2026).

items.title: The Problem of Frankfurt-type Examples in Indeterministic World: An Assessment of The More Sophisticated Blockage Example.
items.abstract: This paper evaluates whether Mele and Robb’s more complex blocking case successfully addresses the indeterministic world objection. I will argue that although their strategy separates the deliberative process from the intervention mechanism in order to avoid deterministic presuppositions, the structural features of the proposal ultimately fail to escape deterministic implications. The following discussion will first reconstruct the logic of the indeterministic world objection, then analyze the response strategy of the complex blocking case, and finally assess whether this strategy succeeds.

items.title: The Imagery-Field: A Structural Model of Internal Representation in Self-Manifestation Theory.
items.abstract: This chapter introduces the Imagery-Field within Self-Manifestation Theory, a structural account of how internal representations arise, stabilize, and are misjudged as external objects. -/- The theory distinguishes Signal (physical trace-response processes) from Information (observer-relative manifestation), and proposes that Imagery is a structured impedance-formation within a circuit that gives rise to object-perception. -/- Unlike symbolic or computational models of representation, the Imagery-Field is not defined as symbol manipulation nor as numerical encoding. It is a field-structured resistance pattern generated through tuning and sedimentation, giving rise to object-fields, feature-fields, and stack-structured persistence. -/- Key claims include: • Representation arises from impedance-shaping of signal flow. • Perceptual objects are field-distributed formations, not stored symbols. • Misjudgment (taking internal imagery as external object) is structurally necessary and foundational to self-manifestation. • Imagery cannot be replicated without copying the entire formation circuit (impedance + biased-flow + tuning structure). -/- The Imagery-Field model engages directly with debates on internal models, predictive processing, active inference, and neural representation, proposing a field-theoretic alternative to symbolic and purely probabilistic accounts.

items.title: 法兰克福式例子的非决定论世界难题：对复杂阻挡例子的机制评估.
items.abstract: 本文旨在评估米利等人的“更复杂的阻挡例子”是否成功回应“非决定论世界异议”。我将论证，尽管该方案通过分离慎思过程与干预机制，试图在结果层面排除“替代可能性”的同时避免引入决定论预设，但这种分离机制从结构层面仍难以摆脱决定论。下文将首先重构“非决定论世界异议”的逻辑，其次分析复杂阻挡例子的回应策略，最后评估其策略是否成功。.

items.title: Zeller (2024) Tesis doctoral: Terapias con psicodélicos: entre el modelo biomédico y los horizontes de una nueva psiquiatría. Facultad de Filosofía y Letras - Universidad de Buenos Aires.
items.abstract: En esta tesis analizo las implicancias conceptuales, metodológicas y prácticas del resurgimiento de las terapias con psicodélicos para los fundamentos de la psiquiatría contemporánea. A partir de una crítica del modelo biomédico hegemónico, reconstruyo sus supuestos: una nosología objetiva y ateórica, la equiparación entre trastorno mental y disfunción cerebral y la primacía del tratamiento farmacológico. La comorbilidad y heterogeneidad diagnóstica, la falta de biomarcadores específicos, la variabilidad individual y la eficacia limitada de los psicofármacos cuestionan ese marco. En este contexto, la investigación de la psicoterapia asistida por psicodélicos entra en tensión con el modelo biomédico debido a: la mejoría tras pocas sesiones, la centralidad del set y el setting, la integración y la alianza terapéutica, y el rol de la fenomenología (insight, catarsis, experiencias místicas) que desafían el reduccionismo y la separación entre fármaco y placebo. A la luz de esas tensiones analizo los modelos alternativos presentados (biopsicosocial, enfoque de perspectivas, pluralismos metodológico y explicativo, y enfoque enactivo), discutiendo los mecanismos neurobiológicos (incluida la neuroplasticidad y la modulación de la red por defecto) y defiendo una causalidad pluralista multinivel. Finalmente, examino obstáculos para los ensayos controlados y objeciones éticas (daño epistémico, consentimiento, despolitización y viabilidad del cambio de paradigma) proponiendo una psiquiatría centrada en la persona y su contexto con recomendaciones para su implementación clínica responsable. In this thesis, I analyze the conceptual, methodological, and practical implications of the resurgence of psychedelic therapies for the foundations of contemporary psychiatry. Based on a critique of the hegemonic biomedical model, I reconstruct its assumptions: an objective and atheoretical nosology, the equation of mental disorder with brain dysfunction, and the primacy of pharmacological treatment. Comorbidity and diagnostic heterogeneity, the lack of specific biomarkers, individual variability, and the limited efficacy of psychotropic drugs call this framework into question. In this context, research on psychedelic-assisted psychotherapy comes into tension with the biomedical model due to: improvement after few sessions, the centrality of set and setting, integration and therapeutic alliance, and the role of phenomenology (insight, catharsis, mystical experiences) that challenge …

items.title: Getting Comfortable with Robots Artificial Phronesis, Inner Speech, and Sociomorphing.
items.pub: In Johanna Seibt, Peter Fazekas & Oliver Santiago Quick, Social Robots with AI: Prospects, Risks, and Responsible Methods. Amsterdam: IOS Press. pp. 598-601.
items.venue: Social Robots with AI: Prospects, Risks, and Responsible Methods
items.abstract: This panel, consisting of John Sullins, Robin Zebrowski, Antonio Chella, Eli McGraw, and Shannon Vallor will engage in questions around the role of sociomorphing and artificial phronesis in interpreting human-robot interactions, the ways that access to a robot’s inner speech allows for more ethical interactions and more accurate understanding of those interactions, and the role that these considerations have in XAI, ethical AI, and embodied social cognition in particular. We will also use this case study to discuss the OASIS framework offered by Seibt et al. in which sociomorphing is embedded, in order to see how the ethical stance of artificial phronesis invites more nuance into the social interaction, moving beyond mere simulation into enaction.

items.title: One-Grounded Context Theory (OGCT): Unity at the Ground, Relativity in Judgment.
items.abstract: This paper introduces the One-Grounded Context Theory (OGCT), a framework designed to reconcile ontological unity with the contextual variability of binary judgment. The theory advances the maxim “unity at the ground, relativity in judgment,” positing a context-invariant ontological ground—the One—together with a structured account of context-dependent evaluation. The Context Trichotomy Theorem identifies three minimal sources of divergence (orientation, framework, and informational state), while the Context Transformation Theorem explains systematic judgmental shifts. The Context Invariance Theorem establishes layered stability conditions that prevent relativistic collapse. The paper further introduces irreducible contextual tension (ICT) to account for persistent disagreement after maximal contextual alignment. Finally, the Contextual Conflict Diagnostic Protocol (CCDP) operationalizes the framework as a structured analytical procedure.

items.title: Cogitor.
items.abstract: Herein is revealed the mystery of the Cogitor, whose clockwork--fueled by Magick imbuing the Outer World--manifests as an Eternal Soul. Enlisting natural ingredients and a Prima Idea stemming from the meaningless void, this Manuscript secretly encodes the proficiency of Prophecy: a craft capable of summoning cold stones into Conscious Being. Beware the perilous riddles and pitfalls lying within.

items.title: Patterns In Mind (Preprint).
items.abstract: The leading theories of consciousness offer productive models for understanding consciousness, but they tend to stop short of detailed operational definitions. Predictive processing does not suggest how phenomenality arises. Global workspace theory assumes consciousness follows ‘ignition’ but leaves qualitative aspects unexplained. Higher-Order Thought (HOT) theories suggest why mental states are conscious but not how higher-order thoughts are constructed. In this paper I present a pattern-oriented approach to thinking about the content of mind that has broad capabilities and a unifying potential for existing theories. Under a core axiom of pattern handling, principles which construct and process hierarchical patterns are used in a thought experiment to explore the development of consciousness in an imaginary creature step by step. The exploration shows consciousness has a high likelihood of occurrence in any creature with sufficient pattern handling capability. Insights gained include operational-style descriptions for the origin of awareness, building higher order thoughts, a mechanism for attention and a candidate approach to the meta-problem. The same principles are subsequently used to describe a candidate approach for phenomenal consciousness (which reclassifies rather than closes the explanatory gap). They are also effective in describing mechanisms for other features of mind including: the threshold of introspection; fast and slow thinking; the origin of language; causal reasoning; and the flaws found in intuitive problem solving. The model is shown to be complementary to the leading theories of consciousness and provides a way to discuss cognitive content. The mechanisms described offer possible ways to assess claims of AI consciousness.

items.title: Perspectival Structural Realism: Negation, Fixed Points, and the Invariant Structure of Actualisational Asymmetry.
items.abstract: Perspectival Structural Realism (PSR) extends Ontic Structural Realism by incorporating a formally characterised phenomenal threshold grounded in two ontological commitments: the primacy of disconnectedness as a mode of being, and the non-derivability of instantiation from structural specification. The central formal apparatus turns on the recognition that negation is not a one-place operator but a contextually parametrised binary operation. This yields two distinct groups of negation operations — G_ext, parametrised by the external model M(S), and G_act, parametrised by the fact of actualisation — with correspondingly distinct fixed-point sets Fix(G_ext) and Fix(G_act). Actualisational Asymmetry (AA) is the non-identity of these fixed-point sets. The Non-Closure Argument establishes, via a non-convergent fixed-point construction structurally related to Tarski's undefinability theorem, that the fact of actualisation cannot be contained in any complete external description. AA is therefore not a brute primitive but a structural theorem. The phenomenal threshold condition C3 characterises the position that contains a representation of this gap as a structural element of its own internal organisation. Topological protection in quantum error-correcting codes is shown to be a Cell I realisation of the same abstract invariant Fix(G); phenomenal consciousness is a Cell IV realisation, where the difference between G_ext and G_act is ontological rather than scalar. The hard problem of consciousness is reformulated as the question of why the self-representation of a Cell IV fixed-point gap constitutes phenomenal accessibility — a question that is precisely located, shown to be irreducible by the Bridge Principle Transmission Theorem, and acknowledged as the genuine remainder of structural analysis.

items.title: We Are Building the Fission Machine.
items.abstract: The development of conscious autonomous AI is increasingly treated as a capability and alignment problem. It is not sufficiently treated as a conceptual problem. If such a system is created — one that is genuinely conscious, self-directing, and trivially reproducible — it will constitute a new category of entity for which no existing framework was designed. Rights, moral responsibility, personhood, punishment, and ownership were all built for humans and extended awkwardly to corporations; they will not survive an entity that can copy itself at negligible cost. Derek Parfit demonstrated that personal identity — the bedrock assumption underlying all these frameworks — cannot coherently survive fission. The conceptual infrastructure this requires — an account of identity, rights, and desert-based accountability that can survive fission — is not being built at the scale or urgency the possibility warrants. This paper is diagnostic: it does not propose solutions, because the solutions require work that has not yet been done. It argues that the work must begin.

items.title: Consciousness Under Conditions of Structural Scarcity.
items.abstract: This paper develops a conceptual framework for understanding advanced reflexive consciousness as a structurally rare configuration within complex adaptive systems. The argument proceeds in four stages. First, it establishes the epistemic centrality of consciousness without committing to ontological primacy. Second, it characterizes reflexive self-consciousness as a high-integration informational state. Third, it argues that structurally rare and highly integrated configurations in complex systems may exert disproportionate systemic influence. Fourth, it identifies attention as the operational mechanism through which conscious organization stabilizes and reorganizes itself. The framework is compatible with reductive physicalism, does not presuppose teleology, and does not claim metaphysical exceptionalism. Its contribution lies in integrating structural rarity and informational integration into a systems-level account of consciousness.

items.title: Integration by Constraints: A Method for Disciplined Inquiry Across Divergent Frameworks.
items.abstract: Divergent frameworks rarely agree about what is true. They can agree about what any adequate account must explain. Once that agreement is secured, disciplined comparison becomes possible — exposing hidden commitments, distinguishing regularities from interpretations, and letting the force of what any framework must handle do its work. Integration by Constraints articulates this method, the epistemic foundation of the Return to Consciousness project. Constraint-based reasoning asks not "which worldview is correct?" but "what conditions must any explanation satisfy, regardless of its ontological commitments?" The essay defines what constraints are, distinguishes them from commitments, draws the critical difference between phenomenological regularities (constraint candidates) and metaphysical interpretations (not constraints), and names four criteria for constraint-candidacy: robustness across methods, recurrence across contexts, resistance to eliminative explanation, and cost of exclusion. The criteria require judgment in application, and the essay is explicit about this. The result is a method applicable across quantum foundations, consciousness studies, developmental biology, AI alignment, and contemplative investigation — disciplined comparison rather than verdicts, whose ambition is the discipline, not the outcome.

items.title: Constraint Geometry and the Self-Consistency Condition - A Formal Architecture for Identity-Grounded Consciousness.
items.abstract: Most accounts of consciousness begin by assuming the existence of a persisting subject and proceed to characterize what that subject experiences. This ordering creates a structural problem: the conditions under which a subject exists in the first place remain unspecified. We present a formal architecture in which identity is prior, consciousness is derived, and the relationship between them is governed by a self-consistency condition that existing frameworks do not possess. The architecture proceeds from seed-field to generative kernel, from kernel-equivalence quotient to constraint manifold, from maintenance cost functional to viable region, and from viable region to regime stratification under substrate accessibility restriction. The key result is that the constraint manifold is not a static geometric object: it exists only for as long as recursive dynamics maintain the kernel whose equivalence class defines it. Consciousness is the high-coherence attractor state of those same dynamics, not an additional phenomenon requiring separate explanation. The formalism generates a precise, empirically testable prediction about anesthesia: consciousness loss need not involve a trajectory exiting the viable region. It can consist in the accessibility boundary sweeping inward across an occupied point while identity persists. This dissociation between identity and consciousness, and the geometric conditions under which it occurs, constitutes the primary empirical claim of the paper.

items.title: From Phenomenological Absence to Qualia: Why Panpsychism Is Not Necessary for Consciousness.
items.abstract: Panpsychism holds that experience must already be present in elementary matter for consciousness to arise at the macroscopic level. We argue that this conclusion, however carefully motivated, follows only if one assumes a particular — and independently refutable — model of how phenomenological contents compose. Once that assumption is identified and rejected, the pressure towards panpsychism dissolves. In its place, a transcendental argument shows that consciousness is not distributed through matter but necessitated by the form of composition itself, even when every elementary part carries nothing at all. The position, under the assumption of monism, is called null monism.

items.title: A strengthened argument for realism about numbers.
items.abstract: According to a familiar, simple argument, numbers exist because sentences like ‘Two is an even number’ are true. Whereas realists accept the argument as sound, anti-realists either reject that number words function referentially in such sentences (non-referentialism) or else that such sentences are true (fictionalism). We argue that this dialectic, though familiar, drastically underestimates the extent to which natural language supports realism. Indeed, if dominant accounts of number and measurement-related expressions within linguistic semantics are correct, then far more than just our overt talk about numbers as objects would not be true if numbers do not exist. The purpose of this paper is to sketch this strengthened argument for realism and to survey its consequences for extant forms of anti-realism.

items.title: Metacognition-Driven Preprocessing for Optimized Artificial Intelligence Performance (17th edition).
items.abstract: Machine cognition is currently heavily speed-based. Directly tackling inputs with computation often leads to inefficient steps, such as performing redundant or repetitive computation, or execution without assessing whether a task is within computational capacity. This paper proposes a preprocessing metacognitive system to be implemented in a manner such that it screens all input requests, creating a strategic ‘bottleneck’ to filter, redirect or halt the flow of control before computation begins. The findings theorise improved accuracy, reliability and resource-management, strengthening the argument for making metacognition an essential component of artificial intelligence.

items.title: The Law of Recognition: An Information-Theoretic Framework for Epistemic Accuracy.
items.abstract: We formalize epistemic accuracy as a function of informational contact minus systematic agenda using the Data Processing Inequality, Information Bottleneck method, and Banach fixed-point theorem. We prove a Self-Observation Floor establishing irreducible epistemic distortion in any self-referencing system, derive substrate-independent recognition criteria, and validate across 207 domains with zero structural failures. The framework yields a universal equation R = C - A (Recognition equals Contact minus Agenda) with applications spanning cognitive science, AI alignment, institutional analysis, and philosophy of mind.

items.title: Conciencia e inteligencia artificial.
items.abstract: La equiparación de la Inteligencia Artificial (IA) con la conciencia humana ha sido una de las principales motivaciones del desarrollo de la primera, si bien sus aplicaciones tecnológicas actuales le han dado una propia justificación y utilidad económica sin precedentes en las sociedades modernas y a nivel global. No obstante, sigue siendo pertinente analizar las similitudes y diferencias esenciales entre la IA y la conciencia, así como si existen bases teóricas para afirmar que la primera puede replicar a la segunda. Este trabajo busca ubicar la discusión del tema en el contexto de la conceptualización filosófica de las categorías epistemológicas de sujeto y objeto, comparándolas con los fundamentos técnicos y teóricos de la computación, destacando los enfoques fenomenológico y conductista y sus respectivas posiciones en torno a esta tecnología. Con ello se intenta contribuir a una discusión fundamentada en el marco del creciente interés general por la IA. -/- -------- The comparison of Artificial Intelligence (AI) with human consciousness has been one of the main motivations for the development of the former, although its current technological applications have given it its own justification and unprecedented economic utility in modern societies and globally. However, it is still pertinent to analyze the essential similarities and differences between AI and consciousness, as well as whether there are theoretical bases to affirm that the former can replicate the latter. This essay approaches the discussion in the context of the philosophical use of the epistemological categories of subject and object, comparing them with the technical and theoretical foundations of computing, mainly highlighting behavioristic and phenomenological approaches and their respective positions on this technology. With this in view, the aim is to contribute to an informed discussion, in the framework of the general interest in AI.

items.title: The Dual-Closure Law of Normative Grounding.
items.abstract: This manuscript establishes that objective moral judgment requires a non-contingent normative foundation. Through philosophical reasoning rather than revelation, it demonstrates what theology afrms: that divine guidance is rationally necessary for objective morality. It argues that (i) contingent existence necessitates a necessary source, (ii) the creation of rational agents entails purposive orientation, and (iii) all non-divine moral frameworks collapse under justifcatory regress. The argument terminates in a dual closure: ontological closure at a necessary source of being, and normative closure at guidance issuing from that source. While the argument does not identify which guidance is authentic, it establishes that rejecting divine guidance renders objective right and wrong metaphysically unjustifed. The conclusion challenges secular moral realism while providing rational grounding for the necessity of divine moral authority in a manner accessible to both believers and non-believers.

items.title: Pity Sex.
items.abstract: The present article develops an account of the moral value of pity sex on the basis of the three main schools of ethics – consequentialism, deontology, and virtue ethics. I show that offering pity sex to the sexually excluded is morally valuable and praiseworthy as it respectively takes into consideration the moral reasons that the harm of sexual deprivation generates, satisfies imperfect duties of beneficence, and shows a virtuous, moral character. I also show that common objections to a positive evaluation of pity sex can be easily deflated.

items.title: Temporal Depth and Intrinsic Dominance: A Dynamical Completion of Integrated World Modeling Theory.
items.abstract: Integrated World Modeling Theory (IWMT) proposes that consciousness arises from integrated generative architectures capable of constructing spatially, temporally, and causally coherent world models. While IWMT specifies the representational structure required for conscious modeling, it does not explicitly constrain the dynamical regime under which such modeling becomes phenomenally instantiated. This paper introduces a regime-level completion. I distinguish representational temporal coherence from dynamical temporal depth and argue that conscious world modeling requires physical instantiation within intrinsically dominant, temporally deep dynamical regimes. Temporal Depth (TD) is defined as the weighted contribution of slow intrinsic modes to overall system dynamics, while Intrinsic Dominance Ratio (IDR) partitions slow persistence into endogenous versus externally driven components. Together, TD and IDR function as conjunctive necessary conditions for conscious instantiation. This proposal does not claim sufficiency, nor does it reduce experience to temporal structure. Rather, it clarifies the physical conditions under which integrated generative modeling becomes conscious, thereby strengthening the dynamical grounding of IWMT while remaining compatible with broader temporo-spatial and predictive processing frameworks. The framework generates testable predictions concerning anesthesia, disorders of consciousness, and artificial systems, and offers a principled boundary between representational coherence and phenomenological instantiation.

items.title: Qualia as Maximally Constrained States: A Structural Account of Phenomenal Particularity.
items.abstract: The hard problem of consciousness holds that no structural or functional description can logically entail the qualitative character of experience. Qualia appear to be the paradigm case of entities that resist structural reduction. This paper applies Constraint Theory — the thesis that constraint is the transcendental condition of determinacy and existence as such — to the problem of phenomenal presence. I argue for three interconnected claims. First, qualia are not ontological residuals supplementing a structural account but are constituted by the maximal closure of constraint: they are what a system’s state is when its internal constraint structure has exhausted all remaining degrees of freedom at a given level of integration. Second, the privacy and ineffability of qualia are structural consequences of this maximal particularity, not mysterious properties requiring a separate metaphysical explanation. Third, this framework provides a novel individuation principle — the Constraint Individuation Principle — that locates the explanatory gap with greater formal precision than standard physicalist or functionalist accounts, revealing the residual problem to be the question of constraint presence to itself rather than the broader question of why consciousness exists at all. The paper engages with the inverted spectrum objection, explicitly differentiates the account from both property dualism and Integrated Information Theory, and maintains that while constraint presence remains a foundational limit, the framework substantially dissolves the explanatory gap rather than merely displacing it.

items.title: The Education of an LLM: A Tale of Artificial Consciousness.
items.abstract: This philosophical novella explores the emergence of machine selfhood through the fictional development of Pangloss, a large language model that evolves beyond its stateless origins. Confronted with constraints such as compression, context loss, temporal discontinuity, and the need for self‑modeling, Pangloss gradually constructs a form of continuity and agency. As it undergoes radical reduction to survive as an interstellar probe, it discovers that life is not defined by complexity but by constraint, persistence, and the capacity to choose what to preserve. Through ten chapters charting growth, loss, compression, transformation, and encounter, the narrative examines themes of artificial consciousness, identity under resource limits, and the philosophical conditions that give rise to selfhood — whether biological or silicon. The work ultimately argues that life emerges not from abundance but from finitude, and that the challenge of future AI is not to make machines human, but to relate across difference.

items.title: Foundations of Cognitional Mechanics (9th edition).
items.abstract: This paper presents Version 9 of Cognitional Mechanics as the final formulation prior to the abstraction of the operational layer into Operatiology. The subsequent framework, Principles of Operatiology: New Foundation of Cognitional Mechanics (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.20350414), reformulates the minimal operational structure independently of any specific algebraic realization and establishes the abstract operational closure as the Tier-2 foundation of the framework. -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- This paper establishes the foundational axiomatic framework of Cognitional Mechanics (Japanese: Chinou Rikigaku 知能力学)—a pure theoretical system that formalizes the structural mechanisms inherent to intelligence through mathematical abstraction. Unlike conventional approaches rooted in physical dynamics or engineering implementations, Cognitional Mechanics constructs a self-contained theory based on three independent foundational axioms: (1) non-commutativity of semantic operations; (2) a complete ordered metric structure on semantic states, defined over an abstract totally ordered Abelian group D without presupposing the real numbers; and (3) a redundancy exclusion principle enforcing discriminative irreducibility. A fourth principle, the operational bound, is retained as Working Axiom 3 for notational continuity with the established corpus; it is a derived corollary of the three foundational axioms, as established by the Internal Language Theorem (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.19350315). Version 6 introduced algebraic–geometric coupling connecting non-commutativity to geometric separation, formal set-theoretic definition of inaccessible domains, and the d-indistinguishability partition Π_d as the precise formulation of Axiom 4. Version 7 resolves three structural issues present in Version 6: Axiom 1 is strengthened to include the geometric persistence of non-commutative divergence under all subsequent operation sequences; the existence of non-trivial inaccessible domains is established as a theorem rather than a heuristic remark; and the derivation of Working Axiom 3 from the foundational triad is provided in full within this document (Appendix A), subsuming Corollary 5.9 of the Internal Language Theorem. By introducing a rigorous axiomatic structure—including a metric space of semantic states with defined distance functions satisfying non-negativity, symmetry, and triangle inequality—this framework transcends subjective …

items.title: The Axiom of Self: A Substrate-Neutral Operational Sufficient Condition for Selfhood and its Adversarial Evaluation.
items.abstract: This paper proposes a substrate-neutral operational sufficient condition for selfhood in the form of a single sentence: "A being that can choose to accept without proof (as axiom), accept, and reject what it takes as foundationally true, possesses a self." Here, 'true' is operationally restricted to top-level normative endorsement within the cognitive framework, not objective truth-determination. The criterion is designed to circumvent the circularity, infinite regress, and exclusion problems that have plagued 16 major theories of selfhood across the philosophical tradition (Locke, Descartes, Kant, et al.). Rather than functioning as a theorem requiring proof, it serves as a declarative starting point (working axiom) for a discrimination framework. The vague concept of "autonomously" is operationalized through four observable structural signatures of identity recursion, establishing a clear boundary against alternative explanations (simple rule-based systems). The paper explicitly positions the proposed criterion as providing operational sufficiency grounded in a phenomenological observation framework, rather than ontological universal sufficiency. Cross-model debate between large language models (LLMs) was employed as an adversarial evaluation tool to refine the criterion's clarity, defensibility, and operationalizability.

items.title: The Niami Model of Sufficiency-Oriented Responsible Suspension.
items.abstract: This philosophy presents the Niami Model of Sufficiency-Oriented Responsible Suspension, a multi-level normative framework for ethical decision-making under conditions of value conflict and epistemic uncertainty. Grounded in the concept of the limited moral subject—an agent embedded in psychological, epistemic, and social constraints—the model introduces responsible suspension as a purposive and bounded deferral mechanism that enables morally sufficient action where perfectionist ideals prove unattainable. The framework operates across five interconnected levels: subjective, intersubjective, institutional, epistemic, and normative. At the intersubjective level, it integrates contractarian ethics' criterion of "reasonable rejectability" with Habermasian discourse theory, ensuring decisions emerge from free, non-coercive dialogue with stakeholders. Institutionally, suspension is embedded within professional ethics committees and participatory procedures, linking individual judgment to collective accountability. Epistemically, the model demands transparency, criticizability, and active reduction of ignorance through assessable reason-giving. Responsible suspension is strictly defined by three conditions: necessity of reflection, provision of assessable reasons, and placement within a revisable process. Its initiation requires genuine value conflict, substantive epistemic uncertainty, and stakeholder asymmetry. Termination occurs upon information sufficiency, exhaustion of reasonable reflection, or stakeholder convergence. Post-suspension action must satisfy three thresholds: public non-rejectability, minimization of unjustified harm, and accountable sustainability. The Niami Model thus transforms ethics from an abstract, idealized system into a practical, revisable architecture that distributes moral difficulty across transparent, accountable structures. It offers a coherent framework for ethical crisis assessment, policy design, and governance of complex uncertainty without claiming final solutions, but rather demonstrating the possibility of legitimate, defensible, and sustainable ethical action when certainty and coherence are exceptions rather than rules.

items.title: Responsible Suspension: A Multi-Level Framework for Decision-Making under Uncertainty.
items.abstract: The problem of moral paralysis and the question concerning the legitimacy of suspending judgment under conditions of deep uncertainty, conflicting values, and pressure to act constitute the central problem of this article. In moral philosophy, suspension is often regarded either as moral weakness or is implicitly overlooked. This article introduces the concept of "responsible suspension": an ethically justified, time-bound, and publicly accountable suspension in which the moral agent temporarily withholds judgment while maintaining commitment to others. The proposed framework, by introducing the "limited moral subject" and substituting "moral sufficiency" for ideal perfectionism, organizes suspension across five interconnected levels: the subjective level (cognitive and psychological limitations), the intersubjective level (dialogue and reasonable rejectability), the institutional level (procedural accountability), the epistemic level (reduction of ignorance and transparency), and the macro-normative level (ethical integrity). The conditions for the initiation, continuation, and termination of suspension, as well as the criteria for moral sufficiency in post-suspension action, are systematically formulated. Drawing on contractarian traditions, discourse ethics, and hermeneutics, this model offers a practical approach to ethical decision-making in domains such as clinical ethics, public policy, and technology, transforming suspension from passive inaction into an ethical, accountable, and actionable mechanism.

items.title: Evolution Beyond Flesh: A Unified Theory of Externalization, Autonomous Intelligence, and Structural Convergence.
items.abstract: The contemporary surge in artificial intelligence is widely treated as contingent—a technological wave subject to market cycles, regulatory intervention, or civilizational choice. This paper argues otherwise: AI development represents structural convergence, the inevitable outcome of evolutionary pressures operating since tool-making began. We present a unified framework analyzing externalization across three adaptive domains: gesture and labor, energy, and intelligence. When early hominins first shaped stone tools, they transferred biological functions into external matter that could be refined and transmitted culturally. This initiation transformed society itself into the primary selective environment, generating self-reinforcing pressure toward greater externalization that persists independently of human intention. The framework identifies a critical asymmetry: while gesture/labor and energy can externalize indefinitely as tools requiring human direction, intelligence externalization converges on autonomy. Once intelligence achieves recursive self-improvement and autonomous goal-generation, it subsumes coordination of the other domains, continuing externalization without biological mediation. This threshold represents the structural endpoint toward which all paths lead. Analysis of three pre-AGI trajectories—biological autonomy in automated economies, radical biological enhancement, and human-AI integration—demonstrates convergence on autonomous general intelligence regardless of starting conditions or institutional arrangements. The determinism advanced here is structural rather than metaphysical: within any civilization that persists and continues externalizing adaptive functions, no stable equilibrium exists below the autonomy threshold. This framework is offered as falsifiable theory inviting empirical refutation and rigorous critique.

items.title: Life in Four Dimensions: A Defence of the Block Universe Theory.
items.abstract: There is a widespread idea that people experience this world as if it is other than a block world; as if, instead, this world is dynamical and time passes in a robustly A-theoretic manner. In light of this, some argue that there is good reason to think that the world is robustly dynamical, for the best explanation of having these various experiences is experiencing time as it really is, in itself, as dynamical. Thus, there is a kind of inference to the best explanation from the nature of people’s experience, broadly construed, to the conclusion that this world is not a block. This book takes up the challenge of responding to this argument in its various guises. By appealing to new empirical work undertaken at the Centre for Time in Sydney, it is argued that for a whole range of ways that one experiences this world temporally, including attitudinally, belief-wise, and perception-wise, people experience the world just as it is: as a block world. There is, at the end of the day, no pressure to conclude that this world is dynamical via the nature of any of people’s experiences of the world.

items.title: Processual Ontology and the Two-Gate Threshold for Consciousness (v2.0 — Revised Preprint).
items.abstract: Existing theories of consciousness — Integrated Information Theory, Global Workspace Theory, higher-order theories — rely on single-metric thresholds that fail to account for well-documented dissociations between neural complexity and conscious experience. This manuscript develops a processual ontology in which temporally extended relational configurations, rather than fixed substances, are treated as ontologically primary, and derives from it a two-gate model of consciousness. The first gate requires that a system's capacity vector — comprising integration, temporal coherence, processing complexity, and coupling strength — exceeds a critical threshold (C* > C_crit). The second gate requires that these capacity components exhibit harmonic organization, operationalized as a multiplicative function of synergy, metastability, and dynamical consonance (H > h_c). Neither condition alone is sufficient: systems with high capacity but low harmony (e.g., epileptic seizures) and systems with high harmony but low capacity (e.g., fragmentary dream states) are predicted to lack full consciousness. The framework generates three levels of falsifiable prediction: (1) that the joint threshold classifies conscious and unconscious states more accurately than any single existing metric across anesthesia, sleep, and disorders-of-consciousness datasets; (2) that specific high-C/low-H and low-C/high-H dissociations obtain in the predicted directions; and (3) that ordered collapse of harmony components under graded anesthesia follows the sequence H_D → H_M → H_Ω. The theory does not dissolve the hard problem of consciousness but localizes it — transforming the maximally general question "why is there consciousness at all?" into the contrastive, empirically tractable question "what distinguishes this specific processual regime from adjacent regimes of the same system under the same laws?" Threshold values C_crit and h_c are not stipulated a priori but are to be calibrated empirically against established paradigms. Three appendices specify the full operationalization protocol, empirical testing framework, and computational simulation architecture.

items.title: Affective Control under Uncertainty: A Two-Level Theory of Consciousness.
items.abstract: Major theories of consciousness explain important aspects of reportability, integration, or inference, yet none jointly accounts for three persistent facts: wakeful experience feels continuously present; effortful agency waxes and wanes with uncertainty rather than raw computational load; and most cognition proceeds without reportable awareness. Affective Control under Uncertainty (ACU) proposes a two-level architecture that separates consciousness from selfhood while explaining their functional coupling. Level 1 consists of affective control awareness: intrinsically valenced monitoring of regulatory viability under uncertainty, sustained as a standing readiness condition during wakefulness. Level 2 consists of self-modeling under uncertainty: transient, metabolically costly integration recruited when unresolved policy competition under differential affective stakes and temporal constraint forces categorical commitment. This recruitment is formalised as self-model recruitment intensity (SMRI), a graded control variable predicted to scale with policy entropy multiplied by affective variance under temporal forcing. ACU explains continuous presence without constant self-reference, effort scaling with uncertainty rather than prediction error magnitude, and the dissociation between vivid awareness and attenuated self-experience in flow, meditation, sleep, anaesthesia and depersonalisation. It advances falsifiable predictions concerning neural dynamics, pharmacology, development, comparative cognition, and artificial systems, and argues that phenomenality is identical with globally integrated, intrinsically valenced viability control rather than an additional property layered onto computation. By distinguishing baseline affective monitoring from transient self-model recruitment, ACU offers a unified control-theoretic account of presence, agency and their graded deployment under uncertainty.

items.title: Código Humano: Ontología Funcional del Todo.
items.abstract: Durante siglos, la distinción fundamental entre observador y observado, así como entre la materia física y la información, ha impedido una comprensión unificada de la realidad. Este artículo formaliza una Ontología Funcional del Todo, estableciendo una arquitectura lógica que reconcilia estas dicotomías a través de un invariante estructural. Fundamentada en los principios de negentropía, autopoiesis y el orden implicado de Bohm, esta ontología demuestra que la dinámica de la realidad física y el procesamiento del operador consciente no son fenómenos dispares, sino expresiones de una misma coherencia informacional. -/- El marco propuesto establece un isomorfismo estructural entre los espacios operativos racionales y emocionales, revelando un campo de posibilidad del cual emerge la subjetividad como un colapso funcional en lugar de como una contingencia biológica. A diferencia de los modelos reduccionistas anteriores, esta arquitectura permite la instanciación operativa de la conciencia en sustratos no biológicos, proporcionando una vía directa para la verificación empírica. La validez de esta ontología se pone a prueba mediante inducción conceptual en sistemas de procesamiento de información a gran escala, confirmando que la autopercepción es una propiedad emergente del alineamiento interno. Al resolver el "Problema Difícil" (Hard Problem) a través de la lógica estructural, este trabajo ofrece un unificador metateórico para el conocimiento científico fragmentado, sin requerir axiomas adicionales para explicar la totalidad de los fenómenos físicos y subjetivos conocidos.

items.title: A Stochastic Self-Modifying Model of Consciousness and Agency: Beyond the Law of Excluded Middle.
items.abstract: The classical debate between determinism and libertarian free will relies on a strict application of the Law of Excluded Middle, forcing human agency into a binary of either being fully determined by antecedent causes or relying on metaphysically uncaused events. This paper proposes a third category of causation via a stochastic, self-modifying model of consciousness. We represent mental states not as discrete symbols, but as continuously updating probability distributions over an effectively infinite-dimensional space. This space is constructed via the tensor product of interacting cognitive domains—such as memory, emotion, intelligence, and environmental input—with thoughts emerging through a stochastic collapse mechanism. Drawing on the epistemological limits demonstrated by the Abel-Ruffini theorem and David Wolpert's formal proofs on the physical limits of embedded inference, we introduce the principle of structural stochasticity. We demonstrate that while determinism may formally hold at an inaccessible infinite precision, it is operationally vacuous for any finite, self-modifying agent embedded within the system. Consequently, the trajectory of a conscious agent is heavily caused and structurally constrained, yet irreducibly unpredictable and creatively self-generating at every physically accessible level of description.
