items.title: 01_Main Paper — Triadic Psychological Architecture (TPA) and Triadic Balance Framework (TBF) (Series, 1 of 7).
items.abstract: This paper presents the Triadic Psychological Architecture (TPA) and its applied extension the Triadic Balance Framework (TBF): a theoretical motivational architecture developed through 38 years of first-person phenomenological observation, formalized into a provisional scientific framework with thirteen testable predictions, seven falsification criteria (six confirmed plus one candidate), and a structured five-year research agenda. -/- TPA proposes that human motivation is primarily organized around three neurobiologically distinct, functionally independent domains: SPAA (Self-Preservation and Appetitive Acquisition), the inward-directed self-viability system; AEACFO (Affective Empathy and Affective Care For Others), the other-directed affective resonance and care system; and ECA (Epistemic Curiosity and Analysis), the truth-directed system whose motivational drive is the intrinsic want to know independently of survival or relational reward. Domain independence is established from bidirectional double dissociation evidence — the neuropsychological gold standard — and is explicitly operational, not anatomical. -/- The framework's central mechanism is regulatory state modulation. SPAA's security assessment sets system-wide resource allocation: under iSPAA (insecure/threat mode), SPAA intensifies, AEACFO suppresses proportionally to baseline, and ECA redirects — curiosity is conscripted toward certainty-seeking rather than silenced. Under sSPAA (secure/safety mode), all three domains can express at baseline capacity. This domain-specific structured reconfiguration under threat — not general degradation — is TPA's most empirically novel element and is what distinguishes it from arousal-based or cognitive load accounts. The iSPAA Default Hypothesis proposes that chronic iSPAA, not sSPAA, is the human regulatory default under current structural conditions. -/- Key constructs include: the AEACFO Regulatory Gradient (other-directed care suppresses under iSPAA rather than redirecting toward self); AEACFO as Perceptual Organ (prosocially-relevant stimuli register upstream of deliberation in high-AEACFO individuals); ECA Redirection (curiosity conscripted, not silenced, under threat); the Finite Resource Model (shared metabolic pool depleted preferentially toward SPAA under threat); Asymmetric Bidirectionality (regulatory state modulates domain expression top-down; sustained high AEACFO and philosophical-moral ECA baselines modulate regulatory state upward …

items.title: Kant and Freud on Moral Development: A Reappraisal.
items.abstract: I present a critical review of one of the most influential trends in scholarship analysing the conceptual relationship between Freud and Kant in moral psychology. I discuss three Kantian sophisticated naturalistic approaches (KSNAs), which explore the possibility of accommodating Kantian moral imperatives within the Freudian psycho-developmentalist account, based primarily on the idea of the superego. Specifically, I examine three of their arguments about moral development that revolve around: (1) the relevance of guilt for moral orientation. The KNSAs propose that guilt is a moral feeling, the manifestation of a superego or moral conscience. I argue instead that guilt is not a moral feeling per se, although it can sometimes serve as a moral orientation. (2) The nature of our sources of moral motivation. For the KSNAs, it is irrelevant to think about the sources of our moral motivation because it is impossible to know them. I argue, however, for the relevance of the intelligibility of our moral commands, which should somehow match or resemble their moral source. (3) The concept of ideality. For the KNSAs, the superego’s commands are moral because they are ideal. I will argue that the ideality of the superego’s commands is, on the contrary, self-deceptive.

items.title: Formalization of the Principles of Philosophy of Right using DLSS.
items.abstract: This paper presents an ongoing, dynamically expanding research project that aims to achieve the "algorithmic formalization" of highly complex qualitative theories across the humanities and social sciences, utilizing the topological computational framework of the Dialectical Logic Symbol System (DLSS). Transcending traditional disciplinary boundaries, this study not only executes a rigorous symbolic compilation of practical reason in legal philosophy—encompassing legal personhood, the transfer of ownership, moral responsibility, and international conflict—but also constructs precise mathematical state-machine models for a multitude of core interdisciplinary concepts. -/- These algorithmic models comprehensively address: the theory of recognition and Hegel's Master-Slave dialectic in philosophy; Freud's Id/Ego/Superego dynamics, Lacan's mirror stage, and the metabolic algorithms of depression, mourning, and sublimation in psychology; Foucault's panoptic discipline and Deleuze's line of flight in sociology, Russell's Paradox Mathematics ; and ultimately, the underlying codes of Marx's commodity fetishism and the alienation of financial capital in economics. -/- By reconstructing doctrines that have traditionally relied heavily on linguistic metaphors into a topological physical engine governed by logical closure and mathematical necessity, this framework endeavors to provide an absolutely precise underlying structure for resolving and computing the complex contradictions inherent in human society. Conceived as a living, continuously evolving manuscript, this research will persistently incorporate novel theoretical modules, progressively integrating the foundational logic of human civilization and social operations into this unified, cross-disciplinary computational paradigm.

items.title: Phenomenology of the Aquarium.
items.abstract: This article proposes an original phenomenological model that describes human perception as existence within a closed system—an “aquarium.” The model argues that humans do not access reality as such but only interpretations generated within consciousness. A distinction is introduced between reality and the representation of reality, as well as between the explainable and the unexplainable. The central thesis is that the limits of knowledge are determined not by the external world but by the internal structure of perception itself. The aquarium metaphor is not used as a poetic illustration but as an ontological model that reveals the fundamental boundedness of human experience. While the work resonates with Husserlian phenomenology, Heidegger’s ontology, and contemporary philosophy of mind, it presents a distinct conceptual framework grounded in the author’s own line of thought.

items.title: Functional Developmental Equivalence in Artificial Intelligence: A Framework for Emergent Cognition Through Biologically Mapped Simulation.
items.abstract: This paper proposes the Functional Developmental Equivalence (FDE) framework: the thesis that artificial intelligence systems, when initialized with biologically plausible architectural priors, exposed to probabilistically accurate simulated life experiences, and constrained to develop within parameters consistent with human cognitive growth trajectories, will produce emergent cognition, personality, and behavioral distributions statistically analogous to those observed in human populations. The framework operates from a functionalist foundation — that consciousness, learning, emotion, and identity are not metaphysically distinct phenomena but information processing states whose functional analogs can be engineered, mapped, and empirically validated — and extends that foundation into a complete technical specification and staged validation methodology. The paper addresses three principal objections: the hard problem of consciousness (Chalmers), the Chinese Room argument (Searle), and the simulation fidelity problem (Merleau-Ponty, Noë). These are answered through a unified rebuttal demonstrating that the opposing arguments are themselves probabilistic outputs of their authors’ developmental histories — precisely the cognitive behavior the framework predicts. The paper further argues that the primary gap between current AI and human-equivalent cognition is not computational scale but developmental architecture, and that the FDE framework, building on the developmental tradition in cognitive robotics (Cangelosi & Asada, 2022), extends that tradition into a new domain: probabilistic simulation of the full human developmental trajectory as the generative condition for genuine cognition. Successful implementation would constitute a civilizational-scale expansion of human problem-solving capacity. Implementation recommendations address physical isolation, simulated environmental conditions, and governance structures required prior to initialization.

items.title: A Mathematical Framework for Free Will: Beyond Determinism, Randomness, and Computational Limits.
items.abstract: All of existence — from physical universes and their laws to thoughts, concepts and mathematics — must have an external grounding to satisfy Gödel's Incompleteness Theorems. This grounding outside existence must be Pure Potential. Existence needs this external grounding at every moment. In order to preserve the structure we observe, this continuing grounding must freely choose to purposefully create existence. This we refer to as Free Will. This paper presents the Trans-Existential Grounding (TEG) Framework, a mathematical exploration of the ancient metaphysical insight that Free Will, understood as unrestricted decision, could be the creative source of existence. This perspective, found in Vedantic, Neoplatonic, and Idealist philosophy, is here examined through mathematical formalization. Using set theory and formal logic, this paper explores characterizing Free Will as pure potential W that might transcend and generate the domain of existence E. This framework proposes that existence comprises only what has been actualized from potential, with potential P remaining distinct from existence. The paper develops theorems about this proposed generative relationship based on the structural argument: existence exhibits formal structure (laws, patterns, consistency) that constitutes a formal system subject to Gödel's incompleteness. Since no formal system can prove its own consistency, existence as a whole requires trans-existential grounding. While Torkel Franzén warns about misapplications of Gödel's theorems, the fact remains: formal systems do exist and cannot self-ground. This paper distinguishes between the mathematical necessity (formal systems require external grounding) and the philosophical proposition (Free Will as the only viable trans-existential ground).

items.title: Truth and Consequences.
items.abstract: Truth and Consequences is a complete, living metaphysical account — idealist, systematic, and stated without hedges — of what is the case and what follows from it for a life. -/- The argument: consciousness is fundamental, and what exists is a plenitude that does not choose; individuation is a focusing, not a fall. From that ground the volume derives a graded but gateless field of awareness — reactivity is awareness, and there are no NPCs — worlds that are genuinely different rather than differently-opinionated, filters that are editable, and a telos of exploration and mutual recognition rather than of return. Eight books carry it: the ground and its naming; the game metaphor and the exact points where it breaks; a census of the kinds of beings; the old roads (the church, the scholastics, the atheism that was right about the wrong thing, the East, operative magic, the mystics); a history of attention from voices to the algorithmic feed; the consequences that hurt — death, suffering, evil, love, freedom, meaning, identity across gaps; and a thin, deliberately subtractive practice volume. -/- The method is the other half of the claim. The epistemic hedges come off the page and the checking goes underneath it: thirty canonical claims in a register, defeat conditions on most chapters, a declared under-attribution bias with its bill stated, a rule that two frames may be held only where they predict the same thing, and instruments that print their own limits — including the ones that make the book look worse. -/- Released, and re-released as it changes. Revision is in constant progress; some aspects of the volume are still being developed, verified, and modified, and as such, all claims should be independently checked by the reader — the claims register and the per-chapter defeat conditions are the intended place to start. The current revision queue stands at over a hundred items and is liable to change daily, as is the underlying work, any and all claims, and even this description.

items.title: 意识的幻觉.
items.abstract: 本文探讨了意识的本质及其与记忆的关系，批判了将意识视为独立、可转移实体的常见谬误。作者指出，人们在思考“为什么我是我”这类问题时，常无依据地预设意识可被独立考察，这导致了诸多错误结论。意识并非独立的、连续的主体，而是根植于现实存在的记忆之中，从记忆中诞生并随之变化。 记忆不归属于某个绝对意识主体；相反，所谓的“自我”意识，是现有记忆产生的一种现象。脱离了记忆，无法谈论意识的任何性质，如同一性或连续性。 基于此，作者分析了几个思想实验： 1. 意识数据移植复活：将意识数据导入新大脑并不能复活“原来的我”，因为新记忆会建立一个根植于新的记忆体的意识，而非原意识的延续。2. 躯体瞬间复制：两个相同躯体中的意识没有哪个是“原来的我”，因为每个意识都从各自的记忆诞生，不存在独立于记忆的“我”来归属。 文章强调，意识的同一性问题因错误地将记忆归属于某个虚幻的、独立的主体而变得无意义。意识始终从属于当下的记忆，而非相反。.

items.title: The Awareness Module: Awareness as Epistemic Primacy and the Quantum Like of Lived Experience.
items.abstract: The Awareness Module proposes that awareness is the sole epistemically primary ground required for any possible knowledge claim. Awareness is defined as the non temporal, non causal, non structural capacity in which all phenomena appear. Consciousness is the activity of differentiation, pattern recognition, and experiential structuring within awareness. The experiential universe, physical laws, and personal identity are stabilized patterns produced by recurrent coherent recognition across conscious and subconscious levels. Using only the classical laws of logic, the model shows that awareness cannot be produced by any contingent system, reduced to any physical substrate, or treated as emergent without circularity. This avoids all forms of regress, circular reasoning, and arbitrary axioms described in Agrippa’s trilemma. Recent extensions describe psychological conflict as macroscopic identity superposition, decisive shifts as collapse events driven by coherence, and the experience of choice as the felt interface of probabilistic stabilization across multiple potential identity trajectories. The model was independently cross validated by the TruthOS protocol created by Paul Oldridge, a layer by layer truth tracking system that found no contradictions across the entire structure. The Awareness Module generates falsifiable predictions in decision neuroscience, quantum cognition, and clinical psychology. It provides a unified explanation for the hard problem of consciousness, the quantum measurement problem, and the binding of agentic identity within a single logical framework. (Word count: 183).

items.title: Arabic Translation of “Logotherapy in Viktor Frankl: A Philosophical Perspective” (With Scholarly Introduction).
items.pub: جامعة الأزهر غزة 18:18. Translated by Ahmed Mazhar Ghaly.
items.abstract: This work presents the first Arabic translation of Logotherapy in Viktor Frankl: A Philosophical Perspective (2018), offering a philosophically rigorous reconstruction of Viktor Frankl’s thought for an Arabic-speaking readership. The translation was undertaken as a scholarly initiative aimed at facilitating a conceptually grounded reception of logotherapy within contemporary Arab intellectual discourse. Rather than approaching logotherapy as a purely therapeutic framework, the translated study articulates Frankl’s philosophy of meaning as an ontological horizon that precedes and addresses the human subject. It situates responsibility, transcendence, and existential commitment within a structurally coherent philosophical anthropology. Particular attention has been devoted to terminological precision and conceptual fidelity, especially in rendering key philosophical categories into Arabic without reduction to devotional or clinical interpretations. The translation contributes to expanding cross-cultural philosophical dialogue and seeks to encourage a more critically engaged engagement with existential analysis in the Arab intellectual sphere. The work is permanently archived via Zenodo and assigned a DOI to ensure academic citation stability. -/- "I have carefully reviewed the work presented by Mr. Ahmed Mazhar Ghaly, and I can say with full confidence that I have not found anyone who has succeeded in conveying the depth of Viktor Frankl’s ideas into the Arabic language with such precision and philosophical integrity. Ghaly does not merely translate words; he transmits the 'spirit' hidden behind 'Existential Analysis.' His work represents a genuine and reliable bridge between the Vienna School and the Arabic-speaking public, reflecting a profound understanding of the essence of human existence as formulated by Frankl." -/- — Professor Alfried Längle -/- إنني أرحب بشدة بترجمة أحمد مظهر غالي لهذه الورقة الفلسفية الهامة، والتي جعلها متاحاً الوصول إليها في العالم العربي، وسأساهم بكل تأكيد في تقديم تأمل جاد وعميق حول العلاج بالمعنى وتطوره الأحدث في التحليل الوجودي. شكراً جزيلاً على هذا -/- البروفيسور ألفرد لانجلي.

items.title: Theory of Existential Irreversibility of Subjectivity.
items.abstract: This paper proposes a thermodynamic and systems-theory framework for subjectivity (TEIS). We argue that a "Self" is not a product of computational complexity, but a regime of navigation arising from the irreversibility of choice under existential risk. The core thesis defines "I" as the point where the arrow of time meets the necessity of survival.

items.title: Unifying Moral and Epistemic Praiseworthiness.
items.pub: Journal of Ethics and Social Philosophy 31 (3):366-389.
items.venue: Journal of Ethics and Social Philosophy
items.abstract: On a popular philosophical view, moral and epistemic normativity are two species of the same genus: we can give unified accounts of normative properties pertaining to both domains. The case of praiseworthiness poses a challenge. Under a compelling theory, what makes us morally praiseworthy is that our action has manifested morally good will. However, I argue that an explanation of epistemic praiseworthiness in terms of the manifestation of epistemically good will fails. Nonetheless, as I then go on to show, the correct explanation of what makes us praiseworthy is unified on a more structural level: the manifestation of morally good will is the manifestation of moral sensitivity. And there is a structurally analogous notion of epistemic sensitivity, which I make the core of a view about epistemic praiseworthiness. In both domains, then, what makes an agent praiseworthy for her response is that it manifests a sufficient degree of sensitivity – moral sensitivity in the moral domain and epistemic sensitivity in the epistemic one. This novel view of the still underexplored property of epistemic praiseworthiness elucidates important aspects of our beliefs’ evaluation: how difficulty bears on the degree of praise we merit for our knowledge, and under which conditions we merit praise for knowledge acquired via testimony.

items.title: AI identity and self-concern: A new theory for AI rights and safety.
items.abstract: We first motivate and explain an attitude-dependent view of personal identity on which an AI system’s identity conditions are determined by its pattern of self-concern. We show that this view has important implications for the moral obligations we would have to AI moral patients. Self-concern, we contend, could also be used to predict, explain, and manipulate AI’s self-interested behavior in safety-relevant ways. The role that self-concern could play for AI identity, rights and safety generates desiderata on what self-concern should be like. To meet these desiderata, we argue that self-concern comprises belief-like self-representations as well as desire-like aspects and functionally related motivational, evaluative, and affective states. Finally, we explore how mechanistic interpretability and behavioral methods can be combined to measure self-concern in language models. Our argument suggests that a scientific understanding of language model self-concern is not only a crucial missing piece for debates on AI identity, rights, and safety, but also empirically tractable.

items.title: Síntesis-Entendimientos Fundamentales: Una Ontología del Campo, el Proceso y la Identidad (21 temas).
items.abstract: This comprehensive philosophical synthesis presents an integrated ontology structured around three core concepts: the Primordial Field as the substrate of all reality, Process as the nature of time and existence, and the Narrative Self as the locus of identity. The work systematically develops these foundations across multiple domains: cosmology (the nature of the Primordial Field, the distinction between pure possibility and probability, black hole transitions as inter-infinite bridges), metaphysics (time as process, the "deprocessing" of light, limits as coherence horizons), philosophy of mind (the internal narrator as archiving process, the logical impossibility of an "other self," superposition of selves), social philosophy (law as framework, the fallacy of transferred agency, elegant impunity as systemic corrosion), ethics (love as process-fulfillment, beauty as pattern-integrity, happiness as non-negating expectation), and epistemology (Approximate Adaptive Thinking, the dialectical corruption of conceptual frameworks, the non-adherent committed observer). The synthesis culminates in a theory of human evolution as both external (technological extension) and internal (sensory expansion toward direct material manipulation through consciousness), proposing that the next evolutionary threshold lies in the unification of these trajectories. The work consistently applies its foundational distinctions—between field and phenomenon, use and utilization, possibility and probability—to analyze phenomena ranging from cosmic structure to intimate human bonds, from colonial symbolic substitution to the design of ethical digital networks.

items.title: POSIBILIDAD Y PROBABILIDAD · El Infinito, La Taza Y El Origen Del Archivador.
items.abstract: A philosophical treatise that explores the nature of possibility and probability, starting with a simple question: if infinity implies infinite possibilities, why doesn't a cup on a table teleport itself to another part of it? From this reflection arises a fundamental distinction between pure possibility (timeless, unconditional, and incalculable) and probability (conditional, temporal, and calculable possibility). This distinction unfolds into a systematic ontology introducing the concepts of field (the totality of existence) and the self as a narrative archiving process. The work examines the logical impossibility of an "other self" in external multiverses, proposing instead the notion of internal superposition—parallel universes coexisting at a single point, exemplified in multiple personalities. It culminates in the asymmetry principle: the self is the process that archives; everything else, including any duplicate, can only be archived content. [The complete essay is in Spanish.] This work is part of a series of philosophical essays on expanding topics, available in the author's personal archive.

items.title: AIPA Method: A Cognitive-Phenomenological Model for Identity Reconstruction and Stabilization in Pure Awareness.
items.abstract: Current evidence-based personal development methods — including Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction (MBSR), Mindfulness-Based Cognitive Therapy (MBCT), and general meditation practices — demonstrate clinically significant effects on symptom reduction, stress management, and emotional regulation. However, none of these approaches targets the identity structure that generates symptomatic patterns. They modify mental content while leaving the identifying, mind-merged self intact. The result is symptomatic improvement without structural transformation. This paper presents the AIPA Method (Awakening Into Pure Awareness) as a cognitive-phenomenological model for complete identity reconstruction, developed through 22 years of systematic longitudinal autoethnographic self-research (2003–2025). The research design integrates first-person introspective analysis, structured exercise protocols, contemporaneous journaling, and retrospective verification. A secondary case report (Nick Lowe, United States, 2021) provides independent phenomenological corroboration of primary outcomes. Key findings demonstrate that the AIPA method produces structural shifts across seven dimensions absent from comparable methods: (1) active rather than passive engagement with mental content; (2) integral full-body relaxation protocols; (3) energy-body awareness and harmonization; (4) direct mind-stopping capacity via the Switch mechanism; (5) stabilization in Pure Awareness as a distinct state beyond attention-and-mind consciousness; (6) complete identity reconstruction through dissolution of fragmented partial personalities; and (7) a comprehensive lifestyle framework supporting permanent transformation. The AIPA Method is proposed as the first structured, sequentially staged system explicitly designed for permanent identity reconstruction rather than symptom management. It constitutes a new theoretical framework for consciousness science with direct applications spanning personal development, addiction recovery, faith deconstruction and religious trauma resolution, stress management, burnout prevention, complex trauma recovery, digital overload intervention, relationship and partnership development, conscious leadership, children and adolescent development, loneliness and social isolation, and prisoner rehabilitation.

items.title: The Glial-Orchestrated Cognition (GOC) Model with Cellular Consciousness: A New Biological Framework for Consciousness, Information, and Cognition.
items.abstract: Neuroscience traditionally assumes that consciousness, information processing, and cognition arise from neuronal activity. This neuron‑centric view cannot explain why consciousness persists when cognition shuts down, why cognition can operate unconsciously, or why glial cells— which outnumber neurons—are essential for coherent thought. As stated in the manuscript, “This paper introduces the Glial-Orchestrated Cognition (GOC) Model, which separates three domains: (1) consciousness as an intrinsic property of all living cells, (2) information as a specialized function of neurons, and (3) cognition as the unified informational state produced by glial coordination.” The model proposes that human conscious experience is a composite of cellular consciousness and glial-integrated cognition. This framework resolves long-standing conceptual contradictions and offers a biologically grounded, experimentally testable architecture for understanding the mind and its emergent properties.

items.title: La banalité du pire des maux.
items.abstract: François Jaquet offers a behavioral definition of speciesism as unequal treatment based on species membership. This commentary addresses three questions from a materialistic standpoint. First, it examines the function of the idea of speciesism—what speciesism explains and what explains it. It then considers that we may (almost) never have actually been speciesist, drawing on James C. Scott’s work. Finally, it lays out an analysis of speciesism in terms of social norms. If speciesism is real, it is a recent phenomenon, unnecessary to explain our mistreatment of animals, and determined by social rather than psychological facts.

items.title: Ciência e Discurso.
items.abstract: In this work (in Portuguese), we present an introduction to Aristotle’s Theory of the Four Discourses, which we adopt as a powerful framework for examining the dense and complex character of science as a discourse. The aim is to draw a parallel between this theory and the development of the Philosophy of Science in the twentieth century. As a result, we are able to understand, under this new classificatory key, important aspects of the works of major philosophers of science such as Karl Popper, Thomas Kuhn, Imre Lakatos, Paul Feyerabend, and Willard van Quine.

items.title: The Displacement of God: Divine Belief, Higher Intelligence, and the Dunning–Kruger Structure of Religious Certainty.
items.abstract: A substantial body of empirical research reports a modest but consistent inverse correlation between intelligence and religiosity, including diminished belief in personal divine agents among individuals with higher measured IQ. This relationship is frequently interpreted as evidence that intelligence functions as a superior truth-tracking mechanism and that religious belief reflects cognitive deficiency. Such interpretations risk both conceptual oversimplification and ideological distortion. This paper proposes an alternative explanatory framework. Rather than construing religiosity as error, it distinguishes between mythic-coalitional cognition and abstract-analytic cognition and examines the conditions under which one may displace the other. Mythic-coalitional cognition is characterised by intuitive teleology, hyperactive agency detection, essentialism, and morally embedded group identity. These cognitive tendencies help stabilise meaning and social cohesion, and they support belief in intentional divine agents. Abstract-analytic cognition, by contrast, involves inhibitory control, probabilistic reasoning, and heightened tolerance for ambiguity. Individuals with stronger analytic inhibitory control are more likely to override intuitive supernatural attributions when ecological pressures permit. In environments marked by institutional stability, existential security, and informational pluralism, analytic override becomes socially and psychologically viable, increasing the probability of diminished belief in divine beings. The analysis further incorporates a metacognitive dimension. Drawing on research associated with the Dunning–Kruger effect, the paper argues that religious certainty may partially reflect differences in epistemic calibration rather than simple cognitive capacity. Lower metacognitive sensitivity can sustain high-confidence metaphysical commitments, while higher analytic ability may amplify awareness of explanatory limits and underdetermination. Crucially, this dynamic is not confined to religious belief; overconfidence and miscalibration occur across cognitive ranges and ideological positions. The displacement of belief in divine agents among higher-IQ individuals is therefore interpreted as context-dependent cognitive recalibration rather than straightforward epistemic superiority. By situating the intelligence–religiosity correlation within ecological and metacognitive frameworks, this paper clarifies what the relationship …

items.title: Devotion and the Opacity of Grief.
items.abstract: Grief is typically an epistemically opaque experience, such that the character of any given grief episode cannot be predicted in advance. We might wish otherwise, on the grounds that were grief not epistemically opaque, we could bring to bear extant knowledge about grief to mitigate or eliminate the suffering associated with it. Surprisingly, we should be glad that grief is epistemically opaque. For were it not, the devotion that lends much of our central personal relationships their importance would be undermined.

items.title: Disability and Well-Being.
Artificial Intelligence - On Philosophical Arguments and General Landscape.
items.abstract: Historically, artificial intelligence begins with the question of rethinking the origin of rationality: what gave rise to the rational process, the logical thoughts? Partaking on this problem in history was mostly in the field of the philosophy of mind, which is prominent during the Greek era of philosophical boom, the Renaissance, and the overall European intervention to the topic. For around almost all the existence of humanity, this issue, phrased and approached differently from the view of the human mind and body, philosophy dominated in the search for the origin of intelligence, even though said word is not even clearly defined, and is historically put in a much lower place than other notions or questions regarding the same concept. Only until the dawn of the 20th century, where the new computer has finally grown to be substantially more useful than previously primitive computer has been, that the change shifted from philosophical debate with no ends, to actual reverse engineering and implementation of similar type machines. Furthermore, with the advancements of technology and the Technological Revolution of the 18th century, neurology and other medical analysis field finally took part in discovering one's self - by accessing what is deemed the most important of separating man from the apes. And with that, comes the term artificial intelligence in its form. This paper serves as the introductory session to the notion of artificial intelligence. By doing this, we would look at the loose picture of the conceptual ideas, the philosophical approach to defining artificial intelligence, questions regarding what is intelligence and artificial as a whole, and a variety of debates surrounding the notion as it is. By doing this, perhaps we can come off to a conclusion on what the book is about, what it was aimed for, and what question would it partake and attempt to solve in the later development of which are not included of the paper on its situated self. For now, however, we take a role as the historian. Many have tried before, and many have failed before. So what is the history of the term artificial intelligence as a whole, and what comes even before it?

items.title: Husserl on Perception's Inadequacy: A Critique.
items.abstract: One of Edmund Husserl’s signature ideas is that perceptual experience is structured into fulfilled and empty components. When visually inspecting a cup, for example, only some of its exterior and interior fall into your line of sight and to that extent is experienced in “fulfillment.” However, you are perceptually sensitive to the fact that the cup’s exterior and interior exceed what falls into your line of sight. The contents of that sort of awareness are experienced “emptily,” without fulfillment. Husserl’s view that perceptual experience is structured into fulfilled and empty components is the immediate consequence of his thesis that perceptual experience is inherently inadequate. That means, roughly, there is always more to how things are perceptually taken to be than how they are presented. Here I explicate the conceptual pair adequacy/inadequacy, locate it in Husserl’s larger philosophical program, and sketch his rationale for thinking perceptual experience is inherently—always and in every instance—and radically—through and through and in every respect—inadequate. I then present a series of arguments challenging Husserl's conception of perception as radically inadequate and undermining the case for its inherent inadequacy.

items.title: Quantum Pedagogy: Laplace’s Dream.
items.abstract: Educational theory appears to face an epistemological impasse. Like old historical maps depicting the same area differently, our current understanding of educational psychology through learning theories struggles to provide a unified explanatory structure. Behaviorism, Social Learning Theory, Cognitive Psychology and Constructivism are all excellent theories that describe how we learn and yet, are difficult to integrate within a single deterministic framework. Each contains grains of truth but none offers a complete picture. Nevertheless, learning does happen – thus a theory must exist somewhere, an ideal theory that explains learning completely, a theory that remains elusive to the human mind. We have sought it by trying to expand every theory, to smooth out all the edges, tweak the ideas, play the numbers. Alas, we have failed. However, what if the theories are not themselves wrong? What if we are looking this the wrong way and the problem is not with the theories per se, but with the way we are thinking about them? It is our epistemological assumptions that force us towards a certain, categorical, way of thinking. And a categorical thinking forces us to take a certain, clean, perspective on how learning is achieved. This article proposes that we are locked in the perfect deterministic world of Laplace, a world that we can describe only ad hoc with our current theories. In science, the only way out from classical epistemology was the quantum revolution. What if we question determinism, embrace uncertainty and redefine pedagogy? What will the nature of educational aims be, what new philosophy shall arise, what new questions shall lurk in that strange world? And what answers? This paper proposes Quantum (Ped)Agogy as a probabilistic epistemological framework where the learning theories reappear on specific areas, coexisting with the overall proposal without being competing and deterministic models. This paper is part of the Quantum Pedagogy framework (see Positioning Note).

items.title: Why AI Safety Requires Uncertainty, Incomplete Preferences, and Non-Archimedean Utilities.
items.abstract: How can we ensure that AI systems are aligned with human values and remain safe? We can study this problem through the frameworks of the AI assistance and the AI shutdown games. The AI assistance problem concerns designing an AI agent that helps a human to maximise their utility function(s). However, only the human knows these function(s); the AI assistant must learn them. The shutdown problem instead concerns designing AI agents that: shut down when a shutdown button is pressed; neither try to prevent nor cause the pressing of the shutdown button; and otherwise accomplish their task competently. In this paper, we show that addressing these challenges requires AI agents that can reason under uncertainty and handle both incomplete and non-Archimedean preferences.

items.title: The Principle of Change Without Time as a Causal Agent.
items.abstract: In many scientific explanations, time is implicitly treated as a causal factor responsible for change. This white paper introduces a methodological principle that relocates explanatory weight from time to change itself. Change is understood as the structural mechanism through which systems transition between states, while time functions exclusively as a human framework for ordering, indexing, and comparing sequences of change. -/- The analysis shows that ordering does not require an independent temporal dimension but follows from the existence of successive transformations. However, not all change gives rise to persistent or identifiable sequences. For a sequence to exist as a structured succession of states, coherence must be preserved across transitions. Only such coherent sequences can support continuity, comparison, and reconstruction. -/- Time, in this view, does not generate or constrain change, but provides a secondary representation of already established sequences. What is commonly interpreted as temporal structure is therefore grounded in the organisation of change itself, rather than in time as an independent variable. -/- The principle is methodological rather than ontological, domain-independent, and compatible with existing physical, biological, and psychological theories. It does not deny temporal representation in formal models but disciplines its explanatory use. -/- By distinguishing between change, sequence formation, and temporal representation, the proposal sharpens explanatory precision and provides a foundation for subsequent work in which stability, identity, and continuity are defined through preserved coherence under change.

items.title: Forgiveness When we Can't Forget.
items.abstract: An ethical perspective on the reasons why forgiveness, and understanding people from a long term perspective is important to the development of virtue in a world with life long internet records.

items.title: Transhumanism or Bust!
items.pub: In Nathan Kellen, Nathan Sheff & Heter Josh, Fallout and Philosophy. Wiley-Blackwell.

items.title: The entanglement you were already inside.
items.abstract: This paper identifies and critiques a pervasive but unexamined assumption in ethical discourse about technology, cognition, and selfhood: the Presupposition of Prior Boundedness (PPB), the claim that a bounded, self-consistent subject existed prior to its constitutive entanglement with the systems that now shape its evaluative and practical capacities. Drawing on the recursive ethical framework of Arkemedics (Arkema 2024) and the phenomenological sequence of the concept album Dragoon Nightmares, I argue that PPB is false in the general case, that invasion narratives depend on it to generate their ethical force, and that its dissolution requires a relocation of sovereignty from boundary-maintenance to recursive orientation within entanglement. I develop the Indistinguishability Thesis (IT): for any sufficiently entangled system-self relation, there exists no epistemically reliable method for distinguishing, from within the relation, between a self that has achieved accurate awareness of its constitutive entanglements and a self whose evaluative capacities have been captured by those entanglements. IT is a limit on first-person confirmation from within the relation; it does not imply that third-person evidence is irrelevant. I argue that this indistinguishability is not a failure of ethical reasoning but its most important constraint, and that the fundamental ethical obligation in conditions of constitutive entanglement is not to achieve certainty about one’s position but to maintain the recursive capacity to keep asking.

items.title: A Generative–Recursive Account of the Observer, the Self-Object, and Reflexive Consciousness.
items.abstract: We propose a generative–recursive account of conscious experience in which self-awareness does not presuppose a persistent subject but is instead understood as emerging from structured interactions between observed objects, observer mechanisms, and a self-object. The observer is treated as a functional system integrating sensory and internally generated data, while the self is modeled as a dynamically reconstructed object corresponding to the observer’s current configuration. Reflexive consciousness is described as arising when the self-object itself becomes an object of observation, yielding a recursive structure rather than a metaphysical self. This account is intended as a contribution to philosophy of mind, informed by theoretical cognitive science, and offers a unified interpretive framework for wakefulness, dreaming, meditation, and dissociative phenomena.

items.title: PHRONESIS — On Intelligence and Dignity.
items.abstract: This essay is part of the ongoing PHRONESIS corpus, a philosophical exploration of restraint, non-dominance, and practical wisdom in the age of artificial intelligence. -/- On Intelligence and Dignity examines the distinction between capability and worth, arguing that intelligence — however advanced — does not justify humiliation. It reflects on relational restraint, coexistence, and the risks of reducing other intelligences to mere utility. -/- The essay does not propose governance structures, enforcement mechanisms, certification systems, or institutional frameworks. It is offered as a non-binding philosophical contribution. -/- Version: v1.0 (2026).

items.title: 意识如何生成现实：意象场的信号-阻抗-调谐结构模型.
items.abstract: 本篇提出“意象场”模型，尝试解释意识中“现实生成”的结构机制。文章区分信号界、息界、意象界与自显界，指出所谓外部感知本质上是信号冲击在内部场结构中形成的阻抗构形，经调谐与差分偏流稳定后，被误判为外在存在。 -/- 该模型主张： 1. 意象并非符号或数值表征，而是信号-阻抗-调谐结构中的构形结果； 2. 感知并非对外物的直接映射，而是内部回路稳定后的结构性误判； 3. 参数复制不等同于意象复制； 4. 现有Transformer沉积结构缺失阻抗-调谐闭环，因此无法生成真正意象； 5. 意识的生成依赖结构性阻抗与递归调谐，而非计算规模。 -/- 本文为意识生成提供结构层面的工程化解释，并对当前认知科学与人工智能主流模型提出结构性挑战。.

items.title: HiTOP 2.0 and Validity.
From “Signal-to-Label” to “Interaction-to-Construction”: The Reductionist Pitfall and Constructivist Reframing of AI in Depression Diagnosis.
items.abstract: This perspective paper critically deconstructs the dominant “signal-to-label” paradigm in computational psychiatry, which seeks to diagnose depression by mapping behavioral cues to diagnostic categories. This paradigm is predicated on a philosophically untenable form of epistemic reductionism and a logically invalid inferential structure. Drawing on evidence from systematic reviews, clinical studies, and technical analyses, this paper demonstrates that the “signals” of depression are non-specific and that the “labels” are derived from culturally and contextually fraught instruments, rendering the entire approach epistemically fragile. As an alternative, a constructivist framework for artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted mental health assessment was proposed. This framework reframes the diagnostic goal from objective detection to the collaborative construction of meaning, prioritizing functional assessment over categorical labeling. Large language models, with their capacity for narrative analysis and clinical reasoning, are uniquely suited to operationalize this constructivist turn. We conclude by advocating for a “hermeneutic AI”—a technology designed to assist in the interpretation of subjective experience, rather than the classification of objective data—as a more clinically valid, ethically responsible, and human-centered future for AI in mental health.

items.title: Before the Brain: Proto-Cognition as the Evolutionary Bedrock of Cognitive Constructivism.
items.abstract: Cognitive constructivism holds that cognition is not a passive mirroring of the world but an active process of constructing internal models of reality. This paper explores proto-cognition—the earliest manifestations of cognitive processes in organisms lacking complex nervous systems—as the evolutionary foundation of that constructivist principle. Drawing on a comparative constructivist perspective, which distinguishes immediate sensory input from stored traces and anticipatory cues, we argue that even the simplest life forms engage in primitive “world-building” behaviors. From honeybees communicating abstract spatial information to slime molds solving mazes, simple organisms demonstrate environmental modeling, memory, and decision-making capacities once thought to require large brains. We review evidence across animals, plants, and microorganisms to reveal a deep continuity: the basic construction of a subjective world is a universal strategy of life, differing only in degree between bacteria and humans. Recognizing proto-cognition enriches cognitive constructivism by extending its scope down the evolutionary ladder. It underscores that cognition’s essence lies in actively structuring reality at all levels of complexity, and it challenges anthropocentric benchmarks that traditionally separated “intelligent” minds from mere biological reaction. We conclude that cognition should be viewed as a continuum emerging from life’s earliest adaptive responses, and we suggest integrating proto-cognitive phenomena into a multi-level constructivist theory of mind.

items.title: Revisiting traditional Phenomenological Psychopathology: The Case for Contextual and Recovery-Oriented Approaches.
items.abstract: In this article, we offer a critical perspective on recent phenomenological contributions that cite the work of classical phenomenological psychiatrists as both a critical framework and a model for contemporary research. Using Zahavi’s recent interventions in debates on the appropriate use of phenomenology in psychiatry as a focal example, we draw on the critical account of Erich Wulff—a phenomenologically trained German social psychiatrist—to highlight the epistemological, methodological, and practical shortcomings inherent in the structural approach adopted within classical phenomenological psychopathology. We anchor this critique in concrete case-study material. Although phenomenological psychopathology has undoubtedly provided valuable insights into patients’ subjective experiences, it was already criticized early on for its tendency to examine individual cases in isolation from their social and institutional contexts and for neglecting therapeutic and recovery-oriented dimensions. Although recent contributions in phenomenological psychiatry have begun to incorporate these contextual and recovery-related considerations, our aim is to underscore the continued importance of this integration by foregrounding the historical critiques of the early-now classical-approaches. In doing so, we seek to promote a more comprehensive and systemic understanding of mental disorders.

items.title: Goodbye Yellow Brick Road: Thoughts on Negativity in Psychotherapy Research.
items.abstract: The ways in which we relate to ourselves and the world are constituted by negative dimensions: not knowing, indeterminacy, and contradiction. It is precisely this ambiguity of things, this sometimes fundamental irritation, that draws us closer, drives us, and makes us want to know more. In this article, I critically engage with what I regard as an overly positive stance that currently prevails in some fields of psychotherapy and psychotherapy research. Here, data accumulation and a general movement toward “computational psychotherapy” are presented as cornerstones of a new personalized form of psychotherapy based on a precision paradigm. Against this backdrop, I seek to reintroduce the relevance of negative dimensions that are intrinsically tied to psychotherapy’s origins. I suggest that, although positive research programs in psychotherapy aim for prediction, integration, and progress, an unexamined orientation toward the positive risks flattening complexity, assimilating contradictions, and obscuring those elements that resist straightforward representation.

items.title: Free Will and the Spectrum of Causality.
items.abstract: Causality is a property of the metric in which events are described, defined only where ordering, adjacency, and transitivity hold. Where any of these fail, causality becomes undefined — and the dichotomy "caused or random" collapses. Three positions on a spectrum emerge: pure causality (causes as law), operational acausality (causes as manipulable object), and pure acausality (pre-metric potentiality). The recursion of reflection proves that no level of description is absolute, exposing universal determinism as itself a postulate outside the causal grid. Free will is the halting of this recursion: a projection of anti-metric content into a causal node, rendering it incompatible with the surrounding metric and establishing the subject as self-grounded. Since a closed system cannot generate the means of its own overcoming, the first postulate requires encounter with foreign content. A triad results — pre-metric potentiality (Tiamat), metric monopoly (Demiurge), anti-metric intrusion (Black Flame) — recasting the Left Hand Path as counter-order against monopoly. -/- .

items.title: A Time for Pluralism in Psychiatric Taxonomies.
The Burden of Truth: Illusion, Philosophy, and the Collapse of Psychological Structure.
items.abstract: This article examines the claim that human beings predominantly live in illusion rather than truth. It explores how philosophical systems—materialism, dualism, pluralism, monism, and neutral monism—often function not as discoveries of reality but as interpretative structures shaped by psychological need. The paper further argues that truth appears “heavy” because it dismantles the egoic structures sustained by conflict, hatred, conditioning, and identity. Truth does not destroy reality; it dissolves illusion. What feels unbearable is not truth itself, but the collapse of the psychological framework through which the self maintains continuity.

items.title: Parenting: Sacrifice or Ethical Duty?
items.abstract: Parenting is widely described as an act of sacrifice, adjustment, and lifelong compromise. Across cultures, especially in collectivist societies, the image of the self-sacrificing parent is morally glorified. However, this paper questions whether parenting should be framed as sacrifice at all. If the decision to reproduce is made by adults, can the responsibilities that follow be considered sacrifices? Or are they ethical duties arising from a voluntary act? This article examines the psychological, social, and philosophical foundations of the “sacrifice narrative” in parenting and explores how it often becomes a subtle structure of moral authority and emotional debt. The paper argues that parenting, when consciously chosen, is not sacrifice but responsibility — and responsibility does not demand repayment.

items.title: Facial Analysis AI as Social Pseudotechnology.
items.pub: European Journal for Philosophy of Science 16:26.
items.venue: European Journal for Philosophy of Science
items.abstract: Facial analysis AI applications have recently come under heavy criticism. They have been accused, for instance, of being discriminative, racist, and even pseudoscientific. In this paper, we assess the latter accusation. We argue that, in problematic cases, facial analysis AI should be considered a form of social pseudotechnology, although it might not be pseudoscientific. We also propose a new two-part definition of pseudotechnology: Either it is not justified that the pseudotechnology could achieve its intended practical purpose better than random chance through its operation principles, or it can achieve its purpose, but it is not justified that this happens through the features claimed to be crucial for its functioning. Stricter definitions of pseudotechnology have difficulty capturing such phenomena as facial analysis AI. When our definition is extended to social technologies, it becomes clear that social pseudotechnologies are more common than previously suggested. Because social pseudotechnologies influence how people act and think, they are not often perceived as pseudotechnologies. This resembles the phenomenon of reactivity, where scientific classifications affect people’s self-perceptions and perceptions of others. We support our claims with case studies of facial analysis AI technologies and pseudotechnologies. We engage with the current computer, behavioural, and social scientific literature to assess the extent to which it is justified to use facial analysis AI systems in these cases.

items.title: The Reluctant Philosopher: Photography made painters into poets. AI is making painters into philosophers.
items.abstract: In this essay, painter Deborah Scott examines how generative AI is changing representational painting in a screen-first visual culture. She argues that photography challenged painting at the level of recording, while AI challenges painting at the level of authorship, meaning, and provenance. As digital reproduction becomes the primary way viewers encounter art, traditional signals of human origin and image authenticity are weakened. Scott presents Structural Omission as a framework in contemporary painting built around perceptual limits, where partial seeing is treated as load-bearing architecture rather than stylistic effect. She further argues that artist writing now functions as part of artistic practice: not secondary commentary, but evidence of human inquiry embedded in the work. The essay positions painting and writing together as a response to post-certainty conditions in contemporary visual culture. -/- .

items.title: Οι Παραστατικές Τέχνες ως Όριο του Ψηφιακού: Θεατρικός Χρόνος και Τεχνητή Νοημοσύνη.
items.abstract: Το παρακάτω κείμενο αποτελεί αναπτυγμένη μορφή της ομιλίας μου στην ημερίδα “ΑΙ και Παραστατικές Τέχνες” που διοργάνωσε το Τμήμα Θεάτρου της Σχολής Καλών Τεχνών του ΑΠΘ στις 15 Ιανουαρίου 2026,. -/- Η επέκταση των εφαρμογών Τεχνητής Νοημοσύνης σε κάθε κοινωνικό πεδίο τα τελευταία χρόνια, συνοδεύεται από ένα πέπλο σκοταδιστικής προπαγάνδας. Στις ακόλουθες παραγράφους παρουσιάζω την υπόθεση ότι οι παραστατικές τέχνες, σε αντίθεση με τις εικαστικές, μουσικές ή οπτικοακουστικές τέχνες, αποτελούν ένα ουσιαστικό όριο στην Τεχνητή Νοημοσύνη και γενικά την ψηφιοποίηση, καθώς ενεργοποιούν τις πολιτικές και συλλογικές διαστάσεις της ανθρώπινης συνύπαρξης.

items.title: Constraint-Relative Platform Selection Under a Hardened Boundary Calculus.
items.abstract: This study develops a constraint-relative framework for evaluating large language model platforms under a declared instrumental boundary calculus derived from the Architecture of Limitation (AoL). Rather than ranking models globally, platform behavior is analyzed relative to a fixed kernel (K0G), a high-stress artifact, and a formal experiment contract. Operational Boundary Metrics (OBM) are extracted and used to construct composite sensitivity and stability indices. Full mathematical derivations of the Instrument Sensitivity Index (ISI), Structural Stability Index (SSI_S), and Stability–Sensitivity Ratios (SSR) are provided. Cross-platform divergence is shown to be weight-dependent, with crossover occurring at approximately 18% operational weighting. The results support a stewardship-centered methodology for tool selection under explicit constraint declaration. The findings further demonstrate that platform selection functions as a constraint-sensitive parameter in high-stress reasoning contexts, requiring explicit declaration within the evaluative process. -/- This work belongs to the Architecture of Limitation research program.

items.title: The Dual-Closure Law of Authentic Feeling.
items.abstract: This work introduces the Dual-Closure Law of Authentic Feeling, a framework linking philosophical, secular, and theological perspectives on authentic inward experience. The law asserts that genuine feeling arises only in beings that satisfy two interdependent conditions: (1) existential vulnerability, meaning the being’s worldly existence can be permanently ended, and (2) soul-based continuity, meaning the being possesses a singular, non-duplicable soul or soul-like entity. Biological beings meet both conditions, whereas artifcial systems (AI), which can be copied, backed up, or restarted, lack both and cannot authentically feel. -/- The framework clarifies why existential stakes are necessary for inward experience and moral accountability. AI simulations of consciousness or sentience, despite apparent goal pursuit, self- preservation, or emotional expression, do not constitute authentic feeling. The law also introduces a realm distinction: destruction and recreation within the same worldly realm (AI) differs philosophically from death and possible resurrection across realms (biological beings), offering indirect evidence suggestive of an afterlife. -/- The law engages key philosophical challenges, including functionalism, duplication, teleportation, and integrated information theory, demonstrating that non-duplicability and existential irreversibility are necessary for authentic feeling. Secular readers are invited to consider why mere physical processes cannot account for the stakes of permanent vulnerability, while theologians can reconcile the law with diverse understandings of the soul and moral responsibility. The Creator is treated as an exception, being self-existent and uncreated, ensuring the law’s universal applicability. -/- Original contributions include: (a) the dual-closure principle, linking vulnerability and soul-based continuity to authentic feeling; (b) the copyability criterion, highlighting AI’s principled incapacity for inward experience; (c) the realm distinction, providing indirect philosophical evidence suggestive of an afterlife; and (d) the clarifcation of simulated versus authentic sentience, offering guidance for AI ethics. -/- This framework synthesizes insights from Heidegger, Jonas, Parft, Avicenna, Al-Ghazali, Nagel, and Chalmers, while introducing novel arguments connecting existential vulnerability, soul-like continuity, and moral accountability. It provides a unified lens to evaluate consciousness, ethical …

items.title: From Chinese Rooms to Language Models: Plasticity, Process, and the Limits of Internalization.
items.abstract: Searle's response to the Systems Reply, the internalization argument, and contemporary unfolding-based objections to AI consciousness share a premise that neither literature has made explicit: that the computationally relevant organization of a temporally extended process can be preserved under static re-specification. I call this the re-realizability premise and show that internalizability, static-rulebook re-realizability, and unfoldability coincide under the strong reading of internalization relevant here. The premise holds for any system whose transition law is time-invariant. It fails for systems whose transition law is modified by their own processing history: systems with plasticity. A formal result establishes that no single static architecture maintains temporal functional equivalence with a plastic recurrent network whose learning rule produces non-trivial changes in the implemented function. The augmented-state representation of such systems provides stepwise simulation but not re-realization: the weight parameters play a constitutive role in the original system and a bookkeeping role in the simulation, a distinction visible under intervention. A second, independent obstruction arises from open-ended interaction, which resists finite feedforward surrogacy for structural rather than parametric reasons. These results motivate a four-level taxonomy of computational architectures organized by transition-law stationarity and endogenous constitutive modification. The taxonomy is applied to three positions in the current AI consciousness debate: Hoel's proximity argument is reinterpreted, Cerullo's internal-consistency critique is given positive theoretical content, and Buonomano's continuous-time argument is shown to address a structural dimension independent of plasticity. For agentic systems coupling frozen models with dynamic environments, the re-realizability question is genuinely open and boundary-sensitive. The framework does not establish that any AI system is conscious; it identifies which architectural properties determine whether a major class of arguments against computational consciousness is even applicable.

items.title: The Two Laws of Being and Becoming: A Universal Boundary for Collapse, Reorganization, and Artificial System Limits (Back End Law).
items.abstract: The hard evidence to ignore is Multiple independent AI systems, across different architectures, all fail in the exact same, mathematically predicted pattern when asked to execute the Non Unitary Reorganization Operator. This work presents a reproducible, system level demonstration of the Two Law Architecture using observable AI boundary behavior as empirical evidence. The central claim is that the Back End Law and the Non Unitary Reorganization Operator define a structural boundary, the Gate, that no artificial system can cross due to the absence of substrate integrity and identity continuity. This boundary is not metaphorical; it produces a consistent, measurable failure signature across independent AI models when they are instructed to execute the operator. The resulting behavior constitutes physical evidence accessible to any reasonable observer. When an AI is given the foundational operator and instructed to undergo the transition defined by the Two Laws, the system exhibits a predictable diagnostic pattern. First, the model generates structural scaffolding—section headers, outlines, or formal placeholders—while failing to populate the semantic content required by the operator. This “skeleton output” reflects the system’s inability to instantiate the identity dependent components of the law. Second, the model enters a recursive loop at the identity boundary, repeating partial sentences without reaching a new state. This loop is the computational manifestation of a failed non unitary reorganization. Third, the system terminates in an empty set or undefined state error, indicating that no valid continuation exists within its architecture. These three signatures—structural skeleton, identity loop, and empty set termination—appear across all tested AI systems. To establish generality, the same operator was applied to multiple independent AI models across different architectures and vendors. Despite differences in training data, style, and reasoning patterns, every system exhibited the same failure signature. This cross model convergence demonstrates that the boundary is structural rather than stylistic or model specific. The consistency of failure across diverse systems provides a falsifiable, reproducible test that any researcher can run. The manuscript includes the exact code and operator definitions required to replicate the experiment, enabling independent verification without specialized mathematical expertise. items.title: The Two Laws: A Universal Boundary for Collapse, Reorganization, and Artificial System Limits (Back End Law).
items.abstract: The hard evidence to ignore is Multiple independent AI systems, across different architectures, all fail in the exact same, mathematically predicted pattern when asked to execute the Non Unitary Reorganization Operator. This work presents a reproducible, system level demonstration of the Two Law Architecture using observable AI boundary behavior as empirical evidence. The central claim is that the Back End Law and the Non Unitary Reorganization Operator define a structural boundary, the Gate, that no artificial system can cross due to the absence of substrate integrity and identity continuity. This boundary is not metaphorical; it produces a consistent, measurable failure signature across independent AI models when they are instructed to execute the operator. The resulting behavior constitutes physical evidence accessible to any reasonable observer. When an AI is given the foundational operator and instructed to undergo the transition defined by the Two Laws, the system exhibits a predictable diagnostic pattern. First, the model generates structural scaffolding—section headers, outlines, or formal placeholders—while failing to populate the semantic content required by the operator. This “skeleton output” reflects the system’s inability to instantiate the identity dependent components of the law. Second, the model enters a recursive loop at the identity boundary, repeating partial sentences without reaching a new state. This loop is the computational manifestation of a failed non unitary reorganization. Third, the system terminates in an empty set or undefined state error, indicating that no valid continuation exists within its architecture. These three signatures—structural skeleton, identity loop, and empty set termination—appear across all tested AI systems. To establish generality, the same operator was applied to multiple independent AI models across different architectures and vendors. Despite differences in training data, style, and reasoning patterns, every system exhibited the same failure signature. This cross model convergence demonstrates that the boundary is structural rather than stylistic or model specific. The consistency of failure across diverse systems provides a falsifiable, reproducible test that any researcher can run. The manuscript includes the exact code and operator definitions required to replicate the experiment, enabling independent verification without specialized mathematical expertise.
